title: மெய்ஞ்ஞானப் புலம்பல்
theme: Pattiragiriyar's lament opens: every couplet asks 'when?' (எக்காலம்) for a step he has not yet taken. The steps run from burning off the senses and the sleep that is not sleep, through the flood of grace, the cutting of birth's delusion and the taking of the body-fort, to the renunciations: women forgotten, kin seen as false, no life killed, idols seen for what they are, the tortoise's withdrawal, and wandering the world like a corpse before Yama sends him back to the womb.
structure_note: Twenty-four kannis after an unnumbered invocation to the elephant-faced god. The stanzas chain: the second line of one becomes the first of the next (3 and 4 the flood of grace, 5 and 6 birth's delusion, 6 and 7 the fort of the body, 8 and 9 wandering like a ghost), so the lament advances by small turns rather than by topics. Only 17 uses the refrain as sarcasm: the idols will never become the Real.
source_issues: 1: an unnumbered invocation (u1) printed before the work's own numbering; its seq is 1 and the work's verse 1 is seq 2.
23: போல்இ ழிந்து is a broken word division for போல் இழிந்து.

reading: To speak this lament, the word of knowledge that gives release, when shall I receive the grace of the elephant-faced one?
nuance: An invocation to Ganapati (அத்திமுகவன், the elephant-faced) outside the work's own numbering; it names the whole poem a புலம்பல் (lament) and claims that its words give release.

reading: Burning off the five senses in which the ego hides, and sleeping without sleeping, when shall I gain bliss?
nuance: தூங்காமல் தூங்கி, sleeping without sleep, is the yogic stillness that keeps awareness, the state Tirumular calls seeing while asleep. ஆங்காரம் உள்ளடக்கிய can mean the senses that hold the ego within them or the senses the ego has drawn in; either way the ego and the five are burned together. 75 closes the third run with the same verb, சுட்டறுத்து.

reading: Staying in the unceasing sleep of Siva-yoga, when shall I dam up the flood of compassion that never dries?
nuance: சிவயோக நித்திரை names the sleep of 2 as a yogic state. தேக்குவது (damming, storing) treats grace as water to be held, and 4 then asks to drink it.

reading: Having dammed up the flood of compassion in order to drink it, when shall I come and take up the portion I left untaken?
nuance: வாங்காமல் விட்ட குறை, the shortfall left unreceived, is taken by tradition as the practice begun in an earlier birth and not finished, which this life is to resume; the plain sense is only 'what I failed to take'. The verse does not say whose the shortfall is.

reading: Not broken within and withered by worry that never rests, when shall I cut off the bewilderment of birth that maya brings?
nuance: மாயாப் பிறவி can be the birth maya makes or the birth that does not die, that is, keeps returning; the second sense is kept in 6, where the same phrase is cut through.

reading: Cutting through the bewilderment of birth that maya brings, when shall I seize the fort of Kayapuri?
nuance: காயாபுரிக் கோட்டை is read by tradition as the fort of the body-city (kāya, the body), so that seizing it is mastery of the body in yoga. The spelling காயா also allows 'the city that does not wither'. The verse gives only the name and the act of capture.

reading: To bring the fort of Kayapuri under my hand, when shall the direct experience that does not perish come and join me?
nuance: மாயா அனுபூதி, undying anubhuti, is direct experience as opposed to learning; it is named as the means to the capture of 6, not its reward. 62 returns to anubhuti as enjoyment (போக அனுபூதி).

tamil: சேயாய்ச் சமைந்து, செவிடு ஊமை போல் திரிந்து
பேய்போல் இருந்து உன் பிரமை கொள்வது எக்காலம்?
reading: Becoming like a child, wandering like one deaf and dumb, staying like a ghost, when shall I take on madness for you?
nuance: பிரமை is ordinarily delusion; here 'your பிரமை' is the one bewilderment worth having, the mad fixation on the Lord that the Siddhars wear as a guise of idiocy. The child, the deaf-mute and the ghost are the three outward forms of it, and 9 adds the corpse.

reading: Wandering like a ghost, lying like a corpse, and thinking of woman as mother, when shall I complete my tapas?
nuance: பெண்ணைத் தாய்போல் நினைத்து is the ascetic's standing rule for every woman, and it opens the run of stanzas on women (10 to 13). தவம் முடிப்பது, finishing tapas, recurs in 15 with a different condition.

reading: When shall I live forgetting the women who show a foot, show a hand, show the eyes and the face, and so show infatuation?
nuance: The four காட்டி set out the woman's display limb by limb, and the fifth, மால்காட்டும், is what the display produces in the one who looks. The verse blames the showing and the forgetting is asked of himself.

reading: Leaving off the bewilderment of desire for good women, and closing both eyes, when shall I stay merged?
nuance: கண்ணிரண்டும் மூடி, both eyes shut, answers 10's eyes that show: what the eyes are not shown they cannot be caught by. கலந்திருப்பது, staying merged, has no named object; the Lord is understood.

reading: When shall I cease being struck and held fast in the pouch of the vulva, spread open like a cut wound?
nuance: The image is deliberately ugly: அல்குல் as a wound that has been cut open, and the man as something that has been hit (தட்டுண்டு) and stuck there. 13 keeps the wound and makes it the one that does not heal.

reading: Not lying sunk in the wound that does not heal, when shall I console the mind that will not be consoled?
nuance: ஆறாத புண் carries over 12's wound and so can be the body of the woman or desire itself; both readings keep the mind as the thing that is stuck. தேறாத சிந்தை, the mind that will not be cleared, is the real subject of the stanza.

reading: Seeing in my mind that father, mother, children and brothers are false, when shall I cut off the crookedness within?
nuance: பொய் here is not that the kin do not exist but that they are no refuge and no lasting bond, as the Siddhars say of the kin who cannot follow at Death's call. திருக்கு, the twist or crookedness, is the attachment that bends the mind toward them.

reading: Not wandering about killing and torturing firm-rooted lives and eating them, but thinking of them as my own life, when shall I complete my tapas?
nuance: தன்னுயிர்போல் எண்ணி is the Kural's measure of compassion applied to the renouncer's diet; the stanza names killing, torturing and eating as one act. மன்னுயிர், the lives that abide, is also the Kural's word for living beings.

tamil: ஆவி என்ற சூத்திரத்தை அறிவது இனி எக்காலம்?
reading: Without earning the name of sinner and falling into the barren hell, when shall I now know the thread that is the breath of life?
nuance: ஆவி என்ற சூத்திரம், the sutra of the life-breath, is taken by tradition as the secret working of prana, the Siddhars' breath practice; சூத்திரம் is also the puppet-string and the formula, and the word returns in 39 and 40 with both senses in play. The plain sense, the secret of what the breath is, holds without the practice.

reading: A chiselled stone, red paste pressed into a shape, and copper scoured with tamarind: when will these become the Real?
nuance: The only stanza where எக்காலம் means never. The three are the materials of images, stone, paste and polished metal, and the verse does not say the god is elsewhere, only that these are not it. பொருள் is the Real, or the thing of value.

reading: Amusements, comforts, true display and false display: when shall I live having forgotten the whole habit of them?
nuance: மெய்ப்பகட்டும் பொய்ப்பகட்டும் treats show that has something behind it and show that has nothing as one habit (வாடிக்கை) to be dropped; the verse does not rank them.

reading: Leaving behind silk clothes, gold ornaments, pretence and evil deeds, when shall I desire your feet?
nuance: பாவனை, pretence or imagining, sits between the ornaments and the deeds: the finery, the self-image and the sins are one list. The first address to 'you' (உன்பாதம்) in the poem.

reading: Like a tortoise that sees a man coming and draws in its five, when shall I take the form of a mute and subside?
nuance: The Kural's tortoise, with the man approaching added: the withdrawal is from a seen danger. ஊமை உரு, the shape of a mute, joins the deaf-mute of 8 to the drawn-in senses, so that silence is the restraint's outward sign.

reading: Palanquins, halting-houses, latticed windows and mansions: when shall the thought that delights in the sight of them cease?
nuance: The four are things seen, not owned; கண்டு களிக்கும் கருத்து, the mind that enjoys looking, is the fault, which is why the stanza follows the silk and gold of 19.

reading: Having searched out and seen the Father's dwelling-place, when shall I now wander daily like a dead corpse?
nuance: The order matters: first the place where the Father is, found by inquiry (ஆராய்ந்து), and only then the corpse-like wandering of 9 and 23. The place is not named; the Siddhars put it within the body or the heart.

reading: Keeping what remains of dharma, and seeing the bones within as white bones, when shall I now see myself lowered like a cast-off corpse?
nuance: ஒழிந்த தருமம் may be the dharma that remains after renunciation, or the dharma one has given up; the syntax does not settle it. The second line is corrupt in the source (போல்இ ழிந்து for போல் இழிந்து). The sense that holds is seeing one's own body already as the skeleton it will be.

reading: Forgetting petty pleasure, knowing awareness by awareness, when shall I cut off the hold that falling into the womb has taken on me?
nuance: அறிவை அறிவால் அறிந்து, knowing awareness by awareness itself, is the knowledge the Siddhars set above books. கோள் is a hold or seizure, and also a planet: the grip rebirth took on him, or the planetary fate fixed at conception; the first fits the chain into 25.

reading: Before Yama takes me by the hand and puts me back into a womb, when shall I agree to be shaped and ruled by you?
nuance: The pair கருப்படுத்தி (putting into the womb) and உருப்படுத்தி (giving form, setting right) makes Yama and the Lord rivals for the same work on the same body. The run ends on உடன்படுவது, consent, as the one thing asked of himself.

title: மெய்ஞ்ஞானப் புலம்பல்
theme: The lament turns to death and return (the lamp that goes out, the release not had in eight hundred yugas) and to the marks of the Saiva: white ash, Siva's guise, service to his servants, the light on the hill that Vishnu as a boar could not find. Then the body is run through its figures of contempt, puppet, nine-stringed house, worm-nest, salt-pot, rice-bag, a thing to be thrown off, and the run ends with the great secret the four Vedas cried for and did not see, and the darkness of every birth from grass to man.
structure_note: Chaining is looser than in the first run; instead the stanzas group: death and the guru (26 to 27), the Saiva marks (28 to 31), doctrine and absorption (32 to 35), the belly and its wants (36 to 38), the body as puppet and vessel (39 to 47), and the close on the net, the secret and the births (48 to 50). சூத்திரம் runs through 39 and 40 as puppet-string and as formula.
source_issues: 37: செஞ்சலத்தினால் திரண்ட is loosely attached and the sense is uncertain.
45: காண்டத்தை in the first line cannot be fixed with confidence.

tamil: தூண்டு விளக்கணைய தொடர்ந்து இருள் முன் சூழ்ந்தாற்போல்
reading: Like darkness closing in as soon as a lit lamp goes out, when shall I learn the way I died and came back alive?
nuance: The lamp going out is death, the darkness that follows the interval, and வந்த the return into a body; the stanza asks to know the mechanism of rebirth (வகை), not to escape it yet. மாண்டு பிழைத்து can also be 'nearly dying and surviving', but the rebirth sense fits the chain into 28.

reading: Without my mind whirling and withering like a fish in a creel, when shall I seek out the noble one and bow at his feet?
nuance: தூரி is the fisherman's basket; the fish in it is caught and still thrashing. ஆரியன், the noble one, is taken by tradition as the guru, and the bowing at the feet fits that; it is also an epithet of Siva.

reading: To gain the release not reached in eight hundred yugas, when shall I shine wearing the white ash?
nuance: The stanza gives the ash as the means to release, with no inner reading attached; எண்ணூறு யுகம் is a round number for all the past births. It sits oddly beside 17, which denies that stone and copper can be the Real, and beside Sivavakkiyar's question what the ash is for.

reading: Not wandering here wearing a false guise, when shall I excel wearing the guise of Siva?
nuance: அவவேடம் is Tirumular's word for the ascetic's dress worn without the life. சிவவேடம் can be the true Saiva emblems or the form of Siva taken on within; the stanza keeps வேடம் for both and so does not say whether the true guise is still a guise.

tamil: தொண்டருக்குத் தொண்டன் எனத் தொண்டு செய்வது எக்காலம்?
reading: When shall I serve as a servant to the servants of Siva, who drank the poison for the gods and dances in the hall?
nuance: Two acts name the Lord: the poison drunk for others and the dance at Chidambaram. The service asked is at one remove, to the devotees, the தொண்டருக்குத் தொண்டன் of the bhakti tradition rather than the Siddhars' usual solitary line.

reading: When shall I tell of the lamp's light on the hill, which Vishnu did not find though he took the form of a boar and dug up the earth?
nuance: The story is Siva as the column of fire, Vishnu digging as a boar for its foot and Brahma flying for its crown; the hill is Annamalai, where the flame is lit as a lamp (தீபம்). The stanza gives the light to the one who can only tell of it, not to the god who dug.

reading: The sweet clear nectar, the inner meaning of Siddhanta, the seed of release: when shall I think of it first of all?
nuance: Three names for one thing. The nectar is the Siddhars' inner nectar or the sweetness of the teaching; உட்பொருள் makes the Siddhanta a text with a hidden sense; முதல் நினைப்பது, thinking of it first, puts it before everything else that is thought.

reading: Leaving behind all of Vedanta and the Veda, when shall I now stay alone in absorption?
nuance: நிட்டை (nishta) is the absorbed state and ஏகாந்தம் solitude in it. The leaving is of all scripture (எல்லாம்), without the usual distinction between the Veda's rites and its end; whether the texts are discarded or finished with is not said.

reading: Not spending the days of my life seeking some other place, when shall I seek the place that is reached and sleep there?
nuance: மற்றிடம் against உற்றிடம்: the place elsewhere against the place one is already at or that is fitting, read by the Siddhars as the body or the heart. உறங்குவது is again the sleep of 2 and 3.

reading: When shall I know the way those of the hall say that it is false that those here today will be here tomorrow?
nuance: மன்றுளோர் may be the men of the assembly, the wise, or the one in the hall of the dance; the saying itself is the plain stuff of the impermanence chapters. The ask is not to be told it but to know it in their way (வகை).

reading: Not drinking ganja, opium and toddy and withering, when shall I drink the five-fold nectar?
nuance: பஞ்சாமிர்தம் is the offering of five sweet things poured over the image; the Siddhars also read it as the nectar within. The three intoxicants are those Sivavakkiyar names as the fraud-yogis' habit, and the contrast is between two things drunk.

tamil: சஞ்சலத்தை விட்டு உன் சரண் அடைவது எக்காலம்?
reading: To gain the release in this birth that gathered through the red waters, when shall I leave agitation and reach your refuge?
nuance: செஞ்சலம் (red water) and சஞ்சலம் (agitation) are a sound-pair. The red water is taken as the blood of the womb from which the body gathered (திரண்ட), so that the body born of blood is the one in which release (சென்ன மோட்சம், release in this janma) is to be had; the syntax is loose and I can't fix what திரண்ட modifies.

reading: Seeking food for the belly in every place where someone will give it, when shall I now stop this fretful wandering?
nuance: கும்பி is the belly as a pot. The stanza is against the renouncer's own begging round, not against householders' giving; the fault is வெம்பித் திரிகை, roaming in distress for food.

reading: Wandering until the dancing thread is cut, when shall I praise you before the day comes on which this thing is thrown away?
nuance: ஆடுகின்ற சூத்திரம், the thread that dances, is the string of the puppet of the body, cut at death; போடுகின்ற நாள் is the day the corpse is put out. சூத்திரம் then changes sense in 40.

reading: Not wandering about calling the house of nine threads 'I', when shall I discern and know the thread of Siva?
nuance: நவசூத்திர வீடு is the body: a house with nine strings (the puppet of 39) or nine openings, the nine gates. சிவசூத்திரம் is then the formula or working of Siva, as tradition takes it, the secret of 16 in Siva's name; the pun on சூத்திரம் as string and as sutra carries the sense and cannot be resolved into one.

reading: Leaving the worm-nest from which excrement and urine flow and spread, when shall I stand hidden and merged beneath your twin feet?
nuance: புழுக்கூடு, the nest of worms, is a stock Siddhar and Thiruppugazh name for the body; the stanza sets the flowing filth against the feet as two places to stand.

reading: Throwing down this puppet that I took up as a sinner in this life to match the two karmas, when shall I stand praising you?
nuance: இருவினைக்கு ஈடாய், as the equivalent of the two deeds, makes the body the exact payment for good and bad karma; பொம்மை, doll or puppet, keeps the string of 39. The body is thrown down (போட்டு) before praise, not after.

reading: Before this salted pot breaks and takes a womb again, when shall I become the subject of the Lord whose matted hair holds the water?
nuance: உப்பிட்ட பாண்டம், a pot that has had salt put in it, is the body: salt-cured and keeping, yet a clay pot that breaks. அப்பிட்ட வேணியன் answers it with the water (அப்பு, the Ganga) put in Siva's hair; the two இட்ட set the brittle salt-pot against the one who holds the river.

reading: Doing service and seeing the vision of Siva's form, when shall I shed the puppet and gain the fruit?
nuance: பாவை is the doll or image, here the body, as பொம்மை in 42; the service and the vision come before it is shed, so the body is used up rather than refused.

reading: Like the dark cloud that drew up water and went back, when shall I set the pot aside and reach the Supreme?
nuance: காண்டம் is taken as water (a lexicon sense), so the cloud takes water from the sea and returns to the sky; it could also be a portion or a section of a text. பாண்டம், the pot, is the body of 43. The simile's point seems to be a return to the source after a taking, but the first line cannot be fixed.

reading: Not carrying this leather bag of rice about and withering, when shall I throw off the filthy inert body and reach you?
nuance: துருத்தி is a leather water-bag; filled with cooked rice it is the body, a skin full of food. சடம், the inert thing, is the body as mere matter, set against உனை, the one reached.

tamil: தொடக்கைச் சதம் எனவே சுமந்து அலைந்து வாடாமல்
reading: Not carrying the bond as if it were lasting and withering under it, when shall I strip off the garment of the body and know you?
nuance: தொடக்கு is a bond or fetter and சதம் permanence or a hundred; 'carrying the fetter as a hundred' may mean taking it for lasting, or for wealth. உடக்கை is read as உடுக்கை, clothing, so the body is a garment to be removed (கழற்றி), as the pot and the bag were in 43 and 46.

reading: Not caught and perishing in the bond of desire's net, when shall I stand joined in the lamp of the sounding bell?
nuance: ஓசைமணித் தீபம் joins sound (ஓசை, the bell மணி) and light in one object; tradition reads it as nada and jyoti, the sound and light met within at the crown. The plain image is a lamp that rings, and the stanza asks to be joined in it (ஒன்றி), not to see it.

reading: When shall I look upon the great secret that the four rare Vedas called out for and did not see?
nuance: கூப்பிட்டும் காணாத, cried out for and still did not see: the Vedas are not false but are left outside, calling. பார ரகசியம், the great or heavy secret, is what 33 left the Vedas for.

reading: As grass, as beast, as worm, as the form of a man: when shall the darkness of every birth depart?
nuance: The ascending list of births is the one Manikkavasagar's Sivapuranam opens with (புல்லாகி பூடாய்), compressed to four; இருள், darkness, is what all of them share, not any one of them.

title: மெய்ஞ்ஞானப் புலம்பல்
theme: The third run is about ripeness for grace. It borrows the figures of love for the soul's longing: the girl come of age for her bridegroom, the wife whose mind is elsewhere in her husband's embrace, the woman waiting for a lover who does not come at the hour; and the figures of detachment, the tamarind free in its shell and the lotus leaf on water. Love melts body and bone, tears fall like pearls, the honey of Siva-bliss pours; then the stanzas climb the body's centres from Ganapati at the root to the guru's feet at the crown, and end in sleep in absorption with every instrument burned away.
structure_note: Four groups: ripeness and the guru (51 to 54), detachment and the love-figures (55 to 60), melting love and its tears (61 to 66), the six centres with their presiding gods in ascending order and the crown (67 to 73), and a close on the seed of all things and absorption (74 to 75). The centre-stanzas each give a shape or element and a god and ask only to see, bow or ask the way.
source_issues: 60: எவ்வனத்தின் and கவ்வனத் are unusual forms, perhaps for எவ்வணத்தின் and கவ்வும்; the first line may be corrupt.
73: கிடை in உச்சிக் கிடை நடுவே is uncertain.

reading: Not letting my thought cling to any one thing that suits it, when shall ripeness come and I stand watching for your grace?
nuance: பக்குவம், ripeness, is the key word of the run: grace is not asked for directly but the state in which it can be received. தக்கும் வகைக்கு ஓர் பொருளும் is any object that happens to fit the mind's liking.

reading: To embrace the lord of her season and take joy, when shall the maiden's season come and take hold of me?
nuance: தெரிவை is the sixth of the seven ages of woman in Tamil poetics, the age of full womanhood; the soul is the girl not yet ripe for her bridegroom, the Lord. The erotic figure is kept whole, and 53 reads it back as ripeness for the guru.

reading: Knowing all the cherishing that comes with the ripeness a maiden reaches, when shall I know the guru, think of him and worship?
nuance: சீராட்டு is the fuss made over a girl come of age; the stanza makes the guru the one who knows the soul's season and so the one to bow to. 52 and 53 are one figure in two halves.

reading: Though I live with women who make trouble, when shall I now become like the ripe tamarind, firm within its shell yet apart from it?
nuance: The ripe tamarind pulls away from its shell while staying inside it: the standard Tamil image for one who stays in the household and is not attached. The stanza allows living with women (வாழ்ந்தாலும்) and asks only for the inner separation, unlike 9 to 13, which asked to forget them.

reading: Without attachment, like the lotus leaf spreading on the water, when shall I put kin away and my mind stand far off?
nuance: The leaf lies on the water and is not wetted; with the tamarind of 54 it makes a pair of images for being in a thing without being held by it. சுற்றத்தை நீக்கி is gentler than 14's seeing kin as false.

reading: Having seen in full the pleasure a man's own wife gave him in the play of love, when shall it now be told to me?
nuance: The subject of சொல்வது is not given: the Lord or the guru telling him, or himself telling it after seeing. The figure is the bliss of union as a husband knows his wife's delight, a thing that can be seen but has to be told to one who has not had it; 57 to 59 continue with love's other faces.

tamil: உருகுமனம் போல் என் உளம் உருகுவதும் எக்காலம்?
reading: Like the heart that melts when the hour comes for the lover from outside and he is not seen, when shall my heart melt?
nuance: அயல் புருடன் is a man other than the husband; the woman waiting for a lover at the appointed hour is the model for longing. The Siddhar takes the adulteress's ache, the sharpest longing he knows, as the measure for love of the Lord, without comment on its morality.

tamil: தன்கணவன் தன் சுகத்தில் தன்மனம்வே றானது போல்
என் கருத்தில் உன் பதத்தை ஏற்றுவதும் எக்காலம்?
reading: Like a woman whose mind is elsewhere even in her own husband's pleasure, when shall I set your feet in my thought?
nuance: The wife in her husband's embrace with her mind on another: the soul in the world's pleasures should keep its thought on the feet. The figure inverts the ethical poems, where the straying mind is the fault; here it is the model.

tamil: தேடித் தவிப்பவன் போல் சிந்தை வைப்பது எக்காலம்?
reading: Like a man who searches in anguish for the slender woman who joined him and parted, when shall I set my mind so?
nuance: கொம்பனையை, the creeper-like woman, is the stock phrase of love poetry. After the woman's longing in 57 and 58 this gives the man's, so that both sexes' love-sickness are drawn on.

reading: As infatuation with any object is, in whatever way it is, so when shall I set my mind in a meditation that grips like that?
nuance: எவ்வனத்தின் is read as எவ்வணத்தின், 'of whatever kind', and கவ்வனத் தியானம் as a meditation that seizes (கவ்வு) as desire seizes; the words are unusual and the first line may be corrupt. The sense that holds is that the grip of desire is the model for the grip of meditation, which closes the love-figures of 56 to 59.

tamil: கண்ணால் அருவி கசிந்து முத்துப் போல் உதிரச்
reading: With tears streaming from the eyes and falling like pearls, when shall I think of the Supreme that was told to me?
nuance: சொன்ன பரம்பொருள், the Supreme as spoken, is the thing the guru told, not the thing itself; the tears come with the thinking, as in the bhakti poems, and the stanza asks for both at once.

reading: With the body melting, love melting and the bones melting, when shall the experience of enjoyment join me?
nuance: போக அனுபூதி, the anubhuti of enjoyment, answers the undying anubhuti of 7: there it was the means to master the body, here it is the fruit of a body melted by love. The three உருக give the melting from flesh to bone.

reading: Leaving this life that has no standing, like a bubble on water, when shall your flood of great bliss and grace rise in spate?
nuance: The bubble is the body of the impermanence poems; the flood of grace is the one dammed up in 3 and 4, now asked to overflow (பெருக்கெடுப்பது). Water on both sides of the stanza: a bubble on it, then a river of it.

reading: Melting love and pouring understanding over it, when shall I cut the entanglement of the net of bonds that is sorrow?
nuance: Love first, understanding poured on top (புகட்டி, as one pours into a mould): the order is the stanza's point, and the bonds are cut by the two together, not by knowledge alone.

reading: Knowing the way of the womb and not sending my mind down it, when shall I set my love with eyes pouring streams?
nuance: கருவின் வழி is the way one came into the womb, that is, desire and its organ, or the way back into another womb, rebirth; the Siddhars use the gate of birth for both at once. The love asked for has the tears of 61.

reading: When shall my mind stay wearing the honey of Siva-bliss, clear and ever clearer, as it pours and pours?
nuance: சிவானந்த தேன் is the honey of Siva's bliss, the nectar that flows within in the yogic reading; மனம் பூண்டிருப்பது, the mind wearing it, makes the bliss a thing put on and kept, like the ash of 28.

reading: When shall I stand bowing to the lotus feet of Ganapati at the foot of the root support?
nuance: ஆதார மூலம் is the muladhara, the lowest of the six centres; Ganapati is its god in the common Saiva scheme, and the invocation of 1 is here placed in the body. 67 to 73 climb the centres in order, each with its god, and tradition supplies the names of the centres, which the stanzas do not give.

reading: When shall I raise my eyes and see within me the Creator who sits curled in the good crescent bent in the earth?
nuance: வேதா is Brahma, presiding over the second centre in the common scheme; மண்வளைந்த நற்கீற்று, the good crescent curved in the earth, gives earth where the common scheme puts earth at the root and water with its crescent here. The shapes in 68 to 72 sit one step off the usual list and I can't fix the mapping; கண்வளர்த்து, 'growing the eye', is seeing inwardly.

reading: When shall I perceive and know Vishnu, seated in the middle of the water-crescent, inside the salt gourd?
nuance: அப்புப் பிறை, the crescent of water, is the shape of the water-centre; விட்டுணு, Vishnu, is its god in the common scheme at the third centre. உப்புக் குடுக்கை, the salt gourd, is taken as the body, the salted vessel of 43; it may also be a coded name for the centre itself.

reading: When shall I stand worshipping Rudra, who appears in the triangle that has sprung up with three rings set around it?
nuance: The triangle (கோணம், with மூன்று வளையம், three circles) is the fire-shape; Rudra is the god of the fourth centre in the common scheme. The triangle and the three rings may be the fire-centre's diagram or the three worlds or gunas; the stanza names only the shape.

reading: When shall I begin to ask the way to merge with Mahesvara, who lives in the hexagon of air?
nuance: வாயு அறுகோணம், the six-cornered figure of air, is the air-shape; Mahesvara is the god of the fifth centre in the common scheme. தோயும் வகை கேட்க, asking the way to merge, implies a teacher asked; it is the only stanza of the run that asks for instruction rather than for sight or worship.

reading: When shall you grant the grace that I seek the way near to Sadasiva, who abides within the circular path?
nuance: வட்டம், the circle, is the space-shape, and Sadasiva the sixth of the ascending gods, as in Tirumular's order Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, Mahesvara, Sadasiva. கிருபை செய்வது, that you show grace, is the first stanza of the run in which the Lord acts; the seeking of the way is still the poet's.

reading: When shall I now fix my resolve on the guru's feet that rise between the crown and its sides, and attain them?
nuance: உச்சிக் கிடை நடுவே, in the middle of the crown's breadth, is the top of the head, where the Siddhars place the thousand-petalled centre and the guru's feet above the six gods. கிடை is uncertain (breadth, or a place of lying), but the location at the crown holds; after the gods of 67 to 72 the guru stands highest.

reading: Becoming the earth, and on the earth becoming the five colours yourself, becoming the root: when shall I know the seed from which you sprouted?
nuance: பஞ்சவன்னம், the five colours, are the five elements by their colours (yellow earth, white water, red fire, black air, smoke-coloured space in Tirumular); the Lord is earth, the elements and the root, and the stanza asks for what is before even that, the seed (வித்து) he grew from.

reading: Burning off all the instruments and the inner faculties, whose bonds cannot otherwise be cut, when shall I sleep in absorption?
nuance: கருவி கரணாதி are the outer instruments (the senses) and the inner ones (mind, intellect and the rest), the tattvas of the soul's equipment; கட்டறுக்க ஒண்ணா says they cannot be untied, only burned (சுட்டறுத்து), the verb of 2. The run ends in the sleep the first stanza asked for, நிட்டை for தூங்காமல் தூங்கி.

title: மெய்ஞ்ஞானப் புலம்பல்
theme: Pattirakiriyar's lament continues its one question, எக்காலம் (when?), across the inner work: rooting out crooked thought, discerning the tattvas and the three desires, the Shakti in the centre who must reveal herself, the mind cut with the sword of the five letters and watched while it burns, dying before the body dies, and then the breath-yoga in cipher: riding the vaasi instead of walking the earth, rousing the kundalini and opening the sushumna, drinking the milk of the moon-hall, and standing at last with no impurity, no maya, no honour and no clan.
structure_note: Every unit is a couplet closing on எக்காலம், so the reading is what each adds. The stanzas fall in loose runs: 76 to 80 on thought, body and desire; 81 to 83 on birth and the Shakti's grace; 84 to 88 on the mind; 89 to 91 on dying before death; 92 to 98 on the inner path against the outer (ladder, closed eyes, walking, breath, kundalini, sushumna, moon-milk, horse); 99 and 100 on being beyond arts, impurity and clan. Unit 87 is from a different printed source and breaks the running numbering of the நூல் units.
source_issues: 87 (siddhar:meynjanap-pulambal:0155-88) is from a different printed source (pmuni0155, numbered 88 there) and is not among the நூல் units; it fits between 86 and 88 as the continuation of 86's chain of மாண்டு, and may be a stanza the main source omits.
95 line 1 has a broken word, கு ண்டலியை, for குண்டலியை.
96 line 2 சலித்தருப்பது is corrupt or irregular; சலித்திருப்பது or சலியாதிருப்பது is likely.

tamil: கள்ளக் கருத்தை எல்லாம் கட்டோடு வேரறுத்து இங்கு
reading: When will I have cut out by the root, bond and all, every crooked thought, and remain here knowing the thought that is within?
nuance: கள்ளக் கருத்து and உள்ளக் கருத்து are set against each other by rhyme: the deceitful thought is uprooted so that the inner intention (one's own, or the Lord's within) can be known. The same pair, கள்ள மனம் and உள்ளம், returns at 141.

reading: When will I discern, part by part, all that I suffered with this body of states that runs riot?
nuance: அவத்தை is the technical avastha (the states of waking, dream and the rest through which the soul passes) and also plain Tamil for trouble; அவத்தைச் சடலம் is then either the body that carries the soul through its states or the troublesome body. அட்டகாசம் (uproar, riot) is the body's or the states' unruliness. Both readings leave the same request: to take the body's history apart with understanding.

reading: When will I set apart, with the instruments of knowing, all the suffering that the states bring, and grow strong?
nuance: அறிவுக் கருவி, the instruments of knowing, is traditionally the inner organs (mind, intellect, will, ego) and the senses, which are tattvas; the verse asks to use them against the states (அவத்தை) they themselves produce. பெலப்படுவது (பலப்படுவது) is simply to become strong; the pair with 77 suggests analysis as the strengthening.

reading: When will I know, separating them, the many kinds of difference: the elements, the senses, the inner instruments, and what came as bindu and nada?
nuance: The list runs up the tattva ladder from the gross elements (பூதம்) through the senses (பொறி) and inner organs (கரணம்) to bindu and nada, the subtle sources of form and sound. The request is tattva-discrimination, the knowing that these are not the self; the verse does not name what is left when they are set apart.

reading: When will I know the three desires that arise, having parted from them, and when will I cut through, at its base, the root of the desire that has sunk in?
nuance: ஆசை மூன்று, the three desires, is a fixed triad in the tradition, மண் பொன் பெண் (land, gold, woman); the verse does not list them. தோன்றாசை (the desire that appears) and ஊன்றாசை (the desire that has taken root) distinguish the arising from the entrenched, and only the second is to be cut at the root.

tamil: புன்சனனம் போற்று முன்னே புரிவட்டம் போகில் இனி
reading: When will I know, before cherishing this lowly birth, that if the turning circle goes, my birth will then prosper?
nuance: புரிவட்டம், the twisted or turning circle, is unexplained: it may be the round of births, the womb, or, in the breath-cipher, the circling of the breath. புன்சனனம் போற்று முன்னே is also open: 'before I cherish this mean birth' or 'before this mean birth that I cherish'. ஈடேறும் (will be saved, will prosper) is the one firm point: the present birth is to be made to count.

reading: When will the good Tirodhayi, standing in the very centre, show the way to come near grace and act in mercy?
nuance: திரோதாயி is the concealing power (tirodhana shakti), the Lord's act of hiding; Saiva tradition holds that the same power, once the soul ripens, turns to grace, which is why the poet can call her நல் (good) and ask her for the way to grace. நட்ட நடு, the exact centre, is read by the yoga tradition as the central channel or the point between the brows; plainly it is simply where she stands within.

reading: I have stayed saying 'I myself am I'; when will the beautiful one who stands in the centre say 'I myself will reveal it and give it'?
nuance: The two நானே balance each other: the poet's self-assertion and the Shakti's promise. கட்டழகி, the perfect beauty standing in the middle, continues the feminine power of 82 at the centre of the body; the revelation is hers to make, not his to seize.

reading: When will I cut and burn the dense forest of the mind, striking again and again with the sword that is the five letters?
nuance: The mantra is a weapon against the mind rather than an offering to the Lord, and the cutting must be repeated (தொடர்ந்து தொடர்ந்து). The sword of letters returns at 117, where the letters va and ma become the blade.

tamil: வெந்து விழப் பார்த்து விழிப்பது இனி எக்காலம்?
reading: When will I watch this waste mind, that wanders by the paths of the five senses, fall burnt, and wake?
nuance: பாழ்மனம், the waste or ruined mind, is burnt and watched falling; the poet is the onlooker, and விழிப்பது, waking, is his own event after the mind's death. The stanza continues the burning of 84.

reading: When will I have discerned grace, so that kin die, all who have gathered round die of themselves, and anger dies and goes?
nuance: The string of மாண்டு (dying) makes the grammar loose: 'kin, the gathered, oneself and anger' may all be subjects that die, or the kin may literally die while the rest die figuratively. Read with 87, the deaths are inner, the ending of ties and passions through grace rather than the death of relatives.

reading: When will anger die, speech and action die, the 'I' die, the mind die, and the state of release come and be reached?
nuance: This unit comes from a different printed source and completes the chain of மாண்டு begun in 86: anger, speech, deed, I, mind, each dying in turn, with release as what arrives of itself when they are gone. The 'I' (நான்) dies before the mind.

reading: When will the mind that will not settle settle, and when will I see the house of bliss and stay there gazing without blinking?
nuance: இமையாமல் நோக்கி, the unblinking gaze, is a mark of the yogic trance in the tradition; the house (வீடு) is release. The settling of the mind comes first and the seeing follows.

reading: When will I have died already, before the soul in its cage falls dead, slowly, as with a yawn?
nuance: கூண்டு, the cage, is the body; the yawn (கொட்டாவி) is the slow last breath. To die before dying is the Siddhar's state of the living dead, the self already gone while the body stands, taken up again at 90, 126 and 139.

tamil: ஊன் நிறைந்த காயம் உயிர் இழந்து போகுமுன்னம்
நான் இறந்து போக இனி நாள் வருவது எக்காலம்?
reading: When will the day come for me to die, before this body full of flesh loses its life and goes?
nuance: A plain restatement of 89 with the body as ஊன் நிறைந்த காயம், the flesh-filled frame. நான் இறந்து போக is the death of the 'I', not of the body, which has its own later death.

reading: When will I have burnt myself, before the people who themselves will perish come speaking their boasts and burn me?
nuance: சுடு carries both senses at once: the mourners, or the proud, will cremate the body; the poet wants to have burnt himself first, in austerity or in the fire of knowledge, as the mind was burnt at 84 and 85. கெர்விதம் (garvita, pride, boasting) could also be the empty consolations spoken at a death.

reading: When will I look by climbing the ladder of the thread, instead of climbing the ladder of skin and walking far until I am worn out?
nuance: தோல் ஏணி, the leather ladder, is the body, worn out by walking to shrines; நூல் ஏணி is either the ladder of books (the scripture that shows the way) or the ladder of thread, which the yoga tradition reads as the fine central channel one climbs within. The contrast of outer journey and inner ascent holds on either reading, and the next stanzas (93, 94) repeat it.

reading: When will I close my eyes with the Mother and stand embracing her, instead of standing with eyes closed and mouth busy, lost in a daze?
nuance: The rhyme வாயோடு / தாயோடு carries the point: the show of meditation (eyes shut, mouth reciting, mind in a stupor) against the real closing of the eyes in union with the Mother, the Shakti. மயக்கம் can be plain drowsiness or delusion.

reading: When will I ride the vaasi and come, instead of walking the whole earth until my feet give out?
nuance: வாசி is the breath, and in the Siddhars' usage the breath-practice itself; the tradition also hears வாசி as horse (reversing the syllables of சிவா), so riding it is both the breath-yoga and the mount that replaces the pilgrim's feet. The earth walked in vain is the round of shrines.

tamil: ஒலிபடரும் கு ண்டலியை உன்னி உணர்வால் எழுப்பிச்
reading: When will I meditate on the kundalini where sound spreads, rouse it by awareness, open the latch of the sushumna and kindle it?
nuance: ஒலிபடரும் குண்டலி ties the coiled power to sound, as the tradition does: its rising is heard as nada. தாள் திறந்து, opening the bolt, treats the sushumna as a shut door at the base. The rousing is by உணர்வு, awareness, not by force.

reading: When will I stand without obstruction in the sushumna that moves between ida and pingala, and stay there unshaken?
nuance: The three channels are named plainly, which makes this the key to the ciphered 144. சலித்தருப்பது is corrupt or unusual: சலித்து can mean to be wearied or to be shaken, so the sense is either 'to remain without being shaken' or, less likely, 'to stay there and tire'; தடை அறவே (without obstruction) favours the first.

tamil: பாலை இறக்கி உண்டு பசி ஒழிவது எக்காலம்?
reading: When will I leave the root fire, kindle it in the hall of the moon, bring down the milk, drink it and end hunger?
nuance: A cipher verse: மூலநெருப்பு is the fire at the base (kundalini), நிலா மண்டபம் the moon-hall at the crown, and பால் the nectar the tradition says drips from the moon when the fire reaches it; the hunger ended is bodily (the yogi who no longer needs food) and the soul's. Plainly it is a kitchen scene, fire moved and milk warmed, and the cipher is why it is not one.

reading: When will I be in the one space, having let the unbridled horse run into the inner space?
nuance: புரவி, the horse, is the breath in the Siddhars' cipher (compare 143) and in common use the restless mind; ஆக வெளி may be the space of the body (ஆக்கை) or the sky (ஆகாய வெளி). On either reading the restless thing is not tied but released into a space, and the poet rests in the ஏக வெளி, the single space beyond.

reading: When will I live and move in the reality that the many prattling arts cannot reach, and gain tapas?
nuance: பஞ்சரித்துப் பேசும் பல்கலை, the many sciences that chatter, are not condemned as false but as unable to reach (எட்டா) the object; 136 returns to this after the arts have been examined. தவம் here is the attainment, not the means.

tamil: மலமும் சலமும்அற்று மாயை அற்று மானம் அற்று
நலமும் குலமும் அற்று நான் இருப்பது எக்காலம்?
reading: When will I be, with no impurity and no water, no maya, no honour, no good and no clan?
nuance: மலமும் சலமும் is bodily (excrement and urine) and doctrinal (mala, the bond) at once; the list then strips maya, honour (மானம், which is also pride), good fortune (நலம்) and lineage (குலம்). The verse does not say what remains; நான் இருப்பது, 'I being', is the whole of it.

title: மெய்ஞ்ஞானப் புலம்பல்
theme: The lament turns from the breath to knowing: seeing within oneself instead of circling the world, passing from ignorance through grace-knowledge to the house of true knowledge, the fourth state, the light beyond the six adharas, the body of three malas seen as stainless, the three voids made void, 'you' seen in the sky-reality, the letters va, ma, si and a and their dying into the One, the Lord coming as guru, the 'I' that is really 'He', the magnet that draws iron to the feet, and the pranava cut through by holy madness.
structure_note: Loose runs: 101 to 107 on inner seeing and the ascent of knowledge; 108 to 110 on the body, the malas and karma; 111 to 114 on lights, dream and fullness; 115 to 118 on the voids and the letters; 119 to 125 on guru, self and the Lord, closing with the magnet and the pranava. The refrain எக்காலம் is constant and the reading is what each couplet adds.
source_issues: 108 line 2 இன்பமற்று may be a corruption of இன்பம் உற்று; the sense reverses with it.
125 line 1 பித்தாயம் is not a known word; பித்து with a suffix, or a corruption.

tamil: ஓடாமல் ஓடி உலகை வலம் வந்து சுற்றித்
reading: When will I run without running, go round the whole world, and without seeking behold it within myself?
nuance: ஓடாமல் ஓடி, running without running, makes the circuit of the world (வலம் வந்து, the pilgrim's circumambulation) an inner act, and தெரிசிப்பது (darshan) the sight that shrines promise is had என்னிடமாய், in oneself. The stanza completes 94's riding the breath instead of walking the earth.

reading: When will I leave ignorance, touch the limit of grace-knowledge, gain the house of true knowledge and come forth?
nuance: Three stages are named in order: அஞ்ஞானம், அருள் ஞானம், மெய்ஞ்ஞானம், with grace-knowledge as a stage that has a limit (எல்லை) to be touched and passed. மெய்ஞ்ஞான வீடு gives the work its title; வெளிப்படுவது is to emerge or be revealed, the poet's own coming out into the open.

reading: When will I watch until I win, leave all anger far behind, and direct my thought only as far as the word?
nuance: The two மட்டும் are the difficulty: வெல்லும் மட்டும் பார்த்து is 'watching until victory' (over anger, over the senses), and சொல்லும் மட்டும் சிந்தை செலுத்துவது may be 'sending the mind only as far as speech reaches', that is, no further than the guru's word, or 'letting thought go only so far as can be spoken'. The plain part is the leaving of anger.

tamil: நாலாம் பதம் தேடி நான் பெறுவது எக்காலம்?
reading: When will I seek the highest state, set the true reality within, seek the fourth state and gain it?
nuance: நாலாம் பதம், the fourth state, is turiya (beyond waking, dream and sleep) in the avastha scheme, or sayujya, the fourth and highest of the graded releases; மேலாம் பதம் may be the same thing or a step above it. The verse keeps the ascent in steps rather than naming the end.

tamil: எண்ணாத தூரம் எல்லாம் எண்ணி எண்ணிப் பாராமல்
reading: When will I see and know as light within a mirror, instead of counting and surveying, over and over, all the uncounted distances?
nuance: The contrast is between measuring what is far and seeing what is near: the image is at once in the mirror, as the light is, without the labour of range. The mirror is the mind or the inner eye in the tradition; the verse only gives the figure.

reading: When will I know myself, know the nature of being with my Lord, and be settled?
nuance: The order matters: self-knowledge first, then the knowledge of the Lord's company, then சமைந்திருப்பது, being composed or complete. எங்கோமான், our king, is the only name the Lord is given.

reading: When will I see the great light of bliss beyond the six adharas as my attainment, and possess it?
nuance: The six centres of the yogic body are passed, not dwelt in, and the light is above them. பேறு, attainment or gain, treats the light as a possession to be had rather than a place to be reached.

reading: When will I see and know, by seeing, free of pleasure, before the body perishes and goes through the delusion of anava?
nuance: ஆணவ மாயம் joins the first impurity (anava, the ego's darkness) to maya as the delusion that wears the body out. இன்பமற்று is odd: it may mean free of sense-pleasure, or be a corruption of இன்பம் உற்று (gaining joy), which would reverse it; and the repeated காணுதல் and கண்டறிவது make the sentence circular. The firm part is the deadline: before the body goes.

tamil: நில்மலமாய்க் கண்டு வினை நீங்கி இருப்பது எக்காலம்?
reading: When will I see this body, sprung up from the three malas joined together, as stainless, and be free of karma?
nuance: மும்மலம் is the Saiva triad anava, karma and maya; the body grows from them like a shoot (முளைத்தெழுந்த). நில்மலம் is நின்மலம், nirmala, stainless: the same impure body is to be seen as pure, which is the knower's body of the Tirumanthiram, not a different body.

tamil: முன்னை வினை கெடவே மூன்று வகைக் காட்சியினால்
reading: When will you be revealed and reached by me through the three kinds of seeing, so that former karma perishes?
nuance: மூன்று வகைக் காட்சி, the threefold seeing, is unexplained: the three means of knowledge (perception, inference, scripture), the three lights (sun, moon, fire, as at 148), or three eyes. முன்னை வினை, former karma, is what the seeing is to destroy.

reading: When will the light of the eye leaping, the grasping of the intent, and the seeing of the light of the sky all be revealed?
nuance: Three events are listed as past (பாய்ந்ததுவும், கொண்டதுவும், கண்டதுவும்) and their making-manifest is asked for: the poet has had the flashes and wants them to become open sight. In the yoga reading the eye-light is the brow centre and the sky-light the crown; plainly they are glimpses.

tamil: கனவு கண்டால் போல் எனக்குக் காட்டி மறைத்தே இருக்க
reading: When will I fix my thought in the supreme space, while you show me as in a dream and keep hiding?
nuance: காட்டி மறைத்து, showing and hiding, is the Lord's act of concealing (tirodhana, the Tirodhayi of 82); the poet's answer is not to wait for the showing but to hold the mind in the பரவெளி, the supreme space, steadily. The dream is the mode of the glimpse, not its content.

tamil: ஆர் என்று கேட்டதுவும் அறிவு வந்து கண்டதுவும்
reading: When will I discern the one who asked 'who?', the knowledge that came and saw, and the one who said 'look'?
nuance: Three agents, three past acts: an asking, a seeing, a commanding. One reading makes them the soul (who asks), understanding (which sees) and the guru (who says 'see'); another makes all three the Lord's doing within. The verse asks only to tell them apart (பகுத்தறிவது).

reading: When will I see the full fullness, filling every thought I think, above the point, and shed pearls from my eyes?
nuance: முனை, the point, is read by the yoga tradition as the tip of the nose or the brow point where the gaze is fixed; above it is where the vision opens. முத்துதிர்ப்பது, pearls dropping, is tears of devotion; the fullness (பரிபூரணம்) is seen, not reasoned, and at 135 is what all inner speech is finally seen as.

reading: When will I love, with the three voids made void, the first void become emptiness, and that void too made void?
nuance: முப்பாழ் is Tirumular's three voids (of maya, of knowledge or space, of the soul in Siva-Shakti), and the verse voids them, voids the first void into சூனியம், and voids even that; what is left is அன்பு செய்வது, loving. Whether love is what is done in the last void or what remains when the voids are gone is not settled by the grammar.

tamil: சீ யென்று எழுந்து தெளிந்து நின்ற வான் பொருளை
நீ யென்று கண்டு நிலை பெறுவது எக்காலம்?
reading: When will I see the sky-reality, that rose with 'see' and stood clear, as 'you', and gain a standing?
nuance: சீ யென்று எழுந்து is doubled: சீ is the letter si of சிவாய (so the reality rises with the mantra's letter, as 117 continues with va, ma and si), or a hiss or expulsion. நீ யென்று கண்டு, seeing it as 'you', rhymes the two syllables and echoes the great saying 'you are that'; the poet asks to see the vast reality as his own 'you', the second person, not yet as 'I'.

reading: When will I stand contained within the letter a, with the letter va and the letter ma become the sword, and the letter si?
nuance: The letters are those of சிவாயநம: va, ma and si are named, and அவ்வெழுத்து is the letter a (the first of Om, as the Kural's அகர முதல) or 'that letter'. The sword returns from 84: there the five letters together cut the mind, here two of them are the blade and the rest are sheathed in a. Tradition reads such letter-verses as the breath's syllables; the plain sense is the mantra folded into its first sound.

reading: When will I set my thought firmly in what stood as One when all the letters had died and perished, and take love?
nuance: After 117 has folded the letters into a, this voids even that: எழுத்தெல்லாம் மாண்டிறந்து, all letters dead, and the One (ஏகம்) standing without them. Love is again the last act, as at 115; the mantra is a ladder left behind.

tamil: குருவாக வந்து எனை ஆட்கொண்டு அருள்வது எக்காலம்?
reading: When will you take form as grace, being the beginning and the end, come as the guru, take me over and grant grace?
nuance: The guru is grace embodied (அருளாய் உருவாகி), and the one who is beginning and end comes in that form; ஆட்கொண்டு, taking as a servant, is the Saiva word for the Lord's claiming of a soul. The poet does not seek a teacher; he waits for the Lord to arrive as one.

tamil: நான் என்று அறிந்தவனை நான் அறியாக் காலம் எல்லாம்
தான் என்று நீ இருந்ததனை அறிவது எக்காலம்?
reading: When will I know that all the time I did not know the one who knew as 'I', you were there as 'self'?
nuance: Three pronouns do the work: நான் (the knower who says 'I'), நீ (you, the Lord) and தான் (self, the third person). The claim is that the 'I' the poet never examined was all along 'you' standing as 'self'; knowing this is the whole request.

tamil: என் மயமாய்க் கண்டதெல்லாம் எண்ணி எண்ணிப் பார்த்த பின்பு
தன் மயமாய்க் கொண்டதிலே சார்ந்து நிற்பது எக்காலம்?
reading: When will I stand resting in what I have taken as His, after thinking over and over all that I had seen as mine?
nuance: என் மயம் and தன் மயம், 'of my nature' and 'of His nature', are the two ways of seeing the same things; the move is not to give things up but to re-see them as His. The thinking over (எண்ணி எண்ணிப் பார்த்த பின்பு) is the labour that precedes the rest.

reading: When will I know the way space is within space, as a form is born as light within light?
nuance: Two nested pairs, light in light and space in space, with the first given as the model for the second. The tradition reads the inner light born in the outer as the soul's light in the Lord's, and the space in space as the inner sky within the cosmic; the verse states only the nesting.

reading: When will I shut the true reality that gave light into the inner way, bring it out, seal it, and attain release?
nuance: அடைத்து, வெளியிட்டு, சாத்தி, shutting in, letting out and sealing, are the breath's words (the held breath, its release and the closing of the doors) in the yoga reading, applied to the மெய்ப்பொருள் held in the inner channel. Plainly it is a treasure locked away; the sequence of in, out and seal is what makes the breath reading natural.

reading: When will you leap, seize and draw me and set me at your feet, as a magnet pulls iron and draws it into its hand?
nuance: The magnet is the Lord and the iron the poet: the pull is the Lord's, and the poet asks only to be pulled. The same figure serves the Siddhars for the mind drawn to the Real and the Thiruppugazh for the man drawn to women.

reading: When will I take up madness, cut through the pranava, and wander like a red streak?
nuance: பித்தாயம் is unclear: பித்து (madness, the god-madness the Siddhars claim) with a suffix, or a corrupt word. பிரணவத்தை ஊடறுத்து, cutting through Om, is in the yoga reading passing beyond the sound to what is past it (the நாதாந்தம் of 149). செந்தாரை, a red stream or streak, is a meteor, a ray, or a flow of blood-red fire; the wandering is the freed madman's, taken up at 138.

title: மெய்ஞ்ஞானப் புலம்பல்
theme: The lament gathers its themes: lying like a discarded corpse, wandering without caste as Kapila's agama says, casting off the bellows-body and the births as stone, tree, fish, bird and grass, waiting ripe for grace, the house of great bliss, the fullness seen in all inner speech, being dead without dying under the true guru's feet, the Lord as the string that makes the puppet dance, the reality no reading, speech or worship shows, and then the breath in cipher: the twelve-legged horse bound in two chains, the middle leg between the two outer ones, the wind-cow tied to the milk, the homa fire within, the three lights lit in the inner house and the dance seen in the heart, the centre of nada's end, and the sky known as open space.
structure_note: Loose runs: 126 to 130 on corpse, caste, body and births; 131 to 137 on grace, tattva, the centre, the house of bliss, fullness, the arts and birth cut off; 138 to 142 on madness, the living dead, the puppeteer, the hidden Lord and the unshown reality; 143 to 150 in cipher on the breath (horse, legs, cow, moon-boundary, fire, lights, nada's end, open sky). 126 is a near-double of 23 in the same work.
source_issues: 126 is a near-double of 23 (siddhar:meynjanap-pulambal:22): the second lines are the same and the first differ only in கருத்தினை / தருமத்தினை; one is probably a variant of the other carried into the running text.
145 line 2 கட்டி வப்பது for கட்டி வைப்பது.
143 line 1 சில்லம் is unexplained and may be corrupt.

tamil: ஒழிந்த கருத்தினை வைத்து உள் எலும்பு வெள் எலும்பாய்க்
கழிந்த பிணம் போல் இருந்து காண்பது இனி எக்காலம்?
reading: When will I keep the thought that has ceased, lie like a discarded corpse with the inner bone turned white bone, and see?
nuance: ஒழிந்த கருத்து is thought that has stopped, or the one thought that remains when the rest have gone; the near-double at 23 has ஒழிந்த தருமம் instead. வெள் எலும்பு, the bone bleached white, is the corpse long dead; the poet asks to lie as one while still seeing (காண்பது), the living death of 89 and 139.

reading: When will I go about without any division of caste, as the words of the agama spoken by the first Kapila say?
nuance: ஆதிகபிலர் is Kapila, the Sankhya sage whom the Siddhar lists count as one of their own; the ஆகமம் credited to him is unidentified, and the Tamil Kapilar Agaval, the best-known verse attack on caste, may be meant. The verse grounds castelessness in a text, which is unusual for a Siddhar, who more often grounds it in the body.

tamil: ஊதும் துருத்தியைப் போட்டு உனை அடைவது எக்காலம்?
reading: When will I mark gambling, theft and the chain of karma, throw off this bellows that the wind blows, and reach you?
nuance: காற்று ஊதும் துருத்தி, the bellows the wind blows, is the breathing body, the Siddhars' recurring figure. சுட்டி may be 'pointing out' (naming the faults to be left) or 'branding, burning' them; தொடர்வினை, karma that follows, is the third item beside the two vices.

reading: When will I stand united in the lamp of the sounding bell, instead of perishing caught in the net of desire, the bond?
nuance: ஆசைவலைப் பாசம் makes desire itself the net and the bond (pasam). ஓசைமணித் தீபம், the lamp of the bell's sound, joins the two inner signs of the yoga tradition, nada heard and light seen, into one object to merge with.

tamil: புல்லாய் பிறந்த சென்மம் போதும் என்பது எக்காலம்?
reading: When will I say 'enough' to the births I have been born into as stone, tree, fish, bird and grass?
nuance: The list runs across the kinds of life, with stone (கல்) first, so that even the inert is a birth. போதும் என்பது, saying 'enough', is the only act asked for; the verse does not say what ends the births, only that the poet should be sated with them.

reading: When will I rest on no object that suits me, and in thought, ripe, watch for your grace?
nuance: பக்குவம், ripeness, is the Saiva term for the soul ready to receive grace; the verse pairs it with holding to nothing. பார்த்திருப்பது is waiting and watching, not acting: grace is expected, not earned.

reading: When will I understand, in harmony with its root, the tattva that comes swaying and whirling with its base?
nuance: தூர் is a plant's base or stump, so தூரோடு அசைந்து is 'swaying with its base' and வேரோடு இசைந்து 'in accord with its root', the tattva as a plant to be known from the root up; தூர் can also be read as distance, 'moving from afar'. The verse asks to understand the tattvas, not to discard them.

reading: When will I set at the single central root the picture that arose in fear, its parts displaced from the centre?
nuance: சித்திரம், the picture, is unexplained: the body, the mind's images, or the yantra; பாகம் நடு மாறி, its parts shifted from the middle, is read by the yoga tradition as the breath gone into the side channels, and ஏக நடு மூலம், the one central root, as the base of the sushumna. பயந்து எழுந்த, risen from fear or born from, is itself two readings.

reading: When will I go by the high street of knowledge that shows one joy, see the house of great bliss and possess it?
nuance: ஓரின்பம் and பேரின்பம், the one joy and the great joy, are graded: the road of knowledge shows a single joy and the house at its end is the great one. The house (வீடு) is release, as at 102.

reading: When will I see as fullness all that came as cause and spoke in my thought, and praise it?
nuance: காரணமாய் வந்து, coming as cause, and உரைத்தது, what spoke, point to the inner speaking of the Lord or guru in the mind; the verse asks to see all of it as பூரணம், the fullness, rather than as separate instructions. 114 saw the fullness above the point; here it is heard.

tamil: நீ என்றும் இல்லா நிசம் காண்பது எக்காலம்?
reading: When will I see, after examining all the arts that are studied, the truth in which there is never a 'you'?
nuance: நீ என்றும் இல்லா நிசம் is the hinge: 'the truth in which there is no you', that is, no second person and no duality, or 'the truth that you are never not', the Lord's constant presence. The arts (கலை) are examined to the end and found not to be it, as at 99; the verse does not despise them.

reading: When will I take as my aim the Lord who gave the clan, join him without parting, and cut off birth?
nuance: குலம் அளித்த நாயகன் is the Lord who gave the lineages (the maker of clans), or who gave the poet a kin, the devotees; after 127 has refused caste, the only clan is the one he gives. குறியாகக் கொண்டு, taking as target or sign, is the yogi's fixing of attention.

tamil: மத்தடுத்து நின்ற மருள் ஆடு வார் போல
reading: When will I stand seized by madness and have your grace, like those who dance in frenzy when the possession takes them?
nuance: மருள் ஆடுவார் are the possessed dancers of village worship, and மத்து the frenzy that comes on them (or the churning-stick, which is unlikely here); பித்து, madness, is the Siddhars' name for their own state, taken up from 125. Grace is to be had in a seizure, not in composure.

reading: When will I ask to be dead without dying, cooked without being cooked, under the golden feet of the true guru?
nuance: The two paradoxes, சாவாமல் செத்து and வேகாமல் வெந்து, are Siddhar formulas for the body kept while the self is gone, and for austerity that burns without consuming. Both happen at the guru's feet; the verse makes even the asking (வேண்டுவது) something to wait for.

reading: When will I know you, the string that makes me dance while I stay not knowing myself, and gain tapas?
nuance: சூத்திரம் is the puppet's string and the puppeteer's device; the poet dances by it unknowing, and knowing the string is knowing the Lord. The figure returns at 150 as a kite-string, free.

reading: When will my thieving mind clear and see the Lord who stayed hidden, unknown to the heart?
nuance: உள்ளம் and கள்ள மனம் repeat the pun of 76 (உள்ளக் கருத்து, கள்ளக் கருத்து): the Lord hides in the heart that does not know him, and the deceitful mind must clear (தெளிந்து) before the hidden one is seen.

reading: When will I see the reality that is not seen by reading, not spoken by opening the mouth, and does not appear by worship?
nuance: Three means are denied in turn, scripture (வாசித்தும்), speech and ritual worship (பூசித்தும்); the verse does not say what does show the reality, only that these do not. The denial of worship is the sharpest for a devotional poet.

tamil: பின் இரண்டு சங்கிலிக்குள் பிணிப்பது இனி எக்காலம்?
reading: When will I bind the twelve-legged horse that leaps, so that it does not kick the plate, within the two chains behind?
nuance: A cipher verse. The horse with twelve legs is the breath (Tirumular's ஈராறு கால் புரவி), its twelve being the twelve finger-breadths the breath travels or the twelve kalas; the two chains behind are, in the tradition, ida and pingala, or the two nostrils; சில்லம் is unexplained (a shard, a wheel, a plate). The plain sense is a wild horse tethered; the cipher makes it the breath held.

reading: When will I leave the two country legs, go through the middle leg, and sit within the two goat legs?
nuance: Wholly in cipher. நாட்டுக்கால் (the two legs planted in the country), நடுவுக்கால் (the middle leg) and ஆட்டுக்கால் (the two goat legs) are read by the tradition as ida and pingala, the sushumna, and a pair at the upper end (the two brows or two eyes, the 'moving' pair); 96 says the first two plainly. The plain words give a man stepping between legs of unlike kinds, which is not a sentence, so the cipher is the only reading.

tamil: காற்பசுவை ஓட்டி அதில் கட்டி வப்பது எக்காலம்?
reading: When will I fasten the taste of milk, set it in the place and cherish it, drive the wind-cow there and tie it?
nuance: காற்பசு, the wind-cow (காற்று பசு), is the breath; பால், milk, is the nectar of 97; பதி is the place, the town, or the Lord. The tradition reads it as the breath driven to the crown and bound where the nectar is; plainly it is a cow tied where it is fed. கட்டி வப்பது is கட்டி வைப்பது.

reading: When will I meet straight, going through the moon's boundary, instead of letting the mind run loose to many places and not watching it?
nuance: நிலவரை splits two ways: நிலா வரை, the moon's region or boundary (the moon-hall of 97, at the crown), or நில வரை, the limit of the land. With the cipher of the surrounding verses the first is likelier; நேர்படுவது, meeting straight or coming into line, is the mind's arrival after its scattering.

reading: When will I kindle the homa fire and stay within, so as to cross the sea of desire and climb the shore?
nuance: ஓமக் கனல், the fire of the oblation, is kindled உள், within: the Vedic fire is made inner, the yogic fire at the base that the Siddhars set against the outer rite. The sea of desire is crossed by burning, not by swimming.

tamil: உதயச் சுடர் மூன்றும் உள்வீட்டி லே கொளுத்தி
reading: When will I light the three dawn-lights in the inner house and see the holy dance in the heart?
nuance: சுடர் மூன்று are the three lights, sun, moon and fire, which the tradition places in the body as the three channels or the three eyes; உள்வீடு is the body as house. The dance of Chidambaram is moved to the heart, the body replacing the hall.

reading: When will I cross all Vedanta and Veda by climbing into the house, and be at the central root of nada's end?
nuance: வேதாந்த வேதம் எல்லாம் are passed (கடந்து), not refuted: the texts are a stage before the house (வீடு, release) and before நாதாந்தம், the end of sound, where the yogi stands. மூல நடு, the central root, places even that end in the body.

tamil: பட்டம் அற்றுக் காதற்றில் பறந்தாடும் சூத்திரம் போல்
reading: When will I know the sky as cut-open space, like a kite-string that flies and dances when the kite is gone and its loop torn?
nuance: பட்டம் is the kite and காது its ear or loop; with both gone the சூத்திரம், the string, flies free, and the simile is for the self loosed from what it carried. The same word was the puppet-string at 140 that made the poet dance; here the string dances by itself. வெட்ட வெளி, the open, cut-clear space, is the Siddhars' word for the final emptiness.

title: மெய்ஞ்ஞானப் புலம்பல்
theme: Pattiragiriyar's lament continues on its one question, எக்காலம், 'when?': when will he pass beyond even eightfold yoga, set a ladder from the parted body to the ancient city, burn the sastras and the Vedas and find the one formula, know awareness by awareness and sleep without speech, and shoot his awareness as an arrow from the bow of the mind. The second half is a run of similes for the hidden becoming manifest: fire rising from the sea, the worm turned wasp in its nest, gold becoming ornaments, fire from bamboo, the sunstone that burns cotton only in the sun's presence, iron taking the form of fire.
structure_note: Couplets, each ending in the refrain எக்காலம். 151 to 166 ask about states (beyond yoga, pasu and pati, the end of the Veda, mukti); 169 to 175 each open with a போல் simile. Unit 168 is from a second edition and breaks the numbered run.
source_issues: Unit 168 (id siddhar:meynjanap-pulambal:0155-148) is from a second edition: it is unnumbered in the main edition, lacks the refrain's question mark, and is interleaved into the numbered run between 167 and 169.
163 prints என தறிவை with a space inside the word (எனதறிவை).

reading: Beyond the eight-limbed yoga, and beyond what lies beyond it, is the thing that is not reached; when will I reach it?
nuance: Ashtanga yoga is named only to be passed: the goal is placed past the practice twice over (அப்பாலுக்கு அப்பால்). The verse does not say what the unreached thing is.

reading: When body and life, which cling together without clinging, have parted, when will I set a ladder here to the ancient city that cannot be reached?
nuance: ஒட்டாமல் ஒட்டிநிற்கும் describes body and life as joined but not fused. பழம்பதி is the old abode and also the old Lord (பதி); the ladder is set 'here', in this life, which reads as a wish for release before death.

reading: Removing the bond, releasing the soul into the Lord, when will I stay in thought within love?
nuance: The three Siddhanta terms (பாசம், பசு, பதி) are used plainly, and the soul is sent into the Lord rather than made identical with him; 194 later collapses the three into one.

reading: Forgetting rules of conduct, attachment and ritual observance, when will I gain the state of speechless true knowledge?
nuance: ஆசாரம் and அனுட்டானம் are the orthodox terms for prescribed conduct and daily rites; they are to be forgotten, not reformed. The knowledge is பேசா, unspeaking.

tamil: அல்லாது வேறில்லை என்று அறிவது இனி எக்காலம்?
reading: When will I know that the many thousand crores of cosmoses are your creation and nothing other than that?
nuance: அல்லாது வேறில்லை can mean that nothing exists besides his creation, or that the cosmoses are nothing but him; the first is the plainer reading.

reading: When will I recite, know and feel within me the letter called Hari, which stood as the first beginning?
nuance: அரி என்ற அட்சரம் is the crux. அரி is a name of Vishnu, which is odd in a Saiva poet unless, as with Sivavakkiyar's ராம verses, it is cipher; tradition also reads it as the primal letter அ, from which the others come, so that the letter and the First are one. The verse gives no help in choosing.

reading: Burning the sastras, making the four Vedas false, when will I see the one formula and cut off sorrow?
nuance: சூத்திரம் is the terse aphorism that holds a whole science, and also the string that works a puppet (as in 213); either way one hidden thing is set against the whole library, and sorrow ends with seeing it, not with reading.

tamil: அல்லும் பகலும் என்றன் அறிவை அறிவால் அறிந்து
reading: Knowing my awareness by awareness night and day, forgetting speech and what is spoken, when will I sleep?
nuance: தூங்குவது, sleeping, is the rest that follows when speech is forgotten, not slumber; 195 repeats the first phrase and sharpens it.

tamil: முயங்கும் அந்த வேத முடிவு அறிவது எக்காலம்?
reading: When will I know the end of the Veda, which embraces all that moves and stands still as oil is in sesame?
nuance: வேத முடிவு is Vedanta in the literal sense, the Veda's end, and the thing it points to. The sesame image makes pervasion invisible and intimate: the oil is in every seed and nowhere to be seen.

reading: When will I know the one who stood as flesh, as life within the flesh, and as every world, himself?

tamil: என்னை விட்டு நீங்காமல் என்னிடத்து நீ இருக்க
reading: Since you stay in me and never leave me, when will I become one-pointed and never leave you?
nuance: The verse turns the Lord's constancy into a reproach to the poet's own inconstancy; ஒருப்படுதல் is to be resolved, of one mind.

tamil: சொன்னதென்று நான் அறிந்து சொல்வது இனி எக்காலம்?
reading: The limitless sky-thing that cannot be said to be 'this': when will I know it as what has been told, and tell it?
nuance: சொன்னதென்று நான் அறிந்து can mean knowing it to be what the teachers said, or knowing it as a thing that has been said at all. Either way the verse asks for the unsayable to be known and spoken, and leaves the contradiction standing.

reading: Making the mind a bow, the sky's spark its string and my awareness the arrow, when will I shoot?
nuance: The bow is the Mundaka Upanishad's (there Om is the bow and the self the arrow); here the mind is the bow and the target is not named. வான்பொறி, the spark of space, is taken by tradition as the inner light or the breath; the verse does not say.

reading: You who shot me so that I died, and wiped out my disgrace: when will I set you in the open and stand hidden?
nuance: எய்து continues the bow of 163, but the archer is now the Lord and the self the thing shot. வெளியில் வைத்து ஒளித்து நிற்பது asks for the Lord shown and the poet concealed, the ego's death made good; the syntax is compressed and the lines could be divided otherwise.

reading: Like a ferry-boat that is driven by thrusting bamboo poles, when will I know the picture that drives me?
nuance: சித்திரம் is a picture or a marvel, here the unseen mover of the boat; the body is the boat and the poles are the force from outside. 213 says the same with a puppet in the wind.

reading: Without shifting from the state I stand in, without anything attaching in thought, when will I join and know that the state I have gone to is mukti?
Setting within the golden foot adorned with gold and silver, when will I shut it in the flashing space of light?
nuance: The gold and silver on the golden foot are read by tradition as the sun and moon breaths (pingala and ida) brought to the place where they meet, and ஒளிவெளி as the inner space of light; plainly it is the Lord's adorned feet placed within and the light closed in. The verb விட்டு அடைப்பது, letting go and shutting, is itself obscure.

reading: Water dwelling in water joining at the great foot: when will I say in a word how that is?
nuance: A unit from the second edition, without the question mark. Water in water is the stock figure for the soul merged in the Lord with no seam; the poet asks for a single word (ஒரு செப்பு) for what has no seam to describe.

reading: As the worm shut in the nest takes on the wasp's form, when will I, shut in the house, beg for grace?
nuance: In the stock image the worm becomes the wasp by dwelling on it; the poet asks to be shut in the same way and to want only grace. வீடு is a house (the body, or the wasp's cell) and also release, and both senses work.

reading: As the fire hidden in the sea rises up and comes, when will the Siva hidden in the body shine out?
nuance: The sea-fire is the vadavamukha of the Puranas, the fire that lies under the ocean until the end; Siva lies hidden in the body in the same way, present but unseen until he blazes.

reading: As the red light of dawn spreads over the whole cosmos, when will I stand merged in the compassionate holy feet?
As many kinds of ornament come from gold, when will I be born in you and subside in you?
nuance: The ornament is gold in a shape and gold again when melted; birth and subsiding in the Lord keep the one substance. This is the Vedanta figure for the world's relation to Brahman.

reading: So that the sorrow of my being born in a birth lower than a dog's ends, when will I shine like fire-light in bamboo?
nuance: The fire latent in bamboo comes out by friction; the light is already in the poet's wretched birth. நாயிற் கடைப்பிறப்பு is the poet's self-abasement, a stance kept through the work.

reading: As the sunstone's light closes round cotton and burns it, when will I gain grace at the appearing of the noble one?
nuance: ஆரியன், the noble one, is the Lord or the guru. The sunstone burns only in the sun's presence, so the grace comes with the appearing (தோற்றம்), not with the stone's own effort.

reading: As iron with fire kindled in it leaves this form and takes that form, when will I find and know the sweet juice in the sugarcane?
nuance: Two images run together: iron that becomes fire is the soul taking the Lord's nature, and the juice hidden in the cane is the sweetness hidden in the body. How the second follows from the first is not spelled out.

title: மெய்ஞ்ஞானப் புலம்பல்
theme: The similes continue and then give way to the inner states themselves: the turtle whose thought hatches its eggs, butter that will not go back into buttermilk, light that swallows darkness, lightning in the sky, verdigris on copper, the mute's dream. From 187 the poet asks to leave even fixed meditation for the open space and the bare void, to see every form and every pleasure, even that of women, as the Lord, to know where sound and mind are born, to grasp awareness by awareness, and to see the dance that fills the worlds; the run ends with the comic heron glutted on fish.
structure_note: 176 to 185 open with a போல் simile; 186 to 199 are direct askings about states and places (the open space, the void, the hum and Om, the thousand-pillared hall); 200 returns to a simile. The refrain எக்காலம் closes every couplet.
source_issues: 180 carries a PARALLELS note to siddhar:sivavakkiyam:124 (seq 1088); the couplet is a compression of that verse.

reading: As the eggs with embryos take form when the sea turtle thinks of them, when will I reach you?
nuance: The turtle is said to hatch the eggs it laid on shore by thinking of them from the sea; the poet wants to be formed by the Lord's thought of him, or to reach him by his own thinking. The verse leaves it open who thinks.

reading: Like one who leaps out of the house and comes into the open, when will I know the sign for leaping out of the cage?
nuance: கூடு is the cage or nest, the body; the குறிப்பு is the sign or knack for leaving it. Tradition takes this as the yogic leaving of the body (the siddhi of entering another, or departing at will); plainly it is release from the body as such.

reading: As churned butter does not mix back into the buttermilk, when will I, broken free, see you, poor wretch that I am?
nuance: The butter image is of a separation that cannot be undone: once out, the soul does not return to the mixture. உடைந்து, broken, is the poet's own breaking out, or his being broken.

reading: As light swallows darkness and takes one form, when will the darkness that swallows grace depart and I stand?
nuance: The verb விழுங்கி is used twice, once for light eating darkness and once for the darkness that eats grace. The darkness that swallows grace is the primal mala in Siddhanta reading; the verse only calls it darkness.

reading: As lightning rises, lightning subsides and rests in the sky, when will I know within myself what stands within me?
nuance: The couplet is Sivavakkiyar's lightning verse compressed; the source marks it as a parallel. The Lord appears and withdraws within the poet as lightning does in the sky, which stays the same.
