nuance: The verse is obscure and reads as cipher. நகரம் சூறையானது, the city has been looted, is read by tradition as the body-city plundered by death or by the senses, with the potter (குயவன்) as Brahma who shaped it and the one standing in the middle (நடுநின்றான்) as the soul or the Lord within; on that reading the household figures of line 1 are the body's attachments. A plain reading of a town's quarrel and its sack is possible but gives no connected sense. Every part of the reading given is doubtful.

reading: Earth melts, tree melts, maya melts, Vishnu melts, woman melts, man melts, the ways of difference and non-difference melt, the Lord melts, the Mother seated where he melts melts, the one on the serpent bed melts: so is the one word the guru, who thinks and melts, spoke to me.
nuance: உருகும், melts, eleven times, is the word for the devotee's melting in love, here applied to everything down to maya and to the Lord himself. பேதாபேத வகை, the kinds of bheda and abheda, names the Vedantic positions and melts them too; whether the one word (ஓர் மொழி) is a mantra, a teaching, or the word 'melt' is not said. The work ends on the guru's word, as 378 did.

title: அருட்புலம்பல் - முதல்வன் முறையீடு
theme: The opening of Pattinathar's Arutpulambal, a lament addressed to the Lord of Kannivanam: the poet does not know his origin or his end, is maddened by impurity and deeds, and finds every desire in him (for land, gold, women, children, kingship, learning, siddhis, mantras, food, the senses, lust and anger, fear and ego) refusing to leave in the first person, while women's bodies announce that they will ruin him. The chapter ends with the beginning of a long litany: are the days spent as grass, stone, animal, god, demon, king, mother, wife and child not enough?
structure_note: The whole work is in short two-line units with the refrain கன்னிவனநாதா, which the text prints as a separate line every four units (438, 442, 446, 449, 454, 458). The units fall into runs by their closing word: எனக்கு verbs (434 to 437), ஆசை ... என்குதே, where each desire speaks for itself (438 to 447), எண்ணுதே (447 to 449), the body's parts threatening the poet (450 to 452), a direct plea (453), and the போதாதோ litany of births that continues into chapter 29 (454 to 458). The refrain's கன்னிவனம் is taken by tradition as a name of Kanchipuram, and 453 makes the Lord addressed the father of Kandan, so Siva.
source_issues: The refrain கன்னிவனநாதா is printed as a separate line inside every fourth unit (438, 442, 446, 449, 454, 458) rather than as a line of each, so those units have three lines and the rest two.
446 line 2 கைச்சு மின்னுமான் is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: I do not know the root, I do not know the end that ends; the suffering met in the world walks on, seeking.
nuance: மூலம் and முடிவு set the frame: the poet's ignorance is of where he came from and where it ends, the question Sivavakkiyar presses at 989 and 1006. நாட நடக்குதடா can be read as the suffering walking on in search, or as the poet going on in search of it.

reading: By the impurity that is ignorance, understanding and the rest were lost; by the fruit of deeds that do not part, I was seized by madness.
nuance: அறியாமையாம் மலம் identifies the first impurity with ignorance, as Saiva Siddhanta does with ஆணவம். The verse gives two causes in order, impurity and deeds, and madness (பித்து) as the result; the whole lament that follows is spoken as a madman's.

reading: The four beginning with the body I took as myself and was bewildered; I was caught in the net of the powers beginning with mantra.
nuance: தனுவாதி நான்கு is traditionally the four products of maya, body, organs, worlds and enjoyments (தனு, கரணம், புவனம், போகம்). மனுவாதி சத்தி is less clear: மனு may be mantra, so the powers that start with mantra (perhaps the six adhvas), or it may be the human and other orders. Either way the verse says the self was lost in what maya made.

reading: In the forest called great maya I wander; the elements of all the worlds are troubled as if of themselves.
nuance: மாமாயை is the mahamaya of Siddhanta, the pure maya above the impure. தாது may be the bodily humours or the elements, and தாமாய் (of themselves, as if they were I) is hard to place; the line may mean that the poet takes all the world's stuff for himself, continuing 436.

reading: The desire for land has had me eaten by land; the desire for gold and the desire for women say 'I will not go'.
nuance: The three desires, மண், பொன், பெண், are the standard Tamil triad (மூவாசை). மண்ணுண்டு போட்டது is a pun: land eaten the lover of land, as the earth eats the buried. From here to 447 each desire is made to speak in the first person, என்குதே, so the poet's will is shown as not his own.

reading: The desire for children and kin says 'I will not forget'; the desire that is kingship of the quarters says 'I will not end'.
nuance: திக்கரசு, rule of the directions, is the ambition of universal kingship; set beside children and kin it ranges desire from the hearth to the world.

reading: The desire to learn the arts says 'I will not leave off'; the desire to learn siddhis says 'I will not be broken'.
nuance: The siddhis, the Siddhars' own goal, are named here as one more craving beside learning; the verse treats the wish for powers as a bond, not a path.

reading: The desire for mantras says 'I will not forget'; the desire for beauty says 'I will not renounce'.
nuance: சுந்தரம் may be the beauty of others or the poet's own adornment; the verse does not say which. Mantras follow siddhis (440) as a second item of religious craving.

reading: The desire for the kind that binds says 'I will not come loose'; the desire in trade and thrift says 'I will not be broken'.
nuance: கட்டுவர்க்கம், the binding class, may be the household and its ties or the whole category of bonds. செட்டு is thrift or trading, which fits the tradition that Pattinathar was a merchant before his renunciation; the verse itself only names the desire.

reading: The washed clothes I change says 'I will not forget'; the rice pit, too, says 'I will not yet be filled'.
nuance: சோற்றுக்குழி, the pit for rice, is the belly, and தூரேன் (I will not be filled in) is said of a pit. Fine laundered clothes and food are the body's own desires, after the mind's in 438 to 442.

reading: The five senses say 'we will not subside'; the mind's fretting says 'I will not settle'.
nuance: தேறேன் (I will not clear) is said of water and of the mind: the agitation itself refuses to clear. The senses and the mind join the list of speakers, so the poet's whole apparatus talks back.

reading: Lust and anger say 'I will not pass'; and every day the thought comes that we ourselves are king.
nuance: நாமே அரசு is the ego's claim of sovereignty, said daily (நாடோறும்). The pairing காமக் குரோதம் is the Sanskrit kama-krodha, taken as one compound.

reading: Fear and egoism say 'we will not subside'; the ... too says 'I will not come loose'.
nuance: கைச்சு மின்னுமான் is obscure; கைச்சு may be bitterness (கசப்பு) or a word for the hand's grasp, and மின்னும் may be இன்னும் (still). The first line is clear: fear and ahamkara join the list.

reading: The thought takes the body, a bubble on water, for permanent; the desire that rises above all says 'I will not perish'.
nuance: நீர்க்குமிழி, the water bubble, is the Naladiyar's image for the body (27). ஆர்க்கும் உயர் ஆசை may be the desire higher than all others or the desire that rises in everyone; it closes the run of speaking desires.

reading: Even seeing, eye to eye before one's own eyes, bodies burn on the log, the thought comes that we will remain firm.
nuance: கண்ணுக்குக் கண்ணெதிரே doubles the seeing: the pyre is not hearsay. The verse states the contradiction without explaining it, which is the lament's manner.

reading: The thought fondly takes the impermanent for the permanent; it says 'I will not be alone' and 'I will not forget myself'.
nuance: அநித்தியத்தை நித்தியமென்று is the Kural's definition of the lowest understanding (331). தனை மறக்கேன் is the self refusing to forget itself, the opposite of the self-forgetting the mystics ask for; ஆதரவாய் (with fondness) marks the error as an attachment, not a mistake.

reading: The pit of hell says 'I will still eat you'; the loins like a serpent's hood say 'I will ruin you'.
nuance: அல்குல், the woman's loins, compared to the cobra's spread hood (உரகப் படம்), is a stock figure of love poetry turned into a threat; here the body part itself speaks, as the desires did. The hell pit and the loins are set as parallel devourers.

reading: The breasts like young coconuts say 'I will ruin your house'; the eyes like buds say 'I will eat your life'.
nuance: குரும்பை (the young coconut) and அரும்பு (the bud) are conventional comparisons for breasts and eyes; the lament keeps the conventions and makes them threats. குடி கெடுத்தல் is to ruin a family or lineage.

reading: Death, taking a woman's form, plans his deceit; without support here I melt like lac.
nuance: மறலி is Yama. அரக்காய் உருகுதல், melting like lac or sealing wax, is the image of helpless dissolving; 450 to 452 together make the woman's body the disguise of death, the view Tirumular prescribes as a meditation at 1953.

reading: Lord of Kannivanam who in grace bore Kandan: by what means shall I climb up and spread?
nuance: The Lord is identified by fatherhood of Kandan (Murugan), so Siva. ஏறிப் படருதல் (to climb and spread, as a creeper does) is the ascent out of the condition described in 434 to 452; the verse is the first direct plea, and the question is left open.

reading: Are the days that dawned as grass and as shrub not enough? Are the days that passed as stone and as tree not enough?
nuance: The போதாதோ litany, running to 465, counts births through the orders of beings and asks the Lord whether their sum is not yet sufficient to earn release. புல்லாகிப் பூடாய் echoes the famous ladder of births in Manikkavasagar's Sivapuranam, which begins with the same two words; stones and trees count as births.

reading: Are the days ruined as mongoose and as ram not enough? Are the days spent as water creatures and as crawling things not enough?
nuance: கிடம் is probably கிடாய், the ram or goat; நீரியாய் (as a water-dweller) and ஊர்வன (reptiles, crawlers) follow the traditional classes of living things (ஊர்வன, பறப்பன, நீந்துவன).

reading: Are the days gone as elements and as gods not enough? Are the days fallen as demons who inflict torment not enough?
nuance: பூதம் may mean ghosts or goblins rather than the elements; both are classes of birth in the traditional count, and gods (தேவர்) and asuras (தானவர்) are set side by side as equally births to be left.

reading: Are the days destroyed in the mother's womb not enough? Are the days lived as a king and died not enough?
nuance: Death in the womb and a king's death are put together: the shortest and the grandest human life count the same in the tally.

reading: Are the days sunk low as a mother and as a wife not enough? Are the days gone as a child and as a man not enough?
nuance: The poet counts female births among his own (தாயாகித் தாரமாய்), so the soul has no sex across lives. தாழ்ந்த (sunk, lowered) is the verb for the women's births, which may be the poet's judgment on those roles or on the dependence they bring.

title: அருட்புலம்பல் - முதல்வன் முறையீடு
theme: The lament turns from the births endured to the Lord's neglect. After finishing the litany of sufferings (disease, deformity, weeping, Kama's arrows, Yama, Brahma's decree, Vishnu's discus, Rudra's destruction), the poet lists in a run of அையிலை (you did not) everything the Lord has failed to do: remove birth and death, burn the bond, give the ash, the rudraksha and the garb, call him into the devotees' company, grant release, silence and siddhi, fix him in stillness. He then asks for the side-glance of grace and, in a new run of பாரேனோ (shall I not see), begins to describe the Lord's form, feet, anklets, tiger skin, bull, elephant hide, deer and skull garland.
structure_note: Four runs: the close of the போதாதோ litany (459 to 465, now of sufferings rather than births); the ஐயிலை run of the Lord's omissions (465 to 475); a two-unit plea and set of questions (476 to 477); and the பாரேனோ run on the Lord's form, which continues through chapter 30 (478 to 483). The refrain stands as a separate line in 462, 466, 470, 474, 478 and 482.
source_issues: 461 line 1 பட்ட களைப்பபும் has a doubled syllable, for களைப்பும்.
480 line 2 சூரர்கண்டி is obscure and may be corrupt.
The refrain கன்னிவனநாதா is printed as a separate line inside 462, 466, 470, 474, 478 and 482.

reading: Are the days wasted and aching as disease ate me not enough? Are the days born as a ghost, for ghosts to eat, not enough?
nuance: பேயுண்ணப் பேயாய், born a ghost to be eaten by ghosts, adds the preta birth to the count of 454 to 458 and makes even that order prey to itself.

reading: Are the days got as a maimed body, hunched and blind, not enough? Are the days weakened by base food not enough?
nuance: ஈனப் புசிப்பு, mean eating, is either poor food or food got meanly; the count now runs through conditions within a human life rather than through births.

reading: Are the weariness suffered and the anguish not enough? Is it not enough that not even once was I asked 'ruined on your ruined day, were you?'
nuance: The second line is compressed: கெட்டநாள் கெட்டேன் என்று கேளாதும் seems to mean that no one so much as asked after him in his ruin, so the complaint is of being unregarded. The text's பட்ட களைப்பபும் has a doubled syllable.

reading: Are the days spent weeping over impermanence itself not enough? Are the days when all of them carried my burden not enough?
nuance: நில்லாமைக்கே அழுது may be weeping at impermanence or weeping only to no lasting purpose. என் பாரம் எடுத்த நாள், the day everyone lifted my burden, is most naturally the carrying of the corpse, so the second line is the poet's own funeral counted among his days.

reading: Is being brought to the end by Kama's arrows not enough? Is being struck four times by Yama's hand not enough?
nuance: கடைப்பட்டல் is to be reduced to the lowest or last state. நாலும் இடியுண்டல் may be four blows or 'even four'; the number is not explained. Kama and Yama, desire and death, are paired as the two assailants, as in 450 to 452.

reading: Is being cut to pieces by the four-faced one's written leaf not enough? Is being held fast in the discus of the one with honeyed tulasi not enough?
nuance: பட்டோலை, Brahma's written palm leaf, is the decree of fate written on the head. தேன்துளபத்தான் is Vishnu, and his நேமி (discus) stands for his office of preserving; தேக்குண்டல் (being dammed, stagnated) would then be the soul held in the round of sustained existence. 464 and 465 run the soul through the three gods' functions.

reading: Are the days met in Rudra's destruction not enough? You did not know my distress; you did not call me, saying 'come'.
nuance: The first line completes the triad (creation 464a, preservation 464b, destruction 465a), so the soul has been through all three acts. The second line begins the ஐயிலை run: the charge is now the Lord's own neglect.

reading: You did not end birth, you did not take me to follow behind you; you did not end death, you did not ask 'what is it?'
nuance: பின்னாகக் கொண்டையிலை, you did not take me behind you, is the image of the Lord walking with his servant following. The four complaints alternate the great (birth, death) with the intimate (following, being asked).

reading: You did not burn the bond; you did not end my anguish; you did not give the ash you wear, saying 'put it on'.
nuance: பாசம் எரித்தல், burning the bond, is Siddhanta's idiom for the removal of pasa. The ash is asked for as the Lord's own (பூசிய நீறு), given with the word புனை; what the poet wants is to be marked as his.

reading: You did not say 'servant'; you did not give the rudraksha bead; you did not give me your garb to look at the world as a thing to leave.
nuance: அக்கமணி is the rudraksha. The garb (வேடம்) is asked for with its purpose stated, விடும் உலகம் நோக்கி: the renouncer's dress is wanted as the means of seeing the world as something to leave, not as a sign for others. This is the garb Sivavakkiyar mocks (1188); Pattinathar begs for it.

reading: You did not call me into yourself; you did not make me one with you; you did not call me and set me in the company of your devotees.
nuance: ஒன்றாக்கிக் கொள்ளல், making one, is union; the devotees' company is set beside it as a second, humbler ask, and 470 lowers the request further still.

reading: You did not say 'here is one servant for us', a servant to the servants hidden in the high Supreme.
nuance: அடியார்க்கு அடியான், servant of the servants, is the Saiva formula of the lowest and surest place. ஓங்கு பரத்துள் ஒளித்த அடியார் are devotees hidden in the Supreme, so already released; the poet asks to be acknowledged as theirs. எமக்கென்று (for us) puts the words in the Lord's mouth.

reading: You did not have me bear the name; you did not stand so that 'I' ceased; you did not think of me in your protecting grace and call me.
nuance: நாமம் தரித்தல் may be bearing the Lord's name as a devotee's name or wearing his mark; நான் ஒழிய, with 'I' gone, is the ending of the ego that 449 showed refusing to forget itself.

reading: You did not give release; you did not give silence; you did not give siddhi; you did not take me up and cherish me.
nuance: Mukti, mauna and siddhi are listed as three gifts in one breath, with no ranking; சீராட்டுதல் is a mother's fondling of a child, the register the lament keeps turning to.

reading: You did not remove what hinders; you did not make me yourself; you did not end my desire, a fire that cannot be put out.
nuance: தவிர்ப்பைத் தவிர்த்தல், removing the removal, may mean removing the obstacle that keeps him off, or ending the Lord's own avoidance of him. அவிப்பரிய தீ, the fire hard to quench, answers the desires that spoke in 438 to 447.

reading: You did not fix me and keep me in the state of standing; you did not look so that the crowding inner organs perished all together.
nuance: நின்ற நிலை, the standing state, is the state of abiding, as tradition takes it; கரணம் are the inner organs (mind, intellect, will, ego) whose joint ceasing is the condition of it. பார்த்தல், looking, makes the Lord's glance the agent, which 476 then asks for by name.

reading: You did not look so that the bond of the bound world's spectacle fell away; you did not set me saying 'stand in nishtai'.
nuance: நிட்டை (nishtha) is fixed abiding, the yogi's settled absorption; the poet wants to be commanded into it, நில்லென்று. கட்ட உலகக் காட்சி, the world seen as a bound show, is maya as spectacle.

reading: Give the grace of your side-glance, Lord of Kannivanam; crush the impurity that ruins me and look so that I come near.
nuance: கடைக்கண் அருள், the grace of the corner of the eye, is the glance by which the Lord saves; the plea collapses the whole ஐயிலை list into one look. The verse names மலம் again, closing the frame opened at 435.

reading: Shall my longing not cool? Shall I not see and rejoice? Shall I not escape death? Shall my troubles not end?
nuance: காதல் is here the longing for the Lord, not the lust of 445; the four questions turn the complaint into hope, and the பாரேனோ run that follows answers 'shall I not see' at length.

reading: Shall I not praise you, shall I not come seeking your town, shall I not see your golden feet, shall I not stand filled?
nuance: ஊர் நாடி வருதல், coming in search of the Lord's town, is pilgrimage to the shrine of the refrain. பூரித்து நிற்றல், standing filled, is the state of the devotee before the image, and the word recurs as the poet's goal.

reading: Shall I not see the delight of the golden anklet that is Omkara? Shall I not see the fitting thandai and its many gems?
nuance: ஓங்காரப் பொற்சிலம்பு identifies the anklet's sound with Om, so the description of the form begins at the feet and makes the ornament a mantra. The run from here to 495 moves upward over the Lord's body in the order of a hymn of the form.

reading: Shall I not see the victory of the heroes' bell? Shall I not see that beauty which the ... praise?
nuance: வீரகண்டாமணி, the hero's bell, is worn on the leg as an emblem of valour; the Lord is pictured as a warrior. சூரர்கண்டி is unclear: it may be the brave ones who praise him, or a corruption of a word for the anklet-string. The reading of line 2 depends on it.

reading: Shall I not see the beauty of the tiger skin worn at the waist? Shall I not see the triumph of his coming mounted on the bull?
nuance: The tiger skin and the bull (விடை) are Siva's fixed iconography, so the Lord of Kannivanam is now described wholly as Siva. எழுந்தருளுதல் is the honorific for a deity's coming forth, as in a procession.

reading: Shall I not see the beauty of the elephant's hide he wore? Shall I not see the flower hand that holds the caught deer?
nuance: The elephant hide recalls the flaying of the demon Gajasura; the deer in the hand is the one sent by the sages of Daruka forest. The verse names the attributes and not the myths, as a hymn of the form does.

reading: Shall I not see the beauty of the chest hung with the heads of the dead? Shall I not wander crying 'he has taken us as his own'?
nuance: மாண்டார் தலை, the heads of the dead, is the skull garland. ஆண்டார் நமக்கு, 'he rules us' or 'he has made us his', is the devotee's cry of being taken into service; after the skulls, the poet's own wish is to be claimed.

title: அருட்புலம்பல் - முதல்வன் முறையீடு
theme: The close of the plea to the Lord. The பாரேனோ run finishes the description of Siva's form from the throat upward (the blue throat, the moon face, the lips and smile, the ears and crown, Ganga and the moon, the snake, konrai, erukku and datura, the heron feather, the fire, the raised foot on Muyalagan, the hands, the Goddess as half his body, the ash and the crescent), and then turns into a run of கிட்டாதோ (shall I not gain): the day of ripening, the silence beyond speech, the self-purity beyond assault, the open space that ends burning sorrow, servitude to the devotees, and the place where inquiry, worldly care, comparison and attachment have ceased. The last verse names the Lord as the guru of grace who strikes the poet into the state beyond word and mind, and ends in praise of his feet.
structure_note: The பாரேனோ run (484 to 495) ascends the Lord's form from throat to crown and then names the feet, hands and dance; the கிட்டாதோ run (496 to 504) lists the states the poet asks for; 501 and 505 break both runs to address the Lord as குரு. The refrain stands as a separate line in 486, 490, 494, 498 and 502.
source_issues: 485 line 2 திருநயனச் சடையளிருஞ் செழுங்கொழுமை does not parse and is probably corrupt.
498 line 1 வாக்கிற்து is a misprint for வாக்கிறந்து, as the parallel தாக்கிறந்து in line 2 shows.
505 line 1 வசோகசத்திற் is obscure, perhaps for அசோக சத்து.
The refrain கன்னிவனநாதா is printed as a separate line inside 486, 490, 494, 498 and 502.

reading: Shall I not see the cause of the throat that stood darkened? Shall I not see the sight of him standing in the devotees' company?
nuance: கண்டம் கறுத்து நின்ற காரணம் is the poison swallowed at the churning of the ocean; the poet asks to see the cause, not just the throat, so the mark is read as an act of saving. The second line puts the Lord among his devotees, the place 469 asked for.

reading: Shall I not see the face, a great moon ripe with grace? Shall I not see the rich fullness of the holy eyes and the matted hair?
nuance: அருள் பழுத்த மாமதி, the great moon ripened with grace, makes the face the moon and the moon a fruit. Line 2, திருநயனச் சடையளிருஞ் செழுங்கொழுமை, is garbled; it seems to join the eyes and hair in one phrase of fullness, but the words do not parse cleanly.

reading: Shall I not see the beauty growing in the red hollow's piece? Shall I not see the lip that outdid the red fruit?
nuance: செங்குழியின் துண்டம் is unclear: the red hollow may be the mouth and its piece the tongue, or the cheek and its dimple. அங்கனி is the red fruit (the கொவ்வை) to which lips are compared in love poetry; the Lord's form is praised in the idiom used for a beloved.

reading: Shall I not see the light of the smile that casts jasmine moonlight? Shall I not see the beauty of the dark brows?
nuance: மூரல் is the gentle smile and முல்லை நிலவு its white light, jasmine and moonlight in one; அல்லார் புருவம், brows like the night, keeps the inventory in the conventions of akam poetry.

reading: Shall I not see the ears where the makara earrings lie shining? Shall I not see the beauty of the peaked crown and the red matted hair?
nuance: வள்ளை, the ear (from the creeper the ear is likened to), carries the மகரகுண்டலம்; சிகர முடி, the crown like a peak, and the செஞ்சடை complete the ascent of the form begun at the feet in 479.

reading: Shall I not see the sight of Ganga standing with the moon? Shall I not see the way the swelling serpent is worn in the matted hair?
nuance: Ganga, the crescent and the cobra are the three tenants of Siva's hair; பொங்கு அரவு, the serpent that swells, is the hood spread. The verse names the attributes as things to be seen, not as myths to be told.

reading: Shall I not see the forest of matted hair in which the konrai blooms? Shall I not see the solitude adorned with erukku, arugu grass and datura?
nuance: சடைக்காடு, the hair as a forest, lets the konrai bloom in it. எருக்கு, அறுகு and ஊமத்தை are the wild and humble plants of Siva's worship, and ஏகாந்தம் (solitude, or the solitary one) names the ascetic aspect that wears them, a word 497 will ask for as a state.

reading: Shall I not see the festivity in which the heron feather is joined? Shall I not see the bliss of standing with fire held in the hand?
nuance: கொக்கிறகு, the heron's feather, is a less common ornament of Siva's hair, remembered in the Tevaram; the fire in the hand is the dancer's. கொண்டாட்டம் and ஆனந்தம், festivity and bliss, make the form a celebration, preparing the dance of 492.

reading: Shall I not see the lifted foot and the drum-slim waist? Shall I not see the dance upon the struck-down Muyalagan?
nuance: தூக்கிய கால், the raised foot, is the Nataraja's left foot, which the devotee seeks as refuge; முயலகன் is the dwarf under the planted foot, taken by tradition as ignorance or ego. துடியிடை, the waist slim as a துடி drum, is the love poet's word for a woman's waist applied to the dancer.

reading: Shall I not see the swinging hand and its opening gesture? Shall I not see the hand of refuge that grants what is desired?
nuance: வீசும் கரம் is the dancer's swung hand that points to the raised foot, and விகசிதம் (blossoming) may be its open gesture or the face's radiance. அபயகரம் is the hand of fearlessness; ஆசை அளிக்கும் can mean that it grants desires or that it gives love, and the second suits a hand of refuge better.

reading: Shall I not see the great beauty that grows in the half that is the great Mother, while Hari and Brahma praise and the gods cry 'victory, victory'?
nuance: பெரியம்மை பாகம், the Mother's half, is the Ardhanari form, and the beauty is said to grow (வளர்) in it. The gods' acclaim places the form at the dance; the hymn ends its inventory with the Goddess, so the form is complete only as a pair.

reading: Shall I not see the splendour of the fine holy ash? Shall I not see his showing of mercy as the one who wears the moon?
nuance: சந்திரசேகரன், the moon-crested, is given as the form in which the Lord shows தயவு, mercy, as the Puranic story of his sheltering the waning moon has it. The ash that 467 begged for is now seen on the Lord himself, closing the பாரேனோ run.

reading: Though the ruined days are ruined, look now with pity; though the days of suffering were suffered, will the feet not come to me?
nuance: The verse answers the போதாதோ litany: whatever the past has been, கிருபை is asked for now (இனி). பதம் may be the feet or the state; the கிட்டாதோ run that follows takes it as state and lists what the state contains.

reading: Will the day that brings me to ripeness not come to me? Will the solitude that has whirled through every season not come to me?
nuance: நற்பருவம், the good season, is the ripeness of the soul for grace, in Siddhanta the moment when the impurity's hold matures and falls. எப்பருவமும் சுழன்ற ஏகாந்தம் is unclear: the solitude that has passed through every season, or the solitude in which all seasons turn; either way ஏகாந்தம், the Lord's aspect in 490, is now the state asked for.

reading: Will the silence that stands beyond speech not come to me? Will the self-purity that stands beyond assault not come to me?
nuance: வாக்கிறந்து நின்ற மவுனம் places silence past speech rather than as its absence. தற்சுத்தி, purity of the self, is the complement of the malam crushed in 476; தாக்கிறந்து, beyond being struck, is answered in 505 by the guru who strikes.

reading: Will the open space that ends burning sorrow not come to me? Will the clarity that ends even the mind not come to me?
nuance: வெட்டவெளி, the bare open expanse, is the Siddhars' word for the state beyond form, the அருள்வெளி of Tirumanthiram 123. தேறல் is clarity, but also honey or liquor; on that reading the line asks for the drink that ends thought, the nectar of the yogic texts. Both readings stand.

reading: Will being taken as a slave by the devotees who have become not come to me? Will being made to realise, without defect, not come to me?
nuance: ஆன அடியார், the devotees who have become (the Lord, or complete), are the ஓங்கு பரத்துள் ஒளித்த அடியார் of 470; the poet still asks only to be their slave. உணர்த்துவித்தல், being caused to realise, is the Siddhanta term for the Lord's making the soul know.

reading: What shall I say? My guru, hear me: after this I have nothing else at all but you.
nuance: The Lord addressed as the shrine's master is named குரு here and at 505, so the one who gives the states listed is the teacher. நீ அல்லாமல் பிறிதிலை, nothing but you, is the lament's confession of sole refuge, in the plain voice the runs have been building toward.

reading: Will the place where that inquiry dries up not come to me? Will the place where the inquiry one speaks is lost not come to me?
nuance: விசாரம் is both worry and inquiry (vichara); அன்ன விசாரம், that inquiry, may refer back to the questions of 501 or to the mind's worrying in general. சொன்ன விசாரம் தொலைதல், the loss of the inquiry that is spoken, reads best as the end of doctrinal questioning, which the சொல் of 498 and 504 supports.

reading: Will the place where worldly care has ceased not come to me? Will not being bewitched even by the lightning-women of the troop of impurity not come to me?
nuance: மலக்குழுவின் மின்னார், women bright as lightning who belong to the company of impurity, picks up 450 to 452: freedom from their spell is asked for as a state to be given, not a discipline to be done. வசியாமை is not being charmed, the word for a spell.

reading: Will the place where comparison and attachment have ceased not come to me? Will the place of clarity that is beyond telling not come to me?
nuance: ஒப்புவமை, comparison and likeness, ending is the end of thinking by analogy, after a whole chapter of comparisons for the Lord's form. செப்புதற்கும் எட்டாது, out of reach even of saying, closes the list of states at the edge of language.

reading: Guru of grace who strikes me so that I go into the state without sorrow, beyond word and mind: to your paired feet alone I offer praise.
nuance: வாக்கு மனாதீத, past word and mind, is the Upanishadic formula for the Supreme. வசோகசத்து is unclear: taken as அசோக சத்து it is the sorrowless being; the text may be corrupt. தாக்கும், striking, makes the guru's grace a blow, the answer to the self-purity beyond striking in 498. The final போற்றி turns the whole lament into a hymn.

title: அருட்புலம்பல் - மகடூ முன்னிலை
theme: The opening of Pattinathar's lament spoken as a woman to her friend: she bowed to Ganesa asking for grace, and one came, showed his form and took the guru's shape, then burned everything she was made of: the six centres and fifty-one letters, the elements, the senses, the instruments of mind, the three tiers of tattvas and the ninety-six, the stone fort of the body, Om itself and the ego, and both deeds. What is left is a woman alone who knows herself, a house with no one in it, open space, and a town that laughs at her.
structure_note: The whole work is in the second person feminine (மகடூ முன்னிலை): every line ends in -அடி (the friend) or -ஆண்டி (he did, girl), and 'he' is the guru-Lord who came as a man. 506 to 509 and 513 are near-doublets of Azhuganni 33 to 36, so the same cipher of a burned fort is shared between the two laments. The verses run in waves: the burning of the body's constituents (508 to 517, 521 to 525), a question about who he was (518 to 520), the cutting of deeds and the knowing of self (526 to 528), and the public aftermath (529, 530). The first four units carry PARALLELS to Azhuganni; the chapter has no glosses or variant notes.
source_issues: 523 line 1 reads துரிசறிவே where 508 and 516 have the refrain துரிசறவே; probably a copying slip.

506 to 509 and 513 are near-doublets of Azhuganni 33 to 36 (seq 1521 to 1524), and the corpus records the PARALLELS; the attribution of the shared lines to Pattinathar or to the Azhuganni's author is open.

reading: I bowed to the five-handed god asking to receive grace; and one came without delay and showed me his own form.
nuance: ஐங்கரன் (the five-handed) is Ganesa, so the work opens with the usual invocation, but here the invocation is already the story: the prayer is answered by a man who arrives. தன்சொரூபம் is his form; the Azhuganni doublet reads தற்சொரூபம், the form of the self, and the two readings differ in whether what she was shown was him or herself.

reading: To cut off the plundering birth he took the guru's form; to cut off the thieving senses he came as the cause.
nuance: கொள்ளைப் பிறப்பு and கள்ளப் புலன் pair birth and the senses as robbers. குருவடிவம் கொண்டான் says the guru's shape is taken on, not that he is one; the Siddhars' guru is the Lord in a body.

reading: The six supports and the fifty-one letters, the whole fort of deceit, he burned so that no fault remained.
nuance: ஆதாரம் ஓராறு are the six centres of the yogic body and ஐம்பத்தோர் அட்சரம் the fifty-one letters that tradition distributes over them. The fort (கோட்டை) is the body, as in the Meynjanap-pulambal's காயாபுரிக்கோட்டை. The surprise is that the very apparatus of yoga is what he burns; the verse does not say he used it.

reading: The many, many tattvas that breed so much disturbance all lost their heads and burned.
nuance: விகாரம் is change or disturbance; the tattvas are blamed as its source. தலைகெட்டு, losing their heads, is both ruin and the end of their rule.

reading: All those born together with me have died; I cannot stay all alone by myself.
nuance: Plainly a woman mourning her siblings; in the cipher of 508 and 509 those born with her are the faculties and elements that came with the body, which the burning has killed. The complaint that she cannot bear to be alone is answered at 528, where being alone is the ripeness.

reading: Saying 'this is the field where everyone fell', I would perish; if I speak and weep, when will my sorrow abate?
nuance: பட்டகளம் is a battlefield after the slaughter, the body or world after the burning. தொலையுமடி may be 'I would be done for' or 'it would end'; the question of the second line is not answered.

reading: I saw the five elements beginning with earth die and fall; I saw the five senses beginning with the sky-born burn and fall.
nuance: விண்முதலாம் ஐம்பொறி makes the senses begin from the sky, since hearing is the sense of the ether; the two lines run the elements up and the senses down.

reading: The five unparting waters burned to ash; I saw the five beginning with speech die and fall.
nuance: வாக்காதி ஐவர் are the five organs of action (speech, hands, feet, excretion, generation) of the tattva lists. நீங்காப் புனல் ஐந்து is unclear: perhaps the five fluids of the body, or the five senses as a flood that never leaves; the Azhuganni doublet lacks the line.

reading: All the instruments of mind perished, each in its kind, and burned and fell together with their kindred instruments.
nuance: மனக்கரணம் are the inner instruments (mind, intellect, memory, ego); இனக்கரணம், their kin, are the outer senses and organs as tradition reads it. The verse does not list them.

reading: The soul's tattvas burned, their tiers destroyed; how could one praise him, who has taken my awareness away?
nuance: ஆத்தும தத்துவம் is the first of the three tiers of the thirty-six (the twenty-four atma tattvas), and 516 follows with the vidya tattvas and the five pure ones, so 515 to 517 walk the Siddhanta scheme. போதமிழந்தானை can be 'him who lost awareness' or, as taken here, 'him by whom awareness was lost'; the reading turns on it.

reading: I saw the vidya tattvas burn and fall; he burned the five pure ones too, so that no fault remained.
nuance: சுத்தவித்தை ஐந்து are the five siva tattvas of the pure order, the highest of the thirty-six. Even these burn; the refrain துரிசறவே (fault gone) returns from 508.

reading: The branches of three kinds and the thirty-six he burned till they spat and fell, and cut the root of the womb.
nuance: முப்பத்தறுவர் are the thirty-six tattvas just enumerated. மூன்று வகைக் கிளை is not explained: the three tiers of 515 and 516, or the three malas, or the three gunas. கருவேர் அறுத்தல், cutting the root of the embryo, is ending rebirth, and recurs at 523 and 532.

reading: Did he come as a guru, or to destroy my clan? Did he come as a form, or to destroy form?
nuance: Four questions with the same shape. குலம் is caste or family, so the plain sense is a girl ruined for her people; it is also the lineage of births. The last question is the Saiva paradox of a Lord who takes form to end form, and 576 sees him lose his form.

reading: I did not know ruin would come; I did not know, blind to my ruined wit, that suffering would come; I stayed with the Lord ruling me.
nuance: பதி ஆண்டு இருந்தேன் is read as 'I remained, the Lord having taken me'; பதி can also be a town, giving 'I stayed in the place'. கெடுமதி, the wit that is ruined, is what she did not see; the ruin she laments is the one she asked for at 506.

reading: I did not know this was the field where everyone fell; I saw the one without senses, who ends all evil.
nuance: பொறியிலி is taken as the one without sense organs, the Lord beyond the senses that 507 cut off; பொறி also means a trap and luck, and 'the luckless one' is a possible self-mockery. பட்டகளம் returns from 511.

reading: Those within the inner fort all died together; those within that fort, sixty of them, fell.
nuance: அறுபது பேர், the sixty, with the thirty-six of 517 make the ninety-six of 523, the Tamil count of the body's constituents; that is how tradition reconciles the numbers, and the verse does not. உட்கோட்டை and அக்கோட்டை may be two forts or the same one.

reading: They died together; it burned right through; the whole stone fort became a fort of charcoal.
nuance: கற்கோட்டை to கரிக்கோட்டை is the body as a fortress reduced to its own cinders; the verse is the chapter's picture in a single rhyme.

reading: He burned the ninety-six so that no fault remained; the evil eye struck, and he cut the root of the womb.
nuance: தொண்ணூற்றறுவர் are the ninety-six tattvas of the Tamil count. கண்ணேறு is the evil eye, the glance that blights; here it is his glance that blighted her, and tradition hears in it the guru's initiating look (நயன தீட்சை). The text has துரிசறிவே for the refrain துரிசறவே.

reading: Om was ruined, all that is went; the ego was ruined, he cut it off at the root.
nuance: ஓங்காரம் and ஆங்காரம் are paired by rhyme and fall together: the highest mantra goes with the lowest fault. உள்ளதெல்லாம் போச்சு, 'everything that was went', leaves the void the next chapters stand in.

reading: From the earth-hut upward it burned right through; he cut off every trouble of the roaring mind.
nuance: தரையாங் குடிலை is read plainly as the hut that is earth, the body; but குடிலை is also the Tamil name for the pure maya (kutila) at the top of the tattva scale, which gives 'from earth to kutilai', the whole range from lowest to highest. The coded reading fits 515 to 517 better.

reading: He cut off all my former deeds entirely, and so that I might know myself I became one woman alone.
nuance: தான் ஒருத்தி ஆனேன், 'I became a single woman', turns the loneliness of 510 into self-knowledge; தன்னை அறிய is the refrain of 526 to 528.

reading: So that I might know myself he destroyed both deeds to their foundation, and told me the place where I could know myself.
nuance: இருவினை are good and bad karma. தலம் is a place, perhaps the seat in the body or the state; the verse says he told it and does not tell it.

reading: I knew myself; I became a maiden by myself; is this the ripeness, to stay all alone, utterly alone?
nuance: தனிக்குமரி, the lone maiden, after the loss of maidenhood in 531 and 574: the one who was taken is a virgin again, with no other. பக்குவமோ can be a doubt or a wondering assent.

reading: There is no one in the house; I became open space; all I saw turned into a dream, like moonlight cast on a forest.
nuance: வெட்டவெளி, the open expanse, is the Siddhars' word for the state beyond the tattvas. காட்டுக்கு எறித்த நிலா is proverbial for a light wasted on no one; here it may be all she saw, now worthless, or the light that now shines in an emptied place.

reading: Will those who see not laugh? Is it not a song for the whole country? Will those who see not turn hostile? Is it not talk for those who look?
nuance: The chapter ends in the love-poetry convention of town gossip (அலர): a girl whose state is visible becomes a song and a scandal. For the Siddhar the jnani's condition is likewise what the world laughs at.

title: அருட்புலம்பல் - மகடூ முன்னிலை
theme: The second part of the woman's lament: he who was everywhere undid her maidenhood and broke her chastity, and she asks what will come of it, whether caste or sect or the sastras will have her now, and what crime she committed. From the questions the verses turn to describing him to her friend with the refrain காண் ('see!'): beyond speech and mind, the fire-light hidden in a stone, the light within a ruby, the one who made her stay still in the void past burning. She confesses that she had fallen into the void without devotion, and the part ends with the cause that is shown by a hand and not learned or heard, and the one that speech cannot reach.
structure_note: 531 to 534 complete the story of the taking; 535 to 541 are questions to the friend about caste, crime, seeing and speaking; 542 to 547 and 550 to 551 describe him in -காண் lines; 548 and 549 are near-doublets of Azhuganni 37 and 38, and 550 of Azhuganni 39; 552 and 553 confess the failure before him. Units 1 to 48 of the work come from two source files; from 555 on the text is in a single file and printed without word spacing. Seq 554 is an empty unit and is not in the chapter.
source_issues: Seq 554 (siddhar:arutpulambal-2:0276_01-49) has no text in the corpus; the unit is empty and the chapter runs 553 to 555. The work's numbering jumps from the two-source units 1 to 48 to single-source units 49 to 76.
555 and 556 (and all of 557 to 581) are printed without word spacing, from the single source pmuni0276_01; the second source pmuni0083 ends at unit 48.
The section label 'மகடூ முன்னிலையாக உள்ளது' on 555 onward is the source's note that the verses are in the feminine second person, not a heading of the poet's.

reading: He saw this state of mine and was everywhere; he destroyed my maidenhood, he broke my chastity.
nuance: The bridal cipher of the lament: கன்னி அழித்தல் and கற்பைக் குலைத்தல் are the Lord's taking of the soul, told as a seduction. What the chastity stands for is not said; the soul's fidelity to its own bonds, or its separateness, are the usual readings, and the shock of the words is deliberate. எங்கும் இருந்தான், he was everywhere, names the taker as the all-pervading.

reading: The breaking of my chastity, the cutting of the womb's root, the ruin of my beauty, the loss of my awareness:
nuance: A list of four -அமை nouns that is completed by 533. பொற்பு is grace or beauty of form; போதம், awareness, is what 515 also says he took.

reading: what deed will come of all this to me I do not yet know; every word he said has come true, without fail.
nuance: சொன்ன சொல்லெல்லாம் பலித்தது: the guru's word is tested by its coming true, which is the lament's only proof of him. வினை here may be karma or simply what happens next.

reading: He showed and handed over to me the place without night and day; he destroyed my shame; I stood looking at him who looked.
nuance: கங்குல் பகல் அற்ற இடம், the place with no night or day, is plainly timelessness; in the Siddhars' cipher sun and moon are the two breaths, so it is also the state past them. பங்கம் is defect or disgrace. பார்த்தானைப் பார்த்திருந்தேன் is a mutual gaze, which tradition hears as the initiation by look.

reading: Will they admit me to caste? Will I fall within the sastras? Reciting and realising, everything became just as it is.
nuance: The two questions are the ruined girl's and the jnani's at once: neither caste nor scripture has a place for her now. உள்ளபடி ஆச்சு, 'became as it is', is the plainest statement of the result in the work.

reading: What fault did I commit? Though no one saw, would not my mother and all my kin know of it in this wide world?
nuance: The plain sense is the girl's dread that an unseen fall will be known at home. The coded sense keeps the shape: the change in the realised one was unseen, yet shows.

reading: Did I eat those who killed? Did I kill those who ate? Did I forget the desire that thinks every unthinkable thing?
nuance: The first line is a riddle. As protest it means 'I did no crime of that kind'; as cipher it can mean she destroyed the senses that kill and killed the appetites that eat. The third question says what she actually did: she forgot desire (இச்சை), which is the only 'crime' the world sees.

reading: Will they admit me to caste? Will the people of the sects count me in? All my life lived in division has become matter for talk.
nuance: பேதித்து வாழ்ந்தது, living in difference, is her former life among caste and sect; it is now gossip (பேச்சுக்கு இடம்). The questions repeat 535 with sect in place of sastra.

reading: To those who see, am I not a woman? For those who do not see there is desire too. Did those who ate eat anything other than food?
nuance: The sense turns on who sees what. One reading: whoever looks at her sees only a woman, and even the blind feel desire, so the world will read her state as sex; and yet whatever anyone eats is only food, so the many are one thing. Another takes கண்டார் as those who have seen the truth. The verse is left as a riddle.

reading: What those who took took, will those who did not take take it? Have those who spoke seen? Have those who saw spoken?
nuance: The second line is a form of the Siddhars' maxim that the seers do not tell and the tellers have not seen. கொண்டவர் (those who took, or who were taken in marriage) carries the bridal cipher into the first line.

reading: Is it the gift the four ancient Vedas sing of? Does it appear and settle in the heart of servants who are truly servants?
nuance: Both questions may be rhetorical denials (the Vedas cannot sing it, nor does it stay in any heart), or the second may answer the first: not in the Vedas but in the servant's heart. தொண்டாய தொண்டர், servants who are servants, points to the second.

reading: Is it easy to recite? Is it hard for anyone to realise? He is the great one who shines everywhere without difference.
nuance: The first -காண் verse: from here the speaker describes him to the friend. பேதமற (without difference) answers the பேதித்து of 538.

reading: He is the one beyond speech and mind, in whom the mind dissolves; he is hard to look upon, the subtle one among the subtle.
nuance: மனோலயன் may be 'he in whom the mind dissolves' or 'he who is the dissolving of mind'. நுண்ணியரில் நுண்ணியன் is the Siddhars' சூட்சம், the subtle thing within; 556 ends the part with the same claim in Sanskrit.

reading: He is not contained in words; he stands beyond words; he stands like the fire-light that was within the stone.
nuance: கல்லுள் இருந்த கனல் ஒளி, the fire latent in a stone, is present but shows only when struck; the image returns at 591 in the fourth part of the work.

reading: He told me to stay melting in the void beyond heat. Is it a letter on the leaf, or a slip of the hand of the one who wrote it?
nuance: சூடு இறந்த பாழ், the void past burning, is the state after all the burning of the first part; கசிந்திருக்க, to stay oozing or melting, is tenderness rather than heat. The second line asks whether her fate was written (ஏட்டில் எழுத்து, the script of destiny) or is an error of the writer, Brahma; the two lines may not belong together.

reading: He made me stay still; I do not know the formula. Mother! saying 'this is the meaning', he swallowed me whole.
nuance: சும்மா இரு, 'just be', is the Tamil Siddhars' central teaching, and the speaker says she was made to do it without knowing the சூத்திரம், the rule behind it. விழுங்கினண்டி is read as he swallowed (விழுங்கினான் + அடி), the absorption image that 580 and 581 develop; 'I swallowed it whole' is also possible.

reading: Everywhere I looked I saw as the Supreme; I no longer know any doctrine whose strung order has collapsed.
nuance: கோத்த நிலை குலைந்த கொள்கை is a position whose threading has come apart; once all is seen as பரம், there is no tenet to hold. 568 answers with the Lord who takes the strung state for those who string.

reading: Without bathing the image and plucking flowers to adorn it, my heart became a bare void; I do not see the state in which I stood.
nuance: The rites of worship are not refuted but simply not done, and what is left is வெறும் பாழ், an emptiness the speaker cannot even locate. The Azhuganni doublet (37) is the same couplet with its refrain.

reading: Though I had sung and studied, without adorning many flowers, without running about, I lost my form.
nuance: ஓடித் திரியாமல், not running about, is the pilgrim's running to shrines; உருக்கெட்டு is plainly 'I was ruined' and in the cipher 'I lost form'. Azhuganni 38 is the doublet.

reading: He stayed mingled in me like the light within a ruby; he is the greatness that the devotees who cherish and worship him do not speak of.
nuance: மாணிக்கத்துள் ஒளி, the light in a gem, is indwelling without mixture, and 563 repeats it. பேசாப் பெருமை is a greatness not spoken, by those who know it; the silence of 540 again. Azhuganni 39 is the doublet.

reading: From that day to this, through the time when I knew nothing, he was always the common one, free of affliction.
nuance: பொது, common or impartial, is Siva's name as the one who belongs to all; நிராமயன் is the one without disease. The point is that her ignorance changed nothing in him.

reading: Through the mind's disturbance I did not see the one who is pure consciousness, and with my understanding confused I went in by the way of the senses.
nuance: சித்த விகாரம் recalls the விகாரம் the tattvas breed at 509. சின்மயன் is the Vedantic name for the Lord as consciousness; பொறிவழி, the senses' road, is the way she went instead.

reading: Not knowing devotion I fell headlong into the void, and stayed there in agreement, as if it were a fitting sleep.
nuance: The void here is a fall, not the goal of 545 and 548: without devotion the emptiness is a sleep (நித்திரை) mistaken for the state. The line is a self-question (இருந்தேண்டி?) and its grammar, ஒத்தவிட ... ஒத்தும், is awkward; the reading of 'fitting sleep' is a guess.

reading: Not learning, not hearing: see, the cause that points by hand; it is without limit or measure, filled everywhere.
nuance: கைகாட்டும் காரணம், the cause shown by a hand, is the silent teaching by gesture that tradition gives to Dakshinamurti and to the guru's hand-sign; learning and hearing are set against it. The unit is printed without word spaces.

reading: He came to dwell in what speech cannot reach; he is without pollution; he is the knowledge of knowledge.
nuance: வாசாமகோசரம் is the Sanskrit term for what lies outside the range of speech, used by Tirumular too. ஆசூசம் இல்லான், without ritual pollution, closes a part that began with a maidenhood destroyed: no impurity attaches to him or to what he did.

title: அருட்புலம்பல் - மகடூ முன்னிலை
theme: The third part of the woman's lament is mostly praise of him to her friend: the one body unbroken in every direction, the supreme light set in the sea of devotion, the awareness of awareness, without root or top, undiminished by all the beings in all the worlds, the Full One without speech, mind or form, easy to see and not seen, the light in the ruby, inside and outside atom and Meru, the clarity of the sugarcane of knowledge. Then the story resumes: he held her as the hold of those who hold nothing, dwelt in her in open space while everyone watched in daylight, gave her a life that is not living and a true life that is bare void; the virgin palm bore fruit, every place smells of civet, and he swallowed her as hot iron drinks water and fire eats camphor.
structure_note: 557 to 568 are the -அடி and -காண் descriptions of him; 569 to 576 return to what he did to her and what she saw; 577 to 581 close in wonder with four images of absorption (the fruiting palm, the civet scent, iron and water, fire and camphor). The part ends at 581 and the work continues into a fourth part. All units are from the single source and printed without word spacing.
source_issues: All units 557 to 581 come from the single source pmuni0276_01 and are printed without word spacing, so word division is the marker's; the readings of 564, 567 and 581 depend on it.
576 line 2 புண்மாயம் is probably a rhyme-echo of கண்மாயம் or a corruption of புன்மாயம்; the text is kept as printed.
581 line 2 மக்கினம்பட்டு is an obscure form, perhaps for மக்கிப்பட்டு or a variant spelling.

reading: His state is one the ten directions cannot contain; he is the one body, unbroken everywhere, in every direction.
nuance: ஏகம், the one, and இடைவிடாது, without gap, state pervasion as a single continuous body rather than as presence in many places. பருவம் here is state or condition rather than season.

reading: He wells up sweetly for those who have the mind for it; he is the supreme light set within the sea of devotion.
nuance: தித்திக்க ஊறும், welling sweetly like juice, is the first of the chapter's taste images (the sugarcane of 566 follows). The verse makes devotion the sea the light is set in, after 553 blamed the lack of devotion for the fall.

reading: He is the awareness of the awareness of those who stand as inner awareness; by not even a sesame's measure does he rise above what is, nor fall short of it.
nuance: உணர்வுக்கு உணர்வு, awareness of awareness, is repeated at 556 as knowledge of knowledge. எள்ளளவும் உள்ளதிலே ஏறிக் குறையான் is read as neither more nor less than what is: he is exactly the real, without excess or lack.

reading: He has no root and no top, no arising and no subsiding; unknown to anyone he stood as the undivided.
nuance: தூரும் தலையும் இலான், without root or head, is the Tamil way of saying beginningless and endless; தோற்றம் ஒடுக்கம் denies him the arising and dissolution that everything made undergoes. அகண்டம் is the unbroken whole.

reading: However many beings there are in however many worlds, though all of them exist, he is not lessened by an atom.
nuance: The verse answers an implied objection: if he is everything, the many lives would divide him. அணுவும் குறையான் denies it, and the next verses keep the atom as the measure (566).

reading: He is the vast thing without speech, mind or form, without going or coming, the incomparable Full One.
nuance: பூரணன், the Full One, is the Siddhars' name for God as fullness, and here it is defined by what he lacks: speech, mind, form and motion. வான்பொருள் may be 'the great thing' or 'the thing that is sky'.

reading: He is easy to see, and even when seen is not seen here; for those who set a noble mind on him, he is the light within the ruby.
nuance: காட்சிக்கு எளியான் is the Kural's phrase for an accessible king, turned on the Lord. கண்டாலும் இங்கு காணான் is the paradox that seeing him is not seeing him as he is. மாணிக்கத்துள் ஒளி returns from 550.

reading: Even if one praises him and worships him, he is the one whom enduring lives find hard to see; he is the light beyond words.
nuance: The syntax is loose: வாழ்த்தியவனை வழிபட்டால் (if one worships him who is praised) is followed by மன்னுயிர்கள் தோற்றவரியான், hard for lives to see, so that praise and worship do not by themselves bring sight. Another reading has தோற்ற as 'appear', he who rarely appears to lives.

reading: If there are any who inquire into the one who has cut off doubt, he will come into the world and set down his flower feet.
nuance: ஐயம் is doubt, and also alms: ஐயம் அறுத்தவன் can be the one who ends doubt or the beggar-saint who has ended begging, and Pattinathar lived by alms. The verse makes inquiry (ஆராய்தல்) the condition of his coming.

reading: He stood inside and outside both the atom and Meru; he is the clear juice of the sugarcane of knowledge, ripe in every joint.
nuance: அணுவுக்கும் மேருவுக்கும் அகம்புறம், within and without the least and the greatest, is pervasion stated in extremes. கணு முற்றும், every joint ripe, makes knowledge a sugarcane with no unripe node, and தெளிவு its clear juice.

reading: At any time, at this time, 'thus' and 'so': however he is told, he does not hear; he does not take it in through the ear.
nuance: சோத்திரம் is the ear (Sanskrit shrotra). The verse may mean that no description reaches him, since he is beyond hearing as beyond speech (562); or, as complaint, that he cannot be moved by pleading. The first fits the -காண் series.

reading: He is mother to the mother and father to the father; for those who string him into a frame he is the sea of qualities that takes the strung state.
nuance: கோத்தார்க்குக் கோத்த நிலை கொண்ட, taking for those who string the state they string, says that he fits whatever doctrine frames him; 547 had the speaker's own strung doctrine collapse. The sea of qualities is a Lord with attributes for those who need them.

reading: Is it new now? How many days it has been! Moment by moment he gave me grace and understanding.
nuance: இப்போ புதிதோடி is read as a question to the friend, 'is this new now?', with the answer that it has been so for a long time (எத்தனை நாள் உள்ளது). அப்போதைக்கு அப்போது, moment to moment, makes grace continuous rather than a single event.

reading: He held me as the hold of those who hold to nothing; he cut off my fault; he stayed joined with me.
nuance: பற்று அற்றார் பற்றாக, as the attachment of the unattached: he is the one thing those who have let go still hold, and here it is he who holds her. கூடியிருந்தான், he stayed united, carries the bridal sense.

reading: He dwelt in me in the open space; everyone stood watching, in broad daylight.
nuance: வெட்டவெளி, the open expanse of 529, is where the union happens; பட்டப்பகலில் பார்த்திருந்தார் எல்லோரும் is the scandal of 530 again, everyone watching, and also the point of 575, that all saw and none knew.

reading: A life that is truly life came to me, without my living it; without sinking I sank, and nothing was lacking.
nuance: Two paradoxes, வாழாமல் வாழ்வு and தாழாமல் தாழ்ந்தேன்: the true life is not lived as a life, and the lowering is not a fall. சற்றும் குறையாமல், with no lack, echoes the Lord who is not lessened (561).

reading: The false life: I saw that I had had enough of it. The true life: for me it turned into bare void.
nuance: வெறும் பாழாய் விட்டது, 'became mere void', can be heard as loss or as the attainment: the true life, when it comes, is the emptiness of 548 and 545. The verse does not decide, and that is its tone throughout the lament.

reading: I saw with my eyes full the one who destroyed my maidenhood; I do not know my own nature; what maya is this!
nuance: கன்னி அழித்தவன் is the taker of 531, now seen face to face. மாயம் here is wonder or trick rather than the cosmic maya; என் இயல்பு நான் அறியேன் is the knower who knew herself at 528 now not knowing what she is.

reading: To say it in words there is no mouth to say it; everyone has seen it and sat there, and yet they do not know it now.
nuance: சொல்ல வாய் இல்லை, no mouth or no way to say it. The second line turns 571 round: those who watched in daylight saw and did not understand.

reading: He cast a spell on my eyes and I lost my purpose; I saw the one who cast the spell lose his form.
nuance: கண்மாயம் is conjuring, a trick on the eyes. புண்மாயம் in line 2 is obscure (புண் is a wound); it may be a rhyme-echo or a corruption of புன்மாயம், petty illusion. உருவழியக் கண்டேன், I saw him lose his form, answers the question of 518: he came as form to destroy form, and the form went too.

reading: What am I to say of this wonder? Before my eyes the young virgin areca palm bore fruit.
nuance: கன்னி இளங்கமுகு காய்த்தது, a virgin palm fruiting, is the paradox of 528 (the taken one is a maiden) made into an image: the fruit is read by tradition as knowledge or release born in the soul without a worldly cause. The verse only calls it a wonder (அதிசயம்).

reading: Every place that is filled is grace itself; every place that is reached smells of civet.
nuance: சவாது is civet, the perfume of lovers and courtesans in the Thiruppugazh; here it is the scent of grace wherever one goes. ஆர்ந்த (filled) and சார்ந்த (joined) rhyme the Lord's fullness with the soul's approach.

reading: Knowing this scent everywhere to be the natural scent, I sank into that sea of grace that is beyond pleasure.
nuance: இயற்கை மணம், the natural scent, is not applied like a courtesan's perfume but innate. சுகாதீதம், beyond pleasure, places the sea of grace past even bliss; the sinking (மூழ்கினேன்) begins the absorption images of 580 and 581.

reading: He swallowed me as water is taken up by hot iron; he stayed as if he were not there, like the fragrance in a bud.
nuance: இரும்பு நிறை நீர், water on iron, is the Tirumanthiram's image of absorption without remainder; அரும்பு நிறை வாசனை, scent filling a bud, is presence that cannot be pointed to. அன்றே இருந்தான் is read as 'he was there as if not', or 'he was so from that very day'.

reading: Like fire that swallows camphor leaving nothing, he stayed joined within me, merged into me.
nuance: Camphor in fire leaves no ash; the image is of a union with no residue. மக்கினம் பட்டு is obscure; மக்கி means to rot or dissolve, and 'dissolved into me' is the guess taken here. The part ends on the inside (உள்ளே) after a chapter of 'everywhere'.

title: அருட்புலம்பல் - மகடூ முன்னிலை
theme: The fourth part of Pattinathar's Arutpulambal in the woman's voice: she tells her friend that the Lord has mingled with her as river with sea and life with body, and then names him by a chain of similes, gold and its assay, the ruby's light, fire in the flint, the pearl in the shell, sugar in milk, the banyan with countless branches, as the Fullness beyond books, letters, lineage, direction and the five dissolutions, the silent Brahman that burned Kama with a look, present to the awakened and absent to the base.
structure_note: Every unit is two lines closing on the refrain particles அடி, ஆண்டி (ஆன் + அடி: he did, girl) and காண் (see), the address of a woman to her friend (மகடூ முன்னிலை). The couplets alternate between what he did to her (582, 584, 586, 587, 590, 595, 605) and what he is (583, 585, 588, 589, 591, 596 to 604, 606); 592 to 594 turn to who sees him and who does not.
source_issues: 586 line 2 (கள்ளப்புலனறுக்கக்காரணமாய்வந்தாண்டி) is also line 2 of 507 (arutpulambal-2:2); the work carries two numbering runs, the short numbers 1 onward and the long ids 0276_01-NN, and units recur between them.
595 நாட்டினரிகள்: the sense (the Madurai jackals-into-horses sport) needs நரிகள், jackals; the printed split gives அரிகள்.
The units of this work are printed without word-spacing, so several readings (585 தீவகம்/பாவகம், 602 அங்குஷம், 605) turn on where words are divided.

reading: Like sea-water and a river run together, I can see no shore; he stood mingled within me like body and life.
nuance: Two images of union that cannot be undone: river in sea, life in body. கரை காணேன் (I see no shore) is the woman's own state, not his.

reading: As gold is one with the streak that tells its fineness, so is the incomparable Fullness; it is lasting direct experience, like the light inside a ruby.
nuance: உரை மாற்று is the assay: the streak a piece of gold leaves on the touchstone and the fineness read from it, which cannot be separated from the gold. அநுபூதி (anubhuti) is the tradition's word for knowing by experience rather than by report.

reading: He has no bound and no shore, a ship that never sights land; he is everywhere without measure, and stood as the One.
nuance: கரை காணாக் கப்பல் (ship that sees no shore) picks up the woman's கரை காணேன் of 582 and makes it his.

reading: The supreme one made of consciousness joined me like a lamp; he has no imagining in him, and wherever I look, all is the Supreme.
nuance: தீவகம் is an island, and can also be read as தீபகம், a lamp; joined me like a lamp (giving light) or like an island (set in the sea) both stand. பாவகம் is read as பாவனை, imagining or mental construction; it could also be fire. The last clause is plain.

reading: He is within even the innermost; he has no town and no name; he came as the cause that cuts off the thieving senses.
nuance: The second line is a formula that recurs: it is the second line of 507 in this work and of Azhuganni 1522, where the first line is that he took the guru's form to cut off birth.

reading: Through all those earlier births he sat as grace; in this birth he came, and this one is the true substance.
nuance: Grace is said to have been there in every past birth; what is new in this birth is that he came in person (as the guru, 621).

reading: Like light on water he fills everything, the one without flaw; like the light of day he spreads everywhere, the Supreme beyond the supreme.
nuance: நிராமயன், the one without disease, is a name for the unafflicted Supreme; பராபரன் is the Siddhars' usual name for Brahman.

reading: He is subtler than the subtle that no book can grasp; he is the all-pervading Fullness, spread through everything like sugar in milk.
nuance: Sugar dissolved in milk is in every drop and visible in none: pervasion without a separate form.

reading: Can he be known by the eye of flesh, and not only by the mind's eye? He abides pervading, like the flame-light of a lamp.
nuance: ஓருமதோ (can it discern?) is a rhetorical question: only the inner eye sees him.

reading: Like the fire-light that lies hidden in a stone, he is the cause of all, and though he lies hidden close within, he is the incomparable Fullness.
nuance: புல்லியிருந்தும் can be 'though embracing' or 'though lying lowly and hidden'; both keep the point that nearness and concealment do not make him less.

reading: To those in whom awakening has been born he is as fragrance is to a flower of gold; to the base who cannot see him, as fragrance is to a flower of stone.
nuance: Neither a gold flower nor a stone flower has scent, so the contrast must lie in the flowers: the gold flower is precious and the awakened add fragrance to it, the stone flower is dead and no fragrance will come. போதம் is bodha, awakening.

reading: To those who do not forget him even in confusion, and to the knowers of the cause who have cut off the womb, he becomes a fruit in the hand.
nuance: கைக்குள் கனி, the fruit in the palm, is the idiom for what is easily had. The simile of the first line, collyrium-paste and pearl (மைக்குழம்பு முத்து), is obscure: perhaps the pearl showing white against black paste, or the dark and the bright kept together without mixing. கருவறுத்த காரணர் are those who have cut the womb, that is, rebirth.

reading: To poets free of attachment he shows like coral seen through crystal; those who take a shell for silver cannot come near him, and will they ever?
nuance: Shell taken for silver is the stock Vedantic example of false perception; coral in crystal is seeing through a clear medium. The verse sets clear seeing against mistaken seeing, and makes freedom from attachment the condition of the first.

reading: He is not held in a palm-leaf book and is not born of letters; he made all the jackals of the land into fine horses.
nuance: The printed நாட்டினரிகள் reads as நாட்டின் அரிகள் (the lions, or Haris, of the land) but the sense needs நரிகள், jackals: the Madurai sport in which Siva turned jackals into horses for the Pandya. Two lines set the Lord outside books and letters and inside legend.

reading: He outlasts even the fivefold dissolution; he is the one with poison held in his throat and fire in his eye.
nuance: பஞ்சப் பிரளயம், the five dissolutions, is a traditional count of the ends of the world; the epithets are Siva's, the poison drunk at the churning and the third eye.

reading: He guards within and without; from the measureless cosmos onward he guards the world, and guards the ten directions no eye can see.
nuance: Protection, the second of the five acts, is given four scopes: inner, outer, the worlds, the directions.

reading: He is the Brahman that does not speak, the great light beyond speech, the great light that desire and the bonds cannot come near.
nuance: பேசாப் பிரமம் (the Brahman that does not speak) is the refrain-name this part of the work gives him (606, 610); the silence is his, not the devotee's.

reading: He has passed beyond country; he is the clear sea that has passed beyond direction; he is the substance so solid that not even a needle's point can be pressed into it.
nuance: ஊசிமுனை ஊன்ற இல்லா is fullness as density: there is no gap anywhere in him for anything else.

reading: He is the pearl's light within the shell; to those who lack the gaze of consciousness he is the rare substance that stays unseen, like light in water.
nuance: Both images are of a light that is present but not seen unless one looks rightly; சின்மய நோக்கு, the gaze of consciousness, is what 611 says the Lord gave her.

reading: He is the banyan tree with branches beyond number; he is the true substance whose higher states pierce through the sky.
nuance: மேலாம் பதங்கள் may be the higher padas, the states or worlds above, or his feet (பதம்); the banyan is the tree under which Siva teaches and the tree that spreads from one seed, as in Sivavakkiyar.

reading: His flower-feet have passed beyond every lineage and cling to none; he is the rare substance that searched everywhere like a goad.
nuance: வங்கிஷம் (வம்சம்) is lineage or clan; the Lord is outside caste and descent. அங்குஷம் is the elephant-goad; 'as a goad searched everywhere' may mean that he drives and governs all, or the word may be corrupt.

reading: Name has been lost, there is no place from which to tell it; he is the cause who opened his fire-eye to burn Kama with a look.
nuance: நாம நட்டம் is the loss of name: his, as the nameless one of 586, or hers, as the self that no longer has a name to speak from (617, 612). The burning of Kama is set beside the loss of name, desire and ego ending together.

reading: He is red gold never beaten, a pearl never dived for, on a branch no hand can reach, the honey-nectar no fly has entered.
nuance: Four images of what is unmade and untouched: gold not worked, pearl not fished, a branch out of reach, honey no fly has spoiled. The Lord is uncreated and unsullied.

reading: As one tests a bit of gold on the stone against the standard needle and says what its fineness is, so he set me against the standard, joined me to it and took me in whole.
nuance: ஆணி is the touch-needle, the set of gold needles of known fineness against which a streak is compared; அடங்கல் இட்டு is 'included entirely'. The image of 583 returns as what he did to her: she was assayed and absorbed. The syntax is compressed and the agent of each verb is not certain.

reading: Though the beings of the measureless cosmos are so many, he does not say even a splinter's worth, not at all: the Brahman that does not speak.
nuance: The silence is total and the audience is total; the Lord does not explain himself to anyone.

title: அருட்புலம்பல் - மகடூ முன்னிலை
theme: The close of the woman's lament: the Lord set his feet in her stone heart, burned her bonds with a look and told her to stay, showed her his form of consciousness and swallowed her as ghee is held in milk; the ages of dying and being born in hell are nothing now, karma and the four wombs have lost their name, and he who is beyond the three voids and beyond simile has come to earth as the guru. The work ends by asking the knowers of the three voids to forgive similes that fail.
structure_note: Still in the woman's voice (அடி, ஆண்டி, காண்). 607 to 614 are what he did and said to her; 615 to 620 are her account of her own state, with the first-person ஆனேன் and அறிந்தேன் replacing the refrain; 621 is a blessing on the guru's feet and 622 the poet's apology for his comparisons, closing the work.
source_issues: 607 line 2 is printed என்னென்சினுள்ளே for என்னெஞ்சினுள்ளே.
609 line 1 பட்ப்பார்த்த is corrupt: a bare ப் stands where a vowel sign is missing (பட்டப் or படப்).
The units of this work are printed without word-spacing; 620 line 1 (தெத்தபடமானேண்டி) cannot be divided with confidence.

reading: As if a blue lily had bloomed inside a heart of stone, he set his twin feet inside my heart.
nuance: The stone heart is hers, the flower his doing; grace is pictured as the impossible bloom, not as her own softening.

reading: He is the horse of the Vedas, yet those who gallop on it do not know him; he is knowledge that no ear brings, and only those with the right intent see it.
nuance: காதற்ற ஞானம் can be 'earless knowledge', knowledge not gained by hearing (கேள்வி), or 'knowledge without edge or handle', unbounded. The Veda-horse image, ridden fast and getting nowhere, favours the first: reciting is not knowing.

reading: With a look that saw through the deeds of bondage, he showed me love and said: stay.
nuance: The printed பட்ப்பார்த்த is corrupt; பட்டப் பார்த்த (looked so that they were struck) or படப் பார்த்த (looked so that they perished) both give a gaze that undoes bondage. நில் (stand, stay) is the one word he speaks.

reading: The place where sound subsides is the light within Om; this, he said, is the Brahman that stays without speaking.
nuance: The silent Brahman of 598 and 606 is here located: at the end of sound, inside the syllable. Light is found where sound ends, as in the Siddhars' nada-ending teaching.

reading: With the good gaze of consciousness he showed me the form of pure consciousness, made me of his own nature and stood there as himself.
nuance: நோக்கு, the gaze, is one of the traditional modes of the guru's initiation (looking, touching, thinking); here the look alone transforms. தன்மயம் ஆக்கி, 'made me of his nature', is union without loss of him.

reading: He himself looked at me, and now there is nothing but himself; what can I say, girl? There is no place left from which to tell it.
nuance: நவில இடம் இல்லை repeats 603; after union there is no standpoint for a speaker, which the next verses and 622 nevertheless go on speaking from.

reading: To all the people who are here today and die tomorrow he said: stay sweetly forever in the all-fullness.
nuance: The remedy for mortality is not another life but dwelling in the Fullness; the verse addresses everyone, not only the speaker.

reading: Is it not easy if you only look? Is it not the attachment-free attachment? He came to this earth to show the place to everyone.
nuance: பற்றற்ற பற்று, attachment to the one without attachment, is the Kural's paradox at 350; இடம் காட்ட is to show the place or way, the guru's office.

reading: All this time of dying and being born, girl: none of it is anything now; I have become water on iron.
nuance: இரும்பில் உறை நீர் is water that falls on hot iron and vanishes without trace, as 620 makes explicit with தீயிரும்பு; the past births are gone as if they never were.

reading: In what age did it all happen, the dying and being born? All that time I lay sunk in a hell.
nuance: Hell is not a place after death but the whole span of rebirth seen from the far side of it. ஆநரகில் may be அந்நரகில், that hell.

reading: Time has passed away, all karma has gone, and the four kinds of womb have lost even their name.
nuance: The four births of tradition are from egg, sweat, sprout and womb (அண்டசம், சுவேதசம், உற்பீசம், சராயுசம்); நாம நட்டம், loss of name, is the same phrase 603 used of the Lord, now used of the wombs.

reading: Beyond the three voids, as the first void and the whole First, he has come just now and swallowed me up.
nuance: முப்பாழ், the three voids, is Tirumular's scheme (the voids of maya, of knowledge and of calm, or of soul, Supreme and union); Pattinathar sets the Lord beyond even these as முதற்பாழ், the first void. விழுங்கிக் கொண்டான், 'he swallowed me', is the work's word for union (619).

reading: As ghee is held in milk, the supreme light embraced me and swallowed me wholly.
nuance: Ghee in milk is the stock Saiva image of the Lord present unseen in the soul; here it is turned around, the soul being taken into the light.

reading: I became a painted picture, water on red-hot iron; and I knew the awareness that calls the state where all is level 'sleep'.
nuance: தெத்தபடம் is obscure (perhaps தத்தப்படம், a picture or screen, a mere image); the iron image repeats 615. ஒத்த இடம் நித்திரை may mean that the state of evenness beyond waking and dream is what the traditions call sleep, or that for her it is indistinguishable from sleep; the line turns on technical words of the avastha scheme.

reading: Long live the feet of him who came to this earth as the guru: the substance without equal or simile, hard to put into words.
nuance: The work's many similes (ch. 34) are here disowned in advance: he is ஒப்பும் உவமையும் அற்ற, beyond likeness. What is reachable is the guru on earth, named in 614 as the one who came to show the place.

reading: Though I have spoken comparisons and though my similes have gone wrong, the elders who have learned and realised the three voids will bear with me and grant grace.
nuance: ஒப்பாரி is both a comparison and a funeral lament, which is what a புலம்பல் is; the poet apologises for both. The judges he names are not the Lord but those who know the three voids, the knowers of the Tirumanthiram's scheme.

title: அருட்புலம்பல் - இறந்தகாலத்திரங்கல்
theme: The lament for the past (இறந்தகாலத்திரங்கல்): fourteen couplets in which Pattinathar counts the ways he was ruined, by preaching sastras to the unfit, by wealth and influence, by greed for land and gold, by the company of fools and of the blind who had no guru, by taking wives, children and the corpse-smelling body for real, by praise, and even by faultless Siva-worship through countless births that did not free him. The last four turn the refrain from 'I was ruined' to 'I died', with the body named as its own enemy.
structure_note: Each couplet ends கெட்டேனே (I was ruined), and in 625, 627, 629, 630 and 632 the fuller பதியிழந்து கெட்டேனே (I lost the Lord and was ruined). 633 to 635 end மாண்டேனே (I died), and 633 alone has the third person மாண்டானே; 636 returns to கெட்டேனே.
