reading: You call the water you drank in your mouth spittle; should not the Veda chewed in your mouth be called spittle too? You who drink water to make the mouth's spittle go, come back and tell me how the spittle went.
nuance: The argument is from the Brahmin's own purity rule: whatever touches the mouth is எச்சில், so recited scripture is defiled by recitation. The last line adds that the rinsing water that removes spittle is itself spittle, so the rule cannot be satisfied.

reading: The recited Veda is spittle, the inner mantras are spittle, the teachings are spittle, the seven worlds are spittle, the seed in the woman is spittle, the moon is spittle and the light is spittle; there is nothing anywhere in which spittle is not, nothing, nothing.
nuance: 1004 pushed to its end: if contact defiles, everything spoken, taught or born is defiled, down to the moon and the light, and purity has no place to stand. மாது இருந்த விந்து makes birth itself the first contamination, which 1012 and 1013 take up.

reading: How was it before birth? How is it after being born and dying into the earth? If you cannot say it precisely, you people without a mark, I will cut off both your ears with the sword of the five letters.
nuance: The threat is rhetorical: ears that cannot hear the answer are cut by the mantra. குறிப்பில்லாத (without mark or aim) plays on குறித்து (precisely): they have no fixed point from which to answer.

reading: If you shoot the hall with an arrow and say 'move', will it move? If you tell the unshaken milk-ocean 'be troubled', will it be troubled? Will darkness come near the yogi who is free of pleasure? The clear Sivayam within the hall of red gold.
nuance: அசங்கென்றால் சங்குமோ is read as அசங்கு (move) with the sandhi dropped; the hall is the Chidambaram hall and, for tradition, the inner hall. இன்பமற்ற யோகி is the yogi without (worldly) pleasure, free of desire, though the words could be taken as 'joyless'. The three images say the same thing: what is settled cannot be shaken from outside.

reading: What is mind, what is thought, what is life, you Siddhas! What is Sakti, what is Sambhu, what is it that is free of caste distinction? What is release, what is the root, what are the root mantras? In the seed without a seed, say which of these is 'mine'.
nuance: The list runs from the inner faculties to Sakti and Siva, release and mantra, and asks their status in the causeless cause (வித்தில்லாத வித்து). The last phrase, இதினெனதென்று, is read as 'which of these is mine' or 'what is this'; the question is answered by negation in 1009, so the two verses are one argument.

reading: The place where one stands without mind, without thought, without life, without Sakti, without Sambhu, without caste distinction, without release, without root and without the root mantras: in the seed that bore this art, Sivayam ripened.
nuance: The same list as 1008 with அற்று (without) after each item; even Sakti, Siva as Sambhu and release are negated, and what remains is named Sivayam, the five letters as the Lord. The editor's heading ஒடுக்க நிலை (the state of involution) fits. விலைந்ததே is read as விளைந்ததே (ripened, came forth); வித்தை (the art, knowledge) may also be வித்தை, 'the seed' as object.

reading: What is caste? Is not all water gathered water? Is not the gate of the elements one, are not the five elements one? Are not ear-ring, bracelet, wire and anklet one gold? What kind of nature is this nature that proclaims caste difference?
nuance: The argument of 993 (one gold, many forms) is turned from the gods to people: all bodies are the same five elements and come through the same gate (பூதவாசல், the womb). சாதி is asked about as a thing, and the answer offered is that it has no substance.

reading: Milked milk does not go back into the udder, churned butter does not go back into the buttermilk; the sound of a broken conch and lives do not go back into the body; the opened flower and the fallen fruit do not go back onto the tree; the dead are not born, no, no, not at all.
nuance: On the plain reading the verse denies rebirth outright, against the Kural, the Tirumanthiram and the whole tradition of births to be cut. Tradition softens it: the dead do not return to this body, or those who have died to the self are not born again. The images all say one thing, that what has left its source does not re-enter it, and the fourfold இல்லை leaves little room for the softer sense.

reading: When it lay in the inner room you did not call it impure; when it knew the bathing place and bathed you did not call it impure; when it knew the drum and you were born you did not call it impure; how then will you come to join the faultless Lord?
nuance: தூமை is menstrual impurity. The 'it' is the blood: in the womb-room it became the child, at the ghat it was washed, at the birth announced by the drum it was you; none of these was called impure, so calling it impure now is incoherent. Line 3's ப்றையறிந்து is corrupt (பறையறிந்து, knowing the drum, or பிறையறிந்து, knowing the crescent, that is the month), and the last line's logic, why the inconsistency bars union, is compressed.

reading: Poor ones who droop and wander saying 'impurity, impurity': while the impure woman is still there, where did the impurity go? You dive like tortoises and recite the many Vedas; the impurity gathered and rolled itself into word-gurus.
nuance: The last line is the sting: the Veda-reciting teachers are themselves the clotted menstrual blood they shun, since that is what every body is made of. ஆமைபோல முழுகி, diving like a tortoise, mocks the repeated ritual immersion. சொற்குருக்கள் (gurus of words) opens 1014, which continues the chain.

title: சிவவாக்கியம்
theme: The chapter finishes the attack on gurus made of the same blood as everyone else, rosaries and holy baths, and sectarian division (the lord of Tillai and the lord of Arangam are one, moon in his left eye and sun in his right), then turns to what Sivavakkiyar does affirm: the letters A, U and SI and the fifty-one letters held in one, the five letters Sivaya as the real bathing place and the means that calls back the departed breath, the gate (வாசல்) that must be opened for the light to appear, the light sprung in the root channel that makes one a child and Brahman, and the Lord who is not form, not space, not great, not small, and whose beginninglessness the poet turns into a question for the yogis.
structure_note: 1014 completes the antadi chain from 1013. 1017 to 1019 are the Hari-Hara verses; 1022 and 1023 handle letters, 1024 and 1025 resume the நீ catalogue of 972; 1027, 1031, 1032 and 1036 are the வாசல் (gate) verses; 1033 repeats the oath line of 968 and 986. The chapter ends mid-work at 1038, a question to the yogis matched by 1023's.
source_issues: 1029 line 4 reads எழுத்திலா எனழுத்திலோ; எனழுத்திலோ is corrupt (எழுத்திலோ fits the metre and sense).
1023 lines 1 and 2 both ask whether U (அவ்வு / உவ்வு) arose, within A and within U; the repetition may be a copying slip for a different letter in one line.
1018 line 3, ஏறில்ஆறு ஈசனும், and 1021 line 3, செற்றமாவை யுள்ளரைச், are obscure as printed and may be corrupt.
1014 continues 1013 antadi-fashion across the tool's chapter split.

reading: Becoming gurus of words, becoming bodies of light, becoming true gurus, doing the required puja, becoming sat-gurus, telling the sastras, becoming gurus of deeds: all of it is the impurity gathered and rolled.
nuance: Continues 1013: the clotted menstrual blood that became the word-gurus became every other kind of guru too, so no teacher is purer than his birth. A second reading takes திரண்டுருண்ட தூமை as 'all this is so much filth', dismissing the ranks of gurus outright. சோதிமேனி (body of light) among them is striking, since 1027 holds it out as the goal.

reading: Seeing hand-rosaries you stand blinking your eyes; what places do you see as you count and count? If you can look fittingly at the mind that has known falsehood, you may quickly tell it within yourselves, crossing the body.
nuance: கைவடம் is the rosary and கண்சிமிட்டி the eyes closed and fluttering in japa. பொய்யுணர்ந்த சிந்தை can be the mind that knows the falseness (of these shows) or the mind that has known only falsehood and must now be looked at. மெய்கடந்து puns on மெய், body and truth.

reading: As one catches a tiger by showing it a goat, will you bewilder my mind by showing me cattle? King who killed and flayed the elephant by showing the tusk: you must show me release and bring me out.
nuance: மாடு is cattle and, by extension, wealth: the Lord baits the poet with worldly goods as the hunter baits the tiger. கோடு காட்டி (showing the horn or tusk) in the elephant-flaying myth is obscure; it may only keep the pattern of காட்டி in each line. வெளிப்படுத்த can be 'reveal me' or 'bring me out (of the trap)'.

reading: In your left eye the moon, in your right eye the sun; in your left hand conch and discus, in your right the trident, deer and axe; the raised foot, the long crown, beyond the eight directions; who can see the marvel that stands mingled with the body?
nuance: The description is of the joint Hari-Hara form, Vishnu's emblems on the left and Siva's on the right. Tradition also reads it as the body's yoga: moon and sun are the left and right breaths, and the form 'mingled with the body' (உடல் கலந்து நின்ற) is the Lord as the breath itself. மாயம் here is marvel or hidden working rather than delusion.

reading: As a measure of water and a measure of salt become one measure, the ocean-hued one and Isa sit and dwell together in one place; those who speak of Isa with the river in his hair and the moving discus-bearer as different will fall into a hell for nothing.
nuance: Salt dissolved in water adds no volume, a stronger figure for identity than the gold of 993. ஏறில் ஆறு ஈசன் is read as Isa with the river (ஆறு) in his hair or on his bull (ஏறு); the phrase is compressed. வீண் நரகு is a hell entered for nothing, since the division was empty.

reading: The lord of Tillai is he; the one of Tiruvarangam too is he; he who became the bounded worlds and the single release. People who have teeth and a tongue divide him and delight in the telling; those who talk of one's prowess over the other will die with rotting mouths.
nuance: Tillai is Chidambaram and Arangam Srirangam, the chief Saiva and Vaishnava shrines, named only to be made one. வல்லபங்கள் பேசுவார் are those who argue which god is mightier. The curse on the mouth matches the offence, which was speech.

reading: Our father, our Lord, for every direction and every life; the flame that sprouts and rises within the seed that is Sakti; after the mind is clear and the Veda-temple is opened, after seeing the Father's dance, one sees the dance of all things.
nuance: சத்தியான வித்து makes Sakti the seed and the Lord the flame within it, an inversion of the usual order. வேத கோயில் (the Veda-temple) is unglossed; the body, the mind or the Veda's inner meaning are all possible. அடங்கல் ஆடல் is the dance of everything, or the dance in which all is contained.

reading: Perceive the fitting books within yourselves, perceiving and perceiving, and sing; standing with attachment cut, you will reach the Supreme beyond the supreme; if you cut the pride of the hateful ones within and set them in place, the light will live within you forever as kin.
nuance: Line 3, செற்றமாவை யுள்ளரைச் செருக்கறுத்து, is hard: the hateful (or hatred and desire) that are within, whose pride is to be cut, or the enemies within. The first line qualifies the attack on books: books perceived within are to be sung, not thrown out.

reading: What rose as awareness, came as water, entered as the seed and grew as fire: recite the letter in which five and three became one; recite, you, the name 'Rama Rama Rama'.
nuance: The first two lines trace a descent, read by tradition as conception (awareness, fluid, seed, the heat of the womb) or as the elements. அஞ்சும் மூன்றும் ஒன்றதான அக்கரம் repeats the five-and-three mantra of 980 and here names it ராம, which tradition reads as cipher for the breath (see 974). போததாய் (as awareness, from போதம்) may also be 'as a bud'.

reading: Did U arise within the letter A? Did U arise within the letter U? Did A and U stand without SI? You yogis free of change, you must explain this at length.
nuance: A and U are the first two letters of Om; SI is the first letter of Siva and of the five letters. The question seems to be whether the pranava can stand without the Siva-letter, and the first two lines, as printed, ask the same thing twice (அவ்வு / உவ்வு); a copying slip or a deliberate puzzle. The verse asks and does not tell.

reading: You are for all the kinds of virtue, you are the cosmos and the eight directions, you are for every kind of strength, you are the thought of those who seek, you are sleep, you are awareness, you are the light mingled within; your anklet-feet that cannot be forgotten, even if I forget them, dwell in me.
nuance: The last line asks the feet to stay even through the poet's forgetting, so union does not rest on his remembering. The catalogue continues 972 and includes sleep and waking awareness as the Lord.

reading: You are the cosmos, you are what is beyond it, you are the primal root, you are the throat, you are thought, you are the poems; the virtuous who perceive you within, with no lotus, in the straightness of the form they have taken: what sharpness their sharpness is!
nuance: கண்டம் may be the throat (the Lord's dark throat) or 'the piece', the part as against the whole. புண்டரீகம் அற்று உளே (within, without the lotus) is taken as perceiving without the lotus-seats of the yogic body, that is, without a located image; or as 'in the heart-lotus'. The last line praises the knowers' keenness.

reading: In the bewilderment that women with collyrium-dark eyes cast, you have lost yourselves; if you would be free of trouble, and if by a mind that has known truth you gain the knowledge that shines, you will know how to be saved and live for aeons.
nuance: ஐயிறந்து is read as ஐயம் இறந்து (doubt gone) or ஐ இறந்து (having lost the self, or having passed the five). ஊழிகாலம் வாழ்வீர், living for aeons, is the Siddhar claim of a deathless body, or long life by knowledge; the verse does not separate the two.

reading: You mutes bewildered by the gate where the embryo lay: if you can mark and look at the word the guru spoke, you will become a body of shining form and become celestial, and go and join him as a body of holy radiance.
nuance: கரு இருந்த வாசல் is the womb, and the bewilderment is desire for it; the way out is the guru's word attended to. The verse promises a transformed body (உருவிலங்கு மேனி, திருவிளங்கு மேனி), the Siddhar goal of a body of light rather than release from body.

reading: Poor ones who go seeking, saying 'we must bathe at a holy water': tell me clearly where the bathing is. After you have stayed clear within yourselves as the holy water, what is holy water is the five letters Sivaya.
nuance: தீர்த்தம் is used four times and moved from river to self to mantra. தெளிந்து (clear) is both the clarity of water and of mind, the pun carrying the argument.

reading: Straightening the neck and opening the good eyes wide, you people: what sin is this sin of a mouth gone slack and hanging open? The beginningless one that is in the firm seed may dwell in the letter that is no letter, having been there.
nuance: The first two lines mock a posture, the straight neck and fixed stare of show-yoga, ending in a gaping mouth. Lines 3 and 4 are corrupt: எனழுத்திலோ has no sense as printed (எழுத்திலோ, 'or in the letter', fits), and the construction 'in the letterless letter' is tradition's reading of the Lord beyond the written mantra.

reading: If you can perceive, as you eat and sleep, the maya you see and the elements mingled with it, then the ancient six become one, and as the pure one of the Veda that begot them, the primal root that stands as the release of the cosmos is the root.
nuance: உண்டு உறங்குமாறு (in the way of eating and sleeping) places the perception in ordinary life, not in retreat. பண்டை ஆறு, the ancient six, is unglossed: the six centres, the six ends of knowledge, the six faiths or the six limbs of the Veda are all possible. The last line's grammar is loose and the reading is tentative.

reading: You who pity the gate that bore you and die beyond count: you do not know the cause of the bud blooming on the plantain that put it forth. If you can open the hanging gate and look, seeking, the maya that appears will leave and the light will come and appear.
nuance: ஈன்ற வாசல் (the gate that bore you) is the womb, and pitying it is lust for it. நான்ற வாசல் (the hanging gate) is tradition's term for the uvula or the door at the palate through which the breath is raised, as in Tirumanthiram 805; the plantain bud that opens (கான்ற வாழை மொட்டு) is taken as the lotus of the head or the kundalini flowering. On a plain reading the lines are about birth and a plant, and do not connect; the coded reading carries them.

reading: You mutes who swing to and fro, pitying the whirling gate: you do not think of opening the whirling gate to reach the truth; after you open the whirling gate and perceive the truth, you yourselves become the truth that was inside the whirling gate.
nuance: உழலும் வாசல் (the whirling or turning gate) repeats in every line; tradition takes it as the womb-gate that keeps one turning in births, and as the inner door of 1031. ஊசலாடும் (swinging) is the oscillation of the undecided mind. The last line is identity, not vision: the opener becomes what was behind the door.

reading: After you have sought and held within yourselves, for four nazhigai, the light that sprouted and rose in the root channel, you may live as a child and may become the supreme Brahman; by the oath of the one who ate the poison and by the Mother's oath, this is true.
nuance: மூலநாடி is the channel at the root (the base of the spine), and the light that rises in it is what tradition calls kundalini, though the verse does not use the word. நாலு நாழி is four nazhigai, about ninety-six minutes, a daily measure of practice. The two results, a child's body and Brahman-hood, are given together, as at 968.

reading: When you want to stay, can you stay by wishing it? Was it to die that they created you in the earth? Worship, before you die, the five letters spoken by the unshrinking Lord; do not lose your footing taking it as a mere medicine.
nuance: The second line can be a protest (surely not created only to die?) or a statement of fact. மருந்தெனப் பதம்கெடீர் is open: do not ruin your state by treating the mantra as medicine for the body alone, or, with பதம் as the word, do not corrupt the mantra; or the mantra is the medicine, so do not lose it. Compare 1036, where the five letters recall the breath.

reading: Are not all fifty-one letters contained in one letter? Are not the sky-spread mantra and the four Vedas one? Within the sky-spread root five letters it sprouted; it sat as the seat of the limb-linga: Sivayam.
nuance: The fifty-one letters of the Sanskrit syllabary are reduced to one, and then the five letters are made the source of the mantra and the Vedas. அங்கலிங்க பீடம் (the seat of the body-linga) places the linga in the body, as 999 took it out of stone.

reading: The letter Sivayam is the letter in which Siva dwells, the true letter to trust as the means; the breath that has gone out through the doorless gate, the five letters Sivaya will call back by that means.
nuance: கபாடமற்ற வாசல் (the gate with no door) is taken as the nostrils or the opening at the crown through which the breath leaves. The claim that the mantra calls the departed breath back is read by tradition as the mantra governing the breath (vaasi) in life, or as restoring life; the verse states it flatly as உபாயம், the means.

reading: Not form, not space, not a thing that stands attached to one; not belonging to the gate it joins, not the other, not the absent; not great, not small, not even what is spoken; who can see the straightness that stands as the rare one?
nuance: A string of denials like 973, with the gate (வாசல்) now among the things the Lord is not bound to, so even the inner door of 1031 and 1032 is not his. நேர்மை (straightness, rightness) is the poet's name for him in 1025 too.

reading: Is the self beginningless? Is the not-self beginningless? Are the five senses that flowered and their objects beginningless? Are the argument-filled books and Sadasiva beginningless? Yogis who come puffed up, you must answer quickly.
nuance: அனாதி is the word Siddhanta gives to the Lord, the soul and the bond alike; Sivavakkiyar runs it down the list to the senses, the disputing sastras and Sadasiva himself and demands an answer. The taunt வீக்கவந்த (come swollen) matches விகாரமற்ற at 1023, which asks the yogis the same way about the letters.

title: சிவவாக்கியம்
theme: Sivavakkiyar turns the reciters of Agamas back to what is already at home: the curd in the hanging pot, the body that is thrown out when it tips over, the kin who cannot follow at Death's call. Against these he sets the Lord found within, as the breath held near the heart, as the five letters laid over the limbs, as the letters A, U and M, and as the coiled power roused through the root channel; the hall of Tillai and the city of Arangan are read into the body.
structure_note: The run opens with reproach (1039 to 1046: scripture, the pot, wealth, kin and Death), passes through praise and the inner light (1047 to 1053), raises the body-and-life question (1054), and ends in a set of letter-verses on A U M and the five letters (1055 to 1063), several of them in cipher.
source_issues: 1041: குருக்கிடுக்கும் is unclear and may be corrupt.
1047: கன்மகூட்டம் is unclear; the line may intend காயம் (body) rather than கன்மம் (deed).
1058: ஆறுவித்தை is unexplained and may be a corruption of a technical term.
1060: அழுர்ந்து is not a standard form, perhaps for அழுந்து (pressed in).

reading: You recite Agamas that stand outside understanding and cannot grasp the one straight path, lost on the way; like someone who leaves the curd in the hanging pot and goes into the town to look for butter: how can one keep company with such men without understanding?
nuance: The curd at home is the Lord within and the butter sought abroad is what scripture and pilgrimage promise; the verse does not say that, it leaves the image to do the work. அறிவிலே புறந்திருந்த may mean the Agamas stand outside understanding or that the reciters stand outside the understanding the Agamas hold.

reading: You do not look, bones melting, with the two halls joined; you do not discern the one truth that stands as the hall of form; passing beyond the imagining that stands as the hall of the womb, can you be clear that this is the holy hall?
nuance: அரங்கம் (hall, stage) comes four times, and the last, திருவரங்கம், is the name of Srirangam; the verse plays the shrine's name against halls within. Who the two of இருவர் அரங்கம் are is not said; tradition takes the pair as Siva and Shakti, or as the two breaths. The sense turns on this unresolved pun.

reading: You stand in love and desire for the womb-pit, poor wretches and revelling sinners; setting yourselves right again and again by truth, know and know again the reddened five letters and yourselves, whom they dissolve.
nuance: குருக்கிடுக்கும் is obscure: perhaps 'caught in a crevice' (குருக்கு) or something gurus set up. சிவந்த அஞ்செழுத்து, the red five letters, is read in tradition as the pancakshara seen as light in the body. உருக்கழிக்கும் may mean the letters dissolve your form, or that you must dissolve your own form; both readings keep the five letters as what undoes the self.

reading: Being born on earth and talking past all dispute, countless crores of gods say 'mine' and 'yours'; but as the pupil sits in the eye while the eye is covered, it is by this one's eye that the countless crores of gods see.
nuance: The image is the pupil (கண்மணி) in the eye: the seeing in every seer, itself unseen. வழக்கலாது உரைக்கவும் is unclear, 'speaking what cannot be argued' or 'speaking against custom'. 1085 returns to the Lord as the pupil of the eye.

reading: When a clay pot tips over they set it upright and stack it; when a bronze pot tips over they treasure it as still needed; when our pot tips over they throw it out saying it stinks: what maya is this, Lord, that stands mixed into thought?
nuance: The body is the third pot, and the comparison is in what people do with the fallen vessel, not in the vessel itself. எண்கலந்து, mixed into thought or reckoning, makes the maya a thing of the mind. The closing line returns in 1076.

reading: Sinners who pile up the firewood of the great wealth you have made: you do not know that the body will be lit with that firewood and burn; children, wives and kin, all of these are maya; when Death comes and calls, can they come along?
nuance: விறகு, firewood, does double work: the wood of the pyre and, as editors take it, the fuel of pride (கர்வம்); wealth builds the pyre on which the body is burned. The last line is a question, and the expected answer, no, is left to the hearer.

reading: Where he came and joined with the Lady, becoming one and two in the town that gained youth, he wears bones and konrai and dances in the hall; if one recites the five letters, many sins depart.
nuance: The first two lines are hard: ஒருவராகி இருவராகி (becoming one and two) fits Siva and Shakti, and இளமைபெற்ற ஊர் (the town made young) may be Tillai or the body renewed by yoga. The close is plain and, for Sivavakkiyar, orthodox: reciting the five letters removes sin.

reading: While you live beside your mansions with cattle and calves, wealth, wife and children rejoicing, Death's messengers come running and strike all at once; you have seen the truth, the body lying there and the life slipped out, and still you do not take it in.
nuance: உண்மை கண்டும் உணர்கிலீர்: the reproach is not that people have not seen death but that seeing it changes nothing. The verse separates seeing (காண்) from realising (உணர்).

reading: Our Supreme, who set the flawless company of deeds, whom the singing gods remember as the dancing foot; Father who took up the dance in the hall of lasting red gold; blue-throated, death-throated, eternally auspicious one!
nuance: A praise verse with no argument. பழுதிலாத கன்மகூட்டம் இட்ட is unclear: the Lord who set the faultless sum of deeds (karma) in place, or who gave a flawless body (காயம்) to the gods. காலகண்டன், throat of death, pairs with நீலகண்டன், the blue throat from the poison.

reading: Like the ash that burned and rose in a forest with no forest left, in a heart that has reached knowledge nothing 'good' remains at all; if one gathers awareness in with the flawless light and holds it, Sivayam grows clear like honey welling in the comb.
nuance: நல்லதேதும் இல்லையே can be read two ways: the jnani's heart is beyond good and evil, burnt clean like the forest; or no good remains to be sought there. The honey in the comb is the second image, a slow welling after the fire.

reading: If you set apart and consider the open space that ran within you, drinking, and came flying, your mind becomes that; think within the light that melts and runs everywhere, and it becomes the good cause for you.
nuance: பருகி ஓடி, 'drinking and running', suits the breath more than space, so வெளி may be the breath's open expanse or the inner sky; tradition reads both. நின்மனம் அதாகுமே, your mind becomes it, is the claim: the meditator takes the nature of what is contemplated.

reading: Full one, who stands as light and comes as fruit, pure, and who recites the teaching that cannot be taught; running like a road and going through the foot of the sky, 'the first Lord is his own lord' has stood for endless time.
nuance: The syntax does not resolve. விண்ணடி, the foot of the sky, is taken in tradition as the crown of the head, where the light passes out. ஆதிநாதன் தன் நாதன் may mean the first Lord is lord even of this light, or that the Lord is his own lord.

reading: In the hall of Tillai, the mansion the Lord raised, the body that came by understanding was made of the five; when the sound of the instrument has sounded and gone, in the nine gates that slip open, one and a crore of ones sat within as one.
nuance: Tillai (Chidambaram) is read as the body, and அஞ்சு as the five elements that compose it. கருவிநாதம் is the sound of an instrument; tradition takes it as the breath or the inner sound that ceases at death or in absorption. The last line, the one and the crore sitting as one, is the merging of soul and Lord, or of the many souls in the one.

reading: If by love you can bring near and settle the breath that sits in the heart and runs pressing, you can see the devotees' temple within the eight directions that spread out; the dragonfly runs and runs: say it, Swami!
nuance: The method is breath held still, and the means named is love (அன்பினால்), not force. தும்பி, the dragonfly, is a figure for the breath or the soul that darts; the last line's address is abrupt, perhaps a refrain carried in. The temple seen is within.

reading: O breath that bowed and prostrated to Tillai; O maya of single enjoyment that stands beyond the limit; in the open space of the heaven-world beyond the limit, white and red became one and stood joined with truth.
nuance: வெள்ளையும் சிவப்பும், white and red, is a coded pair: tradition reads the seed of father and mother, or Siva and Shakti, or moon and sun. Since it is the breath (வாயு) that bows at Tillai, Tillai is within the body. ஏகபோகம் returns in 1090.

reading: Did the body take the life, or the life take the body? If the body took the life, tell me, what was its form? When the body with its life dies, the life does not die; forget the body as true, see and realise, and then speak knowledge.
nuance: The verse argues: a body that took a life would already have had a form, so the life must come first; and since the life does not die with the body, the body is not the self (உடம்பு மெய் மறந்து). 1083 and 1109 return to the question.

reading: With the letter A you made the seven worlds; with the letter U you took on form and stood; with the letter M the world was deluded; A and U and M together, Sivayam sat.
nuance: The three letters of Om are given three acts: creation, embodiment and delusion, and the three together are the Lord. The verse does not match them to the usual gods or to the five acts; it leaves M, the closing hum, as the letter of maya.

reading: Humans deluded by eating mantras: mantras are not what wells from forgetting; what a mantra is, is the breath that rises in its heat; for those who have eaten the mantra there is no death at all.
nuance: The claim is that a mantra is breath, not a word, and that 'eating' it is drawing it in. மறத்தில் ஊறல் is unclear, 'welling from forgetting' or 'from valour'; மதத்தெழுந்த may be the breath rising in heat or in intoxication. The last line is the Siddhar promise of deathlessness through breath.

reading: What shall I say of what has no grammar? Of the nature that passes beyond the words of the fine Tamil that is recited; as lightning gathers into lightning and becomes lightning, within me there is nothing but the Lord and I.
nuance: The verse disclaims its own medium: Tamil poetry cannot say it. The lightning image, the many flashes that are one lightning, is reused in 1088 with the Lord subsiding within the self.

reading: As the banyan gathers into the banyan seed and becomes the banyan, you have grown and reached enjoyment without any other seed; you do not consider the six-fold knowledge, men without understanding! Look at this within yourselves: it has become Parabrahman.
nuance: ஆறுவித்தை is unexplained: six kinds of knowledge, the knowledge of the six (adharas), or the seed (வித்து) of the way (ஆறு). The banyan in the seed says that the whole is in the self; Parabrahman is a Vedantic word unusual in this corpus.

reading: The mantra that rose from A, as akara and ukara: for those who know which letter it is, there is no rising into birth here; if one seats the mantra that rose from SA in the Supreme, A and U and M together sat as Sivayam.
nuance: சவ்வுதித்த மந்திரம், the mantra risen from SA, is the five letters that begin with சி. தற்பரம் is the Supreme, and editors take it as a place in the yogic body, the centre between the brows; on that reading the verse is an instruction to fix the mantra there. The closing line repeats 1055.

reading: With the two NAs as legs, the uttered MA as belly, the two SIs as shoulders, the excellent VA as mouth and the two YAs as eyes, standing pressed into straightness, the five letters Sivaya stood in right order.
nuance: The five letters are laid over the body as a figure: the paired letters go to paired limbs. The layout differs in detail from Tirumular's (941), which puts MA at the navel and YA as the light above.

reading: Within the moving wheel whose root is the two and the one, you lay coiled in three rings like a curled dog; the conch's sound that rose in contention went through the root channel and sat in the city of Arangan as Sivayam.
nuance: The coiled sleeper in three rings is kundalini as tradition pictures it (three and a half coils); சுணங்கு, a dog, is the Siddhar's homely image for the serpent. இரண்டும் ஒன்றும், two and one, may be the three channels; அரங்கன் பட்டணம், the city of Arangan (Srirangam, Vishnu's), is read as the crown of the head. The verse is in cipher throughout.

reading: As the turtle that moves in the sea climbs the shore, lays its eggs, and while it roams the sea again they take their form, so to think within the body of our light of the gem-hall that stays within the petal is truly the good truth.
nuance: The image rests on the belief that the turtle's eggs on the shore hatch by the mother's thought from the sea: thought alone reaches and forms what is far. மடல், a petal, is the lotus of the heart; மணியரங்கம், the gem-hall, puns again on Arangam. 1070 makes the same point with the wasp's nest.

reading: The letter uttered and risen in the three mandalas, in the pillar that stands striking against them, and in the mouth of the hanging serpent; the mantra the mother who bore and the father raised and spoke: within the one letter that appears there is nowhere else to speak.
nuance: The three mandalas are traditionally the regions of sun, moon and fire in the body; the pillar is the spine or the central channel; the hanging serpent is kundalini or, on another reading, the uvula. The mother and father may be Shakti and Siva or one's parents. 1064 repeats the last line.

title: சிவவாக்கியம்
theme: The one letter within the five: Namasivaya stands inside the body, the five senses are to be gathered into a single letter and silenced so that the Lord speaks, and the gates of the body open upward to a light beyond the sky. Around this Sivavakkiyar sets the one source that became castes and beings, the deniers who say 'it is not', those who do not bow, and, three times, the name of Rama; the breath known and let go keeps one a child.
structure_note: Letter-verses and the five letters (1064 to 1069, 1073) alternate with the images of becoming by thought (1070), the gates (1074, 1086) and the one that became many (1075, 1077). Rama's name enters at 1071 and returns at 1081 and 1082. 1079 and 1084 are in cipher; 1087 is the one breath instruction; 1088 closes with the lightning image shared with 1057 and with Pattirakiriyar.
source_issues: 1067: அலைந்தருள் செய்கிறார் reads oddly of the senses and may be corrupt.
1079: வாமநாடு is obscure and may be a corrupt place-name or technical term.
1082: ராமமென்னுன் appears to run two words together (ராமம் என்னும்).
1088 is paralleled almost word for word by Pattirakiriyar's Meynjanap Pulambal 177 (seq 180), as the corpus notes; one of the two poets has the line from the other or from a common stock.

reading: Three and three and three, which the three gods seek; the three and the five letters, roaring within the letter A; the mother who bore, the father, and the moving nada: within the mandala that appears there is nowhere else to speak.
nuance: The three threes are not keyed; tradition offers the three letters of Om, the three channels, the three regions. The verse reworks 1063 line by line, replacing the one letter with the mandala in which it sounds.

reading: Lying curled like a dog, like a feeding ghost, fools who rose delighting in the stinking pit; if you can cut the snarl of the five who rage, you will become one in six among the six crore matted-haired ones.
nuance: சீறுகின்ற ஐவர், the five that rage, are the senses; கும்பி, the pit, is the womb or the belly. சோறுகின்ற பூதம் is unclear (a being that feeds, or an element). The last line's six crore and 'one in six' has no key; perhaps the six adharas, perhaps the ranks of sages.

reading: The space that deluded you within as a circle; within the eight-fold figure, the containing and the subsiding; within the moving wheel that is eight and eight and eight, what can be reached rose, once we had known our Lord.
nuance: அட்டவக்கரம் may be the eight-letter mantra or an eight-cornered figure; எட்டும் எட்டும் எட்டும் (twenty-four) may count tattvas or petals. எட்டலாம் puns on எட்டு, eight, and எட்டல், reaching. The plain sense is that the body's wheel becomes legible after knowing the Lord, not before.

reading: The one who speaks too is the Lord, and Brahma-knowledge is within you; the five who are desire wander and dispense grace; if you contain those five of desire into one letter and stay without speaking, the Lord will come and speak.
nuance: அலைந்தருள் செய்கிறார் reads oddly, the senses 'graciously' wandering; it may be ironic, or அருள் may be corrupt. The exchange is the point: when the speaker falls silent, the Lord takes over the speaking. 1104 ends the same way.

reading: The five letters Namasivaya and the higher states they give; in Namasivaya's five, the five, and the ancient maya; the five letters Namasivaya stand within us; Lord, speak well the truth of Namasivaya!
nuance: அஞ்சில் அஞ்சும், the five within the five, is left open: the five elements, the five acts or the five senses. The verse puts maya too inside the five letters, so the mantra holds the binding as well as the release.

reading: Supreme, there is no separate fear for you and for me; standing with hand raised and folding the hands in worship are what I owe; Lord of glory whose head melted and gave nectar: the strength you gave me is Om Namasivaya.
nuance: பயம் may be fear or fruit, so line 1 may say there is no separate fruit for you and me. சிரம் உருகி அமுதளித்த, the head melting and giving nectar, is read in tradition as the yogic nectar from the crown; it may also be the moon on Siva's head. The verse accepts outward worship, unusually for this poet.

reading: In its nest of fresh clay the hunter-wasp has set a browned worm; thinking daily, it becomes what it thought; the fresh clay breaks and it becomes the dragonfly that flies away; madmen, understand the shape the Lord fashions.
nuance: The image rests on the belief that a worm sealed in the potter wasp's clay nest becomes a wasp by brooding on it; வேட்டுவன், hunter, is the wasp that hunts worms. One becomes what one holds in thought. A second reading has the clay as the body that breaks and the winged thing as the soul; பிச்சர்காள் may address the mad or the Lord's madmen.

reading: For all who come and stay on luminous Kasi, Visvanatha, whose body is the open light, with the clear Lady beside him speaks the saving taraka: the easy name, Rama Rama, Rama the nectar.
nuance: The tradition is that Siva at Kasi speaks the taraka mantra into the ear of the dying; Sivavakkiyar names it as Rama. A Saiva poet giving Siva the Rama name is the point, taken up in 1081 and 1082 and in 1095's refusal of two gods.

reading: The yoni of the creeper grown from the eye and the water: one may babble of it in the open, but no fruit came of that; the land spread as space and the root knowledge within space: the strong jnanis who are clear stay clear, for certain.
nuance: வில்லவல்லி யோனி is cipher; the creeper is Shakti and the yoni her source-figure, and the phrase returns in 1084. The verse contrasts speaking of it openly, which bears nothing, with the knowledge held within space. மூலவித்தை is the root knowledge or the root mantra.

reading: Om Namasivaya: once one realises it and realises truth; once one realises it and truth clears; once one realises it and realises truth, Om Namasivaya stands mingled within.
nuance: Three nearly identical lines and a fourth that lands: the verse is the chant it describes, and its only addition is the sequence realise, clear, realise, mingle. Nothing is said beyond the refrain.

reading: The nine gates of trouble and the gate that reached meaning; the five gates that speak and what stood swelling and sobbing; opening the good gate and going through the gate of knowledge, those who have seen the boundary gate are not born again.
nuance: The nine gates are the body's openings and the five the senses; the good gate (நல்ல வாசல்) is tradition's tenth gate at the crown. அருத்தடைந்த வாசல் and சொம்மிவிம்மி are unclear. 1086 opens the same upper gate.

reading: The one that was first became forms upon forms, rose as the differences of caste and became every living being; after staying with the origin and rising again into birth, he becomes the jnani of light and stays pure.
nuance: Caste (சாதிபேதம்) is listed among the forms the one took, so it is neither denied nor honoured here; 1098 and 1100 attack it. Line 3 is hard: who stays with the origin and is born again, the one or the soul, and whether the jnani is the one returned.

reading: That the world blossomed with the blossoming pollen as its root; that the blossomed flower came with its intoxication, fed and let go; that the five senses with their organs were confused and fell on the earth; this dazzling, confused maya: what maya is this, Lord?
nuance: The flower and its pollen are the figure for generation: the body grows from seed as the world from pollen, and ends with the senses fallen. The closing cry is 1043's.

reading: All that is on the earth and all in the wide sky, the bright flame that stands joined to them without any place of its own; without anyone's place, within and without, the one who has seen its fine places knows Siva and is the jnani.
nuance: ஓரிடமும் இன்றியே (without any one place) and சீரிடங்கள் கண்டவன் (who has seen its fine places) pull against each other on purpose: the light has no place, and the knower sees where it is.

reading: Carrying clay vessels you climb the mountain and wander about; you say that things past counting are possible; how can one live together with men who do not bow daily to the Lord with their heads to the ground?
nuance: மண்கிடாரம், the clay vessel, may be the body carried up the hill of life, or the pots carried to hill shrines; the boast of line 2 is of powers. The verse demands daily prostration, which sits oddly beside 1093 and 1094 unless the Lord bowed to is within.

reading: That the book on the tongue perished, that goodness and caste perished, that the chariot one mounts perished, that inquiry lessened: sinners, what maya is this? When the left land becomes a quarrel, on the day the breath subsides the five subside too.
nuance: The list of losses, learning, caste, vehicle, inquiry, reads as the ruin at death or as what falls away in realisation. வாமநாடு is obscure (the left region, perhaps the moon channel). ஐவரும் are the senses or the elements that subside with the life.

reading: Poor ones who keep saying 'it is not, it is not': can what stands as 'not' be said not to be? It is neither 'not' nor a thing; those who have found the limit of what stands with the two joined are not born again.
nuance: The target is the denier (perhaps the materialist, perhaps the Buddhist 'void'); the answer is a double negation, not nothing and not a thing, with the two joined. The verse circles what later Siddhars call சூனியம் without using the word.

reading: Kara kara kara kara, guardian of the guarding aeon; pora pora pora pora, the meritorious one who stood in battle; mara mara mara mara, the one who shot the seven trees: the name that says Rama, Rama, Rama.
nuance: The syllables are chosen so that மர reversed gives ராம, as in the story of the hunter who chanted 'mara' until it became 'Rama'; the seven trees are the sal trees Rama's arrow pierced. The verse is sound before it is sense, a mantra built from repetition.

reading: Born on the wide earth with a body that is a mere interval: when release is said to be this, does one still need to want pleasure? Did the four Vedas, sung, spread over the earth? Seek the name that says Rama, Rama, Rama.
nuance: நேரமான காயம், a body of a moment, or a body made to measure. Line 3 asks whether the Vedas spread over the earth, which may be a taunt (they did not) or a concession (they did, yet the name suffices). The name is set above both pleasure and scripture.

reading: The life comes and takes a body by its goodness and stays; when the life leaves the body it becomes form upon form; the life becomes Siva's maya and they kill one another; the life becomes Shakti's maya and they eat one another.
nuance: The mutual killing and eating of life and maya is the puzzle: tradition reads the soul lost in maya and maya dissolved by the soul's knowledge in turn. நன்மையால் may be by merit (the fruit of good deeds) or by the goodness of the Lord.

reading: The long letter, the circle, and the full creeper's yoni; the long letter and one circle, I did not see one that stood; if, marking it with horn and foot, one says it is in the short letter, our Lord does not stand straight in the one circle of the long letter.
nuance: A riddle in the terms of Tamil writing: நெட்டெழுத்து the long vowel, குற்றெழுத்து the short, கொம்பு and கால் the vowel signs (ெ and ா), வட்டம் the circle, which may be the letter ம, the zero or the bindu. Tradition reads the circle as the bindu and the creeper's yoni as Shakti's triangle; the plain point is that the Lord cannot be written down.

reading: The true thing the gods in heaven cannot know, our Lord who stood mingled as the pupil within the eye; after cutting off birth on earth and setting his flower feet, the great one dwells within us: that is the truth.
nuance: கண்ணில் ஆணி, the nail or pin in the eye, is the pupil: the Lord as what sees in the seer, taken up from 1042. The feet are set (மலரடிகள் வைத்தபின்) as the guru sets the feet on the disciple's head, and then the Lord is within.

reading: Opening the upper gate of the light that stands beyond the sky, when it has entered and mingled within so that the eyes rejoice, forgetting the maya born of earth and its confusion, to stay in accord with the Lord mingled in thought is the truth.
nuance: மேலைவாசல், the upper gate, is tradition's tenth gate at the crown, 1074's good gate. The light is beyond the sky yet enters within; the verse holds the two directions together.

reading: Once you have known the breath within the root breath and let it go, if day after day you fix it as a single gaze before you, you can stay long as a child and become Parabrahman; by the oath of the poison-throated one and the oath of the Mother, this is true.
nuance: The verse is the chapter's one plain instruction: know the breath, release it, hold it in attention daily. The promise is youth and the Supreme, sworn on Siva and Shakti. The word is மூச்சு, not the Siddhars' வாசி.

reading: As lightning rises, lightning spreads and lightning subsides, the Lord within me who stands within me subsides within me; since the eye that stands in the eye does not know the straightness of the eye, I have known nothing but the one who stands within me.
nuance: Two images for one claim: the lightning that rises and subsides in itself, and the eye that cannot see itself. The last line is the poet's confession that he knows only the one within, not the Lord as an object. Pattirakiriyar's Meynjanap Pulambal 177 (seq 180) has the same lightning line as a question, 'when shall I know?'.

title: சிவவாக்கியம்
theme: Sivavakkiyar's fiercest run against rite and rule: stone images, dawn and dusk bathing, 'our god and your god', the sacred thread, menstrual and birth pollution, caste, flesh and leavings. His one argument is turned on each in turn: every body, Brahmin or Saiva, grew from blood and the pollution they call impure, and the Lord did not stand apart from flesh; so purity is nowhere outside and the Lord is nowhere but within. Beside the attack stand the inner worship (feet as linga, breath as thread), the cipher of the mandalas in which the Lord dances, and the counsel to stop wanting.
structure_note: Cipher verses open and close (1089, 1090, 1106 to 1108); between them the polemic runs by topic: stone gods and bathing (1093, 1094), sects (1095), pollution and caste in a connected run (1096 to 1101), scripture (1103, 1104, 1110), flesh (1111, 1112) and leavings (1113). 1102 on wanting and 1109 on the guru's word stand apart.
source_issues: 1092: பஞ்சி ஓதும் in line 1 is unclear and may be corrupt for a word meaning 'recite'.
1099: தாண்மை is not a standard form (தாழ்மை or தன்மை).
1100: நின்ற் at the end of line 4 is broken, probably நின்ற.
1095: வங்கவாரம் is unexplained.
1112: மதிரமாக is unclear (மதுரமாக or a word for drink).

reading: One can stay, one can stay on earth; one can push away even the seven worlds of Hari, Mal and Brahma; in the pit that takes no embryo, in the pillar without legs, once the fire-chamber has been opened, you and I are the Lord.
nuance: The pit that does not conceive and the legless pillar are coded: tradition reads the root centre and the central channel, and நெருப்பறை, the fire-chamber, as the kundalini fire. On that reading the verse promises long life on earth and mastery over the worlds, then union. 'You and I' may be the poet and the Lord, or the poet and a disciple.

reading: Having become single enjoyment, the two becoming one, how do enjoyment and union still fit? When becoming and perishing have both become its concern, there is no dying and no being born, none, none at all.
nuance: ஏகபோகம், single enjoyment, is 1053's term; the two who become one are read as Siva and Shakti, or the two breaths. The question of line 2 is rhetorical: once two are one there is nothing left to unite. அதன்கண் நேயம் is unclear, 'the aim in it' or 'love in it'.

reading: If, with the four Vedas as the elements and the water that mingles there, and with the feet as the linga, one does worship in devotion, the jnanis who open the final door from the ear and cut the bond pass beyond beginning and end and reach the rare release.
nuance: An inner puja: the Vedas as the elements, water as the bath, the feet (the Lord's or one's own) as the linga. காதினின்று கடைதிறந்து, opening the end from the ear, is obscure; perhaps the guru's word in the ear opens the last door. The verse does not condemn worship, it relocates it.

reading: Men who twist cotton thread and recite 'cotton': if you can twist the thread of the bellows and end sorrow, the book in the mind turns to art and the book of time passes away; the five letters Sivaya set the book right and end care.
nuance: If பருத்திநூல், the cotton thread, is the sacred thread of the twice-born, the verse sets against it துருத்திநூல், the thread of the bellows, the breath drawn in the lungs; நூல் is also 'book', so the twisting of thread and the reading of books collapse into one word. காலநூல், the book of time or fate, is what the breath undoes. The reading of line 1 is not secure.

reading: Mute ones who perform the dying rites of the tattvas: can gods become stone? What can I do but laugh? The first shoot of the three-eyed one, whom the three gods cannot know, stays mingled within you as your guard; look.
nuance: சாவதான தத்துவச் சடங்கு, rites of tattvas that die: rites addressed to perishable matter. The question தேவர் கல்லும் ஆவரோ can be 'can gods be stone?' or 'can stones be gods?'; either way the image is denied and the Lord is placed within as காவல், the guard.

reading: Fools who plunge into water morning and evening: what did the frog that lay in the water morning and evening gain? If you rise in good time and think of the root with one of your three eyes, release and attainment come.
nuance: The frog is the reductio: a creature that lives in the holy water gains nothing by it. கண்கள் மூன்றில் ஒன்று, one of the three eyes, is the inner eye at the brow; மூலம், the root, is the Lord or the base centre. 1105 takes up the morning-and-evening of this verse.

reading: Our god and your god: are there two gods? Are there two gods, one there and one here? Is not the first form that stands there and here one? Those who speak sect-quarrel will die with their mouths rotting with worms.
nuance: வங்கவாரம் is unclear, taken as partisan talk or crooked speech. The curse is as fierce as the argument is simple: a god with a location (அங்கும் இங்கும்) is not the first form.

reading: Of what lay between the rooms you say 'that day is impure'; when one is born in the proper order you say 'that day is impure'; when one knows the ford and bathes you say 'that day is impure'; how can one join with base men without forbearance?
nuance: தூமை is ritual pollution, chiefly menstrual and birth pollution; the three cases are the woman secluded (அறையறை இடை, in the inner room), the birth, and the bath that is supposed to end it. The verse opens the run 1096 to 1101, in which pollution is shown to be the source of every body. Line 1 and line 3 are not secure.

reading: That water stood in and came from the space where sound arose; fools who, maddened, writhe and sink in water: what is purity? What is the rule? What is it that stood seen as cleanness? What is the madman's body that came to be, and what difference, O wisdom?
nuance: சத்தம் வந்த வெளி, the space from which sound came, is the first element in the order of evolution; water is a late derivative of the same space, so no purer than what it washes. கட்டு may be the rule, the bond or the knot. The questions are left as questions.

reading: Month by month it is pollution, and the pollution that was forgotten; was it not when the months ceased that the form grew? What nada, what Veda, what good castes? Say how the Veda-reciting Brahmins came to be!
nuance: The argument is biological: the embryo forms when the monthly blood stops, so the body of every Brahmin is made of what he calls impure. 'Forgotten pollution' may be the blood that did not flow because it became the child. The verse asks for a genealogy and expects none.

reading: Was it when pollution ceased that the good lamp stood? Was it when maleness ceased that custom ceased? When lowness ceased and maleness ceased and agitations ceased, in the time when pollution upon pollution ceased, speech ceased and stood.
nuance: A ladder of negations (அற்று) ending in the cessation of speech. தூமை and ஆண்மை may be the female and male principles whose ceasing is the state beyond; தாண்மை is unclear (தாழ்மை, lowness, or தன்மை, nature). சுதீபம், the good lamp, is the light that stands when all this is gone.

reading: Fools who speak of the oozing pollution and the life settled in it as two different things: how then did it come to be? Is it not the stinking pollution that becomes the good castes? Raging fool, that is the shape in which pollution stood.
nuance: The verse closes the gap the purity rules depend on: the life cannot be held apart from the blood it settled in, and the high castes are that blood grown up. நின்ற் in the last line is a broken form.

reading: From the oozing pollution of the woman who saw her trouble, man and woman joined everywhere in the land and the world came to be; the life that had renounced, with pollution itself as its desire: which land is the land that stands free of pollution?
nuance: தீமை கண்டு நின்ற பெண், the woman who saw her trouble, is the woman at her period, as the next line's union shows. Line 3 is hard: the renounced life (சீவன்) that takes pollution as its desire may be the soul drawn back into birth, or the renouncer whose body is still the same blood. The final question has no answer: there is no such country.

reading: Saying 'I want, I want', you wander in vain seeking; though you seek wanting, there is nothing but what is; once you renounce the longing that seeks saying 'I want', the very thing you wanted is quickly seen.
nuance: The verse keeps the object: what was wanted is seen, not dissolved, once the wanting stops. உள்ளதல்லது இல்லையே, there is nothing other than what is, makes the seeking itself the obstacle.

reading: The Vedas the twice-born recite, the excellent Agamas, the firmly set causes and the true books declared, the teaching tied up and kept and all the madness fit for stories: all of it ended as dust once I had known the Lord.
nuance: The list is careful to include the true books (மெய்ம்மை நூல்கள்) with the stories: the point is not that scripture is false but that it ends (முடிந்ததே) at knowledge. பிரானை யான் அறிந்தபின் makes it a report of the poet's own case.

reading: A hundred crore Agamas, a hundred crore mantras, recited for a hundred crore days: what use is that? Six and six and six, and within the heart the one letter: recite the rising excellent letter and the Lord comes and speaks.
nuance: ஆறும் ஆறும் ஆறும் is not keyed; eighteen, or the six adharas counted three ways. The one letter is the pranava or the seed of the five letters. The verse does not reject recitation; it reduces its object from crores to one.

reading: Death who stands mingled in morning and evening: tell me, what is the maya by which evening becomes morning and reddens? If, free of morning and evening, you subside into thought, the Death who stood as morning and evening is not, is not.
nuance: காலன் is Time and Death at once, and morning and evening are both the passage of days and the twice-daily rites of 1094. So the verse reads two ways: escape time by settling in thought, or give up the dawn-and-dusk observance and settle in thought; both end the Death that the alternation is.

reading: Within the eight mandalas, bending two mandalas; within the set mandala, counting, six mandalas; in the mandala touched, appearing, three mandalas; within the mandala of the dance the Lord stood dancing.
nuance: The counts eight, two, six, three are given without a key; tradition reads mandalas as the regions of sun, moon and fire and as the centres of the body. நட்டமண்டலம் may be the fixed (நட்ட) mandala or the mandala of the dance (நட்டம்). 1107 asks the question this verse answers.

reading: Within the eight mandalas, where does the Lord stand? At the two legs, the root channel: there Rudra was seen; the two fish-eyes mingling, the eight directions closed, the upper two mingling, he stood swinging and dancing.
nuance: The question is placed inside the body: the root channel at the legs, the eyes, the eight directions (the senses or the petals), and the upper two (the brows, or the two channels joined above). Which 'two' and which 'eight' is cipher; what is plain is that the dance is located within.

reading: Mother, father, salt water: what is known you do not know; mother, father, salt water became Hari, Ayan and Aran; once mother, father, salt water became the first of the first, nothing became anything but you, mother-father.
nuance: உப்புநீர், salt water, is read in tradition as the parental fluids, the seed and blood of generation; the verse climbs from them to the three gods and to the First, and ends in the one addressed as mother-father. The attack of 1096 to 1101 continues under cipher: the same fluids make gods and men.

reading: Before taking form, how did the body join together? Before conceiving, how were the causes? How does the awareness set in it fit? Mark the word the guru set right, understand it and take it in.
nuance: Three questions about what precedes the body, and no answer but the guru's word. The verse admits that the body's origin is not settled by argument, after a run of verses that argue it from blood.

reading: There is a beginning and no end; then there were no four Vedas; there is light and no word, and nothing that has passed beyond words; the breath that sat in the first three, who knew even itself at the beginning, O Lord?
nuance: The Vedas are set after the beginning, so not eternal. சொல்லிறந்தது ஏதுமில் may mean nothing beyond words exists, or nothing of what passes words can be told. ஆதியான மூவர் are Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra or the three letters; the breath seated in them is the breath of 1056.

reading: 'Flesh, flesh, flesh', you say, speaking follies; how did our Lord stand apart from flesh? As flesh, as babbling, as the one of great name who walks about, the madman who sprouted in flesh: see, he is the Father.
nuance: The target is the horror of flesh as impure, and 1112's 'Saiva fools' suggests vegetarian Saivas. The argument is not that eating is good but that the Lord is in flesh and grew in it; whether that defends eating it is left to the hearer. பித்தன், the madman, is Siva's own epithet.

reading: You drank milk made from blood and grew with it; what was one and other became two, one may say; what is it you cast off as drink, and what is this 'flesh and meat'? What grew into the frame, Saiva fools?
nuance: Mother's milk is blood transformed, so the body was fed on blood from the start; the Saiva who refuses flesh is made of it. மதிரமாக விட்டதேது is unclear, perhaps 'what did you set aside as intoxicant' (மதுரம், sweet, is another reading). The verse asks what the rejected flesh differs from, and answers with the body itself.

reading: The stone that has eaten you throw away saying 'leavings'; are the leavings you see not of the hand, or is it different for the Supreme? Listen about the leavings you see: in the water mingled by the hand, what purity did you get? Fools without insight!
nuance: உண்ட கல் is hard: the stone image that has 'eaten' the offering, after which the food is எச்சில் (leavings), or the vessel one ate from. பாணி is hand or water; the hand that purifies is itself unclean, and the water used has touched mouths. On either reading the rule of leavings is turned on the one who keeps it.

title: சிவவாக்கியம்
theme: Sivavakkiyar sets the priest's purity against itself (Brahmins who shun fish yet bathe in fish-water, who shun goat yet sacrifice it; gods knotted in cloth; water poured into water) and puts in its place a Lord found in the body: the blue lamp at the brow, the five letters climbed as a ladder from NA and MA to SI, the breath as the great light, and ciphered counts of the body's centres. The refrain சிவாயம் (Sivayam) closes question after question about where body, breath and desire were before they were.
structure_note: Not an arranged chapter: the tool's running cut of a long work under one editorial heading (அறிவு நிலை). Still, the stanzas fall into runs: questions and fables of the body's end (1114 to 1120); the attack on Brahmin purity (1121 to 1123); the Lord within and the five letters (1124 to 1130); the triple question of what was before conception, with its answer (1131, 1132); abuse of the jnani and a riddle (1133, 1134); and number-ciphers on the body ending in the fifty-one letters and the lion-roar (1135 to 1138).
source_issues: 1132 line 2 (உருத்தரிக்கு முன்னெலாம் காயம்நின்ற தேயுவில்) repeats line 1's answer where 1131's question was about the breath (உயிர்ப்பு); probably a copyist's doubling, with the breath's answer lost.
1116 line 3 கூவமான் is obscure and may be corrupt.
1123 line 2 முத்தரித்து விட்டது cannot be construed; the stanza's slang verbs (அக்கிடீர், முக்கிடீர், மைக்கிடீர், மொக்கிடீர்) are read by guess.
1128 line 3 உற்றிருநது for உற்றிருந்து and line 4 அரிந்தவன் for அறிந்தவன் are spelling slips in the source.
1130 line 3 பத்தியில் தொடர்ந்தவர் is probably பத்தியிற் தொடர்ந்தவர்; no change of sense.

reading: When sleep comes and forgets the books recited, the learning understood, wife, children and kin, where did they go and hide, or did they stand become everywhere? Tell me, Lord, the mystery of their hiding in the light.
nuance: Sleep is used as a test: whatever vanishes nightly, learning and family alike, cannot be what one is. The last line offers two answers in the form of a question, that they hid somewhere or that they became everything, and leaves both open. 1172 repeats the stanza with mantras and Agamas in place of books.

reading: Like bundles hung on the neck of a buffalo that has calved, you fools knot him up in three or four cloths; the endless Lord who is the three and four worlds, what truth is there in the god you have bound up?
nuance: The target is a god wrapped in cloth, an image or an amulet, set against a Lord who is the worlds themselves. ஈணெருமை is a buffalo that has calved (ஈன்ற எருமை); ஊணிஊணி is unclear, perhaps ஊன்றி ஊன்றி (pressing tight) or a word for tying. மூணுநாலு (three-four) is used twice, of cloths and of worlds, and the second may simply mean 'all the worlds'.

reading: Four cocks and five chicks, as though one brood, quarrel together in the guarded coop; once the old jackal has got into the coop, all four and all five are dead.
nuance: A fable in cipher. The plain reading is a body whose contents squabble until death enters. The numbers carry the coded sense: tradition takes the four as the inner faculties (mind, intellect, will, ego) or the four Vedas, the five as the senses, the coop as the body and the old jackal as death. கூவமான் in line 3 is obscure and may be a corrupt word.

reading: If you rise at dawn and cut the four bindings of the sedge sprouting in the root pond, you can live as a child and become the supreme Brahman; the feet of the poison-eating Lord and the Mother's feet are the truth.
nuance: The root pond (மூலக் குளம்) is, in tradition, the muladhara, and the sedge that sprouts there the coiled power or the desires rooted in it; the four bindings are not fixed (the four faculties, or four states). காலமே means 'early' but also plays on கால், breath. The plain reading, weeding a pond at dawn, stands on its own as an image of daily discipline.

reading: As layers of verdigris form on copper, so the light of the beautiful hall, which cannot be written down, is covered; heat it and heat it until it thins and merges upward, and see how the copper has shed its tarnish.
nuance: The gloss takes அணியரங்கம் as the little hall at Chidambaram, so the light is the dancing Lord's, here inside the self. வெம்பி (burning, grieving) is the discipline, and the simile is also the alchemist's: tarnish burnt off copper. அம்பினில் எழுதொணாத is unclear, perhaps 'cannot be written in water' (அம்பு). Compare 1145, where the tarnish is cut from gold.

reading: If you can seek and seek and gaze with love within yourselves, the one who runs out and runs back will settle within you; even Death who came hunting will stand bewildered and go, and you will remain without lack for crores of ages.
nuance: ஓடிஓடி மீளுவான், the one who runs out and returns, is not named: the breath, the mind, or the Lord himself all fit, and the practice differs with each. The promise of life without lack for crores of ages is the Siddhar's claim of deathlessness, taken by some as the body's and by others as the soul's.

reading: What are you quarrelling about, fools who have lost awareness? You do not know the great light that never quarrels, the prana. If you can cut the knot of the two quarrelling deeds, you can have the great joy that does not quarrel.
nuance: The breath itself is named the great light (பேரொளி பிராணன்), which is the Siddhars' identification rather than a simile. பிணங்கு (quarrel, tangle) opens every line; the two deeds are good and bad karma, and the verse asks for their knot to be cut, not for good deeds to outweigh bad.

reading: The Brahmins say they have never eaten fish, then or now; but the water they dive in and drink is where the fish live. They say they have never eaten deer; but the thread on their chest hangs from a stripped deer's hide.
nuance: The argument is not that one should eat flesh; it is that the purity rule cannot be kept by anyone who bathes or wears the thread, so purity of birth and diet is incoherent. The deer-skin (கிருஷ்ணாஜினம்) is worn with the sacred thread by the initiated.

reading: Brahmins have never eaten goat, then or now; but is not the sacrifice you perform goat-flesh? They have never eaten cow; but is not what you put into your vegetable dish from the cow?
nuance: The sacrifice (யாகம்) is called goat-flesh outright, which turns the Vedic rite into butchery. The last line is less clear: what from the cow goes into the vegetable dish may be ghee and milk, or dung used as fuel; either way the cow's body is being consumed.

reading: A string of jibes built on rhyme: you wear the rudraksha for the one who stands as the beginning of all lives; you strain and press; you blacken yourselves, being born and dying and dying again; you gorge; and what I have made you understand is the truth.
nuance: Each line opens with a slang verb (அக்கு இடீர், முக்கு இடீர், மைக்கு இடீர், மொக்கு இடீர்): wear the bead, strain, put on black, gulp. அக்கு is the rudraksha bead; முக்கு is to strain or to dip; மை may be kohl or the darkness of ignorance. உமைப்பிடித்து முத்தரித்து is obscure (seizing Uma, bearing three?). The sense is a mockery of outward religion, but the lines cannot be fixed word by word.

reading: How did the Lord come and enter the true inner self? As water enters the tender coconut on the red palm. And once the Lord has entered and made the body his temple, there is no more opening the mouth to the people of the world.
nuance: The coconut's water appears inside with no visible door, which answers the 'how' by denying any entrance to watch for. The fruit of the Lord's dwelling is silence toward the world, not preaching, which sits oddly beside a poet who preaches in every stanza.

reading: Passing beyond NA and MA, resting on the SI that cannot be sought, with VA and YA within it as the generous teaching of wisdom, the Shakti filling within and piercing through the crown: those who know this way are, I swear by the Lord, the Lord himself.
nuance: The five letters are climbed as a ladder: NA and MA (in Siddhanta reading the Lord's concealing power and impurity) are left behind, SI (Siva) is the ground, VA (grace, Shakti) and YA (the soul) are found within it. That assignment is the tradition's, as in Tirumanthiram 975; the verse itself only names the letters and the crown. ஒவ்வு சத்தி, the matching Shakti, may be the power of grace or the kundalini that pierces the crown.

reading: Is the letter beginningless? Is the soul beginningless? Are the elements and senses that have entered us beginningless? Are the books full of argument and the shastras beginningless? Is the true guru who cut through to the Supreme beginningless?
nuance: Five questions, no answer. Saiva Siddhanta holds the soul and its bonds beginningless, and the guru's grace too; set as questions beside letter, elements and books, the doctrine is made to defend itself. 1173 repeats the stanza with Sadasiva in the guru's place.

reading: What is it you saw? Whatever is looked at perishes in the looking; if you stay keen, Siva is in the inner intent. Whenever you look, leave the looking itself behind, and you will join like the flower that has bloomed with its fruit.
nuance: குறிப்பில் அச்சிவமதாம் places Siva in the intent or sign, below the act of seeing. The last word, பிறப்பிரே, is odd: 'you who are born' as address, or 'you will be born', which would reverse the sense; the flower-and-fruit image suggests ripening rather than rebirth.

reading: Hold in devotion the great blue lamp that flickers at the brow, stand and stand there until attachment is cut: that is the fruit. Stay joined and look: above the inner light there is a light beyond, and the one who knows where the Father sits is himself beginningless.
nuance: The blue lamp (நீல விளக்கு) at the forehead is, in yogic tradition, the light seen at the brow centre in meditation; the verse does not explain it. உள்ஒளிக்கு மேல்ஒளி, a light above the inner light, ranks the vision below what it leads to. The last line makes the knower, not only the Lord, beginningless. 1130 repeats the image.

reading: You scoop up water and pour it back into water: what do you think you have done, and whom are you thinking of as you pour it all out in vain? If you can think on the root, on the seed, and on the glory that sprouts from the seed, you may reach Siva's state.
nuance: The rite is the water-offering (tarpana, ablution) done in a river. The verse does not ask for a better rite but for thought (உன்னல்) on root and seed, the source of things; சிவபதங்கள் may be Siva's feet or Siva's state. 1175 asks the same question in its first line.

reading: Discern and look at the blue lamp that wavers at the forehead, the light that stands within; those who followed it in devotion have become the Supreme itself, and those who dwell in that place are my masters.
nuance: Near-repeat of 1128, with the result stated: those who follow the inner light become the Supreme (பரமயம்), and the poet calls them his masters (நாதர்), the only place in these stanzas where he bows to anyone.

reading: Before conception, where did the body stand? Before it took form, where did the breath stand? Before grace was received, where did desire stand? Say that Sivayam is what has cut this knot of doubt.
nuance: The gloss on 1132 gives திருக்கு as doubt, so the refrain line says the mantra cuts doubt rather than that it is twisted. Three befores (body, breath, desire) are set against three afters (conception, form, grace). 1132 answers; 1185 asks again with different answers.

reading: The answers: before conception the body was in fire; before form, in fire again; before grace, desire was in the wind; and say that Sivayam is what has cut the doubt.
nuance: Line 2 repeats காயம் and தேயு from line 1 where 1131's question was about the breath (உயிர்ப்பு), so the text is probably doubled by a copyist and the second answer lost. Fire and wind as the pre-states of body and desire follow the Siddhars' element-physiology; the verse gives no account of where grace was.

reading: The dasas and the Saivas of the place, with the children of the outcaste woman, acting together, hurried to throw stones at the jnani walking down the street; what it yielded them was sin, by Sivayam.
nuance: தாதர் (dasas) are the Vaishnava devotees, set beside Saivas; both sects join in stoning the knower. Line 2 is hard: கூதரைப் பறைச்சி மக்கள் may be the sectarians' own slur for the jnani's companions, or the poet's way of saying that high sect and low birth are alike in this. The event may be the poet's own experience, and the refrain closes the verse as a verdict.

reading: The soles whitened from running and running about in sin; the wretched cat came and leapt into the milk; the pandit came and looked and said 'nothing to it'; and the thread snapped. What illusion is this, Lord?
nuance: A riddle stanza. Plainly read, it is a life wasted and ended, with the astrologer's verdict that nothing could be done. In the coded reading tradition offers, the milk is the inner nectar or the seed, the cat the mind or desire that spoils it, the thread the breath that snaps at death. பணிக்கன் is a teacher or astrologer.

reading: A cipher of counts: four for the square, eight for the Vedas, three for the fire, six for the wind in its circle, eight for the mountains of blood, all reckoned above my head: this is the nada that mingled and rose in the radiant body.
nuance: The numbers are read by tradition as the body's centres: the square of four as the four-petalled root lotus, the six of wind as the six-petalled centre above it, the fire's three as the three-angled centre at the navel, the count ending above the head as the ascent to the crown. The mapping is not secure, and 'eight mountains of blood' has no settled sense. What the verse states plainly is that sound arises in the body when the count is complete.

reading: Four and six, ten; then four and three; then ten and six above, gathered into one: when the guru sits within the circled five letters and tells it, the sheath that appeared as skin, body and sound is known.
nuance: The sums (ten, seven, sixteen, one) are the Siddhars' arithmetic, taken by tradition as the ten airs or channels and the sixteen kalas gathered into the one. கோசம் (kosha, sheath) is the body as a covering; the verse says it is known only when told by a guru, from within the mantra, which is as much as the poet will reveal. 1137 carries கோசம் on.

reading: What rose as the sheath, what stood piercing the cage of the body, what was born as the land, is Sivayam, the five letters; the countless mantras are for the Lord to drink, and the fifty-one letters stand filling the vessel.
nuance: The fifty-one letters are the Sanskrit alphabet, the matrikas of mantra theory; the verse ranks them below the five, which are what rose, pierced and was born. ஈசனார் அருந்திட (for the Lord to drink) is odd and may mean the mantras are offered to him; ஆசயம் (vessel, receptacle) may be the body or the heart.

reading: The pedestal of the linga in the body, the twice-five letters, the swelling lotus and the heart of those who join, the light that takes its share there, the five letters spread abroad and the lion-roar sound: nothing is other than Sivayam.
nuance: அங்கலிங்க பீடம் makes the body the linga's pedestal, as the Lingayats also say. ஐயிரண்டு எழுத்து may be ten letters or 'the five and the two'. சிங்கநாத ஓசை, the lion's roar, is in yogic tradition one of the inner sounds heard when the breath is stilled. 1170 repeats the stanza with ajapa's three letters and conch and discus in place of the ten letters and the lotus.

title: சிவவாக்கியம்
theme: Questions about origins (where did form arise in the matchless light, where does the mind rise, sleep and go astray) are answered by turning worship inward: the body is the shrine where the Lord is seen, mind is the flower and water, the breath is the smith's bellows that blows the light into a blaze. Temple and mosque, homa pit, Vedas and bound books come to nothing once the Lord is known; what remains is the one, the one letter, bindu and nada, and the refrain Sivayam.
structure_note: A running cut of one editorial heading (அறிவு நிலை), not an arranged chapter. Runs within it: a series of questions on where form, worlds and mind stand (1139 to 1142); the yoga of root fire, nectar and the dance at the crown (1143, 1144); the one and the uselessness of scripture (1145, 1146); the body as shrine and alchemical blowing (1147 to 1149); the silent yogi and the apophatic one (1150, 1151); ladders of letters (1152, 1153); jibes at Brahmin birth and false puja (1154 to 1158); and the inner body, sun and moon, root circle and seed as the mantra's seat, closing with the heart as the temple (1159 to 1163).
source_issues: 1140 line 4 அவமைதானது is garbled; உவமை (likeness) or அவள் மேரு may be meant, and the question's object is lost.
1144 line 2 பத்தனாரும் is probably அத்தனாரும் (the Father), as line 4 has அத்தன் ஆடல்.
1150 line 3 மவினஞான for மவுனஞான (line 1) is a spelling slip.
1154 line 3 விண்ணம் cannot be construed; the class sent to hell is lost with it.
1158 line 3 தேடிவத்த for தேடிவந்த is a scribal slip; no change of sense.
