reading: Where is the place where form arose within the incomparable great light? Where did it, becoming comparable, pierce through the cosmos? Where did the Supreme, who is austerity itself, stand bearing a form? Where did water, born in the Supreme, stay?
nuance: Four questions on how the formless took form, with no answer. உவமையிலா (without compare) and உவமையாகி (becoming comparable) mark the step from the unmanifest to the manifest; சலம், water, is the first of the elements to be asked about, perhaps as the womb's water or the first fluid of creation.

reading: Where did three bulls calve a single calf in the sky? Tell me where the seven lower worlds stand. From the play of him and her the rare Siva was born, and she herself is Meru: where is that?
nuance: Riddles. Three bulls birthing a calf is an impossible image; tradition takes the bulls as the three channels or three gunas and the calf as the breath or the inner light. Siva born from the play of him and her inverts the usual order and may mean the Siva-state in the yogi; Meru as 'she' is, in body-cosmos reading, the spine. The last words (அவமைதானது) are garbled, perhaps உவமை (likeness).

reading: Where does it stand to rise, where to subside? Where does it move, where is the eye's sleep? Where does it stand to think, and where is the mind's confusion? Jnanis who are able to lay down the rule must explain this at length.
nuance: The subject that rises, subsides, moves, sleeps, thinks and is confused is unnamed; the mind and the breath both fit, and the Siddhars treat them as one movement. The verse asks the jnanis, not the books, to answer, and asks for length (விரிந்து), which the poet's own four lines never give.

reading: Eight gates that turn and play, eight gates that are proclaimed, eight shapes without sides, eight gates where fire plays, eight shapes without a straw in them: you deluded ones who went round and round them! There is also a flower that never budded; by the Lord's oath it is true.
nuance: Five eights, which tradition spreads over the eight directions, the eight siddhis, the eight-petalled lotus and the eightfold yoga; the mapping cannot be fixed from the stanza. The flower without a bud (அரும்பிலாத பூ) is the clearest line: a thing with no origin, the Lord or awareness itself, set against all the eights the deluded circle.

reading: Staying put, kindling the root fire's heat with the breath, so that the honey's chamber opens and one sweetness is tasted; with the three moons from the sky entered into the staff: the yogi who takes this measure while still in the flesh is a yogi indeed.
nuance: The sequence is the standard one of Siddhar yoga: breath heats the fire at the root, the nectar's chamber (தேன் அறை) in the head opens, and sweetness is tasted. மதியம் மூன்று (three moons) and தண்டலம் (the staff's ground, taken as the spine) are the coded terms; the three may be the three kalas of the moon or three centres. ஊனிருந்து, 'while in the flesh', insists that the measure is taken in this body.

reading: When one is thought of as freed, at the crown of the finished cosmos the Father and the Mother danced together in love. You jnanis and siddhas who speak of the dance at Tillai: when the Father's dance began, all things took up the dance.
nuance: பத்தனார் in line 2 is probably அத்தனார் (the Father), as line 4 has அத்தன். The dance is moved from the hall at Tillai (Chidambaram) to the crown of the cosmos, which in body-cosmos reading is the crown of the head; the address to siddhas who 'say Tillai' is a jibe at those who locate it in a town. அடங்கல் ஆடல், the whole dancing, may mean all things joined the dance or that the dance is the end (அடங்கல்) of all.

reading: One, and one, and only one: the whole world is one, then and now it is one, the beginningless is one. Cut the tarnish from the hardened red gold and set it true, and that day you will know the god within yourselves: Sivayam.
nuance: ஒன்று is said eight times in two lines. The second half gives the method: the tarnish (களிம்பு) is what hides the one; the gold is not made, only cleaned. உம்முளே places the god within the hearers, so the oneness is also between them and him.

reading: The planted images, the shastras recited, the homa pit set up to one's liking, the four Vedas in concord, the books tied up in bundles, all that fierce babbling: it all ended as nothing once I knew the Lord.
nuance: தாவரம் (the immovable) may be planted trees or installed images; the list runs from stone to fire to text. பொட்டதாய் முடிந்ததே, 'ended as a dot', is finality rather than refutation: the poet does not argue with scripture, he reports that it dropped away. The first person (பிரானை யான் அறியவே) is rare in these stanzas.

reading: In the round cage the moon grew and rose; close by its frame stood conch and discus; when the axle slipped and the door at the gate was shut, how did the Siva who had risen within the egg get out?
nuance: A riddle on the body as egg and cage. The moon in the round cage is, by tradition, the nectar or the mind in the skull; conch and discus are Vishnu's emblems, here perhaps the two side channels or the ears and eyes; the axle (அச்சு) the spine or the breath. The question is how the indwelling Siva, or the soul, leaves at death once the gates are shut, and the stanza does not answer it.

reading: What is a temple, what a palli, what is the spot you have marked out? What are the mantras you stand mouthing in worship? Bow rightly in the shrine of wisdom and you will see the Lord in the shrine of the body.
nuance: பள்ளி is the word for Jain and Buddhist shrines and for mosques, as well as for schools; set beside கோயில் it levels the sects' houses together. The answer keeps the word and moves it: the palli of wisdom and the palli of the body (ஞானமான பள்ளி, காயமான பள்ளி). The mantras are faulted as spoken 'with the mouth' (வாயினால்), not as mantras.

reading: Good silver counted six, fine copper four, killing lead three, bright red gold two, with the bow-string's sound one: if you can blow so that these shine, the light itself can be made into gold of the eighth touch.
nuance: An alchemical stanza read by tradition as yoga: the metals are the body's elements or states, ஊதல் (blowing) is breath-control, and எட்டு மாற்று is both the purest touch of gold and 'to reach' (எட்ட). நாகம் may be lead, as in alchemy, or the serpent. The counts six, four, three, two, one are not explained. The verse makes a claim about transmutation and leaves the procedure, if there is one, unsaid; it is read here for what it claims, not as a recipe.

reading: Yogis of silent wisdom whose inner dirt is uncut stay dirty though they live in the forest; yogis of silent wisdom who have cut the dirt within have cut off birth, though they sit among corpses.
nuance: The same title, மவுன ஞான யோகிகள், is given to both kinds, so silence and the forest are not what divide them; மனத்தகத்து அழுக்கு, the dirt in the mind, is. பிணத்தடம், a place of corpses, is the cremation ground where Siddhars sat, chosen as the least pure place to make the point.

reading: Not form and not light, it stood as one; not scent and not smell, not reached by the slow channel; not large, not small, not even the speaking breath: who can see the rare straightness that stands?
nuance: An apophatic stanza, denying even light (ஒளியும் அல்ல) after many stanzas that make the Lord light. மந்த நாடி, the slow channel, is unclear, perhaps a nadi of the body or dull inquiry. நேர்மை (straightness, rightness) is the poet's word for what remains when all is denied; 1160 uses it for the line beyond sun and moon.

reading: In the one letter from which the whole world rose, in the two letters whose spoken joy you do not know, in the three letters that rose as the three gods, in the four letters spoken on the tongue: Sivayam.
nuance: A ladder of mantras by letter-count, ending at the refrain, which has four syllables (சி-வா-ய-ம்). The one letter is Om or the letter A; the two are, in tradition, the breath's unspoken syllables (ஹம்ஸ or சோகம்); the three are அ உ ம, read as the trimurti; the four are the refrain itself, so the stanza ends by naming its own closing word as the mantra. These identifications are the tradition's; the verse gives only the counts.

reading: Beginning and end, the root bindu and nada became the five elements; the root bindu and nada became the five letters; the root bindu and nada stood pervading all; the root bindu and nada are themselves Sivayam.
nuance: The first three words of every line are the same, and the stanza is a formula: bindu and nada, the first pair of Saiva cosmology, become elements, letters and pervasion in turn, and are then identified with the refrain. ஆதி அந்தம் (beginning and end) makes them both the first and the last.

reading: All who gave food will live for many crores; all who gave gold may hold lordship; all who gave ... will fall into the hot hell; and all who 'broke in' will surely stand beyond.
nuance: The first two lines are ordinary merit-talk; the last two are not. விண்ணம் is obscure (an ulcer? a corrupt word?) and what sends to hell is lost with it. கன்னம் இட்ட is housebreaking, and that burglars go beyond is either Siddhar irony or code: the one who breaks into the inner house, the thief who knows the theft of 1167. Another reading hears கர்ண (the ear) and takes it as those who received the whispered initiation.

reading: You who stand beyond all recitation, free of sleep and food, free of caste difference, standing without doubt, knowing the intent within faultless understanding, standing with nothing at all: how is it that you move?
nuance: நீர் (you) is not identified: the Lord, who has no caste or need, or the jnani who has reached that state. The list of absences, no recitation, no sleep, no caste, no doubt, no thing, suits either, and the final question (இயங்குமாறு எங்ஙனே?) is the same one asked of the formless Lord's action in Siddhanta.

reading: When you were born, did the loincloth, the shining thread and the tuft come born with you, and all the bundle of bright threads? Did the four forgotten Vedas rise in your mind? What can you say, you who stand with the earth split and the sky fallen?
nuance: The argument from birth: nothing a Brahmin is marked by was present at birth, so none of it is nature. மறந்த நாலு வேதம், the forgotten Vedas, may mean the Vedas no one remembers from a past life, or Vedas learned and forgotten. The last line's split earth and fallen sky is the collapse of the claim, not a cosmic event.

reading: The bellows is there, the smith is there, the golden light is there; if you can think with a mind set right and blow so that it shines, the great pillar will blaze and spread as a mass of flame, and nothing remains but the dancing light and you.
nuance: The smithy is the body: the bellows the breath, the smith the practitioner or the Lord, the pillar the spine or the flame-linga. The verse answers 1149's 'if you can blow' with what the blowing is for, and its end is not gold but a light that dances (நிருத்தமான சோதி) and a 'you' left standing with it.

reading: Dressed in your guise, polishing the vessels, with heaps of incense and lamps, you behave like men who have butchered a goat and shared out the pieces; you spread out all the copper you could hunt up in heaps and throw flowers at it: what kind of worship is that?
nuance: The priests arranging their copper vessels and images are likened to butchers dividing a carcass; the comparison may also recall 1122's sacrifice. மின் துலக்கி is 'polishing to a shine' (the brass), or 'polishing lightning'. The copper that is 'hunted up' (தேடிவந்த) suggests the images are collected goods.

reading: If you can look past the place where you stand clutching the life that sprouted from the womb's impurity, then the Lord who stands at the crown, beyond blame and beyond pointing, becomes the house in which you dwell, with hands reaching the eight directions.
nuance: முட்டுகண்ட தூமை is hard: the impurity that is blocked (the menses stopped at conception) or that is met with. திட்டும் அற்று சுட்டும் அற்று, without blame and without pointing, denies the Lord both censure and reference. முடியில் நின்ற நாதன் is the Lord at the crown of the head, and the house (வீடு) is also release.

reading: Sun and moon, and beyond them the crowding stars that press upward: those who can melt that straight line into the one letter, in the incomparable void, and stay there, are not born again.
nuance: The gloss fixes அருக்கன் and சோமன் as sun and moon, and in yogic tradition they are the right and left channels, so 'beyond them' is the middle way or the crown. தாரகை (star) may be the third light that arises when fire joins sun and moon, as Tirumular has it, or the bindu. The one letter is Om; உருக்கி (melting) treats it as metal, as in 1145 and 1149.

reading: You who stood shaken and tossed on the three ornate circles above the five letters that sprout from the root circle: if that becomes the wisdom spoken in the hall of the leaf-circle, it stands as the fragrant circle, Sivayam.
nuance: வட்டம் (circle) ends the first word-group of every line. The root circle is the muladhara; the three circles above it are, by tradition, the mandalas of fire, sun and moon or three centres; ஓலை வட்ட மன்று (the hall of the leaf-circle) and ஏல வட்டம் (the fragrant circle) are not fixed. The plain claim is that the body's circles become wisdom only when spoken in the hall, that is, when the dance is known.

reading: In the region of the seed, at the doorway of the blood, within the eight pearl-strings in the chamber of the root centre, in the fearless membrane, as Hari, Hara and Brahma: the mantra that is uttered there is truly Sivayam.
nuance: The body's generative places (சுக்கிலம் the seed, சுரோணிதம் the blood) are made the seat of the mantra and of the three gods, so the lowest centre is where the five letters sound. முத்துசரம் எட்டு, eight pearl strings, may be eight channels or the petals of a lotus; அச்சமற்ற சவ்வு, the fearless membrane, is obscure.

reading: Flower and water are my mind, my heart the temple where he fits; the breath runs as the linga, though he fills the whole universe; the five senses that come are the shining incense and lamp; and for the dancing Lord there are no dusk-and-dawn hours.
nuance: Each item of puja is matched to a part of the person, as in Tirumanthiram 1823, and the senses (ஐவர், the five) become the lamp rather than the enemy. The last line denies appointed hours (அந்தி சந்தி) to the Dancer, which cuts the timed rites of the twilight prayers; whether the poet denies them any value or only says inner worship is continuous is left open.

title: சிவவாக்கியம்
theme: The fullest statement in this run of Sivavakkiyar's oneness and his contempt for marks: the Lord who is everywhere entered our body, so 'your god and our god' is only your difference; caste is nothing to the knower; the body is ten months of the womb's impurity, so pride in it is madness. Against ash, guise, bathing and daily mantra he sets the yoga of the tongue turned back and the channel of sound, and the five letters pressed into the heart until the one letter behind them is known; the refrain Sivayam stands for that one.
structure_note: A running cut of one editorial heading (அறிவு நிலை). Runs within it: union and the five letters (1164 to 1167); the state beyond speech and the body from the womb's impurity (1168, 1169); the letters and the near-repeats of earlier stanzas (1170 to 1173); the name in the mouth, false rites and the womb again (1174 to 1177); book-learning and caste set against the knower (1178, 1179); yoga of tongue and channel, the fives, the letters, life and body, the ascent (1180 to 1185); and one god against two (1186 to 1188).
source_issues: 1184 has no main clause and ends mid-sentence (அப்புறத் தலத்துளே); it reads as the first half of a longer unit or a stanza whose last line has been lost.
1168 line 4 சொல்லியாற cannot be construed as it stands (ஆறு, the way, or a corrupt word).
1176 line 3 உன்னிதொக் குளழலும் is garbled; read by guess as 'the heat within'.
1173 line 1 ஆத்துமா for ஆத்துமம் (as in 1126) and 1181's repeated அஞ்சும் with no nouns are as the source has them; 1181 may have lost its glossing words in transmission.
1174 line 2 ராமராம ராம is the only Vaishnava name-mantra in this run; it is not a misattribution, since the stanza's own argument depends on it.

reading: Only when our forms mingled did I know you; what matters it whether you stay or hide, when in every moment I thought of you we stood merged, so are you and I not one? Doubt mingled and went, and Sivayam became clear.
nuance: The poet speaks to the Lord in the second person and claims identity (நீயும் நானும் ஒன்றலோ) as a question. திருக்கலந்து is ambiguous: 'the holy mingled' or 'doubt (திருக்கு, as the gloss on 1132 has it) mingled and left'; the second gives the better sense with தெளிந்தது (became clear).

reading: Clarified in the five letters Sivayam one can become a god; clarified in them one can rule the sky; the thing of the sky is what is grasped with clarity in the five letters; and the truth is what is grasped with clarity in the five letters.
nuance: சிவாயம் has four syllables but is called அஞ்செழுத்து, so the refrain stands for the five-letter mantra rather than spelling it. The first two lines promise godhood and rule of heaven, the last two the truth; the order ranks the powers below the knowing, and தெளிந்து (clarified) carries every line.

reading: As a clay pot with the five hidden in it bobs on the water and spills its contents, so this body and its senses are tossed upon the waters; and as that pot, filling with water, sits settled, so this body, scooping up Siva, sits delighted and still.
nuance: பொய்க்குடம், the false pot, is the body as fired clay; the five (ஐந்து) hidden in it are the elements or senses. The simile turns on what fills the pot: empty, it floats and spills; full, it sinks and rests. The body is not condemned, only shown as a vessel whose contents decide its motion.

reading: The soul flies like a kite on its string; see it with the understanding that experience gives and tie the knot that will hold; do not let it be blamed, do not let the soul go; bind tight the thief who knows the theft.
nuance: The string is the breath, in the tradition's reading, and the kite the soul or mind that would fly off. பட்டறிவு is knowledge from experience, set against book-knowledge. The thief who knows the theft (களவறிந்த கள்வன்) may be the mind, or the Lord himself, whom Tirumular calls the thief-chief who enters and leaves the body; binding him is then holding the Lord in the body.

reading: Night gone, day gone, even the inner Brahman gone; beyond all the cosmic eggs, in form after countless form, the truth of the blissful nature where speech has died and mind has died: to speak it, there is no helper other than myself.
nuance: அகப்பிரமம் இறந்து, the inner Brahman dying, places even the meditator's Brahman among the things that end. The last line (சொல்லியாற என்னில் வேறு துணைவர் இல்லை) is unclear: 'no one but I can tell it', or 'I have no companion but it'; ஆற may be ஆறு (the way) or a corrupt word.

reading: What stayed gathered for ten months as the womb's impurity became two hands, two feet and two eyes, a body thick with sound, shining with taste and smell; and the 'pure' body it became is, when told truly, that impurity.
nuance: The pairs (கை இரண்டு, கால் இரண்டு, கண் இரண்டு) and the sense-qualities (சத்தம், இரசம், கந்தம்) are the elements' marks, so the body is built from the tattvas out of the impurity. துய்ய காயம், the pure body, is said with irony; the stanza's last word is தூமை.

reading: The pedestal of the linga in the body, the three letters of the unspoken mantra, the conch and the discus, all the sky; the yogis who have taken their share there, the five supreme gates and the lion-roar sound: nothing is other than Sivayam.
nuance: The gloss gives அசவை as the ajapa mantra, the unrecited syllables of the breath (in tradition ஹம்ஸ or சோகம்), here counted as three letters. Conch and discus are Vishnu's, so the stanza claims the Vaishnava emblems for Sivayam too. பரம வாசல் அஞ்சு, the five supreme gates, is not fixed, perhaps the five senses or five centres. Near-repeat of 1138.

reading: You devotees who keep saying 'the five letters and the three letters': the thing itself is neither the five letters nor the three. Press the five letters into the heart and know that letter, and the five letters take on the colour of that: Sivayam.
nuance: The mantra is denied as the goal and kept as the means: the five pressed into the heart (நெஞ்சழுத்து) lead to 'that letter' (அவ்வெழுத்து), which is unnamed, and then the five become its colour. The three letters are அ உ ம, the parts of Om. The stanza is the poet's own gloss on his refrain: Sivayam is not the syllables.

reading: When sleep comes to bewilder and forgets the cherished mantras, the Agamas composed, wife, children and kin, where did they go and hide, or did they stand become everywhere? Tell me, Lord, the place where they hid in the light.
nuance: Near-repeat of 1114 with scripture in the place of secular books: the mantras one has cherished and the Agamas also vanish in sleep. 1114 asked the மாயம் (mystery) of their hiding; 1172 asks the இடம் (place), and மயக்க (bewilder) replaces மறக்க (forget).

reading: Is the letter beginningless, is the soul beginningless? Are the elements and senses that have entered us beginningless? Are the worthy books beginningless, and is Sadasiva beginningless? Yogis who have come far, you must answer quickly.
nuance: Near-repeat of 1126 with two changes: the true guru of 1126's last question becomes Sadasiva, so the Lord's own beginninglessness is put among the questions, and the yogis are told to answer at once (விரைந்து) where 1126 named no one to answer.

reading: While the nine-gated body still has its days before it ceases, the name Rama, Rama, Rama, called the ninth: in the mouths of the spiteful it comes as a disease that blocks; in the mouths of the loving it stays, sunk deep and settled.
nuance: A Vaishnava name in a Saiva Siddhar's mouth, which fits the poet's refusal of 'your god and ours' in 1186. ஒன்பதாம் may make the name the ninth, or pair the nine-lettered name with the nine gates. நோய் அடைப்பதாம் is uncertain: the name becomes a blockage in the spiteful, or blocks disease. The stanza's plain claim is that the mouth that says the name, not the name, decides its effect.

reading: What is the water you scoop up and pour? What is the thing you knead in your palm? You fools who mumble under your breath: what is this guise of deceit, this shutting of the eyes? Gently now, gurus, tell us, tell us.
nuance: The rite is the water-offering with the kneaded rice or clay ball (பிண்டம்) and muttered mantra; the shut eyes are the show of meditation. The last line turns on the addressed 'fools' being 'gurus', said with மெள்ளவே (softly) twice, which is mock courtesy.

reading: The seed set in the impurity of the mother's womb, having been carried before, becomes a drop like dew; the inner heat too subsides within that impurity; and what is born afterwards is itself impurity, you madmen.
nuance: Line 3 (உன்னிதொக் குளழலும்) is garbled; 'the heat within' is a guess from உள் அழல். முன்னையே தரித்தும், carried before, may mean the seed was first borne in the father, or that the soul bore a former body. The stanza's argument is the body's origin in blood and seed, made to shame pride in it.

reading: You who bathe daily to remove the dirt and whose dirt is never removed: where was the dirt, and where is what is without beauty? If you can cut the dirt in the place where the dirt was, you can live close to the Light that has no dirt.
nuance: அழுக்கு is said seven times. The question 'where was the dirt' is the whole argument: if the dirt is in the mind, water cannot reach it. அழகில்லாதது (what has no beauty) is odd beside அழுக்கு and may be a play on the sound; the Light without dirt is the Lord.

reading: Gathered from atoms into a mass, through every kind of womb, you were born a human and now lose yourselves in recited books. What is birth, what is death; passing through the still forms of life, what is thinking, what is standing? Think it through for yourselves.
nuance: அணுத்திரண்ட (atoms gathered) and பல் யோனி (many wombs) give an account of how a human came to be, from matter and through other births, before the books; தாபரம் (the immovable, plants) is among the forms passed through. The verse does not answer its questions and tells the hearer to (நீர் நினைந்து பாரும்), which is its point against recited books.

reading: For the jnanis who have gained and known within themselves, untaught, the Soma of scripture and sound who stands as light, who is the beginning, beyond the cosmos and beyond that again, there is not the least thing called caste difference; there is none.
nuance: சாதிபேதம் is denied for the knower, not argued away for everyone: the stanza's subject is the jnanis, and the denial is doubled (சற்றும் இல்லை இல்லையே). போதியாமல், without being taught, excludes the guru too. சுருதி நாத சோமன் names the Lord as the moon of Veda and sound, a yogic epithet.

reading: In the first cause the body does not age. Fold the tongue back toward the nose, go up by the channel of sound, and if you can hold the pair pressed hard with longing cut away, then look and look and every direction becomes the supreme Brahman.
nuance: The tongue folded toward the nose is the khechari seal; நாத நாடி, the channel of sound, is the central channel. இரட்டை (the pair) is unexplained, in tradition the in- and out-breaths or the two side channels, and ஏக்கறுத்து may be 'cutting longing' or a form of ஏக்கம் (panting). The first line's claim that the body does not age at the source is the Siddhars' deathlessness, stated as a condition reached by the practice.

reading: Five and five and five and five stand making trouble; five and five and five sit settled within; if you can sustain five and five and five, then five and five sit settled within you: Sivayam.
nuance: A count-cipher in fives: twenty that trouble, fifteen within, fifteen to sustain, ten settled. Tradition sets the twenty as the five elements, five senses, five sense-objects and five organs of action, the fifteen or ten as the breaths and faculties; the division is not fixed. The last line's ten may also be the five letters twice, which the refrain suggests.

reading: What is it that stands settled as the first of the five letters? What is it you chant, standing in the letter of the heart? What is it that the sword of the five letters cuts? You must separate out and tell the straight truth of the unripe letter.
nuance: Three questions on the mantra's inside: its first (ஆதி), its place (நெஞ்சு), its work (அறுப்பு, cutting, as a sword). பிஞ்செழுத்து, the unripe or budding letter, is obscure, perhaps the seed-syllable or the letter before it is sounded; 1142's flower without a bud may be its pair.

reading: Where was the life before it took up the body? What is life, and what is the body? What is it that joins life and body? You true jnani who took up a body by life, tell me.
nuance: The same questions as 1131, now about life (உயிர்) and body alone, with a third added: what joins them. The jnani addressed is one who 'took up a body by life', that is, anyone born, so the question is turned on every hearer who claims knowledge.

reading: Set the one letter that curls at the mouth of speech; the root channels pass beyond pain and pleasure; raise the pressed letter within the fire, mingle the six lotuses, and in the place beyond ...
nuance: The stanza has no main clause and reads as the first half of a longer unit, or as a list of stages with the result lost. சுழித்த ஓர் எழுத்து, the curling letter, is Om in its written form, or the letter உ; ஆறு பங்கயம், the six lotuses, are the six centres; the pressed letter raised in the fire is the seed-syllable at the root. The place beyond (அப்புறத் தலம்) is the crown or what is above it.

reading: Before form was taken, the sound that life entered; before conception, what the body was: blood; before grace is received, understanding is the root support. Mark this and know it, you gurus whose virtue is gone.
nuance: The third set of answers to 1131's questions, and different from 1132's: there the body was in fire and desire in wind, here the body was blood (சோணிதம்) and life entered as sound. அறிவு மூலாதாரம் may mean understanding is the root centre, or is the root support of grace. The gurus addressed are abused in the same breath they are taught.

reading: Once the Lord who is everywhere has entered our body, they still parcel him into shares and will not come near the hard way. 'Our god, your god': are there two? The difference is yours alone; in truth there is no second.
nuance: பங்கு கூறு போடுவார், they divide into shares, is said of the sectarians who split the one Lord; பாடு சென்று அணுகிலார் may mean they will not approach the labour of the path, or will not approach the body where he is. The verse's claim is not that the gods are equal but that there is one, and that the two are made by the speakers.

reading: Being Hari and being Brahma, being one everywhere in the cosmos, being great, the foot that stood in the world: is it not one? You fools in guise who made it other by saying 'it is spread out': look with understanding, and here and there it is one.
nuance: Hari and Brahma are named as the one's forms, so the oneness claimed in 1186 includes the Vaishnava's god. விரிவது என்று, 'saying it spreads', is the sectarian's error: taking the one's extension as many. பாதம் ஒன்று, the one foot, may be the Lord's foot or the one ground.

reading: You smear the burnt ash on your body and take up the guise; the mantra you think of in the mind and repeat each day: is it in the former mantra, in the root mantra, or in which mantra that the Lord comes and moves?
nuance: The question is rhetorical and its force is that the Lord moves in none of them, but the stanza stops at the question. வெந்த நீறு, burnt ash, names the holy ash by its making rather than its holiness. முந்து மந்திரம் and மூல மந்திரம் are the initiatory and root mantras of a tradition; the poet does not say which tradition.

title: சிவவாக்கியம்
theme: Sivavakkiyar sets the letters of Om and of சிவாயம் against every outward form of religion: the Lord who takes shape in அ, உ and ம, who joins life and body and who dances the whirling cosmoses into one, is to be known inside the body, not in a shaped stone, a hauled chariot, a staff and caste, or a stack of books. Between the attacks run riddling questions to the 'gnanis' about seed, womb and mantra, and a yogic ascent through the six lotuses to a space where 'he is, and I am not'.
structure_note: No commentary orders the chapter. Three verses end with the challenge to the knowers to explain (1190, 1200, 1213); 1193 and 1194 are one sentence split across two units; the polemical verses (1195, 1198, 1199, 1204 to 1207, 1210, 1212) alternate with verses of pervasion and praise (1192, 1197, 1203, 1209, 1211).
source_issues: 1193 and 1194 are one sentence split across two units; 1193 has no main verb.
1190 மிவ்வை is an unusual word; the editors' gloss takes it as good quality.
1198 line 1 and 2: பெரியபாதை பேசுமோ is unclear in syntax and sense.
1207 lines 3 and 4 (குருக்கொடுத்த தொண்டரும் முகனொடித்த பிள்ளையும்) are obscure and may be corrupt.
1210 திடுக்கமுற்ற ஈசனை (the startled Lord) is odd; perhaps திடமுற்ற.

reading: In the cause that is A he stood as many forms, in the cause that is U he took shape, in the cause that is M the world is bewildered, and in the cause that is Si it became clear: Sivayam.
nuance: The sense turns on the four letters. அ, உ and ம are the parts of Om; சி is the first letter of சிவாயம். Tradition reads A as the Lord's manifold creation, U as his taking form, M as the world's delusion in matter, and the letter of Siva's own name as the clarity that resolves them. On that reading the five-letter mantra is set above Om.

reading: Did U enter the letter A and A come to birth? Did the letters U and M stand each within the other? If they stand evenly matched, even when the states of Siva are reached, you gnanis of good nature must explain it at length.
nuance: A series of questions about how the three parts of Om relate, closed by the challenge to the knowers that recurs in 1200 and 1213. மிவ்வை is an unusual word; the editors' gloss takes it as good quality, so the address is 'you knowers of good nature'. Whether the questions are rhetorical or sincere is left open.

reading: The substance that stands filling the primal five, the beginningless four, the luminous three, the formless two and the single just one: that primal one, which has none of them, is the five letters.
nuance: The numbers are coded. Tradition takes the five as the elements or the five letters themselves, the four as the Vedas or the four kinds of birth, the three as sun, moon and fire, the two as Siva and Shakti or sun and moon, and the one as the Lord. அற்ற தஞ்செழுத்து can mean the five letters 'that have shed' all these, or the one that is 'without' them is the five letters; either way the mantra and the Lord are identified.

reading: There is nothing without sky, yet when you enter it there is no sky; nothing without flesh, yet no flesh; nothing without 'I', yet when you approach there is no 'I'; there is nothing without the Self, and it dances, shimmering.
nuance: Each term both pervades everything and vanishes on inspection; only தான் (the Self, or He) remains, and what it does is dance. The verse makes the dance, not a substance, the last word about what is.

reading: Thinking on the letter with the curl, setting it at the mouth of speech, passing beyond pain and pleasure, going through the channel they speak of, raising the fire of the firm akshara, and crossing the six lotuses, in the space beyond ...
nuance: The sentence runs on into 1194. சுழித்ததோர் எழுத்து, the letter with a curl, is taken by tradition as Om (or its ஓ); அக்கிரம் may be அக்ஷரம், the letter, or அக்ர, the tip or crown; the fire raised and the six lotuses crossed are the serpent power and the six supports in the yogic body. The verse describes an ascent through the central channel in the Siddhars' usual terms without naming them.

reading: ... when the drooping eye is gathered and one arrives there, where all the letters have yielded their conjuring, in the space that is release, when one presses in and, the mind dazed, experiences it: then He is, I am not, and no one is.
nuance: The second half of 1193. இந்திரசாலம் (Indra's net, conjuring) is what the letters produce; the space beyond it is called வீடு, release. The closing state is given in plain words: he remains, the 'I' does not. விழுத்தகண் is unclear, perhaps the eye turned inward or closed.

reading: You run about seeking fine bathing waters; the fine bathing and the Lord are within us. If, seeking the bathing at the limit, you perform the single worship, the soul that reaches Tillai dances within Siva's state.
nuance: மஞ்சனம் is the bathing water of a deity or a holy bath. எல்லைமஞ்சனம், the bath 'at the limit', is obscure; tradition takes it as an inner bathing at the body's end, the crown. Tillai (Chidambaram) is named as something the soul reaches inside, so the dance in the hall is placed within.

reading: Life stands within before it takes a body; life becomes A and the body becomes U, and what joins life and body is that Siva; I have told how life took up a body.
nuance: The letters are mapped onto the pair life and body, with Siva as the joining; the third letter is not named. In the Tirumanthiram the same letters are read as Siva and Shakti, so the poet's mapping is his own and not the inherited one.

reading: While the seven cosmic spheres whirl, the endless wombs whirl, old Mal with Ayan spread out and whirl, and the dark Shakti standing beyond the eight directions whirls, the cosmoses as one, the primal dance is danced.
nuance: The whirling (உழல) of worlds, wombs, gods and even Shakti is contrasted with the one dance that holds them. இருண்ட சத்தி, the dark Shakti, is perhaps maya or the goddess in her dark form; the verse does not say.

reading: You fools like ghosts: will the great path that was given shape with water and limbs speak? Know within yourselves, as your own right, the God whom dark Mal and Ayan could not see.
nuance: The first half is unclear. பெரியபாதை, 'the great road', may be the body, shaped from water (seed) with its limbs, which cannot speak of God; or a great ritual way. The second half is firm: the God invisible even to Vishnu and Brahma is to be realised inside, and உரிமையாக makes it one's own right.

reading: You call a stone that was made the ancient substance and recite what names, you poor ones; take into your heart instead the One who became able to make, to create, to protect what was created, and so ruled the world.
nuance: பண்ணிவைத்த கல், the stone someone made, against the one who makes: the charge is confusing the made with the maker. நெஞ்சில் உண்ணும், eat him into the heart, is the alternative to naming him.

reading: As the fourfold womb and the bindu that is spoken of become one and settle and contract inside the banyan seed, so is the arising from the womb, the mantra that is spoken: you gnanis above, explain it at length.
nuance: நாலதான போனி (யோனி) is perhaps the four kinds of birth (egg, sweat, sprout and womb); the banyan seed is the stock image of a whole tree folded in a seed. சூலதான உற்பனம் can be 'the origin from pregnancy' (சூல்) or 'the origin bearing the trident' (சூலம்), Siva's; the verse likens the mantra's unfolding to conception either way.

reading: When you were formless, Mother, I did not know you there; when you were in form I knew you; made clear by the guru, becoming flawless knowledge, when the season ripened it became the supreme Brahman.
nuance: The formless is known only through form, and the form named is the guru. அன்னை addresses the Lord as Mother, so the Shakti and the Lord are not distinguished; பருவம், the ripe season, makes knowledge a matter of readiness rather than effort.

reading: Being born and dying, and remaining unborn; forgetting and remembering, and making clear what was hidden; renouncing and giving, and scooping up pleasure; being born and dying: all are contained in the house one was born into.
nuance: பிறந்தவீடு can be the body, the house one is born into, in which every opposite plays out; or the release (வீடு) that has 'been born', in which they all end. The list pairs opposites so that neither side is preferred.

reading: He is in the eye; he is the Mal who churned the dark sea; he is in the sky and stands reaching there; he who made the earth is within himself; he is within me and stands as everything everywhere.
nuance: The Lord is named as Mal (Vishnu, churner of the ocean) without any sectarian edge, as in 1197 and 1198 where Mal and Ayan are the lesser gods. The series moves from eye to sky to self to 'within me' before 'everywhere'.

reading: Though you seek goats and lands, elephants and armies, a crore of horses, will any of them come and stand beside you? The alms thrown as you ran and the dharma done gladly: that dharma comes and stands like a horse that has bolted and returned.
nuance: வாசி here is a horse, not the breath of the Siddhars' வாசி yoga. The image is of a horse set loose at a gallop coming back to stand before its owner: what one has given returns, what one owns does not follow.

reading: Sesame, iron, blankets, cotton and bronze, garments, coin and cloth for the Lord: if you give fitting gifts to the Vedic one who dwells within, slowly every disease turns back, Sivayam.
nuance: The list is the standard set of gifts made to Brahmins at planetary rites (sesame, iron and a blanket are Saturn's). The verse redirects them to உள்ளிருக்கும் வேதியர், the Vedic one within, which is the Lord in the body or an inner priest; whether the promise about disease is sincere or mocks the rite's own promise is not settled by the words.

reading: People of the town, you gather as one mind, set a copper image on the chariot, tie on the rope and haul it; look, look at the uproar that quarrelling men make over the primal Siddha-Lord whom no one can know.
nuance: The scene is a temple car festival with its processional bronze. புரளி is a disturbance or a lie; போரிலான is unclear, perhaps 'men given to fighting'. The Lord is called ஆதி சித்தநாதர், the first Siddha, the title the poets give themselves.

reading: Men bewildered by a mind that delusion has entered: if you can swim across with the mantra the guru gave, well; otherwise the servants and the child will suffer the twelve toils that cotton suffers.
nuance: Lines 3 and 4 are obscure. பருத்தி பட்ட பாடு is proverbial for the many processes cotton goes through before it is cloth, here counted as twelve, perhaps the toils of rebirth. குருக்கொடுத்த தொண்டர் and முகனொடித்த பிள்ளை (the servants who gave the guru, the child with the broken face) may be corrupt.

reading: In the mother's womb-chamber, as the brightness of fire, coming into that chamber as a rare form, when it stood like itself it cut the obstruction and became open, gave golden fine greatness and grew as the master.
nuance: The embryo is a light of fire that grows into தலைவன், the lord. தடையறுத்து வெளியதாய் can be read plainly as birth, breaking out into the open, or yogically as the light cutting its block and becoming space; the verse allows both.

reading: Can I forget you for even a moment, the unveiled light that dwells in my heart and hides me, the peerless Lord of great light called gold? Grant me birthlessness at your golden feet.
nuance: A plea in the middle of polemic. மறைப்பிலாத சோதி is the light without veil; எனை மறைப்பு, that it hides me, may mean it covers the poet with itself.

reading: Is the staff you grip your own, you madmen who claim to be Brahman? Having dropped the gross guise, do you take up distinctions of caste? If you can speak truly of the Siva you have distilled, you may go and join the Lord.
nuance: Addressed to staff-bearing renouncers who say 'I am Brahman' yet keep caste; the staff that is 'not yours' says that a renouncer owns nothing, caste included. திடுக்கமுற்ற ஈசன், the startled Lord, is odd; it may be a corruption of திடமுற்ற, the firm Lord.

reading: You are Shakti, you are compassion, you are the sound of the hesitant conch; you are siddhi, you are Siva, you are the letters that are Sivaya; you are release, the first, the three gods: know and realise the city of bones within yourselves.
nuance: அத்திபூரம் is the uncertain word: taken as அஸ்திபுரம், the city of bones, it is the body, and the verse ends by placing all it has listed inside it; it could also be a shrine's name. The conch's sound is the inner nada of 1227.

reading: You cheats of the sastras in coats and glittering beads, you liars who pile up books and recite doctrine: what is your fixity, what your knowledge? Say, what is the letter you abide in and what its mark, you treacherous deceivers?
nuance: நிட்டை (nishtha) is settled absorption, set against learning. பட்டை can be the stripe of ash on the brow or the outer bark of a thing; 'the letter you stood in' asks which syllable they have actually realised, not which they recite.

reading: That the true semen was the means; that it turned white and quickly became water within the water; that the cool body wore it and became a form: you clear gnanis, explain this clearly.
nuance: The third of the challenge verses. It traces the body from சுக்கிலம் (seed) through fluid to form and asks the knowers to account for it; whether the question is a test or a confession of wonder is open.

title: சிவவாக்கியம்
theme: The five letters, the three letters and the one letter: Sivavakkiyar says the mantra is known only by one who has slain the wish for birth, that it is drawn in the root centre and heard as nada when inside and outside match, and that once known the letters are not the thing and yet are. Around this run the familiar attacks (bathing morning and evening, offerings to ghosts and village goddesses, raising hands to the god in a seen temple), a run of number-cipher verses on the tattvas and the muktis, and verses of self-knowledge: the eye cannot see itself, the unceasing conch sounds within, truth cannot be spoken in this world.
structure_note: No commentary orders the chapter. The mantra verses (1214, 1217, 1219, 1222, 1223, 1236, 1237) frame it; 1229 to 1234 are a block of number riddles; 1225 to 1227 are first-person verses of interior knowledge; the refrain விளைந்ததே சிவாயமே closes 1217 and 1236 and continues into chapter 66.
source_issues: 1235 is corrupt in every line (தென்னுக, ததோளி யில்லையாக்கி னாய்கழல்); only the last line reads cleanly.
1228 line 2 (வீட்டுவீழில் தாகபோக) is garbled.
1218 line 3 நெற்பறித்தது is unclear and may be corrupt.
1219 line 4 அரிந்துணர்ந்து is probably அறிந்துணர்ந்து, as in 1211, 1239 and 1242.
1230 line 4 ஏன்றெனாவின் is an unclear sandhi (perhaps ஏன்று என் ஆவின்).
1234 lines 2 and 3 (பத்துமாய கொத்தமோடும் அத்தலமிக் காதிமால்) do not parse.

reading: You who cherish deceitful birth in your minds and do not know the truth of the five letters: if you can slay deceitful birth, then you can come to know the truth of the five letters.
nuance: The order matters: killing the wish for birth comes first and knowledge of the mantra follows, not the reverse. The mantra is not a means to end birth but what one understands once birth is renounced.

reading: Bees that love the fruit of a grove with no unripe fruit, you eat honey no bee made and sleep night and day; before you board the sailless ship and land on the far shore, can the knowledge of silence be spoken by the mouth?
nuance: The images are paradoxes: a grove with no raw fruit (all ripe), honey without bees, a ship without a sail; tradition reads them as knowledge that comes without process and the body or practice that crosses without visible means. The question at the end is the firm part: மவுன ஞானம், silence-knowledge, cannot be said.

reading: You babbling ghouls who cry 'ghosts, ghosts': do ghosts take worship, does Pidari take worship, does the primal take worship, does the beginningless take worship? It is the body that is the ghost, and it took it, knowing its account.
nuance: Pidari is a village goddess who receives offerings. The question who actually consumes the offering is answered by the last line: the body, which eats, is the real ghost, and it keeps count. The last line's syntax is loose.

reading: In the root centre, with the three-cornered figure as its base, the mantra that rose in the middle of our Lord's four doors, drawn with eight petals, a cool blossomed figure: I see nothing else beyond it; Sivayam came forth.
nuance: The verse maps the mantra onto a drawn figure in the body. மூலமண்டலம் is the root centre, முச்சதுரம் (three-square) the triangle tradition places there, நாலுவாசல் its four doors, the four petals of the root lotus in the yogic maps; the eight petals belong to another lotus (the heart) or the eight directions. தீட்டம் is unclear.

reading: Seeking the first, running, running, morning and evening to the water; the channel that is the root of light, the pure space beyond speech, the Agama that begins with A, joined to the first ...: becoming difference upon difference, one is born and the body dies.
nuance: Line 1 mocks the morning and evening bath; lines 2 and 3 name what should be sought instead: the central channel as the root of light, தூவெளி the speechless pure space, and the letters from A as the real Agama. நெற்பறித்தது in line 3 is unclear (paddy plucked, or perhaps நெற்றி, the brow); the fourth line gives the fate of those who stay in differences.

reading: Sitting composed within the Supreme's five letters, rising and seeking, seated above, the mantra uttered: as one cuts bamboo, strips the fibre and works it into a tray, so it appears in the thread one has examined; cut through and realise it.
nuance: The bamboo simile says the mantra's truth appears only after work, as fibre appears from the cane. நூல் is both thread and book, so 'the examined thread' is also the examined scripture; அரிந்து (cut) likely stands for அறிந்து (know) and keeps the cutting image.

reading: If you can know, cutting through the cosmoses, the light that rose in the middle of the lotus, the wondrous Mayan who abides with the three circles, there is no raising of hands to the god in a temple you can see.
nuance: The lotus is the heart lotus (the editors' gloss reads புண்டரீகம் as lotus), the three circles sun, moon and fire in the yogic body; மாயன், Vishnu's name, is used for the Lord. The claim is conditional: the knower has no need of the seen temple, not that no one has.

reading: Rogue who dances in the halls at the crossroads; primal hero who stands as the lover within the lover; primal Lord who stands as the devotee within devotees; truth of truth who stands true to the celestials.
nuance: வம்பன், rogue or troublemaker, is affectionate abuse. சந்தி is a crossroads or a junction; in yogic use, where the channels meet. The dancer of the hall is placed inside the one who loves him.

reading: What is 'the Lord'? The mantra known and spoken. One who came in kindness, one who learned all the Puranas, one who came as Kannan, one praised for that cause: what is the One? The true mantra.
nuance: ஏதடா, 'what is it, man', is a challenge in the familiar. The verse answers 'who is God' with 'the true mantra' and lists Purana-learning and Krishna's birth as either what the mantra is not or as its lesser causes; the syntax of lines 2 and 3 does not settle which.

reading: Is it inside or outside, the place where life contracts and stands? You say you must come close and ask. When inside and outside match, it is nada; opening the hidden door, you must see the mantra.
nuance: கள்ளவாசல், the thieving or hidden door, is taken by tradition as the gate of the central channel or the opening at the crown. The mantra is 'seen', not recited, and arises as sound when the inner and outer are equal; the question posed is refused in favour of experience.

reading: The elements that whirled into being, the immeasurable wombs, the weighty gods, the flawless bond, the cosmos beyond ordering, world upon world: what is the body in which all these joined and burned and lay? Tell me.
nuance: A riddle. The body that burned with all this inside it may be the universe dissolving at the aeon's end, or the yogi's body, which contains elements, gods and bonds and burns them in knowledge; the question form leaves it to the hearer.

reading: Within myself, where did I run seeking myself? Because within myself I did not know myself; after knowing and discerning myself within myself, within myself there is nothing other than myself.
nuance: என்னை, 'myself', carries both the self and the Lord within, so the last line says at once that only the self remains and that only he does.

reading: As lightning rises from the sky and subsides into it, the Lord who is thought of stands within me, since he is in me; and as the eye appears from the eye yet the eye does not know itself, I have not known the me who stands within me.
nuance: Two images: lightning that returns to the sky it came from, for the Lord who arises within and stays within; and the eye that cannot see itself, for the self that cannot be its own object. The verse ends in not knowing, not in knowledge.

reading: Passing through the hall that cannot be contained though one contains it, love that cannot be contained though one contains it stays within me; lying or sitting, when affliction comes, or walking, the conch of nada sounds without pause.
nuance: The hall is Chidambaram's, placed within; the sound heard in every posture and even in distress is the inner nada, the conch of 1211.

reading: Garlanded with cool honey-wandering tulasi, anklets ... in sky, in earth and in the void, in the eight and the two, binding the mind with sweetness and holding it so that it does not leave: that is the joy of love.
nuance: Line 2 is garbled. The tulasi garland names Vishnu. எட்டினோடு இரண்டு, 'eight and two', is Siddhar cipher: the Tamil numerals ௮ (8) and ௨ (2) resemble the letters அ and உ, so 'eight and two' is Om, and the mind is bound in it.

reading: One release, three releases, four releases, joined with good; ripening in enjoyment, in merit, release other than release, as release; ripening as the serpent, as a bed, the fire that crossed the sea of good; ripened in sacrifice: what is it, primal God, that stood so?
nuance: The numbered releases match the Saiva scheme of graded states short of union and the union beyond them. நாகம் ... சயனம், the serpent as bed, is Vishnu on Adisesha on a plain reading, or the coiled power at rest on a yogic one. The refrain என்கொலோ ஆதி தேவனே is wonder rather than a question.

reading: Three and thirty-six, with three threes, as maya; becoming the threefold release, as three, three, three and three; the light that appears as three, a lamp that does not dim: how did it enter my soul, our Lord?
nuance: Number cipher. மூன்றுமுப்பது ஆறு gives the thirty-six tattvas; the threes are read by tradition as gunas, malas, lights or states. ஆ (cow) in ஏன்று என் ஆவின் is the soul, as பசு is in Saiva usage, so the light enters 'my cow', the soul.

reading: Five and five and five, and searching within what is not those; five and three and one: so the primal God stood. You who stand in all that was made of five and five and five, who can see you, who are five and five?
nuance: The fives are the elements, senses and organs of the twenty-five; five and three and one may be the Vedas and the one, or eight. The firm claim is double: the Lord is these groups and is also sought within what is not them.

reading: Six and six and six, five and five and five, the rising two and three, seven and six and eight: becoming knowledge of different kinds, truth together with falsehood, the sound that wells up: the Mayan who is maya.
nuance: The number strings are unexplained; tradition reads them as counts of tattvas, letters or breaths. What is not coded is the conclusion: the Lord is the whole, including the false, and he is heard as sound.

reading: Eight and eight and eight, seven and seven, eight and one and three: so the primal God stood. Those who bow at his feet with the eightfold prostration and recite the eight letters stand freed from sorrow.
nuance: எட்டெழுத்து, the eight-letter mantra, is the Vaishnava Om namo Narayanaya on a plain reading, or the five letters with Om and bindu and nada on a Saiva one. எட்டுமாய பாதம் is probably the prostration with eight limbs touching the ground.

reading: Ten and ten, seven and nine; by the good of gaining the land within the ten and four directions; with the ten ... that place, the primal Mal: release is release only for the devotees.
nuance: The verse runs on the pun பத்து (ten) and பத்தர் (devotees). Lines 2 and 3 are obscure; பத்து நாற்திசை is the ten directions. The plain claim at the end is that release belongs to devotees alone.

reading: Becoming the breath, joined in love, what came facing ...; living day by day in love, in the sins that good joins; casting them off and rising above, you made her of the shoulders nothing; loving your feet and never forgetting them, one may become immortal.
nuance: The text is corrupt in every line. வாசி is read by tradition as the breath of வாசியோகம், the Siddhars' breath practice, though the word is also horse (1204); the one firm statement is the last line, that undying love of the feet makes one deathless.

reading: Easily, in the body, is our Lord's dwelling; A and U stood there without perishing, and the kindling light rejoiced in that place; in the one that becomes space, Sivayam came forth.
nuance: The two letters of Om and the light meet in the body and open into space, where the five-letter mantra 'comes forth'; the chapter's refrain. அளிவுறாது (without perishing) and கொளுகையான (kindling) are the uncertain words.

reading: Devotees who speak of the five letters and the three letters: the five letters and the three letters are not that thing, see. After pressing the five letters into the heart and knowing that letter, the five letters and the three letters become that too: Sivayam.
nuance: The three letters are அ உ ம, the five நமசிவாய or சிவாயநம. The verse first denies that either is the goal, then says that after knowing அவ்வெழுத்து, 'that letter' (the one beyond, or literally the letter அ), they are the thing after all. அவ்வுமாம் may also pun on the letter உ.

reading: Because for the false, speaking lies is enjoyment, and because the truthful have no one true to hear them, there is no need to speak the truth; in this world I was afraid to open my mouth with the truth. Why have you made me waste away so, Lord Namasivaya?
nuance: மெய்யர் மெய்க்கு இலாமையால் can be 'because the truthful lack truth' or 'because truth lacks truthful hearers'. The verse is a complaint, not a rule: the fear of speaking truth is confessed to the Lord as his doing.

title: சிவவாக்கியம்
theme: The Lord is within and pervades everything 'like oil in sesame', so the search outside, in temple tanks, copper images and water rites, is folly, and even moral failing does not bar one who can join him inside. The chapter builds its theology by negation (not standing, not sitting, not bond, not release; cannot be grasped, cannot be told) and by the geometry of the root centre, where the mantra contracts to one letter in which five crore mantras are held. Nearly half the verses end in the refrain விளைந்ததே or அமைந்ததே சிவாயமே.
structure_note: No commentary orders the chapter. Verses of pervasion (1242 to 1245, 1255, 1259) alternate with attacks on water rites and image worship (1246, 1247, 1249, 1252), and verses on the unsayable (1253, 1257, 1258) lead to the letter verses (1248, 1250, 1251, 1262, 1263). 1240 repeats its second line as its fourth.
source_issues: 1240 line 4 repeats line 2 with a variant (அறுவுணர்த்தி for அறிவுணர்த்தி); the unit may have lost its true fourth line.
1250 line 2 has a stray asterisk (*முடரே) for மூடரே.
1263 line 2 (சக்கரத்து சிவ்வைருண்டு சம்புளத் திருந்ததும்) is garbled.
1243 line 4 ஆடுவாழின் is an unclear form.
1252 line 1 வண்டுலங்கள் is an unclear word, perhaps வண்டு (beetle) extended for the rhyme with குண்டலங்கள்.

reading: Even if you kill one creature with another and make it your food, even if in the market you lie, steal and do other wrongs, if you can lovingly join the Lord whom the boar sought, that very day know the gods within yourselves.
nuance: பன்றி தேடும் ஈசன் is the Lord whose foot Vishnu as a boar dug to find. Read plainly the verse makes joining him override the whole moral catalogue; read more softly it says that even sinners are not shut out. The editors' gloss takes மன்று as the market.

reading: If you can stay inside that house and teach knowledge to the breath that rides within the fish-house and speaks maya, the desireless Lord stands as everything; after staying in that house and teaching it knowledge.
nuance: மச்சகம் is obscure: 'fish-house' (மச்சம்), perhaps the body or mind in its waters, or மச்சு, the upper storey, the head. வாயு is the breath, or வாய் the mouth, that talks maya. Line 4 repeats line 2 with a variant (அறுவுணர்த்தி for அறிவுணர்த்தி), so the unit may be damaged.

reading: Like paddy that sprouted in the field being pulled as a weed: if people of the world speak the truth, how are they to survive? Apart from the truth that springs up in the heat of longing, all is false, and the land, born into hell, has suffered its suffering.
nuance: The editors' gloss reads விரகு as the heat of longing; the word also means cunning, giving 'the truth sprung from cunning is only falsehood'. Either way the image is of true speech uprooted like a weed among the crop, and the world called hell.

reading: Sinners who seek the dancing Lord here and there, you do not discern the one who is clear; the thief who stands mingled in forest, land, house and void: run seeking within yourselves, look with love and realise him.
nuance: கள்வன், the thief, is the hidden Lord; the pilgrimage 'here and there' is answered by a seeking turned inward.

reading: The assembly of the dancing celestials, the beyond and the here, the four Vedas that seek, the three gods, the long-living elements, the states in which you stand: without the one who dances, none of it is, none at all.
nuance: ஆடுவாழின் ஒழியலாது is unclear: 'if the dancing one ceases' or 'apart from the one who dances'. On either reading everything listed, Vedas and gods included, depends on the dance.

reading: Becoming is within the Supreme and perishing is within the Supreme; going and entering are within the Supreme; the gods and the directions are within the Supreme; everyone is within the Supreme, and I too am within that Supreme.
nuance: பரம் (the Supreme) is used without a name. The last word, யானும், places the speaker inside what he describes rather than before it.

reading: The seven earths, seven seas, eight places with their mountains, the surrounding sky, the ring of hills and the seven worlds they speak of, the ocean-Mal, the sky-holding great egg and egg upon egg: all rise within the light of the one of the aeon and at once dissolve.
nuance: ஊழியான், the one of the aeon, is the Lord who outlasts the cycles that end in ஊழி. The whole Puranic cosmography is listed in order to be dissolved in one light.

reading: You draw water from the pond; why do your hands tire and stop? You men without wisdom and without a drop of moisture in the mind: if with moisture in the mind you can cut away the dirt, are not the light you thought of and you and I one?
nuance: ஈரம் is wetness and also tenderness: the outer water of the rite is set against the inner moisture of compassion. The last line may address the hearers or the Lord; 'you and I' then means the light, the Lord and the speaker.

reading: Born from water, you perform water rites; thinking of whom do you pour away all that water for nothing? If you can think of the root, the seed and the glory that sprouts from the seed, you will reach Siva's state.
nuance: நீரிலே பிறந்து, born in or from water, points to the seed of 1213: a creature made of water bathing in water gets nowhere. Root and seed are the source of birth and of the self at once.

reading: In the ten matched doorways the root letter spreads; it is the root that moves as the pairing of release and siddhi; the dance that is the great hand of the five mad senses: in the people of the bone-city it was set in place, Sivayam.
nuance: பத்தொடொத்த வாசல் is read as the ten gates of the body (nine openings and the crown) or the ten channels; மூலவக்கரம் is the root letter, the seed mantra. அத்தியூரர் may be the people of a shrine called Atthiyur or, by the pun of 1211 (அஸ்தி, bone), the dwellers in the body. மாகரம் is unclear.

reading: If you hold within you, as your own nature, the measureless light that is atom and cosmos, that is release; instead you mutter 'muna muna' inside, pressing your fingers together, and bewilder yourselves day after day doing worship to copper.
nuance: செம்பு is the copper of the image. விரலை ஒன்றி is counting japa on the fingers or holding finger seals. அணுவினோடும் அண்டமாய், atom and cosmos, is the Siddhars' pairing of the minute and the whole without the compound அண்டபிண்டம்.

reading: Before one faces the root letter, all is folly covered in folly; what folly is this, fools? If the five elements, which are death, contract into the five, does one join the temple, or join the Beginningless?
nuance: ஆலயோடு is probably ஆலயத்தோடு, the temple, shortened for the metre, though ஆல் could be the banyan; the rhetorical answer is the Beginningless. காலனான அஞ்சுபூதம் makes the elements themselves death; their contraction 'into the five' is the dissolution of the gross body. The text has a stray mark before முடரே.

reading: Being the root as the three-cornered figure and also the end, as one; becoming that square and contracting into a single letter; as the lamp of knowledge that shines within the body, the true square: the truth of the mantra one utters is Sivayam.
nuance: The geometry of 1217 again: the triangle at the root contracts to one letter. மெய்ச்சதுரம் makes the body itself the 'true square', the shrine in which the lamp burns; the one letter is taken by tradition as Om or சி.

reading: You do not cut away the dirt of the mind; like earrings you dip yourselves in the tank. Of old your own four-faced one flew about seeking and could not find him; those who see will find him mingled within you, look.
nuance: Brahma flew as a swan seeking Siva's head and failed. வண்டுலங்கள் and குண்டலங்கள் (beetles? earrings) are chosen for rhyme and their sense is loose; the point is the tank-dip without a cleaned mind.

reading: It is not standing and not sitting, not slender and not thick; not bond and not release, free of all conceiving; not smell and not hearing; in the imperishable sky, how is one to speak of the one that stands without end?
nuance: The negations include release as well as bond, so the verse places the Lord beyond the Saiva pair itself. கேடிலாத வான், the imperishable sky, is where it stands, and the question of how to speak of it is left open.

reading: The reason that the fitting water entered and stood within you; you do not discern the One that two bulls bore as a calf; you do not know the cow that is dying beside you; what guise is this, in which the guru dwells and roams?
nuance: Cipher. 'Two bulls bore a calf' is read by tradition as the two parents or the two breaths producing the one; ஆ, the cow, is the soul (பசு) and perhaps the body dying at hand; the 'fitting water' is the seed. The last line can be the Lord wandering in the guru's guise, or a rebuke to one who wears a guru's guise without knowing these things.

reading: Are you not the five letters that dance in the sky? Are you not the supreme consciousness that stands spread out as sparks? Since our Lord is the one enjoyment of every life, our Lord and I stood as one: Sivayam.
nuance: அம்பரம் is the sky and also echoes அம்பலம், the hall; சிம்புகள், sparks or fragments, is the one consciousness scattered as many. ஏகபோகம், the single enjoyment, is union.

reading: The moon with twin lights is the Supreme that moved and stood; the moon with beautiful light, that none of you know; the Supreme that passed beyond the dark-lit veil; the garland-lit great state is the foot of the one Lord.
nuance: The meaning turns on the moons. ஈரொளிய திங்கள், the twin-lit moon, is taken by tradition as the moon that shines with the sun's light and its own, or as the inner moon at the crown fed by the two channels; காரொளிப் படலம், the dark veil, as maya. None of this is said in the verse.

reading: It cannot be grasped, cannot be softened, cannot be chewed in the mouth; cannot be pushed away, cannot be approached, and so within the mind it cannot be settled, cannot be made clear; the inner fruit of the supreme consciousness cannot be split open: how am I to tell of it?
nuance: A string of negative verbs ending in ஒணாது; குதட்டு, to chew, treats the thing as a fruit that the mouth cannot work on, which the next line names the inner fruit.

reading: By speech, by mind, by the reasoning one judges with, thinking on the look that cannot be looked at, who looks at the look? If the unlookable look comes, and one looks and looks and looks, the unlookable look comes and looks at the look where we are.
nuance: நோக்கு, the gaze, is repeated until the subject and object swap: the seer cannot be seen by the seeing, but when the unseeable sight arrives it looks back at the one looking. The verse completes 1226's eye that cannot see itself.

reading: Within and without, spread through the whole world, standing like oil in sesame, our Lord who moves everything: after he softly came and entered me and performed true tapas, what giver is like this giver, and what colour is his colour?
nuance: It is the Lord who does the tapas, inside the poet, which reverses the usual direction of practice. வண்ணம் என்ன வண்ணம் asks what nature a pervading thing can have.

reading: I have seen no Veda, since I have no burning birth; you became the form in which knowledge stands and became all the worlds; as light within the light, with turiya and the state beyond, the primal root became the first: Sivayam.
nuance: வெம்பிறப்பு இலாமையால்: having no hot birth to escape, the poet has no use for a Veda. துரியம் and அதீதம் are the fourth and the beyond-fourth states, named here as where the Lord stands.

reading: Within the fallen knot, twice a span long, you cherish that city and are born and die and wander in it; if you can renounce and cut off the five who are the boat, seeing the small measure you mingle as crores: Sivayam.
nuance: The opening is coded. A plain reading takes சாண் இரு மடங்கு ... சரிந்த கொண்டை as a woman's body and the 'city' as the womb of desire into which men are born again; another takes it as the crown of the head two spans up, the city of the Lord. தோணியான ஐவர், the five who are the boat, are the senses that carry one and must be left; காணி, a small land measure, grows to crores.

reading: If five crore mantras are held within the five, then, to say it in the heart, within you, in the one letter that is thought; if the five, the four and the three become one and are held within you, the five became a single letter: Sivayam.
nuance: A contraction: all mantras into the five letters, the five with the four- and three-letter forms into one letter, which tradition takes as Om or சி. The holding is 'within you', so the reduction is also an interiorisation.

reading: The letter hidden within the letter, the letter hidden inside that; ... in the wheel ...; like oil hidden in sesame, our Lord hides within every letter and stands: who can see this rightness?
nuance: Line 2 (சிவ்வைருண்டு சம்புளத் திருந்ததும்) is garbled and is left untranslated. The frame is clear: letters nested in letters, and the Lord hidden in each as oil is in the seed, the image of 1259.

title: சிவவாக்கியம்
theme: The five letters as the whole of religion. Sivayam is found inside the body (the root gate, the semen, the letter, the coil), the fire pit, the Rig Veda and the threads on the pot are asked what they are, the dancer of Thillai is the only god, and caste, alms and the distinction of you and I dissolve in the one body whose food, sleep and pleasure are the same for all. The jnani who is filled within and without has nothing left to think.
structure_note: No editorial order; the heading அறிவு நிலை is the editor's. The verses alternate between cipher readings of the body and the mantra (1264 to 1271, 1280 to 1283, 1285, 1286), confessions and assertions about the one Lord (1272 to 1274, 1277, 1279) and attacks on ritual, false gurus, caste and misplaced charity (1276, 1284, 1287, 1288). Most end on the refrain சிவாயமே or a cry of யாவர்காண வல்லரே.
source_issues: 1274 line 4 reads சிந்ததையில், a misprint for சிந்தையில்.
1284 line 4 is 1207's line 4 (பருத்திபட்ட பன்னிரண்டு பாடுதான் படுவரே) with the words reordered; the two verses are near-doublets.
1269 lines 2 and 3 recur almost word for word as 1373 lines 1 and 3.
1285 line 1 துதிக்கவும் may be corrupt; the sense of the line is unclear.
1273 line 3 வேயிலாய (bamboo) is odd for the sky; a variant may be lost.

reading: Since the inner meaning of the Agamas is the undivided root, you, the Supreme, are held without thirst or enjoyment; setting the one foot, within the five letters that make known, it stood as the one enjoyment: Sivayam.
nuance: அகண்டமூலம், the undivided root, is the claim: the Agamas reduce to one thing, and that thing is the five letters. ஏகபாதம் (one foot) and ஏகபோகம் (one enjoyment) are unexplained; tradition would take the foot as the Lord's single step or the one syllable, and the enjoyment as union.

reading: Above the root gate a triple current; the mantra that rose in the middle of the four gates and the eight fingers; the form is one and becomes five; you who stand wandering here, I saw no difference: Sivayam grew.
nuance: The sense turns on body-places and counts. மூலவாசல் is the root centre; முச்சரம் may be the three channels or three currents of breath; எண்விரல் (eight fingers) matches the breath-measures of Tirumular, where the breath goes out twelve fingers and eight return. The plain point is that the one form seen in all these is the five letters.

reading: In the base of the semen, within the letter that whirled; at the base of the letter, you, the primal light, sat; at the base of the letter U, within the five letters that are known, becoming the letter itself it sat: Sivayam.
nuance: சுக்கிலம் is semen, the bodily bindu of the Siddhars. அக்கரம் and உக்கரம் play on அ and உ, two of the three letters of Om, and on அக்கரம் meaning any letter. The verse makes the Lord a letter seated in the body's seed; the mechanics are the cipher's.

reading: Within the coil, the Lord who cut within; the Dancer who destroyed thought in the sphere that was seen; the true substance that shines as the moon blossomed in the sky: the sphere I found and held is nothing but Sivayam.
nuance: குண்டலம் may be the coiled power at the base, as tradition reads it, or simply an ear-ring or circle. மண்டலம் recurs three times with different senses (the sphere seen, the sphere where thought died, the sphere found). The moon in the sky is the yogic moon at the head on a coded reading, and the plain moon on another.

reading: Five around and one chamber, a space beyond speech: you do not discern that it stands as Shakti and Siva. Shakti is your body; the Siva within is the wavering life. Madmen, you have not known the form in which the Lord stood.
nuance: The five are the elements or the senses and the one chamber the body or heart; the verse does not say. The clearest line is the third: the body is Shakti and the life in it is Siva, so the Lord's form is the living person. பித்தர்காள் (madmen) is Sivavakkiyar's usual address to the unknowing.

reading: Within the five letters where the mantra called the root sprouted, within the truth of the knowledge that the four Vedas recite on the tongue, because the one whose throat drank the poison, Hari and Brahma are there, the mantra one cries out is none but Sivayam.
nuance: ஓலம் என்ற மந்திரம் is the mantra cried out, the cry for help; the verse says the only such cry is the five letters. The three gods are placed inside the mantra rather than the mantra addressed to them. Lines 2 and 3 return almost unchanged in 1373.

reading: You who go off driving yourselves away with 'the tattvas': if the tattva is Siva, are you not the Supreme too? After setting the root foot in nada, which is the released life, know and realise the Father within yourselves.
nuance: An argument from identity: if what you call the tattvas is Siva, you who are made of them are the Supreme. முத்திசீவன் நாதம் (nada, the released life) may be in apposition or a sequence; the syntax of line 3 is loose. The verse presses toward the identity of self and Lord that later Siddhars state outright.

reading: Mulan who spoke the three for the three tens and three: jnanis who come and join, my head is at your pure feet; after setting it so, if you can recite so that the nature and the five letters appear, you will see the pure light.
nuance: மூலனே is the vocative of Mulan, which is Tirumular's name; the verse seems to greet the Siddhars' parent, and the numbers (three tens and three, three) may be the thirty-six tattvas less three, the three thousand verses, or a cipher I cannot fix. Line 2's துய்யபாதம் என்தலை puts the speaker's head at the jnanis' feet.

reading: In the heaven above, in the seven weights of worlds, in Nambar's own land, in the island called Naval: there is no god, none, none at all, but our Lord who dances in the hall at Thillai rich with mansions of red gold.
nuance: A surprising verse from a poet who elsewhere mocks temples and images (999): the dancer of Thillai is named as the one god, with a threefold இல்லை. நாவலென்ற தீவு is Jambudvipa, the Indian continent; நம்பர்நாடு, the Lord's own land, may be Siva's heaven.

reading: Becoming five in earth, four in water, three in fire, two in the fine wind and one in the sky, becoming natures that differ: who is able to see the rightness that stood as nothing but you?
nuance: The counts five, four, three, two, one are, as tradition takes them, the qualities of the elements: earth has sound, touch, form, taste and smell, water four, fire three, wind two, space one. வேயிலாய (bamboo, hollow) is read here as the sky; the word is odd. The Lord is the one thing in all five, differently.

reading: One in the ether, two in the moving wind, three in the red flame, four in the fine water, five in the fivefold earth: who is able to see the Lord who sat so, clearing maya in thought?
nuance: The reverse of 1273, from space down to earth. தெளிந்த மாயை can be the maya that has cleared or the Lord cleared of maya, and the two readings differ on whether maya is the obstacle or the display. சிந்ததையில் is a misprint for சிந்தையில்.

reading: If you can hold steady, free of the mind's modifications, the jewel-lamp that has no thought stands eternal; but if the Veda that everyone recites must babble within you, then what you saw in a dream is true: you have become clear, Sivayam.
nuance: The second half can be read as irony, that taking the chanted Veda for the truth is taking a dream for real, or as a promise, that for the cleared mind even the dream is true. The first half is plain: the lamp without thought is the still mind, and it does not go out.

reading: What is the fire pit you set up? What is the Rig Veda? What are the threads wound round the baked clay pot? What is it that clung to the light that sprang from the pillar standing firm, Pattanatha Pattar?
nuance: Four ஏதடா in a row, addressed to a Brahmin priest by name or title (977 has சட்டநாத பட்டரே). The threads on the baked pot are the ritual kumbha. The light sprung from the pillar may be the Narasimha story, or the body as the pillar from which light rises; the challenge is what the rite has to do with that light.

reading: As one leaf of the lotus that sprang up in water stands joined with the water yet is without water, see the quality of the learned Supreme that sprang up in the earth and stands joined with the earth.
nuance: The lotus leaf unwetted by water is the stock image of being in the world without attachment. பண்டிதப் பராபரம், the learned Supreme, may be the Lord as knower in the world or the jnani who has become the Supreme; on the second reading the verse is about the sage's detachment.

reading: What if they sleep, what if they wake, what if awareness goes and withdraws? What if the five fine senses go off in every direction? For jnanis who stand filled as the body fitted within and without, there is nothing at all to think.
nuance: The jnani is not asked to control sleep, waking or the senses; they are made irrelevant. நிறைந்திருந்த (filled, full) is the condition: one who is the whole has no object left for thought. The repeated இலென் (what of it?) carries the tone.

reading: The one letter that reciters recite is one; it is the body called Veda that proclaims this and nothing else; nada is one; the four-faced one, Vishnu and I are one: this is the rightness of my having realised the one that stood with nothing at all.
