nuance: ஓர்எழுத்து, the one letter, is Om on the usual reading, or சி. வேதம் என்ற தேகம் makes the body itself the Veda. The claim 'Brahma, Vishnu and I are one' is the strongest identity statement in the chapter; the syntax of line 2 is uncertain.

reading: In the lotus space that swelled and held the axis, when it lodged and held, it becomes the great hollow of the element; when it moved within the fire, becoming forms and light, taking form upon the horn: that is the form in which the guru stood.
nuance: Cipher throughout. புண்டரீக வெளி is a lotus centre, heart or crown; தாது is element or semen; கொம்பு (horn, branch) is a recurring word in Sivavakkiyam for a channel or the spine (1302, 1309, 1314, 1315, 1317). The guru's form is seen as light formed in the body. I cannot fix the sequence.

reading: If you ask how those of earth and those of heaven came: nada and bindu mingled with earth as light does, the Lord and Shakti and the five elements, giving with earth and destroying; and so the seven are, even today.
nuance: A cosmogony in one breath: nada and bindu, Siva and Shakti, the five elements make and unmake beings. The seven (ஏழும்) may be the seven worlds or seven births. The last line's grammar is loose.

reading: The light that withdraws, the one who stood at the navel, the one at the middle place, the one who climbed up on the walking foot, the two who stand released, with the true and the false: know the Beginning that stood without beginning, standing near.
nuance: A list of body-places and persons (navel, middle, foot) that tradition would map onto centres and breaths; the 'two who stand released' may be the sun and moon, the two channels, or prana and apana. The verse only names positions; who stands in them is not said.

reading: You, the light hidden in the mantra that rose, in the letter that withdraws and in the reckoned sphere; after you have died within the reckoned sphere, within the laughing sphere Sivayam excelled.
nuance: மரித்து, having died, within the sphere is the dying while alive of the yogi, as tradition reads it; the 'laughing sphere' (சிரித்த மண்டலம்) is unexplained, perhaps the state after that death. The three மண்டலம் of 1267 recur.

reading: You did not bow with honour to the true guru who set you right. Madmen who hand out gurus, can you swim across holding that? The madman who hands out a guru and the disciple who came to take one both took the twelve beatings that cotton takes.
nuance: குருக்கொடுக்கும் (giving a guru) is the trade of making gurus, and the verse damns giver and taker alike. பருத்திபட்ட பாடு, what cotton suffers, is a proverb for being beaten; the twelve may be its stages of working. The last line is 1207's last line in a new order.

reading: The open eye praising, the sound of bindu and nada, passing beyond Meru and the cosmic sphere, in the space of Indra's magic where all the letters have perished: that you and I mingled there, of what nature is it, Lord?
nuance: The union is placed beyond Meru (the spine, on the coded reading, or the world-mountain), beyond the cosmic egg, in a space where letters, that is mantra, no longer hold. இந்திரசாலம் is illusion-magic, so the space is itself called a trick. துதிக்கவும் (praising) may be corrupt.

reading: After knowing 'Om namo' as the puppet within, after knowing it as the puppet within the thought of the sun-body: 'there is a you and an I', 'there is good lineage and all that'; realise within yourself that food and food are one.
nuance: பாவை, the puppet or doll, is the life that moves the body (compare 1289's ஆடுகின்ற பாவை). Lines 3 and 4 read best as scorn: once the inner puppet is known, the talk of you and I and good caste (நலங்குலம்) comes to this, that all eat the same food. The sarcastic உண்டடா is the key to the tone; a straight reading is also possible.

reading: When food is given to those who have conquered the five senses, does it rise to the Lord who stands as the good senses? Giving and bestowing on wanderers who have not conquered the five senses and roll in vanity is itself vanity.
nuance: The gift is judged by the recipient's mastery, not his need; line 2 may be a question expecting yes, that food given to the sense-conquered reaches the Lord. வம்பர், the idle or wanton, are the pretended ascetics. The verse makes charity to the unworthy a waste, which the Kural's definition of giving does not.

reading: Are the five senses, the nails that hold us, alike for all or not? Is the heavy suffering of being born from a womb alike or not? Idle men, you prattle; if you realise the truth, food, sleep and pleasure are alike for you and for me.
nuance: The argument against caste from the body: the same senses, the same birth, the same needs. ஆணியான ஐம்புலன்கள் makes the senses nails that pin everyone alike. உமக்கெனக்கும் ஒக்குமே, the same for you and me, puts the poet, presumably low-born, beside the hearer.

title: சிவவாக்கியம்
theme: Sivavakkiyar's cipher at its thickest: silence (மோனம்) in its many kinds, the whirl-point (சுழிமுனை) and the maiden (வாலை) in it, the syllables கூ and கீ, the red flame, the horn and the bow's curve, all naming what the breath finds when it climbs the five letters. Around this run the attacks: millions who call themselves yogis and jnanis, disputants, caste-talkers and dung-pickers, who search all their days and never see.
structure_note: 1289 to 1293 move from the five letters through the breath's ascent to an apophatic Lord; 1294 to 1298 and 1301 are the attacks, built on fourfold repetition (கோடிகோடி, வாதிவாதி, சாதிசாதி, ஆண்மைஆண்மை); 1299, 1300 and 1302 to 1313 are the cipher of the whirl-point, the maiden and the silences, nearly every one ending சிவாயமே or மோனமே. 1290 runs on into 1291 without a verb of its own.
source_issues: 1290 has no finite verb and reads as the first half of a sentence that 1291 completes; the division may be the editor's.
1294 line 1 ஆகிகூவென்று and line 3 பூகமாய் are obscure and may be corrupt.
1299 line 1 மிங்கு and line 4 கியானம் (for ஞானம்) look like dialect spellings or copying errors.
1298 line 2 and 1307 line 3 வாதி is probably ஆதி (the First), as the sense requires.
1293 line 4 சுவன்றிடான் and 1301 line 4 மூனிலாமல் are words I cannot identify.

reading: Jnanis who recite the four Vedas and seek within the five letters where the running five senses are stilled: the three qualities in which the learned gather are within the letters, and Sivayam came to be as the dancing puppet.
nuance: குணங்கள் மூன்று எழுத்துளே can be the three gunas inside the letters or the three letters (அ உ ம) of Om; the two readings are both open. ஆடுகின்ற பாவை, the dancing puppet, is the life or Shakti moving the body, as in 1286.

reading: In the chakra of the worlds, in the space of the lord of the elements, the wind packed within the fire of the swelling lamp; at the gate where the two, sun and moon, move, changing the staff and climbing up, in the sporting space ...
nuance: The stanza has no finite verb and seems to be the first half of a sentence that 1291 finishes. தவன and சோமன், sun and moon, are the right and left channels on the yogic reading tradition gives; தண்டு, the staff, is the spine; the space where the two play is the central channel. The wind packed in fire is the breath held at the root.

reading: Mounting the vaasi gently in the silent five letters, after entering the sphere of light that filled up to the sky; in the measure in which he and I mingled in truth and experienced it, he is and I am not, and it became 'no one'.
nuance: வாசி ஏறி, riding the breath, is the Siddhars' word for breath-practice, and the mantra is its mount. The last line moves in three steps: he exists, I do not, no one at all; the verse does not stop at the first. மவுன அஞ்செழுத்து, the silent five letters, is the mantra said without sound.

reading: In the sword's sheath the sword is held; in the mouth's sheath the mouth is held; in the man's sheath the man is held, see what a rare art; in the foot's sheath the foot is held, and the nature of natures; in the day's sheath the day is held: you and I have seen it.
nuance: Six times உறை (sheath, case) with அடக்கம் (held, contained): everything rests hidden in its own container, and the man in the body is one case among them. வித்தை, the art, is the trick of this containment. What exactly is contained in the day's sheath or the foot's is not said.

reading: He does not praise, does not destroy, does not become a form of maya; he does not slip, does not rage, through all the time of time; he does not droop, does not stir, does not become pure incense; he does not ... and does not speak: the subtle of the subtle of the subtle.
nuance: Twelve negations in a row describe the Lord by what he does not do, and end on சூட்சம் thrice, the word for the hidden subtle thing that runs through this chapter. சுவன்றிடான் is unknown to me and may be corrupt.

reading: The bliss of the letter that was uttered as 'kū': millions say 'yogi, yogi' and never come to know and see it; the monkey mind swelling here and there like a palm, millions upon millions remain saying 'the One, the One'.
nuance: ஆகிகூவென்று is obscure; கூ is one of Sivavakkiyar's cipher syllables (with கீ, ஊ, ஈ), which tradition takes as names for the breath or the mantra's parts. மனக்குரங்கு, the monkey mind, is the common image for restlessness. பூகம் (areca palm) is likely a tall, swaying thing; the line may be corrupt.

reading: Millions upon millions of the world's people, seeking and seeking the First, their days passed in vain; searching and searching, their bodies wrinkled; joining and joining in crowds, millions upon millions stand.
nuance: Four lines of fourfold repetition (கோடி, நாடி, தேடி, கூடி) act out the futility they describe. The fault is not the seeking but the standing in crowds (கூடி நிற்பர்) at the end of it: the search is social and outward.

reading: He is not black, not white; the cause of the Supreme's standing: he does not sit, does not hide, does not become one or two; he is not single, does not die, does not cease, does not perish: the Beginning that one who reached 'kī' and 'kū' in thought has seen and known.
nuance: A second apophatic list after 1293, which ends with a condition: the Beginning is known by whoever holds கீ and கூ in thought. The syllables are cipher; the plain claim is that the Lord has no colour, number or end.

reading: 'Disputant, disputant': he does not know the silt; blowing and blowing, his light dimmed, he babbles; street after street he picks up bull dung; 'caste, caste, caste, caste': he does not see the letter SA.
nuance: Each line is a fourfold word followed by a failure. வண்டல் (silt, sediment) may be what settles when the mind is still; ஊதி (blowing) may be the breath-practice done wrongly or the bellows of the alchemist; the bull dung is gathered for the sacrificial fire. சகாரம், the letter SA, is the first letter of சிவாய on tradition's reading, so the caste-talker misses the mantra's beginning.

reading: Fools who talk 'prowess, prowess, prowess': the form of the First that is to be seen stands through all the time of time, having become a bond that is silence and song, having become shame, at the gate of the sea, here and there and everywhere.
nuance: Almost every word is contested. ஆண்மை is prowess or manliness, and may be the boast of powers; வாதி may be a misprint for ஆதி (the First); நரலை is the sea, and its gate is unexplained, perhaps a body-place. The point that survives is that the boasters miss what is in front of them.

reading: Returning from the letter 'ming' with 'kū', sleeping with the moon, the moon changes and stands; because in the whirl of the body's great point it becomes one, darkness ends, meditation is complete, and the flame-light is seen.
nuance: அங்கமா முனைச்சுழி, the whirl at the body's great point, is the central channel's opening at the brow or crown as tradition reads it; the moon changing is the breath moving from one channel to the other. மிங்கு and கியானம் (for ஞானம்) look like dialect or copying errors. கங்குலற்று, darkness gone, is the one plain phrase.

reading: The secret of the flame rising, the secret of the channel's end, the secret that rose dense and sat as one, the secret that is solid, the secret of the maiden in the wick, the secret the sea raises: the one who has seen and known these is the jnani.
nuance: Six சூட்சம், each a stage of the inner fire; the jnani is defined as the one who has seen them, not the one who recites. திரியின் வாலை, the maiden in the wick, is the flame itself as Shakti; கழிமுனை, the channel's end, is the tip of the central channel on the coded reading.

reading: Dogs who say 'jnani, jnani', millions upon millions; disputants who talk of a rainy day with no sky, millions upon millions; fools who do not see the nature of the selfless ocean say 'we knew it before' without ..., millions upon millions.
nuance: வானிலாத மழைநாள், a rainy day without a sky, is an impossibility, so the disputants argue about nothing. தானிலா சாகரம், the ocean without self, is the state they cannot see. மூனிலாமல் is unknown to me; முன்னறிந்த may be the boast of prior knowledge or of knowing the First.

reading: On the subtle horn, in the flame of the whirl-point, in the pungent flower at the gate where the Broad One dwells, on the shy horn in the temple where he lived, on the island of initiation Sivayam excelled.
nuance: A chain of locatives in cipher. கொம்பு (horn) is the channel or spine; விபுலை, the Broad One, is a name of Shakti or earth; வீ is flower or death; தீட்சையான தீவு, the island of initiation, is the place the guru's initiation opens. The whole is a map of the body that I cannot read with confidence.

reading: The silence that surged, the silence enclosed, the silence that stayed, the silence that wavered, the silence that is the Ganga, the silence that burst forth, the silence that is the moon: these are the silence in which Siva stood.
nuance: Seven kinds of மோனம் and an eighth that is Siva's own. The verse makes silence a thing with states, like the breath, and Siva's silence the sum of them. The Ganga and the moon are both on Siva's head and both yogic figures for the flow at the crown.

reading: In the street of silence, in the maiden of the whirl-point, in the street of drinking, in the red flame that clung, in the corner of knowledge, at the gate where the sea rests, the red flame of 'ōn' rose: Sivayam.
nuance: ஓனம் is probably ஓம்; பானம் (drinking) may be the drinking of nectar or a misprint for பானு (sun). The locatives (street, corner, gate) are the body's ways. The one event is the rising of the red flame.

reading: The maiden who rose, the maiden who wearied, the maiden who sprang up, the maiden who is morning, the maiden who rose esteemed, and the knowledge that stood hidden: boiling up and massing together, they became 'kū' and 'kī'.
nuance: Five வாலை, the young goddess as the power in the body, in five states, resolve into the two cipher syllables. The structure matches 1303's silences; the maiden's states may be stages of the breath, which the morning (காலை) suggests.

reading: 'Kū' and 'kī' becoming silence, the principle of principles; in the spreading of the triple flame that rose in 'mū'; the fullness that fits as honey fits in the flower; breath, breath, breath, breath: it reached the hearts of the loving.
nuance: The honey in the flower is the one clear image: the fullness is in the body as sweetness is in the blossom, neither outside nor added. முச்சுடர், the three flames, are sun, moon and fire on the usual reading. ஆவி, breath or spirit, repeated four times, carries it to the அன்பர்.

reading: Men who talk of prowess: see, as a thing to be seen, the street together with the sun; then you can cut away the dross; the pillar-like subtlety of the First becomes radiance; it is the nada that danced at the gate of shame.
nuance: அருக்கனோடும் வீதி, the street with the sun, is the right channel or the sun-path of the breath on the coded reading. வாதி again for ஆதி. கசடறுக்க, cutting dross, is the metallurgist's word for refining. நாண்மை is unclear, perhaps the day (நாள்) or shame.

reading: In the shade where nada danced at the gate, in the street of the Veda, in the triple flame spread wide, in the 'kī' that is song, in the 'kū' that stirred: I know the refuge, the gate of the elements, the Beginning.
nuance: புகல் அறிவன், I know the refuge, is the only first-person claim in a run of locatives. பூதமான வாயில், the gate of the elements, is the body on the simplest reading; the Beginning is found there.

reading: Breath, breath, breath, breath, the breath of the five horns; dwelling and dwelling on the earth, men; the idle do not know it, though it is here and here; sinners, sinners, men fallen on the ground.
nuance: ஐந்து கொம்பின் ஆவி, the breath of the five horns, is the life moving in the five senses or elements. The fourfold words (ஆவி, மேவி, வாவி, பாவி) rhyme the breath with the men who never notice it. வாவி is a tank or a call; the line is unclear.

reading: The light that sprouted in the seed, in the middle of the bow's curve, shining in the pearl, the lamp that is silence; they do not know the Lord who is like the mass within the conch; the subtlety of the maiden lying and rolling in the wick.
nuance: வில்வளையின் மத்தி, the middle of the bow's curve, is the point between the eyebrows on the usual reading, the bows being the brows (compare 1324, 1325). நத்து is the conch or snail, and the Lord is the body within its shell. வத்து is read as வர்த்தி, the wick, after 1300.

reading: The silence that drains and swells, evening with morning; men who know how evening becomes morning; the red flame sprouting in the angle of the corner; the silence that stayed, having left the lullaby and the sun.
nuance: மாலையோடு காலை, evening and morning, may be the two breaths or the two channels, so that knowing how one turns into the other is knowing the breath's change. தாலை (lullaby) and பானு (sun) in the last line are obscure in context.

reading: The nada that hurried in the street of silence: speed without flaw, what speed is that speed! In the corner of song, in the ripened maiden, the red flame of knowledge walked: Sivayam.
nuance: The one verse of this run that admires rather than maps: வேகம் என்ன வேகமே is an exclamation at the speed of the inner sound. கானம் is song or forest; the maiden is ripe (கனிந்த), as a fruit, before the flame moves.

reading: In the street of the crown's middle, in the kind that remained, the fresh moon spreading and sporting; the lamp that is vermilion, the silence that is meditation, the silence that is bound: Sivayam passed beyond.
nuance: உச்சி மத்தி, the middle of the crown, is the highest centre. ஒழிந்திருந்த சாதி, the kind or caste that remained, is odd; it may mean what is left when all else is gone. செச்சி (vermilion, or the plant of that name) and கச்சி are rhyme words whose sense I cannot fix. கடந்ததே, passed beyond, closes the chapter.

title: சிவவாக்கியம்
theme: The cipher followed as a route through the body: the way of Paychalur, the horn, the bow's curve, the whirl, the crown, where the red flame rises past the moon and nada runs. The chapter's two plain verses (1334, 1335) give the same route in yoga's own words: lotus posture, the root fire roused by the wind, the nine gates sealed, the spine, the six centres, nectar drunk at the moon, the good yogi who reaches the crown and comes down. It closes on where life withdraws, on release and siddhi as a pair, and on the one letter beyond which there is nothing to say.
structure_note: 1314 to 1333 are the cipher, mostly chains of locatives ending in சிவாயமே or மோனமே, with a few attacks on seekers and boasters (1316, 1318) and two stanzas on the breath's birth and death in the body (1328, 1333) that share a formula. 1334 and 1335 are the plain yoga verses, and 1336 to 1338 generalise: the hidden gate, mukti and siddhi, the one letter.
source_issues: 1320 line 4 நாலை is obscure; probably a misprint for வாலை or நாளை.
1325 line 1 மத்தயில் is a misprint for மத்தியில்; line 4 கிந்து is probably விந்து.
1337 line 2 ஆகுமத்தி அப்புலன் is garbled and gives no construable sense.
1327 line 1 ஒன்பதாத்திலே and 1324 line 4 கட்குவைகள் are words I cannot identify and may be corrupt.
1328 and 1333 share a formula (பறந்ததே ... பாய்ச்சலூர் வழியிலே ... இறந்தபோதில்) with the verbs changed; they are variants of one stanza or a deliberate pair.
The new concepts vaasi, suzhumunai, sootcham and vaalai are declared in both ch068 and ch069 so that each file passes check on its own; they should be merged once into concepts.json.

reading: Nada rising like a mill from the five horns; with the bud the flower blossomed, purity attained; when the red flame rose, the teacher slipped loose at once and became the five elements: the silence that flew away.
nuance: ஆலை is a sugar mill or press, so the sound rises as a mill's does. தேசிகன், the teacher or the dweller, may be the guru or the indwelling life; its slipping loose and becoming the five elements reads as the body's dissolution at the flame's rise, or as the self's release. The two readings differ on who leaves.

reading: On the sudden horn, in the nature of the tattvas, in the striking 'ā', in the 'ū' where Hara dwelt, in the grove called 'iduthi', in the triple flame that stood, nada ran saying 'naduthi' and settled well.
nuance: The -துதி words (சடுதி, அடுதி, இடுதி, நடுதி) are rhyme-makers whose sense I cannot fix; the letters ஆ and ஊ are cipher like கூ and கீ. The triple flame is sun, moon and fire on the usual reading. The event is nada running and settling.

reading: The silence of Vishnu who settles, the silence where Hara dwelt, the silence of the elements composed, the silence held, the speed that owns the eyelid, the silence of the shining crown: men who know themselves do not look upon the corpse.
nuance: சடம், the inert thing, is the body; those who know themselves (தமையறிந்த) do not attend to it. இமையும் கொண்ட வேகம், the speed that has the eyelid, is the flash within a blink. The silences are listed as in 1303.

reading: In the way of Paychalur, in the whirl where the Supreme dwelt, at the tip of the ripening horn, on the mountain where the fruit is: what is it that smells so? The expanse rests here; the light that stands pressing, drawing breath from breath.
nuance: பாய்ச்சலூர், the town of leaping or flowing, recurs in 1328 and 1333 and is cipher for the breath's course or the central channel, as tradition takes it, not a place. மூச்சினோடு மூச்சை வாங்கு, drawing breath by breath, is the one plain phrase. The question ஏதடா asks what the fragrance or stench at the fruit is.

reading: A few are those who seek 'light, light' and fail; a few are the men who seek 'the First, the First'; a few are the idle who say 'disputant, disputant'; the whole flame stands as right, right, right, right.
nuance: Three kinds of seeker, each சிலவரே, a few, against the one whole flame (முழுச்சுடர்) that stands as நீதி. The verse puts even the seekers of light among those who fail; the flame is not reached by naming it.

reading: Becoming flame, rising there, the time it became incense; before earth and sky were made one as a trouble, the Beginning that stood spreading became the five elements and stood as prowess, dense through all the cosmos.
nuance: A cosmogony: the Beginning spreads into the five elements and fills every world. ஆண்மை (prowess, manliness) is the odd word, as in 1298 and 1307; here it may mean the sovereign self. இடரதாய், as a trouble, is unexplained.

reading: Men on earth who see and know the light that stood, their eyes cooled, and go about in love: they will see the vision at the upper point of the throat; the withering gone, the ... surging, nada too rejoices.
nuance: கண்டம், the throat, is the fifth centre; the vision is placed above it. காதலுற்று, in love, is the condition of the seers. நாலை in line 4 is obscure, perhaps a misprint for வாலை (the maiden) or நாளை.

reading: The red flame of shining silence, the light that drained, and nada, crying out like tanks in the space emptied of Karuvur; the nature that spread with no fear at all; the lamp that is the Lady, trembling and crying out at the pleasures.
nuance: கருவூர், the embryo town, is the womb or the body's seat (compare 1332); the space emptied of it is beyond birth. நங்கை, the Lady, is Shakti as the lamp. கயங்கள்போலக் கதறி and நயங்கள் கோவென்று are obscure; the stanza's sense beyond its nouns is not recoverable by me.

reading: At the tip of the lamp's crown, in the channel of the sun's light, in the 'kū' where anger changes, in the fire that stood boiling, the subtlety settled in the corner of heat, and the release that is a curse: cut off, it shines.
nuance: திவாகரம் is the sun's light. சாபமான மோட்சம், release that is a curse, is the hard phrase: either release bound up with the curse of birth, or release that is itself a curse to one who wants more, or two items in the list, curse and release. தடிந்து, cut off, may govern either.

reading: The teacher whirled in the maiden of the triple point; in the maiden with a guise, in the corner where the vast dwelt, at the gate filled with the beloved moonrise, the silence that spread stood fanning and fanning.
nuance: திரிமுனை, the triple point, is where the three channels meet on tradition's reading. சந்திரோதயம், moonrise, is the yogic moon at the head. தேசிகன் again may be the guru or the indwelling self; வேசம், guise, is what the maiden puts on.

reading: Nandi who stood wearied on the silence of the inner lotus; becoming 'kī' with a hiccup in the middle of the bow's curve; the red flame that hurried as if thorns were packed in it; the vision that stood driving on like heaps of liquor.
nuance: Nandi is Siva, as in Tirumular. விக்கல், the hiccup, may be the catch of the held breath. The similes of thorns and heaps of liquor are not ones I can place; கட்குவைகள் may be corrupt. The bow's curve is the brow.

reading: From the navel by the way of the whirl to the middle of the crown, the red flame that leapt past the moon's light and the organs; becoming the bond in the bow's curve, the magic of the five elements; standing like a drop in 'kī', it said 'kīch mūch'.
nuance: The clearest route in the chapter: navel, whirl, crown. கரணம், the organs, are the inner instruments the flame passes. கிந்து is probably விந்து (bindu). கீச்சுமூச்சு is onomatopoeia for a squeak and a breath, with மூச்சு the breath itself; the verse ends in the body's own noise.

reading: With the breath called 'secchai', the letters SI and VA stood fresh: the nature of the supreme space. In the 'ū' of desire, in the 'ī' that rose there, in the angle of the crown Sivayam rose.
nuance: சிகாரமும் வகாரமும் are the letters சி and வ, the first two of சிவாய, so the five letters are built from the breath. செச்சை is vermilion or a flower-name and here names a breath. ஊ and ஈ join the cipher syllables; பச்சை, green or fresh, is the state of the letters.

reading: In the six-cornered angle, in the ninefold that is set, so that the Lady's navel is discerned saying 'thāru'; the silence the five held there saying 'kūru'; what stood holding a vulture spread: Sivayam.
nuance: ஆறுமூலைக் கோணம், the six-cornered figure, is the hexagram of the yantras or the six centres; ஒன்பதாத்து is obscure, perhaps the nine gates. நாவி is navel or musk. பாறு is a vulture or spreading; the last line is not recoverable by me.

reading: It flew, when it was milked, by the way of Paychalur: what was born was breath, not female nor male. Did it renounce, did it excel, did it become pure and lofty? Not at the moment of death: Sivayam shines then too.
nuance: The plain claim in line 2 is that what is born in the body's way is the breath, which has no sex. கறந்தபோது, when milked, is odd; it may be the drawing of the breath. The last line can be 'not only then' or 'not then but now'; the formula returns in 1333 with துறந்தபோது for கறந்தபோது.

reading: In the space where grace was, in the darkness where the sun stood, in the whirl where the substance was, in the way that rose turning over, in the phase where clarity was, in the net where one stood bewildered: from the way where the guru was, it became 'ū' and 'ī'.
nuance: Six locatives, each a quality placed in a space (grace, darkness, substance, clarity, bewilderment), then the guru's way as the source of the two syllables. The sun standing in darkness is the hidden light of the body on the coded reading. கலை is phase or art.

reading: The Beginning settled in the one letter: with song and on this earth there is no seeing and knowing it; it became itself and itself; in the evening and morning that were composed it was like millet and its change: Sivayam.
nuance: ஓர் எழுத்து, the one letter, is Om on the usual reading. தானும் தானும் ஆனதே, it became itself and itself, is identity without a second. ஏனலோடு மாறுபோல், like millet and its exchange, is unexplained; it may be the field's change from seed to crop or a barter image.

reading: The flood the river took, the god established there, the rain the thicket took, the distance that shone, the silence that took pride, the shining inner lotus: in the contrary 'ū' it died away: Sivayam.
nuance: The list ends with a death (மடிந்ததே) rather than a rising, as if the inner lotus and its silence are themselves passed. மாறுகொண்ட ஊ, the ū that turned contrary, may be the breath reversed. The images of flood, rain and distance are not ones tradition explains for this verse.

reading: In the angle seen at the gate, the five shining ones dwelling; seeing the shadow and leaning on it, abiding as the head-king; the bee of the body having seen it, having gone there to Karuvur, having gone saying 'it will leap': it flew: Sivayam.
nuance: காயவண்டு, the bee of the body, is the life entering a body, and கருவூர், the embryo town, the womb: the stanza tells the soul's descent into birth, seeing a shadow, leaning on it, ruling as head, then flying off. The five who dwell are the elements or senses. The reading of the whole as birth is mine; the words are a sequence of participles.

reading: It flew, when it renounced, by the way of Paychalur; it forgot, settled in the hand of the warriors who seized it; it was born; at the moment of death, in the 'kī' without harm, the silence that excelled became clear: Sivayam.
nuance: The formula of 1328 with the verbs changed: flew, forgot, was born, and at death the silence cleared. வாணர், the warriors or the Vanar, who seize may be the senses or Death's men; பீடிடாமல், without harm or without seat, is unclear. The pair of stanzas tells the breath's whole career from entry to exit.

reading: Seating the body in the lotus posture, rousing the fire at the root with the wind, sealing the gates, five and four, with the final mudra, it goes by the root vina-staff past the lotus temple and through the root nadi.
nuance: The one verse in these chapters in yoga's open vocabulary. மூல அனல் is the root fire, kundalini in later usage, raised by மாருதம், the breath; the nine gates (five and four) are the body's openings, closed by mudra; வீணாதண்டு, the vina's staff, is the spine; முளரி ஆலயம், the lotus temple, is the heart or a centre passed on the way. What goes is the breath or the fire; the subject is unstated.

reading: Beginning at the feet and up to the crown, crossing the six great grounds, our primal light that passed beyond the space beyond; drinking nectar at the eye of the lord of the stars, in the joy of true knowledge, the yogi who strikes the crown and comes down is the good yogi.
nuance: ஆறுமா நிலம், the six great grounds, are the six centres; உடுபதி, the lord of the stars, is the moon, whose nectar the yogi drinks at the head, as in Tirumular. இறங்குகின்ற, coming down, is the mark of the good yogi: he reaches the crown and returns, rather than staying.

reading: 'Is it inside or outside, the place where life withdraws? You must come slowly, draw near and ask', you say. When what is and what is born coincide, that is nada; open the thief's gate and see, men.
nuance: The questioners want the place of life's withdrawal located and taught; the answer refuses inside and outside and gives a condition instead, the coincidence of being and birth (உள்ளதும் பிறப்பதும்), which is nada. கள்ளவாசல், the thief's gate, is the hidden door, which tradition takes as the opening of the central channel.

reading: Release and siddhi are a pair; the Murti who embraces; the five senses that arose otherwise become ... in that sense; Father, eternal one, poison-throated one: with love, every day, recite and know and realise him within the heart.
nuance: முத்தி சித்தி தொந்தமாம், release and attainment are joined, is the claim of the opening: the Siddhar's powers and his liberation come together. Line 2 (ஆகுமத்தி அப்புலன்) is garbled. The close is plain devotion: daily recitation with love, and inner knowing.

reading: Becoming three and two and five, the gods strove and rose; becoming three and two as five, all the worlds strove; the mother who bore and the father being the nada that moves: there is nothing to say beyond the one letter that appears.
nuance: மூன்றிரண்டும் ஐந்துமாய், three and two making five, may be the five letters, the five elements or three gunas with two more; the verse gives only the counts. Mother and father as nada make sound the parent of gods and worlds; the one letter that appears is Om on the usual reading, and the last line ends the argument: beyond it nothing is sayable.

title: சிவவாக்கியம்
theme: Sivavakkiyar reads the five-letter mantra (சிவாயம், அஞ்செழுத்து) as a thing inside the body and the mind rather than a formula learned from books: it is the letters A and U blossoming, the fire in the triangle, the serpent's mouth, the embryo in the womb. Around this run the refrains 'isn't it one?' (ஒன்றலோ) and 'it became Sivayam' (சிவாயமே): temple, tank, fire, air, senses and worlds are all one thing, and the body that knows this is itself the vision. The chapter closes by denying that letters, soul, elements, senses and scriptures are beginningless; only the truth mingled with all of them is.
structure_note: The verses alternate between coded accounts of the five letters and the inner fire (1339, 1341, 1343 to 1346, 1348, 1349, 1352 to 1355, 1359 to 1362) and plain-spoken rebukes and questions to the confused (1340, 1342, 1347, 1350, 1351, 1356 to 1358, 1360, 1363). Many verses end on the refrain சிவாயமே; 1343 and 1344 share a last line, as do the pairs 1347/1357/1358 with the question ஒன்றலோ.
source_issues: 1350 line 1 (விட்டடி விரைத்ததோ) and 1355 line 3 (மட்சரத்தில் உட்கரம்) are obscure and may be corrupt.
1343 and 1344 share their last line (கருத்தினின்று உதித்ததே கபாலம் ஏந்தும் நாதனே); this looks deliberate, but one may have borrowed it from the other.

reading: Melting space, the five letters and the rhythm of bindu and nada, melting the drop and mixing in ghee until everything is pure, and knowing the two both in space and in that act, Sivayam became clear by the nature that passes beyond space.
nuance: The verse is an alchemical figure for an inner event: உருக்கி (melting) is said of space and of தளி, which can be a shrine or a drop, and நெய் (ghee) suggests an oblation. இருவர் (the two) is traditionally Siva and Shakti, or the sun and moon of the yogic body. What the plain sense of the melting is remains open.

reading: You people confused by the mantras you have learned, will you recite them when you are dead? The mantras are within you, and so are you who valued them; the mantra is the five letters of the mind.
nuance: The second line is the hinge: a mantra held in memory dies with the one who learned it. மனத்தின் ஐந்து எழுத்து relocates the pancakshara from speech to the mind, which the rest of the chapter develops.

reading: Beyond the three regions, in the work of the three-eyed one, within the supreme awareness the spring is Sivayam, the five letters; after the supreme self arose and the pillar became everywhere, this side draws in and everything became the linga.
nuance: முப்புறம் (three regions) may be the three worlds or the three cities Siva burned; தாணு (the pillar) is a name of Siva and, in yogic reading, the spine. உற்புனம் is obscure, perhaps a spring. The last line turns the installed linga into the whole, which pairs with the chapter's mockery of temple stone.

reading: Is the dancing jiva the five elements, the light that joined them, or the root that frolics? Is it what stood and saw the land, or the learning the tongue acquired? Having seen the house of release and burst open, it became the open space.
nuance: The questions deny each candidate: the soul is not the elements, nor the light, nor what it has seen, nor what it has learned. வெட்டவெளி (bare open space) is the Siddhars' word for the final state, and வீடு கண்டு puts seeing release before becoming it.

reading: When the form took shape, the truth that stood level with the jiva, and in anything that has rightness, is Sivayam, the five letters; after settling, pressing and subsiding into single enjoyment, the Lord who carries the skull arose from the thought.
nuance: கருத்து is thought or intention, but beside கரு (womb) in the next verse it may also mean the womb; the Lord then 'arises from the womb' with each birth, or 'arises in the thought' of the one absorbed. ஏகபோகம் (single enjoyment) is read as union. The last line is shared with 1344.

reading: When conceived and risen it became the lotus seat; when conceived and risen it became the causes; when conceived and risen it became two eyes to see; and from the thought arose the Lord who carries the skull.
nuance: கருத்தரித்து is literally 'holding the embryo', so the verse follows the embryo as it becomes the lotus seat (the base centre, in yogic reading), the causal faculties and the eyes. The Lord then arises in the womb, or in the thought; see 1343. The verse makes embryology and theology one story.

reading: The fire that is in the triangle, in the six, two and eight; the jiva that is the five letters, blossoming with the letter A set in it; the truth that is the light and the beginningless truth: becoming that and becoming itself, it will hide as void.
nuance: மூன்றுகோணம் (triangle) is traditionally the base centre where the fire sleeps, and the numbers are read as petals or centres; none of this is in the text. அவலமாய் can mean 'as void' or 'in distress', and the verb மறைந்திடும் (hides, vanishes) leaves open whether the hiding is the Lord's or the soul's.

reading: Our Lord who was born and rose, in the open space of the holy stage, became the four directions through the mouth of the hanging serpent; after it passed the three cities as three and three rings, the sound of that letter, born and risen, stood everywhere.
nuance: நான்ற பாம்பு (the hanging serpent) is the coiled power in yogic reading, and திருவரங்கம் is both Srirangam and 'holy stage'. மூன்றுமூன்று வளையம் (rings in threes) and அவ்வின் ஓசை (the sound of the letter A, or 'that sound') are coded; the plain sense is that one sound fills everything.

reading: Isn't it one everywhere? Aren't the fourteen worlds one, here and there one, the beginningless one, the standing things and what bears them one? Sivayam arose in your share and ours alike.
nuance: ஒன்றலோ (isn't it one?) is the refrain of 1357 and 1358 too. உங்கள் எங்கள் பங்கினில் (in your share and ours) is a jab at the caste and sect divisions that the poet attacks elsewhere: the same thing arose in both.

reading: The light that dances in the sky is the root of the fire; sky and self blossomed with the fierce one set in them; setting the body in the pit of the sky and melting it, Sivayam sat with the First in the sky.
nuance: அம்பரம் is space and also the cloth, and the hall of the dance is heard behind ஆடும் சோதி. அகோரம் (Aghora, the fierce face of Siva) returns in 1355 as something 'set' before blossoming. அம்பரக் குழி (the pit of space) is read by tradition as the space in the crown.

reading: The unfading flower blossomed, with the bee's hum on the tongue; running, taking form, it blossomed as the letter U; dancing and dancing until the body was caught within and passed, we walk about joined: that is the form in which the guru dwelt.
nuance: வாடிலாத பூ (the unfading flower) is the inner lotus, and the bee's hum on the tongue is the mantra as sound. உகாரம் is the U of Om. The last line makes the guru's state the end of the whole process rather than its beginning.

reading: Did it sprout from the root that was let go, or did it stand melting that root? Did the jiva that reached out see the fourteen worlds? Is it the light of Sadasiva standing as a flat form? Will those who know the round house become the gods of the sky?
nuance: விட்டடி விரைத்ததோ is obscure and may be corrupt. வட்டவீடு (the round house) recurs in 1351; tradition takes it as the circle of space in the head or the sphere of the whole, and the questions may be rhetorical denials or genuine.

reading: The light the gods fill is in the human embryo, and all the gods of heaven come and settle inside it; after knowing the round house of sky and earth, they became the rubies that fill the whole heaven.
nuance: The claim is that the gods are inside the human embryo, not above it. வட்டவீடு, the round house, carries over from 1350; here it spans heaven and earth, so the body as cosmos is in view. Who 'became the rubies' is unclear: the knowers or the gods.

reading: If, holding the breath to twelve and reaching the five colours, one stays standing within the space and settles in another place, the jiva moves in the place that is the head; those who thought on this and searched it out became the supreme Brahman.
nuance: பன்னிரண்டு கால் நிறுத்தி is read as holding the breath (கால், wind) to a measure of twelve, the span the breath travels in yogic texts; it could also be twelve feet or supports. பஞ்சவண்ணம் (five colours) is the elements, or the coloured lights seen in meditation. சென்னி (the head) is the one plain body-place.

reading: Seeing the summit with the eyes shut, where did one see the truth? If the human mingles inside the upper storey, even the door of spittle becomes single enjoyment; the green Mal and the Lord are Sivayam that spread beyond.
nuance: மச்சு மாளிகை (the upper storey of the mansion) is read as the head, and எச்சிலான வாசல் (the spittle door) as the mouth; so the verse says the mouth itself becomes union when the mind is in the crown. பச்சை மால் (green or dark Vishnu) and ஈசன் being one Sivayam repeats the poet's refusal of sect.

reading: Set in the mouth, in the sound of the letters of the good hum; the temple set and the tank dried there in the branch; the body made by inquiry, the jiva set from no beginning and the fire the wind let loose: all of it grew as Sivayam.
nuance: நல்லுரிசை (the good hum, or 'good rishi') is unclear, and கொம்பிலே உலர்ந்ததும் (dried in the branch, or horn) is obscure; it may picture the inner tank drying up as the fire rises. The verse gathers mantra, body, soul and breath into one growth.

reading: Uttering the letter as the root of the beginningless fire, opening the letter too and blossoming with the fierce one set in it, after passing so that the inner hand in the earth-row was caught, Sivayam sat with the First in the letter.
nuance: அட்சரம் (the letter) appears in every line, and the verse is a cipher for how the uttered letter becomes the inner fire. மட்சரத்தில் உட்கரம் is obscure; மட்சரம் may be a corrupt form. அகோரமிட்டு அலர்ந்ததும் repeats 1348.

reading: You are confused in mind by temples and tanks, by gurus taken on their badges, and by the rest; if you know and realise the Cowherd and Hara, it is like sitting down with your mother and your father.
nuance: குறியினிற் குருக்களாய் is gurus known by their marks, the outward signs rather than knowledge. மாயிலும் மடியிலும் is unclear (peacock and lap? or some other pair of objects of confusion). ஆயன் (the cowherd) is Vishnu beside Hara, both to be known as one; the mother-and-father image returns in 1384.

reading: Isn't the temple one everywhere, and the tanks and their waters one? Aren't fire and air one, and isn't Siva there one too? Isn't the jiva that became everything and abides one? Those who know this body become the vision itself.
nuance: The list moves from temple and tank through the elements to Siva and the soul, all answered by the same ஒன்றலோ. காயம் ஈது அறிந்த பேர்கள் (those who know this body) says where the oneness is known: not in the many temples but in the one body.

reading: Ears, eyes, nose and mouth: isn't what mixed them one? What was raised with light and the five pleasures: aren't they one? Didn't the recited scriptures arise from one? Those who know the house of nada become Lords.
nuance: The senses, their pleasures and the sastras are traced to one source. நாதவீடு (the house of sound) is the inner place of nada, and நாதர் (Lords, masters) answers it with a pun: those who know the house of nada are nathar.

reading: The letter mingled within the letter that rose as A, and the mantra that rose as Sa, were in the abode of Sambhu; you people confused by the maya that rose as Ma, what rose as U took form together with A: that is the truth.
nuance: Each line opens with a letter: அவ், சவ், மவ், உவ். Tradition reads ம as the letter of malam and maya (so மவ்வுதித்த மாய்கை), சி or ச as Siva, and அ and உ as the two that make Om. சம்புளத்து is unclear, perhaps 'in Sambhu's place'. The verse gives the letters, not their keys.

reading: In the letter called A, did the other letters end? Did the letter A arise from the letter A? Did U and A stand well joined? You jnanis free of change, you must expound this at length.
nuance: The questions concern the parts of Om and whether A contains, generates or joins the rest; the verse does not answer them and asks the jnanis to. விகாரமற்ற (without change) marks the jnani as one past the changes the letters stand for.

reading: Shakti is your body; the wavering jiva within it is Siva. Madmen, there is nothing more to babble beyond this. Five purities, one hall, a space beyond words; to become Shakti and Siva and be cool is the truth.
nuance: The first line is the plainest statement in the chapter of the body-as-Shakti doctrine: the body is her, the soul is him. சுத்தி ஐந்து கூடம் ஒன்று (five purities, one hall) is coded, perhaps the five elements purified in the one body. தண்மை (coolness) names the end as calm rather than power.

reading: In the channel of the seed, in the embryo of blood, on the mound that sprouted at the three-cornered gate, within the true square, shining in the true body as the lamp of knowledge, the mantra uttered is Om Nama Sivaya.
nuance: சுக்கிலம் and சுரோணிதம் are the male and female seeds in Siddha medicine, so the verse places the mantra in conception itself. முச்சதுர வாசல் and மெய்ச்சதுரம் (the three-cornered gate, the true square) are body-places tradition maps onto the base centre; the text does not say which.

reading: The letters are not beginningless; the soul is not beginningless; the elements that entered and the senses are not beginningless; the worthy books and the scriptures are not beginningless; the truth that stands level and mingled with all of them is the beginningless.
nuance: ஆத்துமம் அனாதி அல்ல denies the soul a beginningless existence, which sets the verse against Saiva Siddhanta, where soul, Lord and bond are all eternal. Read with 1361, the soul is Siva within and so has no separate eternity; the verse may also simply rank everything named below the one truth.

title: சிவவாக்கியம்
theme: The Lord is within like oil in a sesame seed, and the chapter attacks every outward route to him: Vedas recited in a crowd, the Lord looked for in a palm leaf, ash smeared on a body that has been born and died in every birth, lamps and smeared floors, and the three stones that are broken, trodden and worshipped. Against these it sets the hall (அம்பலம்) that is A, U, M, the beginningless and the dance, the one letter in which the body and the red flame arose, the mother-father who is none but oneself, and the tongue pressed back along the knowledge channel.
structure_note: Questions to the master and to the jnanis (1364, 1366) open the chapter; rebukes to the confused (1365, 1367 to 1369, 1372, 1374, 1376, 1380, 1382, 1386, 1388) alternate with litanies on the hall (1370, 1377, 1378), a hymn of 'you are' (1379), and coded verses on the letters and the yogic body (1371, 1381, 1383, 1385, 1387).
source_issues: 1378 line 4: ஒனிந்ததே is not a word; ஒளிந்ததே or ஒடுங்கியதே is likely.
1383 line 4: அஞ்செழித்தும் for அஞ்செழுத்தும்.
1387 line 1 (காக்கை மூக்கை ஆமையார் எடுத்துரைத்த காரணம்) is corrupt; 1180 (sivavakkiyam:216) has the same verse with the first line ஆக்கைமூப்பது இல்லையே, and the two are a doubled unit.
The gloss attached to 1382 (அந்த - முடிவு) belongs to 1383, where அந்தமில்லை occurs; 1382 has no அந்த.
1365 (சடக்கிலாறு வேதமும்) and 1376 (ப்ரவாதபூசை ஏய்த்தியே) have obscure phrases that may be corrupt.

reading: What is it that stood soft, and what, standing apart, touched? Our noble one, you must tell us truly. The one thing that stood as female, standing apart and touching: when that is told truly, release has mingled within.
nuance: The question is put to a teacher (உத்தமா). பெண்மையாக நின்றது ஒன்று (the one that stood as female) is taken as Shakti, who is apart from the soul yet touches it; விட்டுநின்று தொட்டது could also describe the breath or the mind. Release is said to come with the true telling, not with a practice.

reading: If you restrain it, will the universe be held within the five letters? You who know as truth the body taken up by the inner mystery: because you have not recited the six Vedas so as to hold them, does the carrion dog speak in many different ways?
nuance: The syntax does not resolve. உடக்கு is glossed as the inner secret; சடக்கிலாறு வேதம் may be 'six Vedas' or a corrupt phrase; விடக்கு நாய் (a dog after carrion) is an insult for the sectarian who argues. The first line can be read as a sneer or as a real claim that the cosmos is in the five letters.

reading: How the true chakra became the means, how the cool body took on a form, and how it grew white and ripened in water: true jnanis, you must explain this at length.
nuance: The poet asks rather than tells. வெண்மையாகி நீரலே விளைந்து (grown white in water) is taken by tradition as the seed, bindu, from which the body forms, or as the moon's nectar; the verse leaves it as a question. The address விரிந்துரைக்க வேணுமே repeats 1360.

reading: Like oil in a sesame seed our Lord is everywhere and within you, yet you fools swing to and fro; if you can straighten the crooked tail of a thieving dog, you can see the light that stands as the giver in its truth.
nuance: The dog's tail that cannot be straightened is proverbial for the mind that will not be corrected, so the condition is nearly impossible, or a dare: fix the mind and the light is seen. ஊசலாடும் (swinging like a swing) pictures the wavering between outer routes.

reading: You say 'the Pillar is there' in the books you desire, with the knowledge you wanted; you neither hold him nor forget him. The one Pillar is the root channel, the channel within you; apart from seeing him there, everything else is like the confusion of a dream.
nuance: தாணு (the pillar, a name of Siva) is placed in the மூலநாடி, the root channel of yogic anatomy, so the verse makes book-knowledge of God a dream and locates him in the body's channel. தரிக்கிலீர் மறக்கிலீர் (you neither hold nor forget) catches the half-belief of the learned.

reading: You argue in words and waver in your minds, you mutes, like a nazhi measure that has no quarter-measure inside it; four quarter-measures make one nazhi, within you. You argue in words, but the Lord abides within the mind.
nuance: உழக்கு is a quarter of a நாழி, so the image is of a measure that forgets it is made of its parts: the disputants forget that what they argue over is already measured out within. The exact point of the arithmetic is not certain, and தவக்கிறீர் is an unusual form.

reading: A is the hall; the beginningless is the hall; U is the hall; the truth is the hall; M is the hall; form is the hall; Si is the hall: Sivayam has become clear.
nuance: அம்பலம் is the hall of the dance at Chidambaram, repeated eight times until it means the whole. The letters are A, U, M of Om and Si of Siva, so the hall is the mantra; 1377 and 1378 continue the litany with the dance's terrible and wrathful faces and with gold and eternity.

reading: The chakra flew and ran, with a board upon the chakra; like the oil pressed in the mill, air and fire mingled with light in the upper place, and the aeons were thrown into confusion; when it entered the entrance, how did it go?
nuance: The verse is a cipher and ends in a question. சக்கரம் may be the drawn diagram, a wheel, or a centre of the body; the oil-mill repeats the sesame image of 1367; சிங்குவாயு and உக்கிலே are obscure. The question போனவாறது எங்ஙனே (how did it go?) is asked again of the Lord's 'parting' in 1382.

reading: You who count the breast that grew and rose as maya, examine in truth within yourself the body of the jiva that holds grace; if you listen to the words of the great who have gained shining knowledge, the right thought will enter your stainless heart.
nuance: The first line may rebuke those who dismiss the body (or woman) as illusion, in keeping with the poet's praise of the body as Shakti; or கொங்கை may be a figure for the swelling of pride or desire. அருள்கொள் சீவர் ஆர் உடம்பு is loose: 'the body of the grace-bearing souls'.

reading: Do you know the one knowledge that the four Vedas recite? As the knowledge-awakening uttered through the four watches of the night, the poison-throated one, Ayan and Mal, thought on deeply, settled in the heart as Sivayam.
nuance: The one knowledge of the Vedas is Sivayam dwelling in the heart; the three gods are named as its forms, not its rivals. நாலு சாமம் (four watches) matches the four Vedas and may hint at recitation through the night.

reading: What you call 'around' you do not place at the end of scripture; where did it sit, dancing day and night? For devotees ripe in love, the one in the Supreme is a void. Madmen, how can you think this out and speak of it?
nuance: சுற்றும் (around, surrounding) and அத்தம் நித்தம் are unclear; the first line may say that the sectarians never reach the Vedanta where the circling ends. பாழ் (void) is the Siddhars' word for what remains when the Supreme is reached, and the verse denies that it can be reasoned about.

reading: However he stands to be made clear, however they say the Lord graciously rose to his friends, so does the primal supreme self dwell in grace; and the three impurities are cut off like an elephant that a lion has come upon.
nuance: The first two lines are loose, with எங்ஙனே (however) three times picking up the last word of 1371. The plain claim is in the last line: the three malas (anava, karma, maya in Siddhanta) are destroyed by the approach of the Supreme, as a lion kills an elephant.

reading: Within the house, sweeping and smearing the floor, setting out many lamps and performing a puja that deceives; doing good tapas, seeking the feet of the one Lord: the right conduct that is learned, find it within yourselves.
nuance: அற்றவுள் அகம் is unclear: the inner house of the one who has let go, or simply the house. ப்ரவாதபூசை ஏய்த்தியே is obscure, perhaps a puja of mere talk (பிரவாதம்) that cheats. சரிதை is சரியை, the path of outer service; the verse moves it inward.

reading: What stood watching is the hall, the hall where the Supreme dances; what stood as dance is the hall, the terrible is the hall; the word is the hall, fire is the hall, wrath is the hall: Sivayam has become clear.
nuance: The litany of 1370 continues, now with the dance's fierce aspects: கோரம் (the terrible), வன்னி (fire), சீற்றம் (wrath). The hall is not only Chidambaram but every act and mood of the Lord.

reading: Going on from place to place, the fine golden hall; the beginningless hall that stood then and stands now; the hall that is the end and endures for ever; standing joined and joined within, Sivayam was hidden there.
nuance: The hall is found in every place walked to, and is beginningless and final at once. ஒனிந்ததே in the last line is not a word; ஒளிந்ததே (was hidden) or ஒடுங்கியதே (subsided) fit the metre and sense.

reading: You are the father, you are dharma, you are every deity; you are the flood and you are clarity, you yourself are siddhi and mukti; you are bindu and you are the yield, you are the Veda above it all; you are my father, you are the Lord, the Isan who took me as his own.
nuance: A hymn of நீ (you) in a chapter of rebukes. சிந்து may be the sea or river, or a drop; விந்து and விளைவு (bindu and its yield) make the Lord both seed and harvest. என்னை ஆண்ட (who ruled me) is the language of the Nayanmars.

reading: Poor ones, born and dead and perished in every birth, and born again in this one: what is this ash you smear? If, along with the water, you can cut off the impurity and remove desire, you can see clearly in the bell-sound of nada.
nuance: அப்பு is glossed as water, so the ash and the bath are taken together as the outward cleansings, and the verse asks for the cutting of malam and desire instead; another reading makes அப்புடன் மலம் the body's own water and filth. செப்பு நாத ஓசை (the sound of a copper bell, or 'the nada sound I speak of') is the inner sound.

reading: The eightfold yoga and the moving nada, and within the eight letters the U and the A, blossoming apart, the mantra went up through the staff of the veena and settled in the eight letters as Sivayam.
nuance: வீணாதண்டு (the veena's staff) is the spine in yogic reading, so the mantra rises through it. எட்டு அக்கரம் (the eight letters) is not explained; it may be ஓம் நம சிவாய counted as eight, or the eight syllables of a longer formula. The eight of yoga and the eight letters are set side by side without a key.

reading: You fools who babble 'Lord, Lord': how did our Lord ever part from the Lord? As Lord and as Lord and as the great world itself, your body, you madmen, is what sprouted from the Lord.
nuance: The repeated பிரான் makes the point by sound: there is no second Lord to call to, and no distance to cross. The body is not what hides him but what grew out of him, which is the chapter's answer to ash, Vedas and stones.

reading: No beginning, no end, no four Vedas that came to be; no light, no word, a pure space beyond speech; no justice, no love, nothing that can be fixed; once the First is seen, even the five letters are not.
nuance: அஞ்செழித்தும் is a corruption of அஞ்செழுத்தும். The verse strips away even what the chapter elsewhere uses, the five letters, light and the Vedas, and leaves தூவெளி, the pure expanse, which in Tirumular too is the final state. 1340 located the mantra in the mind; here even that is left behind.

reading: Mother-Father: when the Father sat as you, you did not know it; you who became Mother-Father are the bond of the First. Since there is no one but you as Mother-Father, there is no one, no one at all, but you.
nuance: அம்மையப்பன் (Mother-Father) is the one Lord as both, and the verse says the hearer is that one. ஆதியான் பாசமே in line 2 is unclear: 'you are the First's bond', or 'that is the First's bond, that you do not know it'. The doubled இல்லை of the last line is the poet's emphasis.

reading: In the first one letter the red flame sprouted; in that one letter the body was born and formed; in that one letter it stood as one; know and realise that one letter too.
nuance: ஓர் எழுத்து (one letter) is traditionally Om, or the single letter of Siva; the verse does not name it. Flame, body and unity all come from it, and the last line asks for the letter to be known, not recited.

reading: Gathering in a crowd you recite the Veda together; in which letter does the Lord sit inside the palm leaf? Set your gaze and seek within the four and the three; the Mother dances inside the dancing-place: that is the truth, by her oath.
nuance: ஏட்டகத்துள் ஈசன் (the Lord inside the palm leaf) is the chapter's sharpest line against book-learning. நாலுமூன்று (four and three) is coded: seven, as the centres or the worlds, or twelve as their product. ஆட்டகம் is glossed as the place of the dance of bliss, and அம்மை ஆணை is either 'by the Mother's oath' or 'the Mother's rule'.

reading: For the reason the ancients set out, press the tongue, bend it inward and go up through the channel of knowledge; if, watching with longing, you praise the two letters of the mantra, every direction you look becomes the supreme Brahman.
nuance: The tongue bent back and up is the khechari seal of the yoga texts. The first line (காக்கை மூக்கை ஆமையார்) is corrupt: 1180 opens the same formula with ஆக்கை மூப்பது இல்லையே, 'the body does not age', which gives the verse its point. இரண்டெழுத்து (two letters) is read as சிவ or as அ and உ.

reading: You break a ringing stone in two; the stone set in the doorway you tread on until it is worn smooth; on the stone kept for puja you offer flowers and water. Tell me, which stone is the one the Lord is pleased with?
nuance: Three stones from the same quarry: one broken, one a doorstep, one a god. The question has no answer the worshipper can give, which is the point; 1458 asks the same of the planted stone that is circled with flowers and mutterings while the Lord is within.

title: சிவவாக்கியம்
theme: The chapter turns from attack to method. The Lord is not in another town but in the six centres of the body; the way to him is to raise the root channel, kindle the fire in it, drive the breath (வாசி) until earth and sky shake, open the three bolts and let the nectar come down. Around this it sets the four paths with their four fruits (1400) and at once qualifies them: those who reach Siva's state are those who received grace, and the four are made firm only by the one who has seen the way. Vishnu and Brahma dug the earth and flew the sky and did not find the root or the crown; the servant who looks within with love does.
structure_note: The verses are chained: each opens with the last word or phrase of the one before (வாருமே / பாரும், திண்ணமே / திண்ணம், இருப்பனே / இருப்பன், கொள்வரே / கொள்ளுவார்கள், and so on through to 1413). Within the chain, 1400 to 1402 treat the four paths, 1403 to 1407 the raising of the root channel, 1408 to 1411 grace and love over learning, and 1412 and 1413 the final settling in the one letter.
source_issues: 1394 line 4 (சமருவியே) and 1402 line 1 (திறமலிக்கு) are obscure and may be corrupt.
1406 line 1 (அயந்தியானம்) and line 3 (அறிந்துமீள வைத்திடா வகையுமரணம் ஏத்தினார்) do not parse cleanly; the reading is a guess.
1405 line 3 (தாகமேரு நாடியே அனேகமான வாறுபோல்) is obscure.

reading: You bind the mantra as a means, tied up with a potsherd; even when it is bound, will the Maker live there? The air that moves within the eight and eight and eight: set it in the circled letter Ya and realise it.
nuance: ஓடு வைத்துக் கட்டி pictures the written mantra tied up with a shard as an amulet, and the verse asks whether the Author (கருத்தன்) can be bound. எட்டும் எட்டும் எட்டு (eight and eight and eight) is a breath count or the cells of a chakra; ய is one of the five letters, drawn in a circle on such diagrams. The plain point is that the breath, not the amulet, is where he is found.

reading: Saying 'he is not in this town', where do you run seeking? How can the Lord sit and live in that other town? Know and realise the Lord who dwelt in the six within the final hollow, in the final Si and the A.
nuance: The two towns are a figure for pilgrimage, or for seeking the Lord outside the body. பொந்தில் ஆறு (the six in the hollow) is read as the six centres; சீயில் அவ்வில் (in Si and A) gives two letters of the mantra as his place. The last line is coded; the first two are plain.

reading: Within you who have entered, the hymn that was set by the filling; if the gathered eye, tongue and nose are drawn round it, the one who wears the rudraksha beads and the konrai will dance in the hall, and the great light will not speak of it with love afterwards.
nuance: பூரியிட்ட is unclear: filling (பூரகம், the in-breath) or the earth. சட்சு, சிங்குவை and ஆக்கிராணம் are Sanskrit names for eye, tongue and nose, so the senses are gathered inward. The last line is obscure; it may say that what is seen cannot be told afterwards, or that the light tells only the loving.

reading: Fools fix their eyes on the flesh that rose later; if again with flesh they make the maya of pleasure, painful deeds will close round them afterwards. For those who have been lovers of the Lord, release is like swimming across a river.
nuance: மாங்கிசம் (flesh) comes three times in 1392 and 1393 and is read as the body desired and the body as such. பின்னெழுந்த (risen later) may mark the flesh as secondary to what formed it. ஆறு நீந்தல் (swimming a river) makes release a crossing to the far bank, a stock image for passing the flood of birth.

reading: You sit within the place you have left, free of grief; three doors are shut and one door is the door of vision; when the bolt of the shut doors is opened and gone, see the sure Lord clearly within the flesh itself.
nuance: The three shut doors and the one door of sight are coded: tradition reads them as the three lower channels or the three states against the fourth, or as the senses against the brow. The verse ends by placing the Lord in the flesh (மாங்கிசத்துளே) that 1392 warned against, so the body is both the snare and the shrine.

reading: It will be, it will be, it will be: that beginningless thing. If you can seek and seek the feet of the One and stand praising him, you can live as the child of Uma whose speech is sweet as syrup; with strength, join the fire and do not grieve.
nuance: The triple ஆகும் answers a doubt the verse does not state. To be Uma's child is to be Murugan, or to be adopted by the Mother. வன்னியை சமருவியே is unclear; சமருவி may be a corrupt form, and 'join the fire' takes it as the inner fire of 1395 and 1405.

reading: If you say your love has ripened to the wish to be her child: there are four steps, and since two of them come after thinking, kindle the fire in the root channel and drink that water; by way of the lady of fragrant hair you reach the feet of the Lord.
nuance: நாலு பாதம் (four steps) are the four paths of 1400; the line about two of them is unclear. The fire in the மூலநாடி and the water drunk are the coiled power and the nectar of yogic reading; ஏலவார் குழலி (the lady with cardamom-scented hair) is Shakti, through whom one reaches Siva's feet. The verse answers devotion with yoga.

reading: If you can bow and praise him with love, in the truth attained he will take away dying and birth; when the breath of the consort of the kohl-eyed lady mounts the sky, the strong deeds you did before will scatter, and that is certain.
nuance: வாசி is glossed as wind: the breath as the Siddhars' practice, which 'climbs the sky' (வானில் ஏறி) when it rises to the crown. The verse gives two routes in one, love and praise in the first half and the breath in the second, and makes the destruction of past karma follow from the breath's ascent.

reading: Listen, you fine people who told the news and said 'certain': the Lord can be known and seen when love melts within. If you drive the breath so that earth and sky both shake, our Lord will draw near and dwell in our own sea.
nuance: வாசியை நடத்திடில் (if you drive the breath) is the practice named, and the shaking of earth and sky is its sign, taken as the body's trembling or as a figure. நமது கடல் (our sea) is unclear: the body as ocean, or the sea of the heart. திண்ணம் chains the verse to 1396.

reading: I will be in the count of eight by eight and become another; I will become fire, air, water, earth and the long sky. Those who have bathed in the guru's flood will know, by his mark, the Lord of light who entered the womb and mingled with time.
nuance: The speaker of the first two lines may be the Lord or the realised poet; எட்டெட்டு எண் (the sixty-four) is read as the arts or the tattvas, without warrant in the text. குருப்புனல் (the guru's flood) is the guru's grace as a river to bathe in, replacing the tirtha, and கருப்புகுந்த says the Lord himself entered the womb.

reading: Jnanis who grasp the hint in their minds will take it; those ripe for it will gather it up if they praise with longing. Inside and outside, awareness to awareness, the light that stands clear: realise its rightness.
nuance: குறிப்பு (the hint) and பக்குவம் (ripeness) make the knowing depend on the hearer's state, not on instruction. உணர்வதற்கு உணர்வு (the awareness of awareness) is the Lord as the knower behind knowing.

reading: By clear chariyai one goes and gains salokam; by clear kiriyai and puja one may reach samipam; in clear yoga one reaches sarupam; and clear jnana, in all four, reaches sayujyam.
nuance: This is the Saiva Siddhanta scheme of four paths and four fruits stated whole, which is rare in Sivavakkiyar. நான்கிலும் (in all four) may mean that jnana crowns the other three or that it alone reaches union; 1401 pulls against the scheme at once.

reading: The clear-sighted say 'they will reach jnana'; but there is no such thing as reaching by the rightness of the four steps. Those who reach Siva's state are those who have received the holy grace; seeing the way to reach it, make the four and the works you do firm.
nuance: The second line (நாலுபாதச் செம்மை என்றதில்லையே) can deny that the four paths are an order of reaching, or deny that they are 'right' in themselves; either way grace, not the path, is the cause. The last line keeps the four as what grace-receivers do, so the verse qualifies 1400 without discarding it.

reading: Those who are not firm in the rightness of the four steps, the ignorant, wander the land seeking and drift in vain; if you can show the mark and look within by that mark, you reach the true foot of the one with fragrant matted hair.
nuance: திறமலிக்கு is obscure, perhaps 'to the strong' or a corrupt form. தேசநாடி அலைவது (wandering the land seeking) is pilgrimage, set against looking within by the குறி (sign, mark), which in the Siddhars is the inner target of the gaze.

reading: You fools who do not know the release of those who have reached: are not the tattvas with their army themselves the crimes? As the bull climbs the sluice when the sluice is opened into the channel, raise the root channel in the body upward and plant it firm.
nuance: படையுடைய தத்துவம் (the tattvas with their army) calls the body's constituents sins, in the Siddhanta sense of what binds. The sluice image is loose: ஏறு may be a bull or 'rising', and the point is a sudden upward rush when the gate opens. மூலநாடியை உயர ஏற்றி is the raising of the root channel, the chapter's method.

reading: Planting it and raising it, piercing the circles and opening the three bolts, if one mounts the fitting channel, nectar comes down; the Lord will appear to his servants as 'this is right', and the soul joins the Supreme and lives there.
nuance: தந்தி is glossed as nadi. மண்டலம் (the circles) and மூன்று தாள் (three bolts) are the three regions of sun, moon and fire and the three knots of yogic anatomy in traditional reading; the text names only the number. The nectar coming down after the ascent is the standard sequence of the Tirumanthiram's bindu chapters.

reading: Raising the fire in the root channel with love, if the striving in infatuating maya ceases, then, as the channel of thirst becomes many, those who bowed with love to the feet of the One will know.
nuance: அனல் எழுப்பி (raising the fire) repeats the method of 1395 and 1403; the condition added here is the end of striving in maya. தாகமேரு நாடியே அனேகமான வாறுபோல் is obscure: 'like the Meru channel of thirst becoming many' may name the central channel (மேரு, the spine) and its branching.

reading: Knowing and looking within you, the meditation is within you; to have the feet of the One without being born again is the truth. Those who knew and did not set themselves to return praised the way past death; press on, open the upper door within you and look.
nuance: அயந்தியானம் is unclear: 'meditation on Ayan' or a corrupt அந்தத் தியானம். Line 3 is loose; it seems to say that those who did not arrange a return to birth found death itself to be the praised way, or praised the deathless way. மேலை வாசல் (the upper door) is the crown opening of 1393's door of vision.

reading: If you can look clearly within yourself as light, light will rise and the song of turiya will be reached; sitting in the primal chakra he bathes in the holy water. See it without wavering, setting the breath right.
nuance: துரிய கீதம் (the song of the fourth state) is the inner sound heard past waking, dream and sleep, and the inner தீர்த்தம் replaces the bathing at tanks that 1356 and 1357 mocked. பிராணனைத் திருத்தி (correcting the breath) is the one plain instruction.

reading: In the thought of the clear ones who have become both the Goddess and Siva, I become the fragrance that rises and wafts from the flower; and all the traces of deeds that fell into the womb and rose from it, see, the fire burns them up, as darkness before the sun.
nuance: The speaker is the Lord, or the poet speaking as him, as in 1398. மரு may be fragrance or the flower itself. கந்மவாதனை (the karma-vasanas) are the traces carried from the womb, and the gloss gives பரிதி as sun and அங்கி as fire: they vanish as darkness before the sun.

reading: See: standing in the nature our father the Lord set for you, you will reach the right thing by knowing the middle. Mal and Ayan went hastily seeking the root and the crown, one digging the earth and one born into the sky, and found nothing.
nuance: The myth of Vishnu as boar digging for Siva's feet and Brahma as swan flying for his crown is told in two lines. நடு அறிந்து (knowing the middle) is the key the poet sets against them: the middle is read as the central channel between the two, or as the balance between extremes; the text does not say.

reading: You say for show that Ayan and Mal did not see him; if one is insolent, can even a king be approached? If, as far as service goes, you can worship and look with love, the devotion that of old burned the three cities will ripen in you.
nuance: The myth of 1409 is turned on the hearer: those who repeat it as proof are themselves insolent (மிண்டினால்). The last line is ambiguous: devotion to the one who burned the three cities, or a devotion that is itself the fire that burned them.

reading: It is complete: apart from him I see nothing before or after. What can hold on to the one that has no holding? Is it by learning that the Lord's feet can be seen? Ask with love and affection those who have gained them.
nuance: பற்றிலாத ஒன்றுதன்னை பற்றிநிற்க (to hold on to the one without holding) is the Kural's paradox of clinging to the one who does not cling. The verse answers its own question about learning by sending the hearer to those who have reached, which is the guru's role without the word.

reading: In the time when the state you have heard of is gained, the wasting confusion of the tattvas will be removed; in the house of release it becomes open space and comes to shine; joining fire and wind, it raises them up from the breast.
nuance: வன்னி மாருதம் கூட்டி (joining fire and wind) is the kindled breath of the whole chapter; குயத்தை விட்டு (from the breast, or from the body) is unclear. The order is unusual: release and its shining come first, the raising last, so the verse may describe what the attained state does rather than how to reach it.

reading: Can one raise the root channel and make it easy? If you can draw and pull in the assembly that does not deceive, then, passing beyond deep sleep and beyond dream, pressing in, to settle in the one letter is the truth, sir.
nuance: The first line may ask whether the raising can be made comfortable or doubt that it can. மழுப்பிலாத சபை (the assembly without deception) is obscure, perhaps the gathered senses or the hall of 1370. சுழுத்தி and சொப்பனம் are deep sleep and dream, the states passed to reach the fourth; ஓர் எழுத்து (the one letter) closes the chapter where 1385 left it.

title: சிவவாக்கியம்
theme: Sivavakkiyar turns from the yogic body (breath, the letters a and u, the nine gates, the middle channel) to a running attack on the rules of pollution, on caste, on book-knowledge and on worship of worn or built lingas, arguing each time from the body itself: the body that was formed from menstrual blood and semen, that holds the Lord within, and that ends deeds by the breath. The chapter closes with a short run of first-person verses on the oneness of 'you and I'.
structure_note: 1414 to 1419 are chained by their opening words (ஆனதே, உலாவும், கும்பிடும், நீங்கும்) and describe the yogic state; 1420 to 1424 are questions put to jnanis and ritualists; 1425 to 1427 attack caste; 1428 to 1432 attack external worship; 1433 and 1434 are personal; 1435 to 1438 return to the attack on penance and books.
source_issues: 1419 line 3 (விரக்கில்என் மறைக்கில்என்) is hard to construe and may be corrupt.
1426 line 4 (மனு எரிக்க) is unclear and may be a corrupt reading.
1429 line 3 (பூட்டகாயம்) is unclear; the word may be damaged.

reading: There is nothing else: breath, substance and body are the state given where the good Lord's feet join; when love in me endures and I work the breath, the old deeds say 'leave' and go far, far away.
nuance: வாசியை வருந்தினால் is the verse's hinge: வாசி is the Siddhars' word for the breath worked as a practice, and வருந்துதல் (to labour, press) takes it as effort on the breath. The first two lines are compressed and their syntax is loose; the plain sense is that deeds depart when breath practice and love go together.

reading: Pati has come to be; pasu and pasam have ceased; the malas, the senses and the deeds are gone. Did wind come and meet a fire set in the forest? Within the flesh, fixing on the air, one roams in union with it.
nuance: The three terms of Saiva Siddhanta, pati, pasu and pasam, open the verse, and the fire-in-the-forest question is a figure for how quickly bonds burn when the breath (வாயு) is joined to them. The chained opening (ஆனதே from 1414's last word) marks this run of verses as one sequence.

reading: What rose and pressed in as 'u' and 'a' roams; the five senses that roamed rest in one place; the moon there becomes love, stands, and nectar is eaten; mark and know our Lord who roams, and worship him.
nuance: உவ்வும் அவ்வும் are the letters உ and அ of the pranava, and in the Siddhars' usage also the two breaths or the two channels; the moon that becomes love and yields nectar is, as tradition takes it, the inner moon at the crown. A plain reading has the senses stilled and a sweetness tasted; the coded one maps each term to a body-place.

reading: Within the worshipping thought, trusting Guhan and the five-handed one, seeking them at left and right as ours; seating our Lord and the Mother and the one in the middle; as a bee follows, the word follows on, and sloth departs.
nuance: Murugan (குகன்) and Ganesha (ஐங்கரன்) at left and right, with the Lord and the Mother and a middle one (நடுவன்), reads in tradition as the three channels: the left and right nadis and the central one. The plain reading is a devotional placement of the family of Siva. தும்பிபோல வாசகம் (the word like a bee) may be the hum of the mantra.

reading: The five senses depart, and the heaped strong deeds, and the desire that is ego; from within the Omkara, when the nine have ceased and one stands in the one, to stand resolved by the word of the sleepless Lord is purity.
