nuance: யுத்தி (reasoning, tactic) is the weapon, not grace or mantra: anger is undone by thinking. சிற்சொரூபம் (the form of chit, awareness) is named as a lamp, and செய்ய பொருள் (the red or right Thing) is the Siddhars' usual name for the Supreme.

reading: We stood firm on the mountain called the eternal, finished what we set out to do and became stainless; truly the one beyond us does not perish, and we shall live for ever.
nuance: நின்மலம் (stainless) is the Siddhanta word for freedom from the malas. எங்கள் கடந்தான் is read here as the one who is beyond us; the line claims both his imperishability and the poet's own unending life, the Siddhar's usual claim to a deathless body or state.

reading: Making the horse called mind our mount, fastening the bridle called intellect in its mouth and climbing properly onto the saddle called anger, we rode off to the place of clarity.
nuance: The horse is explicitly the mind here, not the breath that the Siddhars elsewhere call horse or வாசி; the intellect bridles it. சினமென்னுஞ் சீனி (the saddle called anger) is odd: sitting on anger may mean keeping it under one, or the word may be corrupt.

reading: Setting our foot on the sandal called desire, trampling the thorn-forest of ego to the root, lighting a fire in the bad quality called kaasai, we have passed beyond time and death.
nuance: காசை is unclear: perhaps greed for money (காசு), perhaps a corrupt word. காலாகாலம் கடந்தோம் can mean beyond all time or beyond Kala, Death. Desire is a sandal worn under the foot: used, not renounced.

reading: The fierce and cruel enemy called Death we drove away with the sword called kalpa; we crossed beyond birth on this earth and saw the Supreme.
nuance: கற்பம் is the medical Siddhas' rejuvenating preparation and also the inner practice said to replace it; the verse does not say which, only that it is the weapon against Yama. தற்பரம் is the Supreme beyond the self.

reading: With the mind dissolved like a fly fallen in honey, seeing without bewilderment the vision of the form of awareness, finish the mercury-gem that lets one fly in the sky, put it in the mouth and stand and dance.
nuance: சூதம் is mercury, and tradition reads சூதவான்மணி as a bound-mercury pill (குளிகை) held in the mouth to give the power of flight. A plain reading takes the flying and the gem as figures for the freed mind. The fly in honey is both absorption and being stuck; the verse means the first.

reading: I saw the good raised foot, I saw the light, I saw a dancer within the pure space; the foot set on my bowed head is the foot of the true guru.
nuance: The raised foot is Siva's in the dance (தூக்கிய பாதம்), and the verse makes it the same foot the guru places on the disciple's head at initiation. சுத்தவெளி (pure space) is the inner expanse where the dance is seen.

reading: Snake who lived in the hole at the foot of the banyan, you have entered the hole at the foot of the pipal; look and look at the tip of your tail, draw in and sleep standing, and dance.
nuance: The two trees and holes are cipher: tradition takes the snake as the coiled power or breath moving from one seat in the body to another, and watching the tail-tip as turning back to its root. The plain picture is only a snake changing holes and sleeping.

reading: In four streets stand four pillars, and in the middle street a golden pillar; garland that shining golden pillar with flowers and dance.
nuance: The four streets and the central golden pillar are read by tradition as the nadis or directions and the central channel or spine (the மேரு); the garland is worship of it. Nothing in the stanza fixes this, and the numbers may count something else.

reading: Though the ocean shifts, will Meru be shaken? Even if it were uprooted, even if the aeon of time itself turned, stand with firmness unmoved, according to the truth of knowledge.
nuance: மதி உண்மைப் படிக்கே makes the firmness rest on what the intellect knows to be true, not on will. The syntax of the first two lines is loose; the sense is that Meru does not move for the sea.

reading: Take the wind as your prey and eat it, draw water into the mouth for the ... , let the fire-crescent cool and heat, and in the open expanse join without bewilderment and dance.
nuance: The snake eating wind is the breath practice: வாயு as prey, தேயு (fire) and the crescent (moon) as the sun and moon breaths or heat and coolness, வெட்டவெளி as the open space reached. வருடிக்கு is obscure, perhaps corrupt.

reading: Making a circle in the hole of the stainless path, spreading the great hood that is the moon, praise again and again the primal foot of the faultless Parapara and dance.
nuance: வளை is the snake's hole and also a bangle or ring; மண்டலம் is the coil and also a sphere or a period of practice. The hood as the moon (மதி, also intellect) is cipher tradition takes as the mind or the moon-centre opened; the plain command is to praise.

reading: Running until the legs ache to forests, mountains, rivers, lords and Kasi: can any fruit be seen? To settle in the state that is the way to release, stand at the ghat of Vedanta and dance.
nuance: The list of pilgrimage places is answered by a different துறை (ghat, landing), that of Vedanta: the bathing-place is moved from the river to knowledge.

reading: Those without even a sesame seed of love in the heart never gain release in this old world; cut the bonds of the thieving senses, see and worship Kalakala and dance rejoicing.
nuance: The verse puts love as the condition of release before the restraint of the senses, and names the Lord as காலகாலன், Death's death, so that love and the end of dying are set together.

reading: As frost flees far at the sight of the sun, in the pure place where one's own bonds are scattered, see and behold the noble one, and with love hold him and follow without parting.
nuance: ஆரியன் (the noble one) may be the Lord or the guru; the following and holding fit either. சொந்த பந்தம் (own bonds) is kinship and property, which vanish before the sight like frost before the sun.

reading: Join the stainless mind to the Thing that is seen, as a magnet draws iron and holds it; and in calm, like the pot and its rope, follow without wavering and dance.
nuance: The two images differ: the magnet is attraction that needs no effort, the pot tied to its rope is a bond that does not slip. காட்சியான வஸ்து (the Thing that is seen) makes the object of meditation something already perceived.

reading: Is there any feeling in a chiselled stone image? Is there any feeling in the fools of this world? Does the flaw of copper go by scrubbing with tamarind? Ignorance does not leave the fool.
nuance: The chiselled stone and the tamarind-scoured copper are the stock images of the idol in Siddhar verse; here they serve as comparisons for the fool, whose insensibility is like the stone's and whose fault, like the metal's, does not come off with polish.

reading: Like searching for a needle in a great heap, release is not caught by the teachers of local custom; by the act of the gracious root guru we gained bliss.
nuance: தேசாசார தேசிகர் are teachers of the usage of the country, ritual custom; against them is set the மூலகுரு, the root or first guru. The needle in the heap (போர், a stack of straw) is the futility of searching for release through them.

reading: As a bottle-gourd drawn on a palm leaf is no use for curry, wandering the eight directions does not gain the goal; those who build a temple in every country and worship daily do not see the Lord's feet.
nuance: ஏட்டுச் சுரைக்காய் (the gourd on a leaf) is a proverb for book-knowledge that cannot be used, and the verse applies it to pilgrimage and temple-building: both are representations that do not feed.

reading: Those who know themselves and live by it hide themselves; those who do not know themselves are the ones who show themselves off; such knowers do not think to cherish some other god, for they cherish the great light.
nuance: The second half most naturally continues the self-knowers: the one who knows himself needs no separate god because the great light is already his object. It could also describe the show-offs as men who cherish nothing but display; the first reading fits the chapter.

reading: Standing at the whirl-point in the breath, see the light that spreads everywhere like taste in milk, as ... gold is set to hold gold, and dance rejoicing and rejoicing.
nuance: கால் is read as breath or wind, so காலிற் சுழுமுனை is the whirl-point reached in the breath; it could also be read bodily. பற்றுப்பொன் பற்றவைத்த பான்மை (the way gold is set to catch) is unclear, perhaps gold plating or a goldsmith's solder; the line looks damaged.

reading: Once you have drunk the honey of the sky that overflows and runs, count the bond of the body you took on and this life in the country as vomit, and with great gladness clear your heart and dance.
nuance: வானத்தேன் (the sky's honey) is in tradition the nectar that flows from the head in yoga; the plain reading is the taste of the Supreme. ஓக்காளம் (vomit, nausea) makes worldly life not merely passing but repugnant once that taste is known.

reading: The four Vedas, the six kinds of shastra, the many tantras, the puranas, the arts, the proclaimed Agamas and the various other books: all are vain books.
nuance: The list is exhaustive and includes the Agamas, the Saivas' own scripture; the verse gives no exception and no reason, and its ground is the chapter's: what is known within is not in any book.

reading: The many differences of religion and the differences of caste belong to the people of the world, not to true sadhus; will the mind of those who have climbed the summit change? Learn the Siddhanta of the Siddhas and dance.
nuance: சித்தர் சித்தாந்தம் (the Siddhas' conclusion) is set against the sects' siddhantas; it is a teaching with no sect and no caste. The verse does not abolish caste for the world, only denies it any hold on those who have reached the height.

reading: Does pure awareness come from doing puja? Is there merit in walking round the earth? Resolve that the primal Thing can be reached in the time when desire is gone, and dance.
nuance: The two questions expect no; the positive condition is only ஆசை அற்ற காலம், the moment desire is absent, with no practice named in its place.

title: பாம்பாட்டிச் சித்தர் பாடல்
theme: The fifth part of Pambatti's kummi to the snake turns from attacking outward religion to the inner method itself: the world is false and the root alone worth knowing, merit and penance are void without the Lord's feet, and in a long run of eight-foot stanzas the snake is shut in the body's pot, raised through the sushumna and the letters of the five-syllable mantra, and set dancing in the open space, ending in silence and the end of birth.
structure_note: Ten four-line kummi stanzas (2080 to 2090) on knowledge, devotion and renunciation are followed by fifteen eight-line எண்சீர் விருத்தம் stanzas (2091 to 2104) that are almost wholly cipher: letters, pots, pillars, ships, a gun, smithies and the snake's dance. Several open with the formula 'we will shut the snake in the ... pot' (2096, 2104), continued in chapter 107. Every stanza ends in ஆடாய் பாம்பே; the readings give what each stanza adds.
source_issues: 2090: the stanza's syntax is loose (இறந்தவர் ஐவரவர் இட்ட மானவர் / எய்தும்அவ ரிறந்தாரென்று) and may be damaged.
2093: அளிபுலந் and சீனி are unclear and may be corrupt.
2097: ஆயத் துறை in line 7 is obscure.
2101: line 4 (கருதி யருகல்வி ஒப்பஞ் செய்வோம்) does not parse cleanly and looks damaged.

reading: If one knows the root, one can see all three worlds beforehand and reach eternal release; is there any gain in knowing a great many roots? Be clear that the world is false, and dance.
nuance: The plain contrast is one root against many: knowing the single source against a herbalist's or scholar's knowledge of countless roots. மூலவேர் can also point to the root-centre (மூலம்) of the yogic body. சகத்தைப் பொய் is the Vedantic world-is-false, said flatly.

reading: They do not say the world is beginningless but say the beginningless one made it; they do not know the Real. Say that apart from the power of the great state of kalpa there is no other power, and dance.
nuance: The first two lines can be read as Pambatti holding, against those who teach creation, that the world is itself beginningless, or as mocking anyone who argues about origins while ignorant of சத்து, the Real. The second would sit better with 2080's world-is-false. மகத்துவ நிலைகற்பம் sets the kalpa, the deathless state or preparation, above every other power.

reading: The Siddha seated in the house of a thousand and eight petals, the wondrous Siddha who fills the whole cosmos, the causal Siddha who grows high without a body, has become the light within the eye.
nuance: The thousand-petalled lotus at the crown (here a thousand and eight) is the seat; the same one fills all the அண்டம் and is the light in the eye, so the crown, the cosmos and the eye are one place. The Lord is called a சித்தன், a Siddha, in the Siddhars' own title.

reading: If one sets uppermost the Lord whose form is letters, sought at the centre of the forty-three-angled state, all the upper worlds become servants to his soft feet.
nuance: நாற்பத்துமுக்கோணம் is read by tradition as the forty-three triangles of the Sri Chakra, at whose centre the deity sits; அக்கரச் சொரூபம் makes the Lord a body of letters, the mantra itself. Without that key the number is only a diagram.

reading: Those who have seen never tell, and those who tell have never seen; those who wear an assumed costume do not see the King's state; dance and dance.
nuance: The first two lines are the Siddhar proverb கண்டவர் விண்டிலர், விண்டவர் கண்டிலர். The third adds the costume: the ascetic's outward garb is one more way of telling without seeing.

reading: Before the one who dances inside the hut of six kalas goes off to the neighbouring house, build a fort round him; once he has parted, it is hard to bring him back; hold him close and do not let him go.
nuance: The dancer in the hut is the life or breath in the body; the neighbouring house is death or another body. ஆறுகலைக் குச்சு may be the body of six centres or of six kalas. The plain sense is to guard life while it is here; the coded sense is to hold the breath within.

reading: What use is doing every one of the countless merits, if the heart does not think of the One's feet? Be sure that without devotion the fruit of hard penance comes to ruin.
nuance: The verse does not reject merit or penance but makes them void without பத்தி; பாழ்படும் (goes to waste, to the void) is a strong word for the Siddhars, who elsewhere use பாழ் for the highest emptiness.

reading: What is gained if every world becomes one's own, when one does not think of our Lord's lotus feet? Thinking that this worldly life may be cut off today, remember the Maker's feet and dance.
You put on the wedding finery, rejoiced greatly and stood bewildered with children, house and kin; if even after seeing the corpse's finery you do not renounce, it is only a companion to birth.
nuance: மணக்கோலம் and பிணக்கோலம், the bridal array and the corpse's array, rhyme: the same body is dressed twice. The verse blames not marriage but failing to renounce after seeing death.

reading: I will tell you one great medicine to cut off both birth and death, so hear it eagerly: know the way to open with the key the lock of the mind and the door of thought, and dance.
nuance: The great medicine (பெருமருந்து) is not a drug but a knowing; the lock and door are the mind's, so the release is an opening of the mind rather than an escape from the body.

reading: The five who died were the ones he loved; tell everyone that they have died; and stand and dance so that those on earth may know the way, saying that the one who forgot is one.
nuance: The five dead are most likely the five senses (or the five airs) killed in practice, and he who loved them the self; மறந்தவர் ஒருவர் may be the one who has forgotten the world. The syntax is loose and the stanza may be damaged; this reading is a guess.

reading: Becoming a snake at the root of ஆ, spreading its hood in the field of bliss, folding in at the root of ஊ, running and stretching out the tongue of வ: when the Siddha snake-charmer taught the mantra in which சீ lay, we cut the root of birth in ம and passed beyond maya's bonds.
nuance: The syllables are the cipher: ஆ, ஊ and ம give the pranava's a, u and m, and வ and சீ the letters of சிவ in the five-letter mantra. Tradition takes the snake as the coiled power rising through the syllables. சித்தப்பிடாரனார், the Siddha snake-charmer, is the guru and also Pambatti's own name.

reading: Those who speak tantra know [only] themselves; those who speak the single mantra do not know its meaning; mantra-chanters circle the wall inside the round house and do not find the gate. Go up into the sky, pull up the root, make a pill with the knowledge called grace: if you eat this medicine there is no more birth.
nuance: The first line is ambiguous: தம்மை அறிவார் may be sarcastic (they know only themselves) or a real concession. The second half borrows the herbalist's procedure (pull the root, roll the pill) for an inner one: the root is pulled in the sky, the binding agent is grace.

reading: Building a ship of clay, setting up a heavy mast for all to see, making the field of the senses the rudder, hoisting the sail of the support called knowledge, holding it within the circle called space and sailing it to conquer the sea of Vedanta: the ship the clear-minded jnani sails has reached the holy feet.
nuance: The clay ship is the body, the clay of 2039's potter. அளிபுலம் and சீனி (sail, or saddle as in 2057) are uncertain words. Vedanta is here a sea to be crossed and conquered, where in 2067 it was a landing-place.

reading: One must feel within the heart, know both the inner and the outer, slowly rouse the fire, drive it into the water of the street, drive off the thieving senses, stand seeing above the nose between the eyes, seek the clear supreme light: we have seen the holy feet.
nuance: கனலை எழுப்ப (rouse the fire) is the waking of the inner heat or kundalini; கண்ணுக்கு மூக்குமேல் is the gaze fixed above the nose between the brows. வீதிப் புனல் (the water of the street) is obscure, perhaps the channel along which the fire is sent.

reading: On the summit of the pillar of Om, know both inner and outer; cutting off egoism and anger, damming the flood of bliss, joined firmly to the Steadfast One beyond the hour of death, calm, sleeping without sleeping and reaching ease, dance saying thonthom.
nuance: ஓங்காரக் கம்பம் is the spine or central channel taken as Om, the pillar of 2063. தூங்காமல் தூங்கி, sleeping without sleep, is the Siddhars' phrase for samadhi. தாணு (Sthanu, the immovable) is Siva.

reading: We will shut the snake in the pot of longing, set it dancing in the open space of Vedanta, pluck out the causes and feed them to it, make it dance standing in the harsh expanse of time; mounting the horse and circling the whole old world, seeing the eternal subtlety and reciting the mantra beyond words, we brought it back and gained the four.
nuance: விரகக் குடம் may be the pot of passion or of separation: the body. The horse (துரகம்) is the breath. ஒருநான்கும் is unexplained: tradition might take it as the four kinds of release or the four aims of life. உரையற்ற மந்திரம், the mantra without words, anticipates 2104's swallowed letter.

reading: Letting the snake that stood in the body-pot wander in the sea of compassion, driving it far through the loving sushumna, seeking to fix the eternal Thing, climbing the vast space of maya and searching to attain the stainless Thing, we crossed the landing of the ... and joined the bliss of the void beyond.
nuance: The stages run body, compassion, sushumna, maya's space and the void beyond (அப்பால் பாழ்): the highest state is called பாழ், emptiness. ஆயத் துறை is unclear: a toll-landing, or the landing of the tattvas.

reading: Taking the thought that stood at the root place up through the whole sushumna to the bindu-circle in the upper place, it lives on that path; by the compassion of the holy young mother, becoming the form of knowledge of the supreme state, standing with Mal who sleeps on the banyan leaf, we joined bliss.
nuance: The movement is from the root (மூலம்) to the bindu at the head. பாலத் திருத்தாய் may be the young mother, the Vaalai of the Siddhars, or a mother of milk. Vishnu asleep on the banyan leaf is an unusual figure here, perhaps for the mind dissolved in cosmic sleep. வேலை வழி (the sea's way or the way of the task) is unclear.

reading: Making one the mind, the horse that gallops in the street of the five senses, crossing the worlds bound by mala, seeking the state of the abiding guru's feet: crossing the five places and the earth is crossing the moon's sphere too; leaving the troubled sea of this earth, become bliss and dance.
nuance: The horse is the mind again, as in 2057; here it is not bridled but made one-pointed (ஒருமைப்படுத்தி). The five places and the moon's sphere are read by tradition as the lower adharas and the moon-centre in the head.

reading: Taking the form of the teacher called guru, making the aimed knowledge the gun and grace itself the bullet, going beyond it in bliss, firing at the mind's path of the women called delusion so that it burns without coming back, saying it struck within the great ring, hold to the one who holds to nothing and dance.
nuance: The gun (துப்பாக்கி) and bullet (உண்டை) are rare in this corpus and show the stanza's lateness. பற்றானைப் பற்றி, hold to the one without holding, is the Kural's paradox in two words. மருளென்னு மாதர் may mean the women who are delusion, or delusion as a woman.

reading: We will stop the wind in the coppersmith's cave, kindle fire in the blacksmith's forge, make gold on the head of those who spoke, make learning equal ... ; we will burn away the bond of women, see the mark of the true Thing and reach what we desired; not babbling, not babbling, staying still, we joined Parapara.
nuance: கால் is both leg and wind: stopping it in the cave is the breath held. The smithy and gold-making are the alchemist's tools, which the stanza may mean literally or as inner work. Line four is obscure. The close, பன்னாதே, சும்மா இருந்து, puts silence above all the furnace-work.

reading: We will set fire to the divisions of caste, plant a pole in the open market, play at the branching of the streets, make kinship in the house we should not, search and roam and then fall asleep, and delight in the pleasing woman: the five primal Brahmas do not know this.
nuance: Read plainly the stanza flaunts transgression: burning caste, entering forbidden houses, enjoying a woman. Read in the Siddhars' cipher the streets are the nadis, the woman is Vaalai or Shakti, and the sleep is yogic. Both readings stand; the first line at least is plain. The five Brahmas may be the five deities over the elements.

reading: Taking our stand on the long letter, twisting the tail on the letter that does not leave, spreading the hood on that released letter, moving and dancing on the way of the sky, settling even on the struck letter, gathering in the twelfth letter, we joined the holy feet of the preceptor who firmly gave us grace.
nuance: The stanza is a ladder of letters: நெட்டெழுத்து (long vowel), the unleaving letter, the letter let go, the twelfth letter (ஔ is the twelfth vowel, or the twelve finger-breadths of breath). No key in the text fixes which letters are meant.

reading: We will shut the snake in the pot with a needle's hole, roam round the whole world, forget the stained birth, set it dancing in the space where the mind agrees, feed it the stained senses as prey, climb and dance on the summit the mind has reached, and swallow even the spoken letter: we are free of birth and death.
nuance: The pot with a needle's hole is the body, perhaps its narrow opening at the crown. பேசும் எழுத்தையும் விழுங்கி, swallowing the letter that speaks, takes the practice past mantra into silence, the end that the letter-stanzas lead to.

title: பாம்பாட்டிச் சித்தர் பாடல்
theme: The last four stanzas of Pambatti's song continue the formula 'we will shut the snake in the pot': the body-pot is named in turn by nail, thread and the letter ma, and through it the snake climbs the pillar and the ladder, the breath weaves its cloth, the body is put to the crucible, and the practitioner, having offered mind, speech, body and the five senses, stands as the letter si, Siva.
structure_note: Four எண்சீர் விருத்தம் stanzas (2105 to 2108), each opening with a different pot and ending in ஆடாய் பாம்பே, except 2107, which ends in a warning to keep the secret. 2106 drops the snake for a weaving cipher. All four are cipher throughout.
source_issues: 2107: பத்தெட்டு மூன்று படி has no evident key, and the closing line (பார்த்துரை யிதன்மெய் பலிக்க வெண்ணி) is loosely constructed.

reading: We will shut the snake in the nailed pot, climb the fort of fire and look, set it dancing on the ruby pillar, feed it mind, speech and body as prey, cut even the rope of shame, stand seeking the feet of the Lord in whom there is no Death, find the way up the ladder and climb: no one knows this.
nuance: The fort of fire and the ruby pillar read as the heat at the base and the central channel (compare the golden pillar of 2063 and the pillar of Om of 2095); the ladder is the ascent through the centres. மனம் வாக்குக் காயம், the three instruments, are themselves fed to the snake. நாணிக் கயிறு is the rope of shame, and நாண் is also a bowstring.

reading: We will spin the thread north and east, set the warp in the whirl, roll the ball of yarn on the path that is walked, weave the cloth on the path that is not walked, throw the shuttle on the western bank and sell what we gathered everywhere; we can also gather it in and keep it within the One: we have seen the primal foot.
nuance: The loom is a cipher with no key in the text. Tradition would take the thread as the breath, the whirl (சுழல்) as the sushumna, the walked and unwalked paths as the side channels and the central one, and the cloth as the body or the work done in it. The last line turns the trade outward and then back: what is spread everywhere can also be held in the One.

reading: We will shut the snake in the pot of strings and take our pleasure within the sushumna; we will beg alms with a bowl; we have crossed the steps of ten, eight and three; we will put the filthy body to the crucible; as the knowing one gives us firm assurance, thinking that the truth of this word will bear fruit, see and speak: careful, careful.
nuance: சூத்திரம் is a string or mechanism (the puppet's string of 2047) and also a formula. புடம் is the alchemist's calcining fire: the body itself is to be refined, as in karpa practice. பத்தெட்டு மூன்று is a count tradition might fit to tattvas or centres; the text does not say. பதனம் பதனம், take care, closes the song by guarding the secret.

reading: We will shut the snake in the pot of ம, we have scooped up and eaten the breath of the jewelled circle, we will push away the pots of வ, leap past the crooked dream, let it dance in the open sea of space, offer the five instruments as sacrifice, and saying we stand become the form of சி, see the holy feet, be clear and dance.
nuance: The letters are those of the five-letter mantra: in the usual Saiva reading ம stands for mala or the body, வ for grace, சி for Siva. The snake begins in ம and ends as சி, so the stanza is a passage through நமசிவாய from bond to Siva. பஞ்ச கருவி are the five senses, and வாசி is the breath as practice.

title: சங்கிலிச் சித்தர் பாடல்
theme: Sangili Siddhar's kummi, sung to the 'blissful girl' (ஆனந்தப் பெண்ணே), opens with a lineage (Thirumular as guru, the siddha host) and a climb through the body's centres by their presiding gods, Ganesha at the root, the Brahmin in the navel lotus, Vishnu and Lakshmi, Rudra and Rudri, Sadasiva's feet, with the breath (வாசி) as the horse that carries the climb. Its second half turns on the body: a filthy carcass, a salted pot, a bellows, a wedding that becomes a corpse-show, and everything born of earth returning to earth, in which the Lord nonetheless clings like oil in sesame.
structure_note: Twenty-five kummi stanzas with one refrain. 2109 to 2112 are invocation and the letters of Om; 2113 to 2122 are the yoga of breath and the six centres with their gods, closing on self-knowledge and the mantra of mother and father; 2123 to 2128 are the body as fort, pot, bellows and corpse; 2129 to 2133 are the earth argument: all things come from earth, go back to earth, and nothing (parents, body, kin, wife) is சதம், lasting. The chapter break at 2133 is the editor's; the question of 2133 is answered in 2134.
source_issues: 2113 line 4: தானறிந்துய்வாயா runs தான் அறிந்து உய்வாய் together with an extra final ஆ; read as உய்வாய்.
2124 line 4 and 2122 line 2: தெரிந்துக் கொள்வாய் and அறிந் துக்கொண்டு carry a spurious doubled க் after the participle; read தெரிந்து கொள்வாய், அறிந்து கொண்டு.
2126 line 3: வேத்தாள் is not a standard form; read as வேற்றாள் (a stranger). The reading is uncertain.
2128 line 1: பெண் னோடுபின் is split across a space; read பெண்ணோடு பின்.
The chapter division at 2133/2134 cuts the rhetorical question of 2133 from its answer in 2134; the two chapters are one kummi of 36 stanzas.

reading: Praising the feet of the Ganesha at the root, hold in your mind the feet of Valai, Tripurai, the Mother, in the supreme awareness that is the threefold flame everywhere, blissful girl.
nuance: மூலக் கணேசன் is Ganesha as the god of the root centre (மூலாதாரம்) in the traditional scheme of six centres, each with its deity; the stanzas that follow climb that scheme. முச்சுடர் is tradition's sun, moon and fire. வாலை and திரிபுரை are the young goddess and the goddess of the three cities, here one Mother; the refrain's ஆனந்தப் பெண் may be the same goddess, the listener, or the poet's own soul.

reading: Our guru is Thirumular; one who has always praised and hymned his feet should bow to the feet of the host of great siddhas who are free of doubt, blissful girl.
nuance: The claim of Thirumular as guru is a lineage claim and not a date; 2135 and 2144 add Bogar as the poet's பாட்டன் (grandfather, or guru's guru). The siddhas are praised as a community (குழாம்), as the Tirumanthiram praises the devotees.

reading: The circle of Om became the body, and then the mute letter became the life; know yourself the way in which it becomes ரீங்காரம் and ஸ்ரீங்காரம், blissful girl.
nuance: ஊமை எழுத்து, the mute letter, is tradition's name for the unsounded part of Om (the final nasal or the half-measure); the stanza makes Om the body and the silent part of Om the life in it. ரீம் and ஸ்ரீம் are seed syllables of the goddess, as the next stanza's letters are those of the five-letter mantra. The plain claim is that body and life are made of sound; the particulars are the cipher.

reading: When அ joins உ it becomes ய; knowing that, stand in the clarity that is சி and discern, blissful girl.
nuance: The arithmetic of letters is not grammar: tradition reads அ as Siva, உ as Shakti, and ய as the soul, the letter of the five-letter mantra that stands for the bound soul, with சி as Siva's own letter. So read, the stanza says the soul arises from Siva and Shakti and must stand in Siva. The stanza itself gives only the letters.

reading: Will those who have seen and known the five elements think even a little of attachment to this world? Know the way of yoga yourself, without agitation, and be saved, blissful girl.
To those who know the state of tapas it becomes known through jnana itself; so know well what the nine siddhas and the others saw and made clear, blissful girl.
nuance: நவசித்தர், the nine siddhas, is a traditional list (its members vary by source); the stanza invokes them as authorities, so the knowledge is handed down as well as seen.

reading: If you know the state of the breath, the mind, pleased that tapas is accomplished, mounts the horse called தேசி and makes its search; know that, blissful girl.
nuance: The horse is the Siddhars' standing figure for the breath, and tradition hears வாசி itself as the horse; தேசி (shining, or of the country) is the horse's name here. The claim is that knowing the breath is the whole of tapas (தவம் வாய்த்தது), a stronger claim than 2114, where tapas is known through jnana.

reading: Those who have known Nandi's court never give up the quest of the breath; know well the seat of the Brahmin in the navel lotus and be saved, blissful girl.
nuance: அந்தணன், the Brahmin, is read by tradition as Brahma, the god of the second centre in the six-centre scheme, though the stanza places him at the navel (உந்தி), which the scheme gives to Vishnu. நந்தி கொலு, Nandi's court or audience, is the Lord's seat at the crown, or the guru's presence. The ascent continues in 2117 and 2118.

reading: Bowing at the place where Vishnu and Lakshmi dwell and passing beyond it, you will go on and see above the service of Rudra and Rudri, blissful girl.
nuance: The gods are stations of the climb: Vishnu's centre and Rudra's centre, each with his consort, in the traditional assignment of deities to the centres. The stanza says only that one bows and passes on; where in the body these places are is tradition's gloss.

reading: Whatever puja one performs, even if one has seen and known that the Supreme is one, is not the means by which thought subsides the fine feet of Sadasiva, blissful girl?
nuance: The stanza places both ritual and the monist's knowledge (பரம் ஏகம்) below the stilling of thought, and makes the Lord's feet the means of that stilling. Sadasiva is the god of the highest centre in the scheme the stanzas have climbed.

tamil: நானே நான் என்று அறிந் துக்கொண்டு பர
reading: Knowing as 'I myself am I' the arising that is the Siva-Supreme which stands filled as itself alone, know the supreme quest, blissful girl.
nuance: உற்பனம் (also 2141, பர உற்பனம்) is an arising or appearance, here of the Supreme as oneself. நானே நான் is the first-person form of the great saying; what fills everything is known as 'I'. The stanza follows 2118, which made the feet the means, so the identity is reached by the feet and not by assertion.

reading: Knowing that deceitful birth and death are no more than a residual trace that goes before, if you do pranayama without agitation you become the Supreme, blissful girl.
nuance: வாசனை is the trace or latent impression that carries the soul from birth to birth; the stanza makes birth and death themselves that trace, and sets pranayama alone as what dissolves it. The promise, தற்பரம் ஆவாய், is as strong as the Tirumanthiram's சிவன் அவன் ஆமே.

reading: Even having passed beyond chariyai and kiriyai, even having achieved yoga and received grace, without the proper letting-go of jnana nothing is of any use, blissful girl.
nuance: ஞான விசர்க்கம் is obscure: விசர்க்கம் (visarga) is a release or discharge, so perhaps the letting-go that jnana is, or the jnana that lets go; a copyist's slip for விசாரம் (inquiry) is possible. Either way the four Saiva paths are ranked with jnana as the only one that counts.

reading: If one knows oneself as 'this is what I am', must one then still go looking for the Supreme? The one who knows the mantra that mother and father taught is the jnani, blissful girl.
nuance: அன்னையும் அப்பனும் may be the parents, or Shakti and Siva as the teaching pair, which tradition prefers and 2109 and 2118 support. The first half is a rhetorical question: self-knowledge makes a separate search for the Supreme needless, which continues 2119.

reading: Beyond this eight-span body there is the one with nine gates that takes on beauty; for those who know its coolness and walk by it, eight places come into view, blissful girl.
nuance: The eight-span body and the nine gates are standard; what lies 'beyond' (இதுதாண்டி) the one while being the other is the cipher, perhaps the gross body and the subtle body, or the body and the practice in it. எட்டுத் தலங்கள் may be eight inner stations or the eight siddhis; தண்மை (coolness, or nature) is also open. The next two stanzas repeat இதுதாண்டி for the fort and the pot.

reading: Five persons joined together to rule and built a pleasure-house; know that the Gingee fort you have seen is this, blissful girl.
nuance: The five are the elements (tradition) or the senses; the building is the body, and செஞ்சிக் கோட்டை, the hill fort of Gingee, is a real fort of the poet's country made into its figure. The verse is a riddle of the kind the Siddhars set: the famous fort is the one you are sitting in.

reading: Beyond this filthy carcass, beyond this salted pot, beyond this torn bellows: tend well and become clear, blissful girl.
nuance: Three of Pattinathar's names for the body in one stanza, each with இதுதாண்டி, 'beyond this', from 2123: the body is to be seen through, not merely despised. உப்பிட்ட பாண்டம் is the clay pot cured with salt, kept yet brittle; பீத்தத் துருத்தி the torn wind-skin.

reading: The mother bore me and the father raised me; without taking them for strangers, hear the particulars of this, blissful girl.
nuance: வேத்தாள் is read as வேற்றாள், a stranger. The stanza is a hinge: the plain parents of a plain birth lead into the inquiry of 2127 to 2133, which ends by asking whether those same parents are lasting. A coded reading, with Shakti and Siva as the parents as in 2122, is also possible.

reading: Thinking this carcass great, I sat and wasted my time; when I looked to see which carcass is my own, I did not find one clearly, blissful girl.
nuance: சொந்தச் சடலம், a body that is one's own, is what the search fails to find; the body is held but not owned.

reading: With the woman who delighted in the wedding show, then bearing and raising children, not knowing that it becomes a corpse show, why babble in vain, blissful girl?
nuance: மணக்கோலம் and பிணக்கோலம், wedding array and corpse array, differ by one syllable, and the stanza turns on that rhyme.

reading: When I looked closely into where all things came from, it appeared clearly to me that their origin is in good earth, blissful girl.
nuance: The earth argument of 2129 to 2132: things come from earth, the body's earth is fired into a pot, all things are earth, and what is of earth perishes. மண் is both the element and the soil.

reading: After death they take the body and entomb it, and some days later take that earth and fire it into a pot that serves the people of the world, blissful girl.
nuance: சமாதி here is the burial, as of a siddha, not the yogic state. The body's earth becomes a useful pot: the stanza is matter-of-fact where Tirumular's potter verses are elegiac.

reading: When one pauses to consider that all things are earth, the Lord is there in each of them, clinging like the oil in sesame, blissful girl.
nuance: The sesame image is the Siddhars' standard figure for pervasion that cannot be seen; here it answers the earth argument, so that the reduction of all things to earth does not leave them godless.

reading: What is born on earth perishes; what is watched and kept perishes; what the eye sees perishes: see and know this, blissful girl.
Are the parents who bore you lasting? Are the body, birth and kin lasting? Are the others lasting? Is the wife you took lasting, blissful girl?
nuance: சதம் (lasting, real) is asked five times and never affirmed; Pattinathar's 249 denies the same word seven times and then affirms it of the Lord's feet. The question runs over the chapter break into 2134.

title: சங்கிலிச் சித்தர் பாடல்
theme: The close of Sangili Siddhar's kummi: no one is lasting once the soul leaves its cage, so the way is the suzhumunai, yoga without craving, the breath that turns night to day and the single expanse. Holy baths, temple rounds, forest wandering and ritual observance are set against the one test, whether the running mind has stopped and the fourth state, silence, has been reached; and the song ends by telling how Bogar came and named the poet Sangili Siddhar for the chain he wore at his neck.
structure_note: Eleven stanzas. 2134 answers 2133 (no one is lasting); 2135 and 2144 frame the rest with the poet's lineage from Bogar, his பாட்டன்; 2136 to 2138 give the method (suzhumunai, yoga without desire, the night made day); 2139 to 2143 weigh kin, pilgrimage, forest penance, ritual and learning against silence.
source_issues: 2144 line 4: சாற்றைத்தெரியும் is not a regular form; read as சாற்றினதைத் தெரிவாய் or சாற்றைத் தெரி (know the proclamation). The reading is uncertain.
2137 line 2: சுட் டறுத்து த்தள்ளி has a stray space before த்தள்ளி; read சுட்டறுத்துத் தள்ளி.
2141 line 1 is a syllable short against the kummi metre (காடு மலைகள் அலைந்தாலும்); a word may be lost.
The chapter break at 2133/2134 cuts a question from its answer; see ch108.

reading: Whoever remains, they are not lasting; when our soul leaves the cage and goes, you will see clearly that not one of the townsfolk is lasting, blissful girl.
nuance: கூடு, the cage or nest, is the body the soul leaves; the answer to 2133's string of questions is that no one is சதம், neither the dying nor the townsfolk who outlive him.

reading: Having learned this way, as a siddha both here and in the beyond, know as your own the word of my grandfather, the rishi Bogar, blissful girl.
nuance: பாட்டன், grandfather, is a lineage term; with 2110 (Thirumular as guru) it places the poet in Bogar's line. இகத்தும் பரத்தும், here and beyond, is the siddha's double competence, the claim the medical and alchemical Siddhars make for their art.

reading: Those who wander without knowing the way are crores upon crores in this great land; those who have come to know the suzhumunai have found the way of ease, blissful girl.
nuance: The whole world's wandering is set against one anatomical knowledge; சுகவழி, the way of ease or bliss, picks up the refrain's ஆனந்தம்.

reading: Desire gone, having seen the wisdom of grace, having burnt off and thrown out vain manliness, letting go attachment, do yoga and live in this world, blissful girl.
nuance: வீண் ஆண்மை, vain manliness, may be sexual vigour, to be burnt off as the celibate yogi's discipline, or self-assertion. இந்தப் பாரினில் வாழ்வாய் keeps the yogi in the world, which is the Siddhars' usual stance against the renouncer's departure.

reading: Having turned night into day and known it, having seen and known the one expanse, if you quickly learn this method, this world will praise you, blissful girl.
nuance: இரவைப் பகலாய் இருத்தி is cipher: tradition reads night and day as the moon and sun breaths (left and right channels), so that making night day is bringing the breath to the sun side or the centre; a plainer reading is wakefulness kept through sleep. ஏக வெளி, the single expanse, is the inner space that other Siddhars call the place without night and day.

reading: What if the parents who bore you are alive, what if the wife you took and the children are there? If one does not do good tapas, see, we belong to Yama, blissful girl.
nuance: இருந்தால் என்ன, 'what if they are there', is Pattinathar's formula (277); the stanza adds what the kin cannot prevent, that without tapas one is Yama's kin (நமனுக்கு நாம் சொந்தம்), turning the word for ownership against the family.

reading: Though you bathe at holy waters, though you go round many temples, though you take darshan of the images, say: is the fourth, silence, there, blissful girl?
nuance: நாலாம் மோனம், the fourth that is silence, is read by tradition as the fourth state (துரியம்) beyond waking, dream and sleep; it can also be silence as the fourth path after chariyai, kiriyai and yoga, which fits 2121. On either reading the pilgrimage acts are not condemned, they are asked whether they have produced it.

reading: Though one wanders forests and hills, though one performs ritual observances, for those who have not stopped the running mind the supreme arising does not come, blissful girl.
nuance: கன்மானுட்டானம், the performance of prescribed ritual acts, and forest penance are both measured by one thing, whether the சித்தம் has stopped running. பர உற்பனம் repeats 2119's word for the Supreme's arising in oneself.

reading: Those who have not burnt away the delusion of the world of maya and the infatuation that has fallen on fair women never reach the house of release, blissful girl.
nuance: The two delusions are named together and given one remedy, burning (தீயா, from தீய்த்தல்); the world's maya and a woman's attraction are the same kind of thing for the stanza.

reading: Though one knows the four kinds of arts, though one knows the ways of jnana, only those who know the higher silence reach the release that does not sleep, blissful girl.
nuance: நாலாவகைக் கலைகள் may be the four Vedas, four classes of learning, or the sixty-four arts counted in four; even ஞான வழிகள், the ways of jnana as taught, are placed below மோனம், which 2140 called the fourth. துஞ்சா வீடு, the release that does not sleep, is release that does not lapse or die.

reading: While he wore a chain at his neck and did good tapas and yoga there, my grandfather came and proclaimed him 'Sangili Siddhar': know the word, blissful girl.
nuance: The stanza explains the poet's name, Sangili (chain), and attributes it to Bogar, the பாட்டன் of 2135; it is the song's signature. The third person (அணிந்துகொண்டு ... இருக்கையிலே ... என்று) is the poet speaking of himself.

title: திரிகோணச் சித்தர் பாடல் (கலிவெண்பா)
theme: The opening of Thirikona Siddhar's kalivenba, a single run-on poem of praise: Siva is the supreme guru, the one form in which Vishnu, Brahma and Rudra shone, the great faith that sees no difference among the disputing sects, the one who is beginning, middle and end, who became the three gunas, the senses and the three impurities, who is the five, eight and fifty-one letters and the pranava, who walks at the root beyond the reach of ida, pingala and the sushumna, and who, false to the false and true to the true, takes a guru's form to free his old servants.
structure_note: The whole work (2145 to 2234) is one kalivenba; each unit here is a two-line slice whose last word begins the next unit's clause, so readings are of the sense that runs across the cut. 2145 to 2149 invoke Siva as guru and as the one behind the Trinity and the sects; 2150 to 2156 are his epithets as Lord of the cosmos; 2157 to 2169 describe him as the one who takes every quality, letter and form, who is beyond the channels and beyond description, and who descends as guru. The epithets continue into chapter 111.
source_issues: 2157 (thirikonar:13) has only one line where every other unit of the kalivenba has two; a line is missing, and the sense is carried by the words that frame it.
The units are mechanical two-line slices of one continuous kalivenba, so almost every unit ends with a word that belongs grammatically to the next unit; readings follow the sense across the cut.

reading: Siva alone is the supreme guru, the preceptor; his feet alone, every day, are what one holds to; and he is the one behind Vishnu, whose epithet the run-on line begins.
nuance: The unit ends in நவநீத, which belongs to the next unit (the butter-stealing, cloud-coloured Vishnu). The first line sets the theme of the whole poem: the guru is Siva, and Siva comes as guru (2168 to 2170).

reading: The blue cloud-coloured one who blossomed gold (Vishnu of the fresh butter), the four-faced one who flashed lightning from his sensing mouth, Brahma the Veda-lord, and the red-matted one of the south: all three are named as the forms of the one Lord of 2147.
nuance: பொறிவாய் மின்பூத்த is obscure; it may describe Brahma's mouths as sparking with the Veda. நான்முகனும் வேதாவும் may name one god twice or Brahma and a separate Veda-lord. தென்பூத்த carries into 2147 to qualify the red-haired Rudra.

reading: The red-matted one too: the Lord arose alone, as the one form in which all these shone with lustre; and he is the great faith (2148) that argues no Vedas.
nuance: ஒக்கத் தனிவந்து உதித்த: the Trinity are not three gods but one Lord who rose alone bearing all their lustre. தர்க்கமிடும் carries into 2148 to qualify the Vedas and shastras as things that dispute.

reading: The many sects need disputing Vedas and shastras; he is the great faith that sees no difference among them, and his sound subsides into nada (2149).
nuance: பெருஞ்சமயம் is set against பலசமயம்: the one great religion against the many. The claim is not that sects are false but that difference (பேதம்) is not seen from the great one. 2151 names the attitude சமரசம்.

reading: He is the one who experiences, with sound subsiding into nada and desire subsiding in the house of the light-space; and his feet rest in the heart of devotees who worship (2150).
nuance: ஒளியம்பரமனையில் I read as ஒளி அம்பர மனையில், the house that is the space of light; tradition takes such space as the inner expanse of awareness. அனுபவிப்போன் makes God the experiencer, a Siddhar turn: the state the yogi reaches is what God already is.

reading: His soft feet are the fragrant lotus that took root and opened in the petals of the heart-spring of servants who worship; and he appears in all eight directions (2151).
nuance: The heart is a spring (சுனை) in which the Lord's foot-lotus blooms; the image makes worship the water, not the offering. எண்டிக்கும் carries into 2151.

reading: Appearing as every kind in the eight directions, he stays as concord; he does not divide, and his simplicity has no guile; he is the first (2152).
nuance: சாதியான் can mean one who appears as every species or as every caste; either way the next word, சமரசம், makes him the harmony among them. பேதமையான் is odd praise, since பேதைமை is folly; here it seems to mean guileless simplicity, as the following வஞ்சம் இலா suggests. ஆதி carries into 2152.

reading: He is the beginning as first, middle and end, and ending them, he is the light of the open void; and across a hundred crore births (2153) he gives release.
nuance: சிதலாய் is unclear; சிதல் is the termite, so a crumbling or scattering may be meant, as the ending of all three phases into the void-light. வெளியொளி (light of the open) is the Siddhars' name for the Lord beyond form, picked up in 2168.

reading: Through a hundred crore births, meditating Shakti and mantra as himself, the whole First One gives release; and his red matted hair is wound up (2154).
nuance: Who meditates is ambiguous: the Lord who holds Shakti and mantra as himself, or the soul who through many births comes to meditate them as itself and is given release. சுத்திய carries into 2154 to describe the wound red hair.

reading: He of the wound red hair does not enter the hearts of those who, though they have mastered the state of yoga, do not aim at him; he wears the young moon and his throat holds poison (2155).
nuance: The verse separates yoga from devotion: yogic attainment without taking the Lord as the mark (குறி) leaves the heart empty of him. This qualifies the whole work's yoga teaching in 2188 to 2194.

reading: Poison-throated, a vision hard to seek, Lord of many crore eggs, light that is formless and formed; and he loves the red lotus (2156).
nuance: அருவுருவான் (formless-formed) is the Siddhanta middle term between form and formlessness, taken up in 2168 where he is beyond both.

reading: Loving the red lotus-bud, the sea and the mountain, he is the one whose three acts are a play; and he is the Siva-siddha (2157) whose word makes things known.
nuance: மூன்று தொழில் is three acts, not the Siddhanta five; creation, keeping and dissolving are meant. சூதுபுரி makes them a game or trick. முண்டகச் செம்போதம் is read as the red lotus bud; போதம் could also be knowledge, giving 'red knowledge'.

reading: The Siva-siddha who set things so that they can be discerned by those who recite; in turiya (2158) he comes to birth as atom, mote and flame.
nuance: Only one line survives for this unit (see source_issues), so the sense is carried by the words that frame it: ஓதும் from 2156 and துரியத்தில் leading into 2158. சிவசித்தன் names the Lord as the siddha.

reading: In turiya he comes as atom, as dust-mote, as flame-light, firming into a form, and is born; and (2159) he becomes the gunas, senses and impurities.
nuance: தோத்தி and தேத்தி are obscure; தோற்றி (appearing) and தேற்றி (firming) are the likely words. The sequence atom, mote, flame, form is a descent from the subtle to the gross, read by tradition as the Lord's own taking of embodiment. சாத்தரிய at the end is unclear (perhaps சாத்திரிய, 'of the shastras') and recurs at 2169.

reading: Having become the three gunas, the five senses and the three impurities, he stays as every quality and gives grace; and he is the letters (2160).
nuance: The Lord is not only beyond the gunas and malas but is them: the bonds themselves are his grace at work. This is a stronger claim than Siddhanta usually makes, where the impurities are other than Pati.

reading: He is the five letters, the eight letters, the fifty-one letters, the tender letter, and everywhere the pranava; and he is the little meaning (2161).
nuance: The five letters are Siva's mantra; the eight may be the eight-syllable mantra (ஓம் நமசிவாய with its seed syllables); the fifty-one are the Sanskrit alphabet as the matrika. பிஞ்செழுத்து (the tender or young letter) is unexplained; it may be the unspoken letter beyond the fifty. கொஞ்சப் carries into 2161.

reading: As meaning, as delusion, as flaw, as word, as grace, the Blissful One stood alone; and his vision does not darken (2162).
nuance: The list pairs opposites, meaning and delusion, flaw and grace, so that nothing is outside him; the thought matches 2159. புரையாய் (as flaw or cavity) is odd praise and may be a copying error for பொறையாய்.

reading: He is unclouded vision to those who have seen, and for those who have not he stands as form and as the subtle; he is the worker, and his rule (2163) is beyond the channels.
nuance: The Lord's mode depends on the seer: direct sight for the realised, form and hidden subtlety for the rest. தொழிலாளி, the worker, picks up the three acts of 2156.

reading: Beyond the reach of ida, pingala and the whirl-point, he walks at the furthest root; he owns the sea and rides the bull (2164).
nuance: சுழி is read as சுழிமுனை, the sushumna; the three channels are the yogi's instruments, and the Lord is said to be beyond even them, yet walking மூலக் கடையில், at the root's end, which tradition takes as the muladhara. The plain sense is that technique does not reach him; the coded sense places him at the base of the body.

reading: The one of bonds who dwells in the house of Parashakti the kutilai, the One without birth or death, the yogi (2165) who cannot be described.
nuance: குடிலை is the primal bent power from which nada and bindu arise, here identified with Parashakti; her house is the Lord's dwelling. பாசன் may mean the Lord of the bonds, who binds, or be a variant of பாசம்-bearer. பிறப்புறப்பு is read as birth and departure.

reading: The yogi of whom none can say small or great, red or black, short or tall; and his bond is mingled with the senses (2166).
nuance: The apophatic list, no size, colour or height, is the Siddhar way of refusing the icon; it belongs with 2168 and 2199. பொறிகலந்த carries into 2166.

reading: He whose bond is mingled with the senses is, for those who have cut the bond, the stainless gem-light of the hall, and the loving one (2167).
nuance: மாசத்தான் is read as மாசற்றான், stainless; the first spelling would say the opposite. மண்டத்தான் suggests மண்டபம், the hall, so the gem-light recalls Chidambaram, named again at 2197 and 2206.

reading: To the false he is false and to the true he is truth, dwelling in each heart, standing in the open; he is the Father (2168) beyond form.
nuance: The Lord answers to the quality of the seeker, as in 2162; the false find only falsehood. வெளிநின்றோன் (standing in the open) recalls the வெளியொளி of 2152.

reading: The Father, the great Mayan beyond form, formlessness, light, space and seed, became guru (2169) and praised, freed his old servants.
nuance: The list surpasses 2155: not formless-formed but beyond both, and beyond the light and space that the earlier units used as his names. கன மாயன் (the great Mayan) is Vishnu's epithet applied to Siva, consistent with 2147 where the Trinity is one.

reading: Becoming guru, he removes the encircling deeds of the old servants who praise him, changes their form, and makes them his own; and he is the great yogi who took a human body (2170).
nuance: உருமாத்தி (changing the form) is the guru's work on the disciple, which tradition reads as the transformation of the body itself and not only of the mind. சாத்தரிய recurs from 2158 and is as obscure here.

title: திரிகோணச் சித்தர் பாடல் (கலிவெண்பா)
theme: The kalivenba turns from Siva to the guru Anandan, the great yogi in a human coat: lord of the gold, silver and stone mountains, the Omkara hill of eight peaks, the man of Kayapuri. Then the guru becomes a warrior who wipes out sect-hatred, tramples the whole order of caste, cuts egoism at the root and routs the mind's and anger's mischief, and finally a horseman: the body is made a horse, the directional wind its cord, the mind its saddle and anger its stirrups, and ridden through the five senses in turiya into the inner fort of bindu and nada, the horse-master who keeps his servants out of hell.
structure_note: 2170 to 2179 praise the guru Anandan by his attributes and places; 2180 to 2187 are the guru as fighter against sects, caste, egoism and the mind's mischief, ending at the drum of silence; 2188 to 2194 are the horse cipher of breath-yoga, each unit adding a piece of harness. Each unit's last word opens the next.
source_issues: Unit 36 is missing: 2179 is thirikonar:35 and 2180 is thirikonar:37, so two lines of the kalivenba are lost between them and 2179's last word does not connect to 2180.
2179 (துரமே கரமாய்) and 2183 (அடர்ந்தமக வாகைக்கு அடங்காப் படர்ந்ததெரு) do not parse cleanly and are probably corrupt.

reading: The great yogi who took the shape of a human coat, the Blissful One whose grace runs before even the bull-rider's, honey-thick (2171) on the lotus.
nuance: மானிடச் சட்டை (human coat) treats the guru's body as a garment Siva put on; the poem has moved from God to the man called ஆனந்தன், named in 2171 and 2172 as எங்கள் குரு. யானிடப முந்தும் is obscure; I read இடபம், the bull, so that the guru's grace precedes Siva's own, but the words may be corrupt.

reading: The god hard even for the one on the red lotus (Brahma) to see, the Blissful One who dwells in the body-stain of his servants, our guru (2172).
nuance: அங்கலமத் தேயுறையும் is read as அங்க மலத்தே உறையும், dwelling in the limbs' impurity: the guru lives in the devotees' bodies, impure as they are. A different division gives அங்கலம், a place name, but none is known.

reading: Our guru Anandan, who removes the sorrow of the devotees who love him so that they stand firm, and asks on their behalf; and he is god to the mountains (2173) that are worshipped.
nuance: யாசிக்கும் (begging, asking) makes the guru an intercessor who asks for his disciples; it can also be read as the guru who himself begs, the wandering ascetic. பூசிக்கும் carries into 2173.

reading: He is himself the god to the worshipped mountain of gold, the mountain of silver and the fair mountain of stone, and to the many hills (2174) whose peaks are eight.
nuance: The gold mountain is Meru, the silver Kailasa, the stone perhaps Arunachala, where Siva is a hill; Trikonamalai (Trincomalee), the poet's name-place, is a rock. Making the guru god of these sites turns pilgrimage inward, as 2174 does with the Omkara hill.

reading: He of the firm mountain that is Omkara, whose eight peaks run as the tender shoot of the letter; and firmly (2175) he is the river of Siva's mercy.
nuance: A hill of eight peaks made of the Om-letter: tradition reads the eight as the eight parts of the pranava or the eight-letter mantra of 2160, and the hill as the body with the letter rising in it. The literal sense, a sacred mountain, stands beside this.

reading: He made the river of Siva's mercy flow so that the marks of the servants who seek him are ground to dust; and the servants who do tapas (2176) lose their old deeds.
nuance: சின்னம் (sign, mark) is unclear; the outward marks of the devotees, their sectarian emblems, or their stains may be meant. ஆடும் (dancing) makes the mercy a dancing river.

reading: The servants who do tapas lose their old deeds and reach the flower of his feet; he planted great bliss in the word they utter; and he is (2177) the chaste one in whom they count fullness.
nuance: பேரின்பம் நாட்டினான்: bliss is planted in speech itself, the guru's or the disciple's, not only in silence; 2196 then calls the guru a silent yogi, so both are held.

reading: Known as the steadfast one, with a heart that does not waver, the fair man of the town Kayapuri; and (2178) he of the slight fragrance.
nuance: கற்புடையான் applies a wife's chastity to the guru: unswerving fidelity. காயாபுரி is where the poet later settles (2209); it can be a town's name or, as a coded reading, the body-city (காயம், body). அற்பவிசை carries into 2178.

reading: He of the hill of qualities, fragrant with the honey that flows untouched by bees, caught in a channel; and (2179) in the cut...
nuance: Honey that no bee has touched, dripping of itself, is a figure tradition takes for the nectar that flows in the yogi's head without any outer cause. வாய்ந்தாறைக் கொண்டு is unclear; I read 'taking it in a river'. துண்டத் carries into 2179 and is not clear.

reading: His arm is a distance (?), the ascetic in whom the arrow of the never-resting breath thunders; and the one who takes up the hand (2180) of the servants.
nuance: The unit is damaged: துரமே கரமாய் does not parse, and the following unit is numbered 37, so a unit (36) is lost between them (see source_issues). சரம் can be arrow or breath; ஓயாச் சரமே முழங்கும் as the ceaseless sounding breath fits the horse cipher that follows.

reading: He who took the banner of the ascetic's garb, saying 'the servants' many enemies must be plundered'; and fierce (2181) he wipes out sect-hatred.
nuance: The ascetic's garb is here a war-flag, not a disguise; the enemies to be plundered are inner, as 2181 to 2187 make clear: sect-hatred, caste, egoism, anger, the mind's mischief.

reading: He wiped out the hatred of sects, trampled and ground the whole order of caste underfoot, and cut (2182) egoism at the root.
nuance: சாதிமுறை எல்லாம் குமைய மிதித்து: not a plea for better caste relations but the trampling of the order itself. The verb is the guru's, so caste is destroyed in the disciple by the guru, not by argument.

reading: He cut egoism out by the root and threw it down, and lopped the part that had grown ashamed, so that (2183) its lingering branches were seen.
nuance: ஆணவம் is the first of the three impurities, the soul's self-centredness. நாணமுற்ற பாகம் (the part that had grown ashamed) is obscure; it may be the remnant of ego that survives as shame, or a corrupt phrase.

reading: He flung the branches that still followed so they went like a storm, and to the thick ... the spreading street (2184) and the hall.
nuance: The second line is damaged: அடர்ந்தமக வாகைக்கு அடங்காப் படர்ந்ததெரு does not yield a clear sense; வாகை is the victory-flower, so a victory that does not stay contained may be meant. The image continues the uprooting of egoism as a tree.

reading: In the street and the hall, before the many castes, wearing the holy ash, he trampled falsehood and shouted (2185), scattering the mischief of anger.
nuance: The subject is the guru: he wears the ash in public, where castes are many, and treads lies underfoot. A different reading makes the many castes the ash-wearers who tread in falsehood, which would make the unit an attack on ritual. The first fits the run of 2180 to 2187 better.

reading: He scooped up and scattered the mischief of anger, gathered it, seized the mischief of the mind and shaped it, 'this for you, this for me', and (2186) trampled the mischief of recitation.
nuance: உனக்கென்கென் is read as உனக்கென் எனக்கென், 'yours and mine', the division the mind makes; the guru takes it and remakes it. குறும்பு (mischief, insolence) is repeated through 2185 to 2186 for anger, mind and speech.

reading: He trampled the mischief of recitation, leapt at Death's messenger and drove him off; and (2187) full of the elements he cuts ignorance.
nuance: ஓது குறும்பு is the insolence of mere recitation, book-learning without realisation; the theme returns in 2221 and 2229. Driving off Yama's messenger is the Siddhar claim to conquer death.

reading: He cuts the delusion of ignorance; he is the drum of experience, true knowledge and silence; and the hooded serpent (2188) is his horse.
nuance: வேளத்தான் is unclear; I read a drum (வேள = a kind of drum) sounding knowledge and silence together, but the word may be a place or a title. பைநாகம், the hooded snake, carries into 2188, where the body becomes a horse; the serpent and the horse are both cipher terms for breath or kundalini.

reading: He changed the long body, pressed it and made it a horse, bound it, fitted the bridle that sounds, and (2189) caught the thin cord called the wind of the directions.
nuance: The horse (பரி) is the cipher for breath, and the rider is the வாசியான் of 2194; வாசி means both horse and breath. The long body made into a horse is read by tradition as the breath-body drawn into the practice. கடிவாளம் (bridle) is restraint of the breath; the following units add rope, saddle and stirrups.

reading: Caught by the thin cord called the directional wind, he tightened it with the halter-rope and trained it; unmoving (2190) he set the saddle of mind.
nuance: திசைவாயு, the wind of the directions, is the outgoing breath that scatters toward the senses; it is a thin thread by which the horse is caught, so the breath is both the horse and the rein. குசை is the rope used to halter cattle.

reading: He set and tightened the saddle called mind, fitted the stirrups called anger, and (2191) with heavy snake-binding gait he drove.
nuance: Mind is the saddle and anger the stirrups: neither is discarded; they are harness by which the breath-horse is ridden. This is a different teaching from the suppression of mind and anger; here they become controls.

reading: In the snake-binding gait, the trot and the shaking walk, he let it reach the high sky and drew it in within; and in sorrow (2192) he shattered the mountain of the body.
nuance: நாகபந்தம், சாரி and நடைதுலுக்கு are horse-gaits, read by tradition as modes of breath, the coiled serpent among them. மாகமுற விட்டு உள்ளடக்கி: the breath is sent up to the sky (the crown) and held within, the retention of pranayama. சோகப் carries into 2192 oddly; it may be corrupt.

reading: He shattered the mountain of the body, the eightfold city, leapt over the five senses that slide down, and in turiya (2193) ran to the inner fort.
nuance: புரியட்ட காயம் (புரியட்டகம்) is the subtle body of eight constituents in Siddhanta; it is here a mountain to be broken, not refined. The jump over the senses into turiya is the yogi's passage past waking, dream and sleep.

reading: In turiya he ran to the inner fort called bindu and nada, and in the dance destroyed the boundary of the nadi that withers; and dancing (2194) he is the horse-master.
nuance: The inner fort of bindu-nada is the seat of the subtle sound and light where the breath ends. நாடி வரம்பு அழித்து, destroying the channel's limit, is taken by tradition as the merging of the channels into the sushumna. கூத்து and ஆடியிடும் make the whole ride a dance, recalling Siva's.

reading: He is the horse-master who rose with swelling fury so that the devotees who serve him do not fall into hell; and seeing him they worship (2195).
nuance: வாசியான் closes the cipher: the one who has the horse and the one who has the breath are one word. The fury (சினம்) is the guru's, turned against the servants' enemies of 2180, so anger used as stirrup in 2190 is the guru's own.

title: திரிகோணச் சித்தர் பாடல் (கலிவெண்பா)
theme: The praise of the guru closes with his sovereignty and silence: his own law his only law, a Siva-yogi of silence who never opens his mouth in anger, the disciple of Chitrambalavan, the knowledge-light with no name, the Karunai Ananda muni who rains bliss and quenches maya's glare, beyond the reach of ida, pingala and the sushumna. Then the poet speaks in his own voice: called a libertine, with enemies everywhere, he wept his way to the guru's country, found the town Kayapuri and settled there, where the Lady Sivananda Valli, Trikonavalli, raised the daughter of kutilai and set her to the art of the staff-dance, making her puppet dance through every sect and scripture until, like a cloud that has flashed, she cooled and knew herself.
structure_note: 2195 to 2206 end the guru's epithets, from his self-law to Chitrambalam's lotus feet; 2207 to 2211 are the poet's own arrival at Kayapuri and the Lady who names and raises the girl; 2212 to 2219 are the girl's training in dance, sects and scriptures, ending in self-knowledge and the old woman who turns to instruct her (which chapter 113 carries). The units remain two-line slices of one kalivenba, and the identity of the girl is the poem's cipher.
source_issues: 2199 is a chain of rhyming epithets (பரியான் உரியான் பசியான் பொசியான்) whose sense cannot be fixed; 2210 யூதார், 2215 முந்நூனூறும் and 2217 கிரிகித்தேன் வம்பி are unclear words, probably corrupt.
2218 has a full stop after தளதளத்தாள் in the middle of the second line, the only punctuation in the work; the kalivenba's run-on continues regardless.

reading: His own command is the only command upon himself; he has no other law over him; and for all time (2196) his fame does not change.
nuance: The guru's autonomy is the claim: no scripture, sect or god rules him, which the attacks of 2181 and 2221 to 2233 presuppose.

reading: He of unchanging fame and the honey garland, the Siva-yogi of silence who does not open his mouth to rage; and straight (2197) his guru is Chitrambalavan.
nuance: வாய்திறந்து சீறாத: silence is defined as not opening the mouth in anger, a narrower and more practical mounam than the stilling of all thought. Yet 2194 gave him fury; the anger is turned on the disciples' enemies, not spoken.

reading: He whose two feet were raised seeking the grace of the feet of the guru who ruled him, Chitrambalavan; and (2198) he wears the garb of Siva.
nuance: சிற்றம்பலவன் is the Lord of the little hall at Chidambaram and also, here, the name or title of the guru's own guru; the poem does not separate the two. இருபதத்தான் is read as the one of two feet; it could also be the one of two states.

reading: Wearing Siva's garb, he rises and shines on the seat of the rich lotus, Jnanaprakasan, the light of knowledge; and if he moves (2199)...
nuance: ஞானப் பிரகாசன் may be a title or the guru's proper name; a Gnanaprakasar is known among Chidambaram teachers, but the poem gives no date. The lotus seat is the yogi's posture and the heart-lotus of 2150. ஆடில் carries into 2199 and its sense there is unclear.

reading: He is the horse and the skin, the hungry and the sodden (?), the great and the rare, the one without a name; and turiya (2200) he passes beyond.
nuance: A chain of rhymed epithets whose sense is mostly sound: பரியான் (horse, or 'large'), உரியான் (skin, or 'fitting'), பசியான், பொசியான். The last three words are the firm ones: great, rare, nameless. பரி recalls the horse of 2188, and turiya at the unit's end connects to 2200's list of what he has passed.

reading: Beyond turiya and its faults, beyond the shining space, beyond knowledge itself, stands the one of the golden feet; and cool (2201) is the muni of compassion.
nuance: தீதம் கடந்து is read as beyond faults; தீதம் may be an error for அதீதம், the state past turiya, which would make the first two words 'beyond turiya-atita'. Either way the guru is placed beyond the highest avastha and beyond போதம், knowledge, as 2168 placed Siva beyond light and space.

reading: The cool Karunai Ananda muni, the Varuna who came to be seen and worshipped, the rain-cloud of bliss; and dawn-red (2202) his radiance stands.
nuance: கருணை ஆனந்தமுனி gives the guru a fuller name than the ஆனந்தன் of 2171; the Kural's rain that makes virtue possible becomes the guru raining bliss.

reading: Like the great light that stands holding the red radiance of dawn, he is the great one who turns off the glare of maya; and undying (2203) he shows the true thing.
nuance: Maya too has a radiance (பிரகாசம்), and the guru's light is set against it as dawn against lamplight; the attraction of the world is admitted to be bright.

reading: He shows the true substance and takes the servants who long for it as the wealth in his hand, the compassionate one; and he who enjoys (2204) body, wealth and life.
nuance: கைபொருளாய்க் கொண்ட: the disciples are the guru's property, the inverse of 2231 where the disciple is told whom to accept. 2204 then names the three things, body, goods and life, that the disciple gives in return.

reading: He takes body, wealth and life with the water of gift and changes the deeds of the gross body, the leveller; and (2205) he is the vision ida and pingala cannot reach.
nuance: உதகத்தால் கொண்டு, taking with water, is the ritual of giving (the water poured over a gift), so the disciple makes a formal gift of self to the guru, and the guru in return alters the karma. சமனன் may be the impartial one or a form of சமன், Yama, who takes life; the first fits the context.

reading: The vision that ida, pingala and the whirl-point cannot reach, the fierce one who ended lust, murder and theft, and without wavering (2206) he took possession.
nuance: The phrase repeats 2163 almost exactly and applies to the guru what was said of Siva, so that the poem's identification of the two is complete. குடோரி is read as a fierce or formidable one; the word is uncertain. Lust, killing and theft are the three gross sins of the Buddhist and Jain lists too.

reading: I am the servant of the servants who hold to the lotus feet of Chitrambalavan who took me; he took me (2207) though people called me a libertine.
nuance: The first personal statement: the poet places himself under the devotees, not under the guru directly, the adiyaar-of-adiyaar formula of Saiva humility. ஆட்கொண்ட is repeated three times across the unit.

reading: 'This man is a libertine,' people said, and I suffered; everywhere I looked became enemy, I sweated, (2208) was shaken and wept.
nuance: தூர்த்தன் is a wastrel or debauchee; the poet records the charge without denying it. The confession opens an autobiography that 2208 to 2211 continue, unusual in the Siddhar corpus where the self is mostly a cipher.

reading: Shaken, blaming fate, with tears running, confused, I came to the guru's country, and shining before me (2209) I saw the town Kayapuri.
nuance: விதிவிதித்து, cursing or laying it on fate, is the ordinary man's response that the poem leaves behind on reaching the guru's land. குருநாடு may be a region or the guru's domain.

reading: I saw with my eyes the town Kayapuri; I went to that town, was sheltered and settled there; and undying (2210) the Lady named her.
nuance: காயாபுரி may be a real town (a Kayapuri or Kayambur is not securely identified) or the body-city, காயம் being body; the poem's method elsewhere favours the double sense: the poet entered his own body under the guru's teaching. ஆதரித்து, sheltered, is the refuge-taking of a disciple.

reading: The Lady named her Sivananda Valli, the famed Trikonavalli, and with the support of those who study (?) (2211) she raised the daughter of kutilai.
nuance: The Lady, மாது, is the goddess, who names a girl Sivananda Valli; ஓது திரிகோணவல்லி may be the Lady's own name, the goddess of the triangle (which gives the poet his name Thirikonar), or the girl's second name. யூதார் is obscure. The girl is the poem's cipher, raised in 2211 as the daughter of kutilai, the primal power: tradition would take her as the soul, or as kundalini, or as knowledge awakened in the poet.

reading: The daughter of kutilai whom she fondled and raised, she sent to the skilled art of the staff-dance; and gracefully (2212) she danced changing feet.
nuance: குடிலை மகள், daughter of the bent primal power, suggests kundalini or the young goddess (வாலை) of the Siddhars; சிலம்பம் is the staff-dance or martial art, read by tradition as the discipline of breath and body. The plain story, a goddess raising a girl and training her, stands alongside and the poem does not resolve it.

reading: Dancing with changing feet, in the manner of kala and karana, switching above and playing in purity, changing the text (2213) she leapt across many sects.
nuance: கலாதி கரணவிதம்: the dance follows the modes of kala (phase, or the five kalas of the adhvas) and karana (dance-unit, or the inner instruments). சுத்தி விளையாட may be playing in purity or going round (சுற்றி). The dance is read as the soul's play through the tattvas.

reading: Joining in the clasp of hands, she leapt and trod on the body of many sects, treading them under; and gently (2214) she gathered the arts.
nuance: பலசமய மெய்லாகு தாவி அதன் மேல்மிதிக்க: the girl leaps onto the body of the sects and treads on them, which continues 2181's trampling of sect and caste, now as dance. கைலாகு பாய is read as striking a handclasp, a dance gesture.

reading: Gently she gathered the art of bharata dance and the handwork of crores of Vedas, and the words of vows (2215) she spoke herself.
nuance: The girl masters dance and Veda alike; the poem has her acquire every learning before the old woman tells her, in chapter 113, whom among the learned to refuse.

reading: Having studied the southern and northern books, she herself spoke crores of them and the three hundred and thirty (?); and in this land (2216) she made the puppet dance.
nuance: தென்னூல் வடநூல், Tamil and Sanskrit books, are set as equals. முந்நூனூறும் is unclear; a count of texts (three hundred, or the thirty and three hundred) is meant but the figure cannot be fixed.

reading: Made to dance the puppet, the puppet learned also many arts of singing; and known to the land (2217) is Trikonavalli.
nuance: பதுமை, the doll or puppet, is the body moved by the soul in the Siddhar image, or the soul moved by Shakti. Who makes it dance is the Lady; so the girl is the dancer and the puppet is what she animates, which suggests the girl is the inner power and the puppet the body.

reading: I went round the whole grandeur of the north mountain of the renowned Trikonavalli on this earth; and (2218) lightning-like she flashed.
nuance: கிரிகித்தேன் is unclear; I read circumambulating (கிரி, hill, with a verb of going round). The north mountain of the goddess of the triangle may be a shrine hill or, in the body-reading, the head. வம்பி is read as renowned (வம்பு) but may be an epithet of another sense.

reading: Like a cloud that has flashed and spent its lightning, her body cooled, and she knew herself and glowed; and the golden one (2219) looked to her ripeness.
nuance: தன்னை அறிந்த, she knew herself: the end of the girl's training is self-knowledge, and the image of the cloud that has discharged its lightning and grown cool is the calming after awakening. The poem's cipher of the girl here comes closest to the soul.

reading: The old woman who had learned the three gunas, looking at the golden one's ripeness, watched her face till it grew fragrant, cut off the crowd, and (2220) speaks to her.
