nuance: முதுகிழவி, the old woman, is the Lady of 2210 seen as the ancient one, Shakti who has mastered the gunas; she tests the girl's readiness (பக்குவம்) before teaching, as a guru does. தொக்கறுத்து is read as cutting off the gathering, that is, taking her aside; the word is uncertain. Her speech runs through chapter 113.

title: திரிகோணச் சித்தர் பாடல் (கலிவெண்பா)
theme: The old woman's instruction to the golden girl, and the end of the kalivenba: a rule for whom the awakened one should receive. Veda-and-Purana men bowing for show, pretenders of chariyai, wretched performers of kiriyai, fools who do not seek, the deceitful, shastra-paupers, the cotton-wads of gotra, book-ghosts, hatha-yoga idlers, left-hand adepts of Kama's text, name-dropping boasters, the mind-proud, sect-virtue gangs and kings of sham silence are all to be turned away; only the ancients of Siva-yoga and the owners of tapas, knowledge and silence are to be called in and told the Siva-substance, and the one who seeks the substance of knowledge is to be joined with grace.
structure_note: 2220 opens the address (listen, firm intellect); 2221 to 2222 set the scene at the gem-gate of turiya; 2223 to 2226 give the four paths, chariyai and kiriyai refused, yoga and jnana admitted; 2227 to 2233 list the kinds to refuse; 2234 closes the poem with the one to seek. The last unit is a single line, the natural close of a kalivenba.
source_issues: 2234 (thirikonar:91) has a single line, which is the normal close of a kalivenba and not a loss.
2228 தூரித்தர் and பஞ்சியளை, and 2231 பாசிப் பதப்பிலுக்கர், are unclear words, probably corrupt or dialectal.

reading: 'Lightning, gold of the mind-lotus where nectar grew, listen with firm understanding': the old woman opens her instruction, and the rare-to-tell (2221) Veda-men she names first.
nuance: The addressee is the girl of 2210 to 2219, so the instruction is Shakti's to the awakened soul; மனக்கமலப் பொன்னே, gold of the mind's lotus, makes her the thing that grew in the heart-lotus of 2150. The teaching that follows is about discernment of company, not about method.

reading: Men of Veda and Purana will bow to your lotus feet out of empty show; do not look them in the face; and in nada (2222) at the gate of turiya appear.
nuance: வெறும்பிலுக்கு, empty display: the scriptural men are not refused for error but for show. The awakened one is told to refuse even their homage, which inverts the usual order where the Vedic man is the honoured one.

reading: Appear at the gem-gate of turiya in nada, show your face in the open so that you are truly known, and then go inside, rarely; and (2223) the chariyai-men who proclaim.
nuance: துரியமணி வாசல், the gem-door of turiya, is read by tradition as the opening at the crown where the fourth state is entered; the awakened one shows herself there to be known and then withdraws within. முகம் சத்தே தெரிய is uncertain: 'so the face is truly seen' or 'the face in true being'. The plain image is of a woman at a doorway choosing whom to admit.

reading: The chariyai-men who proclaim, swelling with pride, will praise you to embrace you; do not go after them; and the praised (2224) kiriyai-fools.
nuance: சளுக்கர் is the proud, the puffed up; the first of the four Saiva paths, outward service, is here a pretension. The poem does not reject chariyai as such but those who make a show of it, the same charge as 2221.

reading: The wretched performers of kiriyai, the fools, will worry to reach your form; pass them by; and the Siva-yoga (2225) ancients admit.
nuance: அசடர், dolts: ritual worship, the second path, is given to fools. கடத்தி, convey past: they are not to be fought but set aside. 2225 then names the third path, yoga, as the first to be welcomed, so the four paths are graded by whom to let in.

reading: If the ancients of Siva-yoga come and prostrate before your flower-feet, call them inside without wavering and speak with them; and the first (2226) tapas-jnana-silence masters.
nuance: The yogis are received as equals in speech, பேசிக்கொள்; the jnanis of 2226 are to be told the Siva-substance. The awakened one is a hostess choosing guests, the Siddhar inversion of the disciple who seeks a teacher.

reading: If the owners of the first tapas, knowledge and silence come, do not shame them; call them and tell them the Siva-substance; and the (2227) fools who do not seek.
nuance: அவமானம் பண்ணாது: the only ones the girl might wrong by refusal are the silent knowers, so the instruction guards against the awakened one's own pride. சிவபொருள், the Siva-substance, is what is to be shared, and only with them.

reading: Do not get caught by the fools who do not seek the Siva-substance; do not cling to the deceitful who do not seek in thought; and the unbending (2228) shastra-paupers.
nuance: Two kinds are refused: fools who never seek and the deceitful who do not seek in the mind though they may in word; the test is inward seeking, not profession.

reading: Do not go near the shastra-paupers who do not bend; do not join the cotton-wads of gotra who argue; and the sutra- (2229) liars.
nuance: தூரித்தர் is read as தரித்திரர், paupers, those poor in everything but shastra; கோத்திரப் பஞ்சியளை, the cotton-wads of lineage, mocks those stuffed with gotra pride as cotton is stuffed; the word may also be பஞ்சையர், the destitute. தக்கமிடும் (arguing, bragging) qualifies them. சூத்திரப் carries into 2229.

reading: Do not take to the desire of lying idlers of the sutras; do not want the desire of the book-ghosts, the true idlers; and the hatha-yoga (2230) men learned in Kama's text.
nuance: புத்தகப்பேய், the book-ghost, is the strongest phrase of the chapter: one possessed by books. பொய்வீணர் and மெய்வீணர், false idlers and true idlers, seem to be a pair, the frauds and the sincerely useless; the second may also mean idlers about the body (மெய்). கையோகக் carries into 2230.

reading: Do not set your mind on the left-hand adepts of hatha yoga who have learned the text of Kama's arts, made for lust; and those who set up a name (2231) and babble.
nuance: கையோகம் (hand-yoga) is read as hatha yoga, the physical practice; வாமத்தார் are the left-hand tantrics, whose texts the poem calls Kama's book made for lust. The attack separates the Siddhars' breath-yoga from sexual tantra, a line not every Siddhar text draws.

reading: If the show-offs of mossy station who parade under a name come, push them away so that their hearts burn, and do not stand; and (2232) do not go to the mind-proud.
nuance: பாசிப் பதப் பிலுக்கர் is unclear; பாசி may be moss or a bead-string, so 'the show-offs of the bead-string station', wearers of rosaries for display. நாமமிட்டு may be taking a religious name or wearing the sect-mark called நாமம். நெஞ்செரிய, so their hearts burn: the only refusal told to be cruel.

reading: Do not go where the proud of mind are; do not aim at the desire of the man who gathers sect-virtue; and the detached (2233) kings of sham silence.
nuance: சீலமதக் கொத்தவன், he who bunches virtue by sect, is one whose morality is a badge of his faith. பற்றற்ற, detached, carries into 2233 as an ironic epithet for the silent rogues.

reading: If the mischievous kings of silence, who claim detachment, fall for you, send them off in the manner that fits them; and the one who seeks the substance of knowledge (2234) join.
nuance: மோனக் குறும்பரசர், kings of silence-mischief: men whose silence is a pose, matching the குறும்பு of anger, mind and recitation in 2185 to 2186. Against them 2226's owners of true silence are to be admitted, so silence itself is not the test; its honesty is.

reading: Praising the able ones who seek the substance of knowledge, join them and go with grace: the poem's last word to the awakened one.
nuance: The kalivenba ends on its single-line close with the one positive command after a dozen refusals: the company to keep is those who seek ஞானப்பொருள், and the going is அருளோடு, with grace, which the whole poem has made the guru's gift.

title: மௌனச்சித்தர் பாடல்
theme: Mounachiddhar's kuravanji: twelve stanzas in the first person plural, a company of Siddhars declaring what they have done and will do. They subdue the ego, seek the guru's and the Lord's feet by Manonmani's grace, bind the breath, kindle the fire at the root, sit in a mountain cave on kalpa without food or sleep, see the supreme open space and the light beyond the ninety-six tattvas, refuse kin, the sinful and the world's doings, and end with the 'I' of anava cut and tapas held as the only refuge.
structure_note: The stanzas are rhymed quatrains of vows (-வோம், -ந்தோம்), without a refrain. 2235 to 2239 give the devotional frame (light, Manonmani, the guru, elders, the thousand Siddhars); 2240 to 2245 the yogic method and its sights (breath, root fire, cave, nose-tip, the shakti-wheel, paraveli); 2246 closes on the ego cut away. The verb shifts once to the singular (2245 அறிந்து கொண்டேன் யானே, 2246 விடுத்தேன்).
source_issues: 2245 தய்யபர வெளி is probably a corrupt form (perhaps தெய்வ or தூய); உரைத்தனங்களை is unclear.
2235 is grammatically incomplete and runs into 2236; it reads as the opening frame of the poem.

reading: Seeking the great primal light every day, singing to win the grace of the Lord's feet, receiving the grace of Manonmani who is light, and holding in the mind the feet of Sukar.
nuance: The stanza is all participles and finishes in the next one, so it is a frame rather than a claim. சுகருடைய பாதம் may name the sage Suka as the poet's guru-line, or mean simply the feet of the blissful one; tradition often counts Suka among the Siddhars' teachers. Manonmani is the Shakti of the mind's transcendence, named again in 2239.

reading: Subduing pride and looking to the state of grace, setting the mind to know all the rare worlds, we will bow duly at the feet of the great, and practise yogic absorption with devotion every day.
nuance: ஆங்காரம், the ego as a faculty (ahankara), heads the chapter as it closes it in 2246. Devotion and yoga-nishtha are paired without strain: the kuravanji makes no quarrel between bhakti and method.

reading: Was it not by burning the ghost's nature that we saw the Brahma-state? Passing beyond Brahma's seat we took our place in the sushumna; not roaming like a dog, we stayed in tapas, having subdued the ego well and with dignity.
nuance: பிரமநிலை and பிரமபதி may be Brahman (the Supreme state) or Brahma the creator, whose seat in the yogic map is a lower centre; on the second reading the stanza is coded, the breath passing Brahma's centre and entering the central channel. நல்லதொரு ஆங்காரம், a 'good' ego that is subdued, is odd; the sense may be that even the good self-regard is held down.

reading: Trusting the deceitful life, we will not fall into anxieties; we will not tire of seeking the feet of the great sages; we will never look at those guilty of the five great sins; we will not forget the friendship of those who have cut off the bond of sinful deeds.
nuance: The stanza is about company: whom to seek, whom to refuse. பஞ்சமா பாதகர் are the doers of the five great sins of the dharma texts (traditionally killing, theft, drink, adultery and keeping such company).

reading: Singing every day with a thousand Siddhars, we will dance the holy dance of bliss together; knowing the siddhi that Mother Uma Manonmani told me, we will live by it, keeping close to the great.
nuance: The Siddhars here are a company, a thousand who sing and dance, not solitary adepts. The teaching comes from the goddess, not from a human guru, but is to be lived out beside the elders. சித்தை could be the siddhi or simply the wisdom she spoke.

reading: Melting and pining in thought to find the state, seeking daily the feet of the stainless Lord, knowing the kala we seized the breath and bound it; raising the fire, we read the root with ease.
nuance: கலை here is probably the breath's phase (the moon and sun channels), and வாசி the breath as practice; கனல் எழுப்பி மூலமதை is taken by tradition as kindling the fire at the muladhara, the waking of kundalini. 'Read the root' (படித்தோம்) is the coded verb: to master or know the root centre.

reading: Giving up food and sleep we practised yogic absorption; cutting off our kin we lived in a mountain cave; we saw the supreme space that sight cannot reach; eating kalpa we grew the body.
nuance: The stanza holds together the two aims the Siddhars refuse to separate: the vision of the open (பரவெளி) and a body made to last by kalpa, the rejuvenating preparation. It claims the body was grown, not escaped.

reading: We will not languish in fond dealings with father, mother and kin; we will not seek works that do not reach and know the state of tapas; we knew jnana in wonder, as the highest thing, and knew the grace of the supreme space.
nuance: The second line is compressed: செய்கை may be any outward work, or the rites, that fails to reach tapas. The refusal of parents and kin repeats 2241 and is the kuravanji's plainest renunciation.

reading: We learned to fix the gaze along the tip of the nose; we knew the whirl of the good root-circle; knowing how to raise the breath, we will cut off desires, and refuse without fail the doings of the world.
nuance: நாசிநுனி, the nose-tip gaze, and மூலவட்டம் சுழி, the whirl of the root circle, are technical body-places; tradition takes the whirl as the coil at the base where the central channel begins. The point is causal: raising the breath is what cuts desire.

reading: Climbing the seat of the shakti-wheel we saw the pure open; holding in mind that all is the supreme open, we will know every day the freed ones who gained siddhi, and come to know with attention what the life-kala is.
nuance: சக்திசக்ர பீடம் is probably one of the body's centres, the seat of Shakti, and சீவகலை the digit or phase of the life, perhaps the moon-kala of the breath; both are coded and their places are not given. The stanza moves from a sight (space seen) to a view (all is space).

reading: We took in what is told of the ninety-six tattvas; in the supreme open we saw the Lord's feet; I came to know what heaven is, seeing for myself the light of the supreme open.
nuance: The ninety-six tattvas are the Siddhars' fuller count of the body's constituents, against the thirty-six of the Saiva texts. உரைத்தனங்களைக் கொண்டோம் is unclear: 'took the accounts of' or 'passed through'. விண்ணுலகு, heaven, is here something seen within, not a place after death.

reading: I cut away with relish the anava that says 'I'; gaining the good, I came to live in a cave; we came having quelled the pride that says 'self'; holding tapas alone as the way, we delighted in the path of the breath.
nuance: ஆணவம் is the first of the malas, the bond of 'I'; the stanza names it and cuts it with a light word (நயந்து, gladly). சரவழி is the path of the breath (சரம், svara), so even the closing tapas is breath-practice.

title: புண்ணாக்குச் சித்தர் பாடல்
theme: Punnakku Siddhar's twenty short stanzas to 'Jnanam, mother' (ஞானம்மா): true knowledge is a priceless gem found by passing beyond ignorance, the life sits in the body like the chick in the egg, and the seeker must give up sleep, see waking as a dream and so make Death bow. Against this he sets those who take samsara for real, the untaught swamis who roam for property, the smearing, talk, puja and hand-waving that are only a target for mockery, the drums and wailing of a funeral that never counts its own days, and a body that is borrowed, wind-filled, filthy and saltless, a false nest the five senses built to rule.
structure_note: Each stanza is three short lines with the refrain ஞானம்மா in the third, the second half of a line turning on 'Jnanam, mother' to deliver the point. 2247 to 2255 teach (refuge, the gem, the chick, the remainder of past births, the waking seeker); 2256 to 2261 mock (swamis, rites, funerals, borrowed things, talkers); 2262 to 2266 return to the guru, the light and the false body. From 2261 the parsed text carries a heading that looks like a lost first line (see source_issues).
source_issues: 2261 to 2266 carry the parsed label 'செத்தவரை மயானம் சேர்க்கும்வரையில் ஞானம்'. It rhymes with 2261's surviving line உத்தமர்போலப் பேசி and is probably 2261's lost first line, misread as a section heading and copied to the following units; 2261 has only two lines.
2262 repeats காட்டில் in its first two lines, perhaps a copying slip.
2256 ஆத்தி is probably ஆஸ்தி (property); 2260 தேவமாதா is unexpected in the list and may be corrupt.

reading: Crying 'refuge, refuge', I leapt and begged to see the holy feet of the goddess Manonmani, Jnanam, mother.
nuance: The opening is a plea for refuge to Manonmani, the Shakti beyond mind; ஞானம்மா, the refrain, addresses knowledge itself as a mother, so the goddess and jnana are run together from the first stanza.

reading: If one passes beyond ignorance, drives the understanding hard and finds true knowledge, Jnanam, mother, it is a gem without price.
nuance: அறிவு (understanding) is the instrument and மெய்ஞ்ஞானம் the find; the verse makes knowledge something one drives toward, not something given.

reading: As a whole chick lies within the egg, so, Jnanam, mother, the life itself stands within the body that is a shirt.
nuance: Two images of the body in one line: the egg-shell, inside which something complete is already formed, and the சட்டை, a shirt or a snake's slough that is put off. The life is whole before it hatches; the body is only its covering.

reading: When the remainder left off does not return and true knowledge is not sought, it is through the remainder once touched, Jnanam, mother, that true knowledge appears.
nuance: விட்ட குறை தொட்ட குறை is a proverbial pair, taken by tradition as the unfinished practice or karma of a former birth that carries over. The stanza seems to say that knowledge arises from what was begun before, even where present seeking fails; the logic of the two negatives is unclear.

reading: Not knowing their own hearts, not knowing the breath, taking household life for truth, Jnanam, mother, they toil in the sea.
nuance: சரம் is the breath (svara), so not knowing the breath stands beside not knowing oneself as the double cause of drowning. சம்சாரம் is both the round of birth and, in Tamil use, family life; the sea (சாகரம்) is the traditional figure for the first.

reading: One may give teaching to the willing any day; but to give teaching to the wicked, Jnanam, mother, brings ruin.
nuance: இட்டர், those dear or willing, against துட்டர், the wicked. The ruin (மோசம்) may fall on the teacher, on the teaching, or on both; the stanza does not say.

reading: Those who would gain release, and those who have set it first in their thought, must give up sleep, Jnanam, mother, and stay with awareness.
nuance: நித்திரையும் விட்டு may be literal sleeplessness, as in the vigils of the ascetics (compare Mounachiddhar's 2241), or the giving up of the sleep of unawareness. நினைவோடு, with awareness or with remembrance, is the positive term.

reading: If you look on waking as a dream, then even Yama who comes in anger, Jnanam, mother, will fall prostrate and go.
nuance: நினைவு here is the waking state as against dream; to see it as a dream is to stop taking the world as solid. The claim is that this seeing undoes death: Yama bows (தெண்டநிட்டு) instead of seizing. It can also be read more plainly, that one who holds waking life lightly does not fear death.

reading: Not knowing the truth by the light of the lamp of yoga, they sink, Jnanam, mother, into the pit called delusion.
nuance: Yoga is a lamp: its use is to show the truth, and without it one falls into மோகம், infatuation. The pit is the dark that the lamp would have shown.

reading: Becoming swamis who never learned the shastras, thinking to seek property, Jnanam, mother, crores of them wander.
nuance: ஆத்தி is probably ஆஸ்தி, property; the garb is taken for gain. Unusually for the Siddhars, the charge is that these swamis have not learned the shastras: here book-learning is a minimum, not the enemy.

reading: Smearing, empty talk, puja and the waving of hands are only a mark for mockery, Jnanam, mother: there is nothing in any of it.
nuance: பூச்சு is the smearing of ash or sandal, கைவீச்சு the hand-gestures of ritual or of preaching. The rhyme (பூச்சு, பேச்சு, கைவீச்சு, ஏச்சு) does the arguing: outward show invites ridicule.

reading: Adorning the vessel, the women with hair unbound, not knowing the reckoning, Jnanam, mother, wept in confusion.
nuance: The scene is a funeral: women loosen their hair in mourning. கலம் may be the pot or bier of the dead, or the body itself as a vessel; கணக்கு, the reckoning, is perhaps the count of days or deeds that the mourners never learned.

reading: Beating the drums and many people gathering, never counting their own days, Jnanam, mother, they waste away and weep.
nuance: The mourners weep for another and do not count their own span: the point is not grief but the failure to draw the lesson from it.

reading: The loincloth is borrowed, the gross body that was taken is borrowed, the divine mother is borrowed, Jnanam, mother; not knowing this, they wander.
nuance: இரவல் (on loan) is the word that carries it: even the ascetic's loincloth and the body are lent. தேவமாதா, the divine mother, is surprising on the list; it may mean the earthly mother who bore the body, called divine, so that the parent too is lent for a time.

reading: Talking like noble men, Jnanam, mother, they roam the world.
nuance: The stanza has two of its three lines. The heading the parser attached to this and the following units, செத்தவரை மயானம் சேர்க்கும்வரையில் ஞானம், rhymes with உத்தமர் and is probably the lost first line: the 'jnana' that lasts only until the dead are taken to the burning ground. With it the stanza mocks graveside wisdom that fades once the body is burned.

reading: Though one lives in the forest and performs golden austerities, Jnanam, mother, without a guru one cannot find and know it.
nuance: கனகதவம், golden or great tapas, is granted its full worth and still found insufficient. The repetition of காட்டில் in both lines may be a copying slip or a deliberate echo.

reading: The good light is the light of knowledge; the light that is no light, Jnanam, mother, is a base light.
nuance: இல்லா வெளிச்சம், 'the light that is not', may be the light of the senses and the world, which is not true light and so is low; or it may be read as 'the light that is not there', the dark. The plain claim is that only the light of jnana is good.

reading: Those who suffer, calling it samsara, calling it an ocean: Jnanam, mother, what use is it that they live?
nuance: The stanza answers 2251: those who toiled in the sea there now only name it and complain. Calling the world an ocean is not escaping it.

reading: This came shut in with wind; this is a filthy pot; this is a stinking corpse, Jnanam, mother, a saltless false nest.
nuance: காத்தடைத்து, shut in with wind, makes the body a thing kept alive only by the breath held inside it. உப்பிலா, without salt, is tasteless and worthless; பொய்க்கூடு, the false nest or cage, returns in 2266.

reading: The five came together seeking to rule as kings, and to move about, Jnanam, mother, they built themselves this false nest.
nuance: அஞ்சுபேர், the five, are taken as the five senses, or the five elements, or the five vital airs; on any reading the body is their building and their kingdom, not the self's. தானமைத்த may also mean 'which he himself built', the Lord or maya as builder.

title: கஞ்சமலைச் சித்தர் பாடல்
theme: Kanjamalai Siddhar's song is Vedantic in vocabulary and prohibitive in form: the world is imagination and dream, the body comes from ego-impurity and is worked by five, and the stanzas pile up negative imperatives, do not argue, do not crave what has not come, do not fall for women, do not trust learning, do not circle temples, against one positive counsel, to still the running mind in the open space of nada's end, hold to the guru's word and feet, and find the self-luminous within the very play of the faculties. Rites, tattva-lists and tapas are a heap and a burden; silence and jnana-inquiry are the essence.
structure_note: A head unit (2267) and twenty-four stanzas of four short lines, each line ending in one rhyme (-ள்ளு, -ாரம், -ாதே, -ந்து) and the fourth usually carrying the point. 2268 to 2275 set the doctrine (the world as maya and dream, the body as ego's product, the guru as the limit); 2276 to 2283 are mostly prohibitions (-ாதே) against company, dispute, craving, women, learning and the belly; 2284 to 2291 return to the soul, the guru's word, the pairs of opposites, speech, the body and the temple, ending on the self-light within the faculties' play. 2292 (ch117) closes the song. Tradition names a Kanjamalaiyan among Tirumular's disciples (Tirumanthiram 1443); whether this song's poet is that figure or a later namesake from the Kanjamalai hill near Salem is not decidable from the text.
source_issues: 2267 is printed as an unnumbered head unit (u1), two lines where the stanzas have four; it is the song's invocation and may be a later editor's heading.
2271 line 4: பொஞ்சம் is unknown; probably a rhyme-word forced against கொஞ்சம், possibly corrupt.
2272 line 1: கேடு-முதல் and other hyphens in this work mark the caesura between the half-lines, not compounds; 2274 and 2277 have the hyphen replaced by a comma.
2281 line 2: கற்றோ மென்று றெண்ணுங் has a doubled ற (மென்று றெண்ணும்); read மென்று எண்ணும்.
2283 line 4: கானந்த முத்தி is ஆனந்த முத்தி with the initial க் carried over from உனக்கு by sandhi; printed as one word.
2281 and 2286 are participial chains with no finite verb; each may continue into the next stanza or be incomplete.
2290 line 4: அமலங்கள் is read as மலங்கள் (defilements) with a prothetic அ; the alternative sense 'stainless ones' is possible but inconsistent with துன்ப.

reading: The awareness that is perfect, full bliss: the ever-blissful feet of Siva, the Supreme Brahman.
nuance: A two-line head or invocation, with Vedanta's names (பரிபூரணம், சிவபரப்பிரமம், சதானந்தம்) given at once to Siva's feet; the song's vocabulary is announced here.

reading: Think on the Supreme that is yours by right; throw off the bewilderment of the world made by maya; utter the rare name of Siva; take up with love the service of Siva's devotees.
nuance: Four imperatives on one rhyme (உள்ளு, தள்ளு, விள்ளு, கொள்ளு); the two inward ones (thinking the Supreme, rejecting maya) are paired with two outward and devotional ones (the name, service to devotees), which the song will not repeat but does not retract.

reading: Inquiry into base worldly life is small pleasure that turns to sorrow, a great horror; the inquiry that is certain is the essence of stainless jnana-Vedanta; that is the essence.
nuance: விசாரம் is used twice, for brooding on worldly affairs and for the inquiry of Vedanta; the stanza does not oppose thinking to not-thinking but one object of thought to another. சாரமே சாரம் doubles the word for essence.

reading: The world is imagination, an expanse produced by the inner faculties, a dream, an Indra's net; if on that day it appears so, that is favourable to the subtle.
nuance: அந்தக்கரணம், the inner faculties (mind, intellect, ego, will), are made the producers of the world, which is Vedanta's idealism; இந்த்ரசாலம் is the conjuror's show. The last line is obscure: perhaps that once the world has appeared as dream, the subtle is in reach. 2291 returns to the faculties and says their play cannot be pushed away.

reading: The world is trifling; if you go along with it, it gives you only a little; the heart that stands fixed in grace, on that day there is nothing equal to it, nothing equal, the ... of true knowledge.
nuance: பொஞ்சம் in the last line is unknown, perhaps a rhyme-word coined against கொஞ்சம், or a corruption; the stanza's sense, the world's little against grace's incomparable, does not depend on it.

reading: Ruin came from ego; throw desire, the root, far off with its bundle; the house of bliss that cannot be contained, on that day the dissolution of mind that strikes joins of itself.
nuance: மனோலயம், the dissolution of mind, is a yogic and Vedantic term for the state in which the mind subsides; the stanza says it comes of itself (தானாக) once desire is thrown out, so the positive state is not made but allowed.

reading: What are the heaps of tattvas? What are the rites called the sastras of attainment? With devotion that does not forget, when you see the guru's feet, then it will be known.
nuance: தத்துவக் குப்பைகள், heaps or rubbish of tattvas, dismisses the Saiva Siddhanta enumerations of thirty-six; சித்தி சாத்திரம் may be the texts of ritual attainment or the Siddhars' own siddhi manuals. Both are replaced by the guru's feet, seen, and the knowing is deferred to that moment (அப்போது).

reading: There are no far distances; to try to touch and catch it is great trouble; trusting the word of the causal teacher and fixing it in the mind, one can see the limit.
nuance: The Supreme is not far and yet cannot be grasped by effort; the way is the guru's word held in mind. காரண தேசிகன், the teacher who is the cause, may be the human guru or Siva as guru. எல்லை, the limit or bound, is the end of the search, not the Supreme's boundary.

reading: The body came from the impurity of ego; in it five sit and do their work by rule; it is a maya that will vanish unseen; I have told you well the formula tried by hand, the means.
nuance: ஆணவம் is the first of Saiva Siddhanta's three malas, the soul's root darkness; the body is its product. ஐவர், the five, are the senses or the elements, tradition giving both. கைகண்ட சூத்திரம், a formula proven by hand, is the alchemist's and physician's phrase, here used for a doctrine.

reading: Do not hold to the company of fools; do not die by the derangement of lust for women; do not fall for display; while the nectar of jnana is there, do not drink poison.
nuance: The stanza's four prohibitions end on the strongest contrast, nectar at hand and poison chosen, which is Tirumular's figure for the ritualist beside the knower.

reading: Do not dispute saying 'I'; do not throw out arguments and hiss in anger; the bond called flesh does not change; if it goes, by your own oath, your mind will not be done with even in death.
nuance: The second half is hard: ஊனென்ற பாசம் மாறாதே may be a statement, that attachment to the flesh does not change, or another prohibition, do not change it. The last line seems to say that if life goes with the mind still disputing, the mind's state outlasts the body; உன்னாணை, 'by your oath', is an asseveration.

reading: Do not push away what has come; do not hold vain desire for what has not come; do not leap about at the mind's will; stay still like a picture and do not utter anything.
nuance: சித்திரம் போல, like a painting, is the stillness of the yogi; the stanza's equanimity toward what comes and does not come is the Kural's ஊழ் chapter in a Siddhar's mouth.

reading: Body-attachment and the bonds of birth: that thing, the small pleasure, is a stinking smell; the Vedanta that is one's portion, if you contemplate the thing, is yours.
nuance: சிச்சீர்க்கந்தம் joins the exclamation of disgust (சீ) to கந்தம், smell; பாகமதான may be the Vedanta that has ripened or that is one's share. The contrast is between the pleasure that attaches to the body and the knowledge that becomes one's own (சொந்தம்) by contemplation.

reading: Desire for women will not do; if that delusion takes hold it does not go even a little; do not die in fear at Yama's hand; do not burn in the fire called wicked desire-bonds.
nuance: ஆசாபாசம், desire-bond, is a compound the Siddhars favour, treating craving and the bond it makes as one thing; it is a fire here where 2276 made it poison.

reading: Crossing the delusion of learning, destroying the dross of thinking 'we have learned it all', lying in the heat of words, desire spreading into the subtle beyond the subtle...
nuance: A chain of participles without a finite verb; it may run into 2282, where the mind is to be caught and set in the open space. சூட்சாதி சூட்சம், the subtle of subtles, is the Supreme; the ஆசை that spreads toward it is the one desire the song allows. The stanza mocks the learned (கற்றோம் என்று) in the Siddhars' usual way.

reading: The thought that runs about: catch it without letting it run, gather it and set it right; seek, and fit it to the arrow; set it within the wide open space of nada's end.
nuance: அம்பு, the arrow, recurs in 2287 (அம்பு பூணும்); tradition reads it as the fixed inward gaze or the straight breath. நாதாந்த வெட்டவெளி, the bare open space at the end of sound, is where the mind is to be lodged; the stanza is the song's one positive method, framed in the same imperatives as its prohibitions.

reading: Do not wander for the span-sized belly; do not be bewildered by daily anxiety; do not be melted in the forge of ego; for you the release that is bliss, stand firm in that.
nuance: அது நிலையாதே can be the fourth prohibition's form carrying a positive sense ('stand in that'), or a statement that otherwise release will not abide (நிலையாது). The சாண் வயிறு, the span of belly for which one roams, is the Siddhars' standing figure for the whole economy of livelihood.

reading: The soul that is the egoist is destroyed by its ignorance; if it thinks of tapas it reaches awareness; and if it holds that state, it becomes the form of Shakti too.
nuance: அபிமானி, the one who identifies, is the soul as ego; the stanza gives three stages, destruction by ignorance, awareness (போதம்) by tapas, and Shakti's form by holding the state. That the end is Shakti's form and not Siva's is unusual in a song whose head unit (2267) is to Siva's feet; the text does not explain it.

reading: Say only what the good guru said; if it is the quest of the pillar, stand in the state of fire; let go of the sects of your own time; eat, and take yourself as being of its own nature.
nuance: தம்பம், the pillar, is tradition's name for the spine or the central channel, and வன்னி நிலை, the fire state, the fire centre at the base or navel; so read, the stanza is a yoga instruction. விள்ளு was 'utter' in 2268 and may be 'split off, let go' here; தற்சமயங்கள் may be present-day sects or the sects of the self. உண்டு, 'having eaten', may be literal or the enjoyment of the state.

reading: Touching sorrow and joy, burning all those pairs so that the rust is gone, then letting go of attachment, saying not one thing, leaving behind the greatness of the end...
nuance: Another participial chain without a close. தொந்தங்கள் are the pairs of opposites (dvandva) of Vedanta; துருசு is rust or dross. அந்தம் பெருமையை விட்டு may be giving up even the pride of having reached the end, or the greatness of the six ends (ஆறந்தம்); the text does not fix it.

reading: What does talk bring to light? Talking and talking is nothing but error, is it not? Because of ... one wears the arrow; what is needed is a flawless inquiry of jnana.
nuance: வாச்சுதலால் is obscure (perhaps 'by its coming about'); அம்பு பூணும் repeats the arrow of 2282. The contrast between பேச்சு (talk) and விசாரணை (inquiry) is the song's own: inquiry is the one use of thought it keeps (2269).

reading: The body is impermanent; in it, infatuation is not contained by desire alone; if one stays alone, that enjoyment, standing as oneself alone, is Siva-yoga.
nuance: தனித்திருந்தால், staying alone, is both solitude and the standing-as-one (தானாகி நிற்பது) that the stanza calls Siva-yoga; the enjoyment (போகம்) desire sought is redefined as the yogi's. The second line is compressed; ஆசையும் ஒன்றால் may mean that desire, being one thing, does not contain the infatuation it breeds.

reading: Give no room to the desire that wants; do not get bound within the pains of the body; do not take birth again; do not let go of love at the feet of the guru-teacher.
nuance: Four -ாதே lines, the last turned positive by a double negative: the one thing not to give up is love for the guru's feet, the song's constant positive (2273, 2274, 2285).

reading: Crores upon crores of austerities, and the japas recited going round that temple: are they not a toil of births? They are the defilements of sorrow that come upon one before one does this.
nuance: பாடான பவங்கள் is read as births that are toil, or the toil of births; the austerities and temple japa are made part of the round of birth and not its cure. இது பண்ணுமுன், 'before doing this', seems to refer to the inquiry of 2287, so that the rites belong to the time before one knows. அமலங்கள் is read as மலங்கள் with a prefixed அ; it could also be 'the stainless', which would reverse the sense, but the line's துன்ப tells against it.

reading: The play of the inner faculties: no one can push it away, whatever the effort; what stands joined to it is bondage; within it, appearing without appearing, is the self-luminous.
nuance: The stanza qualifies 2270: the faculties' conjuring cannot be stopped, only unjoined from (தொந்தித்து, being coupled, is the bondage), and the self-light (சுயம்பிரகாசம்) is found within the play, not after it ends. தோன்றாமற் தோன்றும், appearing without appearing, is the Siddhars' formula for what is seen without being an object.

title: கஞ்சமலைச் சித்தர் பாடல்
theme: The single closing stanza of Kanjamalai Siddhar's song: the form of the name is itself attainment, and seeking it out and becoming clear in it is release; the form of discipline is the seed, and everywhere the eternal substance becomes certain.
structure_note: One stanza, 2292, separated from ch116 by the editor's split; it is the twenty-fifth and last stanza of the song and should be read as its conclusion, answering the head unit 2267 (the feet of the Supreme) with the name.
source_issues: The chapter holds one stanza because the editor's split of the 25-stanza song fell after 2291; 2292 is the song's close and belongs with ch116.

reading: The form of the name is itself attainment; is it not release to seek that out and become clear in it? The form of discipline is the seed; everywhere the eternal substance becomes certain.
nuance: நாம சொரூபம் may be the Lord's name, whose utterance 2268 commanded, so that the stanza makes the name itself the siddhi and release; or it may be Vedanta's நாமரூபம், the world of name and form, in which case the stanza says the attainment is in the very appearance, as 2291 found the self-light within the faculties' play. நேம சொரூபம், the form of observance or discipline, as the seed (வித்து) is the second half's balancing claim, that practice is the seed of what everywhere becomes certain. நிரந்தர வத்து, the eternal substance, is Vedanta's term.

title: நொண்டிச் சித்தர் பாடல்
theme: Nondi Siddhar's limping song is a first-person report of attainment: after bowing to Sivasakti and to a roll call of twenty-two siddhas he says, verse after verse, 'I knew', 'I saw', 'I reached'. The path runs from leaving chariyai and kiriyai through yoga to a silence beyond speech; the places are the body's centres (the nose-tip, the root, manipuraka, vishuddhi, the nine gates), a flight to Sathuragiri, and the gift of the goddess Manonmani, and the song closes by setting the salted pot of the body against the state the guru's word opened.
structure_note: Invocation and the lineage of siddhas (2293 to 2296); the way beyond chariyai and kiriyai and the first vision (2297 and 2298); the long run of attainments under the heading 'I saw beginning, middle and end: the state of silence' (2299 to 2315), which moves from Om and the ego to Sathuragiri, the centres, Manonmani and the body's falseness; and the opening of 'I destroyed ego: the true state' (2316 and 2317), which continues in chapter 119. Units 2299 and 2316 have three lines, the fourth being the heading the editor set as section title.
source_issues: Units 2299 and 2316 have three lines each; their fourth line is the section heading the editor has lifted out as a title (அடிநடு முடிவு கண்டேன் மோனநிலை, ஆங்காரமும் ஒழித்தேன் உண்மைநிலை).
2314: வந்தவழி வந்தவழி is doubled, perhaps a scribal repetition; செப்புக் குயமானார் is obscure.
2305: கவனக் குளிகை is probably கமனக் குளிகை (the pill of flight).
2294: Macchamuni is named among the siddhas worshipped although the corpus attributes the song to Nondi Siddhar identified with Machendranathar.

reading: Bowing daily to the feet of Ambika, the first Parapara who is Sivasakti, and taking refuge in the flower-feet of the elephant of the triangle in the faultless flame-light.
nuance: திரிகோணக் குஞ்சரம், the elephant of the triangle, is Ganapati as tradition places him at the triangle of the root centre, so that the invocation is already a body-map: the Mother first, then the lord of the root. The phrase could also be read as the elephant-faced one worshipped in a triangular yantra.

reading: The roll of siddhas begins: Tirumular, Kalangi, Bogar, the guru-sage of southern Pothigai, Dhanvantari, Karuvurar, Idaikkadar, Atri, Kalaikkodar, Macchamuni and Pulathiyar.
nuance: குருமுனி of Pothigai is Agastya. Macchamuni (Matsyendra) appears in the list although the corpus attributes this very song to Nondi Siddhar identified with Machendranathar; either the identification is late or the poet names a predecessor of the same name. The list reads as a lineage rather than a pantheon.

reading: The roll continues with Sundaranandar, Kapilar, Konganar, Sutamuni, Kosikar, Vedamuni, Nandisar and Sattaimuni, and the poet says he worshipped them and bowed at their feet.
nuance: The two stanzas give twenty names, more than the usual eighteen siddhas; Nandisar stands among the human siddhas, and in 2307 he is called the poet's grandfather, the guru's guru.

reading: Knowing the door of the five senses, discerning the wonder of the true way of the Brahma mantra, and parting from agitation, the poet says he resolutely bowed at the feet of the siddhas and the others.
nuance: அஞ்சுபுலக் கதவு, the door of the five senses, may mean knowing how to shut them, as the nine gates are shut in 2317. பிரம மந்திரம் is unexplained; it may be the pranava of 2303 or the five letters.

reading: Leaving chariyai and kiriyai and touching, beyond them, the foot of the great yoga that is the means, the transcendent appeared there, and the poet asks whether it is in his power to tell what it was to simply remain.
nuance: சும்மா இருந்தது, 'simply remaining', is the Siddhars' and later Tamil mystics' phrase for the state past effort; the stanza treats it as what the verses that follow cannot really say, which sits oddly with their confident 'I saw'. உரிய அதீதம் may be 'the fitting transcendent' or 'the transcendent that is one's own'.

reading: Taking hold of the Parapara space with the mind made one and fixed, seeing the arising of supreme consciousness, the poet drank fittingly the undeparting nectar of bliss, the ancient thing that rests on nothing.
nuance: The syntax is loose: நிராதரமான பண்டு, 'the ancient one without support', may qualify the bliss or stand alone as the object seen. உற்பனம் (arising, manifestation) returns in 2325, where all such arisings are called imagination; the two stanzas should be read together.

reading: The poet says he came to know, knew jnana, saw in full the form of the endless Parabrahman, and broke off attachment to this world.
nuance: The unit has three lines; the missing first line is the heading 'I saw beginning, middle and end: the state of silence' that the editor has set as the section title. The refrain-like 'I knew, I saw' begins here and runs to 2325.

reading: When the pure supreme space itself appeared as light, the poet gained the joy of true knowledge; on beholding Being, Consciousness and Bliss, that all is pervaded by Brahman is hard to put into words.
nuance: சகலமும் பிரமமயம் is the Advaitic formula, rare in the earlier Siddhars and common in the later Vedantic ones. புகலரிதே, 'hard to tell', repeats the disclaimer of 2297.

reading: In the supreme space that is light between the eyes, shining at the middle of the nose-tip, the poet beheld the teacher's holy dance, and the state of silence was touched.
nuance: The nose-tip gaze is the classical yogic fixation; tradition takes the light seen there as the opening of the inner eye. தேசிகன், the teacher, is both Siva and the guru. பரிசமுத்தே is unclear: 'nectar of the touch' (பரிச அமுது) or 'touching, it was reached' (பரிசம் உற்றே); the reading leaves it as touched.

reading: Becoming clear that thought is dream, forgetting even that thought, forgetting the rising kalai, forgetting the self that says 'mine', and renouncing the part that does not churn in the pure ocean.
nuance: The stanza is a chain of forgettings in which even the knowledge that thought is dream is let go. கலை may be the arts or the breath's phases. The last line, உழலாத பாகம் துறந்தே, is obscure: perhaps leaving behind whatever does not dissolve in the pure sea, perhaps a corrupt line.

reading: Having seen in truth what the pranava Om is, the poet gained great good; leaving the ego that says 'we', he found what he sought and knew his aim.
nuance: நாமெனும் அகங்காரம், the ego that says 'we' rather than 'I', is a small variation on the usual தான் or நான். Knowing Om is here a gain and a means; compare the Arutpulambal, where Om itself perishes with the ego.

reading: Leaving desire, given the strength to cut off the five senses that hide and run spreading out, crossing the bond and walking exactly as the guru's word said, without a step astray.
nuance: The strength is given (அளித்து), not won: the one note of grace in a sequence of 'I did'. The stanza has no finite verb and runs on into 2305.

reading: Taking the pill of flight and by it going deep along the sky path, the poet says he went to Sathuragiri, where the great siddhas of austerity live, and rejoiced.
nuance: கவனக் குளிகை is most likely கமனக் குளிகை, the pill of going, the medicine the siddha traditions claim gives travel through the air; ககனமார்க்கம் is then the literal sky. The coded reading, as tradition takes it, makes ககனம் the inner sky and the pill the retained breath or bindu, so that the journey is in the body. Sathuragiri near Srivilliputhur is the siddhas' mountain in these songs. The stanza reports a claim, not a recipe.

reading: With the lordly nine siddhas of supreme knowledge who sit on the rock of austerity, the poet knew the form of Siva, and having seen the lamp-light in his mind he broke off longing.
nuance: தவசுப் பாறை is a named rock at Sathuragiri in local tradition, so the stanza can be read as a place as much as a figure. நவ சித்தர், the nine siddhas, is a smaller count than the twenty of 2294 and 2295.

reading: The poet knew the root support and rejoiced to see there the lamp-light of the three flames; he learned the manifold arts, and by the grace of his grandfather Nandisar he was glad.
nuance: முச்சுடர், the three flames, is the Siddhars' sun, moon and fire, read as the two breaths and the fire at the root. நாலா கலை is 'the various arts' or, forcing the number, four kalai. என் பாட்டன் நந்தீசர்: Nandi as grandfather makes Tirumular, whom 2323 calls 'our guru', the father in a lineage of three, which 2294 began.

reading: Knowing the experience of yoga, the poet saw that the manipuraka is for the best a great attainment, and that remaining in the vishuddhi state so as not to die, one's own state there becomes the good state.
nuance: The stanza assigns fruits to two of the six centres, the navel and the throat; tradition gives each centre its virtue, and here the throat centre carries deathlessness (சாகாது இருந்திட). The grammar of the last line is a string of nominals and the reading supplies the verbs.

reading: The poet stood at what he saw, rejoiced that Sivasakti was there as imagination and went beyond; seeing the path once granted to mother Uma, he drank the intoxication of the rasa drink.
nuance: ரசபானம் can be the alchemist's mercury preparation, which the siddhas claim to drink, or the inner nectar that tradition says drips from the moon in the head; the stanza's போதை (intoxication) suits either. கற்பனை அது என்று, 'that it was imagination', is hard: either Sivasakti's form is seen as a construct to be passed, or the word is corrupt.

reading: Having seen the wonder of the fullness that none can know, the poet's speech subsided; by the grace of the goddess Manonmani, rich in excellence, he knew it and merged in it.
nuance: பேச்சு அடங்கினேன், 'my speech subsided', is silence as an effect of seeing rather than a discipline. Manonmani, the goddess of Tirumular's Bhairavi mantra, gives the knowing here as she gives the means there.

reading: Day by day the poet saw and knew the place beyond desire; he took well the name 'she is Vami', which sages and gods praise, and rose in the Supreme.
nuance: வாமி is the goddess of the left, Vamadevi or Vamesvari; 'taking the name' may mean receiving her mantra, or taking her as one's deity. காமியம் கடந்த இடம், the place past desire, is the state itself, not a location.

reading: Seeing the state called the silence at the end of nada, the poet stayed there, losing sleep and food; he knew the way of Vedanta and, crossing the house of ignorance, saw the higher house.
nuance: நாதாந்தம் and வேதாந்தம் are two of the six ends; the stanza passes through both. உறக்கம் ஊனும் அற்றேன் may be the yogi's wakeful fast or a sign of absorption; 2324 returns to the unsleeping eye. வீடு is used twice, for the house of ignorance left and the higher house seen.

reading: The poet read many sastras, forgot the company of wicked chandalas, learned to know the fit vessel, and joining those with devotion he saw release.
nuance: பொல்லாச் சண்டாளர் is used for the wicked, not for a caste, and is set against பாத்திரம், the worthy vessel: a caste word turned into a word for character, which is how the Siddhars often use it. The verse values reading, unusual in a tradition that mocks book-learning.

reading: This salted pot of a body came the way it came; people who do not know the truth call it good, and like those who make copper their craft they wander the land in desire and churn in bondage.
nuance: உப்பிட்ட பாண்டம், the salted pot that dissolves, is Sivavakkiyar's image for the body. வந்தவழி வந்தவழி, doubled, may mean 'it goes as it came' or be a scribal repetition. செப்புக் குயமானார் is obscure: 'copper-potters', perhaps alchemists chasing gold from copper, or a corrupt phrase.

reading: Certain that this body, an unstable false cage, has no substance, the poet in fear went to a mountain cave, learned the way of Sivajnana and became straight in it.
nuance: அச்சமதோடு: fear is the motive for retreat, an honest detail. The body contempt here sits against 2324, where the fleshly body is kept from perishing in nishtai; the song holds both without reconciling them.

reading: The poet says he abased himself as 'the knowing lame one', Nondi; he knew the fitting state and the clarity of the form of Parabrahman that the guru told.
nuance: The unit has three lines; the heading 'I destroyed ego: the true state' is its missing first line. சிறந்து இழித்தேன் is a paradox, 'I excelled in lowering myself', and the name நொண்டி (lame) is taken as that self-abasement; it may also name the limping சிந்து metre of the song.

reading: The poet realised himself by himself, realised the eight places and the nine gates, then shut those doors, and going through the great high path he reached the holy.
nuance: ஒன்பது வாசல் are the body's nine openings; எட்டுத் தலங்கள், the eight places, is unexplained, perhaps the limbs of eightfold yoga or eight centres in the body. திரு அடைந்தேன் leaves open whether the holy reached is Siva, release or the Lady of the next verse.

title: நொண்டிச் சித்தர் பாடல்
theme: The close of Nondi Siddhar's song, under the heading 'I destroyed ego: the true state': at Manonmani's seat the poet hears the bell-sound of nada and sees Siva's dance, knows the mantra and the circle of Om, names the imperishable thing, takes the title of jnani, and in a nishtai where 'he' and 'I' are gone and the body does not perish he sees every arising as imagination and breaks into song. The chapter's claim is that the true state is seen, not argued, and that whoever takes daylight for darkness has no eye to see it.
structure_note: Sound and dance at the goddess's seat (2318); mantra, Om and the Indra seat (2319); the imperishable thing and the way to moksha (2320 and 2321); the open void and those who cannot see it (2322); the guru Mular and the Vedas (2323); nishtai with the body preserved and the unsleeping eye (2324); all arising as imagination, and the song at Chidambaram (2325).
source_issues: 2323: the quoted saying மூல முதலி மொள்ளே is cipher or corrupt and is left untranslated.

reading: At the seat of the Mother Manonmani, hearing the ringing tone of the bell and the song of nada, the poet at once saw the vision of Siva's holy dance.
nuance: மணிச் சத்தத் தொனி கணகணன: the inner sounds that yogic tradition lists, bell among them, as the stages of nada; the dance seen is Siva's as in 2301, but now at the goddess's seat (பீடம்), which may be a centre in the body.

reading: The poet knew the mantra, reached and firmly knew the circle of the Omkara, realised the Indra seat, and seeing what the state of silence is, his mind took on goodness.
nuance: ஓங்கார வட்டம், the circle of Om, may be a drawn yantra or the round of the syllable's parts. இந்திர பீடம், the Indra seat, is unexplained: perhaps the seat of the senses (இந்திரியம்), perhaps a centre named for Indra as the east. எட்டி அறிந்தேன் is 'reached and knew', not 'knew the eight'.

reading: Worshipping and saying 'this is the imperishable thing', the poet rejoiced within and gained the joy of knowledge; praising that the state of moksha comes to those who know it as the way, he drove off the demon nature.
nuance: பேய்க்குணம், the demon or ghoul nature, is the base disposition; Pattinathar uses the same word of the heart. The stanza alone makes moksha conditional on knowing the way (வழியாய் உணர்ந்தவர்க்கு), which gives the whole report its teaching purpose.

reading: The poet knew the end of the Veda and cooled his heart with the thing that shines everywhere; he reached the space of nada, and to the praise of the people of the four lands he got the name of jnani.
nuance: ஞானி பேர் பெற்றேன் under a heading about destroying ego is either unselfconscious or a reminder that the name is the world's, not his. நாத வெளி pairs the sound of 2318 with the space of 2322.

reading: Those who have come to know 'this itself is the open void, and we are it' do not think of anything else; for those who looked on broad daylight as darkness, is there an eye of knowledge with which to see?
nuance: வெட்டவெளி, the cut-open or bare space, is the Siddhars' word for the state with nothing in it; யாம் இது, 'we are this', is the identity claim the Vedantic Siddhars make. The question in the second half is rhetorical: the fault is in the eye, not in the light.

reading: 'மூல முதலி மொள்ளே', so our guru Mular said in days gone by; clearing the doubt that the four Vedas spoke at such length, bliss welled up and overflowed.
nuance: The quoted words are cipher or corrupt: மூல முதலி may be 'the root, the first' and மொள்ளே a verb of drawing or scooping (மொள்ளு), so perhaps 'draw from the root, the first', as a saying of the guru; the reading leaves it untranslated. நமது குரு மூலர் claims Tirumular as the poet's guru, as 2307 claims Nandi as grandfather. சங்கை may be doubt or the conch; doubt fits தெளிந்து.

reading: With 'he' and 'I' gone, never forgetting the guru's grace, the poet knew himself by himself; he stayed in nishtai, the fleshly body not perishing, in the state where the eye that reached it does not sleep.
nuance: என்னை என்னால் அறிந்தேன், knowing oneself by oneself, repeats 2317. ஊனுடல் அழியாமல் is the siddha claim that the body is preserved in trance or beyond it; set against 2315's false cage, it shows the two Siddhar attitudes to the body side by side in one song. துயிலாத விழி is the open-eyed absorption, as tradition describes it.

reading: Knowing by understanding that all the arisings seen through the expansion of one thing are empty imagination, the poet saw the dance at Chidambaram and broke into a song of bliss.
nuance: ஒரு பொருள் விரிவாலே: the many are the one thing expanded, and so விழல் (straw, empty) and கற்பனை (imagination). The dance at Chidambaram closes the song where the dance at the nose-tip (2301) and at the goddess's seat (2318) began; whether Chidambaram here is the town or the inner hall the verse does not say.

title: காகபுசுண்டர் ஞானம்
theme: Kakapusundar opens his Njanam by collapsing the whole of yoga into one place, the crown of the egg (அண்டவுச்சி), reached by fixing the mind at the uvula so that the breath subsides upward. Against it he sets everything else as waste: the counted supports and places, mantras, nose-tip gazing, tongue-raising hatha yoga, Vedas and Puranas, temples, tirthas and flower pooja. A cosmology of sun, moon and fire twining down one nerve from the crown to the two eyes carries the method.
structure_note: Invocation and the teacher's announcement to his disciple Vasimuni (2326 to 2330); the crown, the nerve and the three lights (2331 to 2337); against mantras, with the sign of the unspoken letter (2338 to 2340); kalpa, samadhi and the forehead eye (2341 to 2346); against ritual, ending with the uvula method that the chapter has been circling (2347 to 2350). Every verse begins with the last word of the one before (அந்தாதி).
source_issues: 2327: காமென்ற வீடமதிற் is obscure and may be corrupt.
2328: விடமுண்ட அண்டமதை is unclear; the sense of the last line depends on it.
2348: பார்த்தீப லிங்கத்தை and கத்தபம்போற் are unexplained words, possibly corrupt.
2347: புரா ணங்காவ் யங்கள் is split oddly across the metrical break (புராணங் காவ்யங்கள்).

reading: We bow to the Being-Consciousness-Bliss that, as the supreme Parapara everywhere, became sun, moon and fire, let the five elements and maya appear, made countless crores of eggs, became endless lives, showed its form even as the differing faiths, and rose and stands in the egg.
nuance: ரவிமதியுஞ் சுடர்மூன்று, sun, moon and fire as three lights, is the image the whole work returns to (2333, 2337, 2395, 2404); tradition takes them as the two breaths and the fire at the centre of the body as much as as cosmic lights. மதபேதமாகவுந்தான் வடிவைக் காட்டி makes the sects themselves forms the One takes, which softens the attacks on sects that follow.

reading: The teacher announces that, having gone in the sushumna at the crown of the egg beyond the city where Om ends, with name gone, he will set out yoga-jnana and make clear collyrium and tilaka, medicine, the eight karmas and the whole art called alchemy, and show the seed of true knowledge.
nuance: The verse is a table of contents: அஞ்சனம் (collyrium, a siddhi of sight or invisibility, delivered in 2402), வயித்தியம் (medicine, 2400), அட்ட கர்மம் (the eight magical acts) and வாதம் (alchemy, 2397 to 2399). காமென்ற வீடம் is obscure; it may be the house of desire or a corrupt word.

reading: He will tell the way called yoga: hold the five senses within the Supreme; whoever, without knowing, talks sects, fails to reach the holy crown, and says the supports are many and the places twelve, stacked one on another, talks bravely and wastes away; look with desire on the egg that drank poison.
nuance: The attack is on chakra-doctrine itself: counting ஆதாரம் and பன்னிரண்டு தலங்கள் is set against the one place. விடமுண்ட அண்டம் is unclear; it may recall Siva who drank the poison, so that the crown is his throat, or be a corrupt phrase.

reading: Every place is the crown of the egg; go to the lotus at the eighteenth tier, lock the mind there without slipping and enter Brahman for good: there there are no mantras, no fate, no intellect, no destiny; it will dawn when the mind is one, so stay pure and do tapas.
nuance: பதினெட்டாங் கோடு, the eighteenth tier, is not explained; the sixteen kalas of the moon plus two, or a count of the lotus's levels, are the usual guesses. மதியில்லை can be 'no intellect' or 'no moon', the moon-breath having ended; the verse's run of negations reads either way.

reading: Listen, son Vasimuni: in the thousand verses he gave earlier he told truly the drugs, salts, bound and melted substances and the way of gems, without a lie; in this book he will tell all the silence in order, so listen bowing.
nuance: The disciple is வாசிமுனி, the breath-sage, and later வாசிநாதா; the name makes the pupil the breath itself. The earlier ஆயிரம் is an alchemical work claimed as Kakapusundar's; the verse marks the turn from alchemy to மவுனம், which the formulas of 2397 to 2403 then undo.

reading: Khechara is the crown of the egg; for those who see it firmly it becomes silence; call it Parabrahma yoga; as it is stacked, awareness is lifted high; the khechara gem, bindu and nada thicken and gather; daily one can see the whole egg dancing with Shakti and hear the sound of anklets.
nuance: கேசரம் is the khechari of hatha yoga, there a tongue seal; here it is a place, the crown, which prepares the rejection of the physical tongue-practice in 2350. கெவுனமணி is obscure (perhaps the sky-gem). The anklet sound is the inner nada, as tradition has it.

reading: In Brahman one can see the certainty: standing in the crown of the egg it produced the sense-organs, created the crop of lives in the world for ever, became the seven kinds of birth called the bond and the four kinds of womb, and so the eggs are endless upon endless.
nuance: ஏழுவகைத் தோற்றம் and நாலுவகை யோனி are the standard classifications of births and wombs. The body-crown and the cosmic egg are one word, அண்டம், so creation is told as happening in the head.

reading: In the middle of Brahman came sun, moon and fire as three; divided they twine and flow downward; he tells the light in the two eyes: beyond the tip of the crown a nerve hangs like a banyan's aerial root, twines straight into the two eyes, and becomes light and fills them.
nuance: The anatomy is coded: the நரம்பு from the crown to the eyes, the three lights flowing down it. Tradition reads the eyes as the seats of sun and moon; the plain picture is of the optic path, which the next verse calls the three-part sushumna in the skull.

reading: When the light of Parabrahman flows along the nerve-way in the ten, it becomes light in the two eyes and the whole egg appears as one; the nerve, the hanging root's circle, becomes the three-part sushumna in the skull; he will tell more for the ear and the tongue.
nuance: பத்திலே is unexplained (ten nadis? ten breaths?). முக்கூறாய்ச் சுழுனை puts the sushumna, usually the spinal channel, in the skull and gives it three parts, perhaps the three lights.

reading: In the root, in the linga, the nerve runs from below upward along the staff and by the nape path, well through the nerve, rising as high as the egg's top; joined with the nerve named before it twines and becomes the brow-centre.
nuance: மூலம், லிங்கம், தண்டு and பிடர் மார்க்கம் are the perineum, the genital, the spine and the nape; the verse traces the central channel without naming kundalini. தமர்போலே (like a hole, or like a drill) is unclear.

reading: What is the brow-centre: it is the crown of the egg that is Parabrahman; the middle of the nerve named before is fixed as the sushumna; when you drive the mind straight at the uvula, the mind leaps into the sushumna and the five elements merge as one.
nuance: Brow-centre, crown, sushumna and uvula are made one place in four lines; the method is to send the mind, not the tongue or the breath, to the அண்ணாக்கு. This is the verse that 2339 and 2350 enforce.

reading: Through the nerve named before the sun, moon and fire fill, twine and flow downward; when one looks at the inner one they subside; we have said openly the gaze of the Nadanta Parabrahman; the bindu too is the crown of the egg: plant the chitta there firmly.
nuance: ஓமடா opens the last couplet as the syllable and as an exclamation. நாதாந்தம், the end of sound, is one of the six ends; the verse claims to tell openly what is usually hidden, a claim 2393 repeats against other siddhas.

reading: The crown of the egg is the ocean in which the fourteen worlds show through the Supreme; this is the way of silence where the siddhi of siddhas plays; when were the mantras born, when did Vishnu and Brahma come, when did the three gunas arise? See the sign of the unspoken letter.
nuance: The questions place mantras, gods and gunas after Brahman, so none can be the way to it. கூறாத அட்சரத்தின் குறி, the sign of the unspoken letter, recurs (2358, 2394): a letter that is not spoken, which the verse offers in place of mantra.

reading: They do not see: were gracious mantras born before Brahma arose? Learning endless mantras without seeing, staring at the nose-tip and calling it the sushumna, wandering in vain like madmen, they perish root and all, worthless cattle; only those who know the sign and look straight at the uvula have release.
nuance: A polemic against nasikagra-drishti, gazing at the nose-tip, which other schools take as the seat of the sushumna; Kakapusundar moves it to the uvula. மூக்குநுனி and அண்ணாக்கு are set against each other as false and true place.

reading: Release: when you think a mantra the mind splits in two; truth is the mind alone as one, sitting apart and pushing away sleep; if the intellect enters Brahman the whole earth will bow to you; not wandering in deceit, the breath that climbs the nape path is itself the kalpa.
nuance: The objection to mantra is psychological: a mantra makes a second thing in the mind. கற்பம், the rejuvenating preparation of the medical siddhas, is redefined as the ascending breath, so that 2341 can speak of drinking it.

reading: When one drinks the honey that is the kalpa called self, its name is sanchara samadhi; the flesh's hunger ends and anger goes; going to the hill of rising and piercing through, the seven screens called honey burn away; for those who go to the centre of the crown all the instruments called king subside and one can watch Death's dance.
nuance: சஞ்சார சமாதி, the samadhi of moving about, is the siddha's waking absorption (also 2376). உதயகிரி, the hill of rising, is a cipher for the crown or the brow. கூற்றுவனாராட்டம் can mean watching Yama's play from safety or seeing Death's dance ended; the sense turns on whether ஆட்டம் is defeat or performance.

reading: One can see: one leg (or wind) is raised high and sings, one is let down; the one that looks upward is named moon, son, and the one that looks downward you may take as sun; and above the crown of the egg, on the way, is the dwelling of the great fire.
nuance: கால் is both leg and wind. Plainly the picture is the dancer with one foot raised; as cipher, tradition takes the upward wind as the moon-breath and the downward as the sun-breath, with fire at the crown. Both readings stand, and the verse seems to intend both.

reading: Not knowing this, siddhas gathered and said there are sixty-four yogas in the world, each different, and wandering they perished, endless crores; one who looked at raja yoga, knew the state and saw is one in a crore; without speaking, with the mind's eye, see the space, the place where the bindu leapt.
nuance: ராசாங்க யோகம், raja yoga, is here the yoga of the mind set at one place, against sixty-four counted methods. The sixty-four match the sixty-four arts and attainments elsewhere in the tradition.

reading: Having seen with the eye all unseen sights, he got the name Kaka Pusundar; wandering a while unseeing, he approached the Brahman called the pole and asked, and it told him without shame to seek in the crown of the egg with the mind and look unbending, and he fixed the mind as one without flinching.
nuance: The teacher's own guru is Brahman itself, துருவம், the fixed pole; no human lineage is given until 2389. The etymology of காகபுசுண்டர் is left to the reader; the crow form is explained in 2373.

reading: Fixing the mind as one in the heart, setting there as one the thing that is supreme bliss, staying filled in nirvikalpa samadhi for many crores of years, when he opened the forehead eye and looked the whole earth was filled as one; so fix the thought as one, remove the door and see the Cause and play.
nuance: லலாடக்கண், the forehead eye, is the inner sight that 2362 develops. கபாடம், the door or bolt, is in tradition the closed passage at the crown (brahmarandhra). The heart (இருதயம்) appears as the place of fixing, against the crown elsewhere.

reading: Playing and becoming awareness, seeing the light of the uncut wheel, knowing the brow eye in the stable egg, removing the serpent's venom, unwavering, kin to no one, pushing off the lure of the jewelled woman, taking Brahman alone as companion, hold the mind in check as silence.
nuance: வெட்டாத சக்கரம், the uncut wheel, recurs in 2350; it may be the wheel of the crown or the unbroken circle of light. அரவு விடம், the serpent's venom, is read by tradition as kundalini's poison, or plainly as the venom of the senses; the verse does not decide.

reading: Told to stand, men of the world will not settle into fixity and samadhi; like experts they will recite Vedas, Puranas, kavyas and crores upon crores of mantras, and saying temple and tirtha they wander about, thieves and hollow; not knowing the one Brahman-state that wins, they fall like a tree without root.
nuance: திருடர்கள், thieves, is the word for pilgrims; the image of the rootless tree makes the state of Brahman the root and all texts and shrines the foliage.

reading: Taking flowers and setting up a linga they do not bow to the ... linga; bathing it and doing pooja the vain ones bawl; when you pluck the flower it has become like a dead body, so see clearly; those who with the mind see within the Supreme have the body of Kailasa.
nuance: பார்த்தீப லிங்கம் is unclear (perhaps பார்த்திப, the linga of earth or of the king, or the luminous linga; the sense of the line depends on it) and கத்தபம் is obscure. The plucked flower as a corpse is the verse's own argument: an offering is a killing. கயிலாசத் தேகம், the Kailasa body, is the siddha's perfected body.

reading: Not approaching the Brahman that is self, saying the gods on earth are endless and this one a guru and that one a disciple, cattle that never saw the hill of rising, doing lies, theft and murder, lusting after prostitutes and becoming vain, such a one will not reach the guru's feet; he will fall into hell.
nuance: The verse condemns both the multiplication of gods and the guru-disciple relation as ways of not approaching Brahman, yet ends by making the guru's feet the goal; 2357 resolves this by making guru and disciple marks of the one Brahman.

reading: Those who raised the tongue to the uvula and gazed got no result; the eyes burst and the body goes; they call it hatha yoga, and it is not fit; set the mind straight at the uvula and look: the breath subsides above and does not look downward, and one can know the uncut wheel.
nuance: அடயோகம் is hatha yoga and the practice rejected is khechari mudra, the tongue turned back to the palate. Kakapusundar keeps the place and changes the instrument: the mind, not the tongue, goes to the uvula, and the breath then stays above of itself.

title: காகபுசுண்டர் ஞானம்
theme: Rules for the disciple and a polemic against the gurus of the world: the mind made an atom and sent to the crown, the kalpa herbs and the nectar reread as inner things, ochre-robed teachers who sell instruction, and siddhas who built rival sastras. The disciple then asks where lives go when all the eggs are void, and the teacher answers with his own history through the dissolutions: Vishnu asleep on the banyan leaf gathering lives in his lotus, the pillar of fire with the androgynous queen within it, creation handed back to Vishnu, and Kakapusundar surviving each pralaya as a crow on the northern mountain.
structure_note: Method and conduct for the disciple (2351 to 2357); the false gurus and the bookish siddhas (2358 to 2360); the true jnani and the forehead eye (2361 to 2363); the disciple's question on the void (2364) and the teacher's narrative of pralaya, the fire-pillar and creation (2365 to 2373); the teacher's longevity and the return of the mind to the crown (2374 to 2375).
source_issues: 2366: வருதியாய் is an odd form, perhaps for வருவதாய்.
2373: the syntax of நலமாக இன்னமுந்தான் அகண்ட மானால் is loose; whether the crow form is taken at each re-creation or once is unclear.
2375: நடுவணைய முச்சிநடு has உச்சி written as முச்சி by sandhi.

reading: Know that the mind itself becomes life, and joining the egg is release; one can ride the horse; the five great sins fly away; making the wide mind an atom and seeing the fate of what is left and what is touched, the sign called kundali is the crown of the egg, and he tells it as the state of the triangle.
nuance: பரி, the horse, is the Siddhars' usual cipher for the breath, so riding it is breath-mastery; a plain reading of a horse is not meaningful here. முக்கோணம், the triangle, is in tantra the seat at the root; Kakapusundar moves it, with kundalini, to the crown. விட்டகுறை தொட்டகுறை is the karmic remainder from past lives.

reading: Do not go about among the men of the world but stand alone; do not overeat; do not speak a one-sided judgement; do not forget the letter; do not wander wearily; do not consort with one possessed by the demon of lust; see the Cause and play.
nuance: A rule-list in negatives. ஓமென்ற and ஆமென்ற அட்சரம் carry the syllable Om and its affirming form; the letter not to be forgotten is the unspoken letter of 2338 rather than a recited mantra, on the chapter's own terms.

reading: Play, pluck and eat the karunelli: the head will not cook, so look with desire; catch and eat the white rat-snake, son, and it becomes the undying leg; drink the milk of the flame without wavering; the pillar of fire has become the sushumna; join the four kalai that are going to the eight, and see the guileless body.
nuance: A plain reading has a herb (கருநெல்லி, black gooseberry) and a snake (வெண்சாரை) eaten as kalpa; in the Siddhars' cipher both are names for the inner nectar and the breath, and the third line, drinking the milk of the flame, is inner on any reading. The verse is history of a claim, not a recipe. கலைநாலு ... எட்டில் is unexplained; the four and the eight may be breath-measures or the moon's digits.

reading: Seeing and seeing, as the mind goes to the egg the four kalai and the eight merge; do not act at odds, for if the mind turns elsewhere you will never know the Supreme; serve and approach the great ones, son, worship and hear this book with love; if they will not tell you, this book will; keep the mind restrained and win.
nuance: The book offers itself as a substitute guru, இந்நூல் சொல்லும், while still telling the disciple to serve the great ones; 2360 explains the distrust.

reading: Vain men speak of a vidya-mantra; leap instead to the hill of vidya, son, for when you climb and look it shows the transcendent vidya-mantra without end; seeing that state you will do creation and destruction in a minute; nectar bubbles up and you may eat the fruit that has no other.
nuance: விஞ்சை is vidya as magic; the verse turns the magician's mantra into the hill of the crown. The claim to create and destroy in a minute is the siddha's share in the Lord's five acts.

reading: One can eat it: when absorbed in Brahman it melts and flows in the firm egg; the sugar of nectar appears, sweet with milk, firmly, son; one can stay there, the body unknowing, and the coat slips off and it is like gold; by the lamp of true knowledge, swelling, look: the world is one.
nuance: சட்டை கழன்று, the coat slipping off, is the snake-skin image: either the body is shed, or the old skin is shed and the body turns gold, the kaya siddhi of 2380. திங்கலாம் may be a verb form or the moon; the nectar from the moon is the usual yogic account.

reading: The one Brahman, as many, became an endless dance in the world: good and evil and the four, the names sun and moon, mountains and endless creeping things, and the marks called guru and disciple; fix with one mind on the Lord in whom nada and bindu have subsided.
nuance: The list includes குருக்கள் and சீடன் among the appearances of the One, which answers the trouble of 2349: the guru-disciple pair is real as a mark, not as a second thing.

reading: The siddhas all set up differences and built sastras as if for good; men locked onto the books and never saw the egg in full; like a deer wandering the forest they speak deceitful mouth-jnana; they do not see the cuckoo shut in the cage; see the sign of the unspoken mantra.
nuance: வாய்ஞானம், jnana of the mouth, is the Siddhars' phrase for learned talk. The cuckoo in the cage is the life or the inner sound in the body, by the usual cipher. The complaint against the siddhas' own books returns as a charge of concealment in 2393.

reading: The gurus of this world of signs scrutinise the harsh Vedas yet, not knowing Brahman, proudly slander the great; putting on an ample disguise and wearing ochre, they roam for show like dogs, mockingly carrying the staff and walking hunched over the earth.
nuance: காவி (ochre) and தண்டு (the staff) are the marks of the sannyasi; the verse attacks the garb, not renunciation. குறட்டிட்டு நடப்பான் pictures the affected stoop of a holy man.

reading: The sinner calls disciples and says he will give instruction to take their money; showing no state of Brahman he tells lies as wide as the sky; it becomes sin for the disciple and a flaw for the guru who prescribes fixity; he does not see the place where things subside, and when it fails he says it was ended by fate.
nuance: The guru's appeal to விதி, fate, is the mark of the fraud: he explains his pupil's failure by destiny because he never knew the place. 2329 had already removed fate from Brahman.

reading: Entering the egg called the sky, seeing the lamp at the centre of the crown of the northern mountain, bathing in the pure Siva-Ganga called honey and putting on the holy name, offering the loving mind as the flower, seeing the harsh Vedas subside, chitta becoming buddhi: those who are clear in this are true jnanis.
nuance: Every rite rejected in 2347 and 2348 returns inside: the tirtha is the Ganga at the crown, the name-mark and the flower are the mind's love. வடவரை, the northern mountain, is Meru and the head.

reading: When you see the egg as one, the many differing mayas flee in panic; you will stand as yourself in every life born in the egg, the whole-egg and the Brahma-egg; when the forehead eye opens it shows mingled all the sights the eye cannot hold; the upper circle, the wide wheel: follow and join it in the space of true knowledge.
nuance: உயிர்தோறும் நீயாய் நிற்பாய், you stand as yourself in every life, is the verse's claim of pervasion, made for the seer rather than for the Lord.

reading: Joining is this: with the mind one and knowing its nature, not dancing about but attentive, not reading many books, going to the space at the centre of Parapara's crown, watching the dance of 'thondhom', seeing the thousand and eight petals tier on tier, know the lamp that does not fade, like rain on withering crops.
nuance: தொந்தோம் is a dance syllable, and may also carry தொம் and தத், the thou and that of the great saying; the verse does not settle it. ஆயிரத்தெட்டிதழ், a thousand and eight petals, is the crown lotus, usually a thousand. பலநூலைப் படித்திடாமல் makes the refusal of books a condition.
