reading: The disciple asks: you have spoken true knowledge and the foot of the state of Parapara; but when all the eggs become void and the Virat Brahman alone stands as one, where are all the lives, where are the siddhas and the three murtis, where is the place that water rests? Guru, tell me this.
nuance: The question is cosmological, where souls are during dissolution, and the answer that follows (2365 to 2373) is a Puranic narrative rather than a yogic one, the only such stretch in the work.

reading: He will tell, son Vasinatha: in the assembly of the gracious Isvara, at the time of the pralaya that tests, Vimala asked Vishnu where living beings, siddhas and sages were to stay, and the cloud-bodied one looked at him, bowed, and considered his answer.
nuance: The scene is told as witnessed; Kakapusundar places himself in Siva's court at the dissolution, as 2366 confirms.

reading: Vishnu will think: I sleep on the banyan leaf, and the weighty living beings and endless siddhas will gather firmly in my lotus, and I will stand sustaining them; and when Vishnu with his bearer said that Pusundar too would come, Siva called me as the sruti and asked, and I spoke good words as a sutra.
nuance: The infant Vishnu on the banyan leaf in the waters of dissolution is the Puranic Markandeya scene. வலவன் may be the charioteer or Garuda. The teacher is summoned as சுருதி, as if he were scripture, a large claim made in passing.

reading: Looking at Siva's face: when all the lives of countless crores of eggs, with the siddhas and sages, and Vishnu too sleep on the banyan leaf, they gather by nature in the lotus of the navel; and passing beyond the five I came swiftly by the street-way.
nuance: ஐவர், the five, are probably the five gods of the five acts (Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, Mahesvara, Sadasiva); வீதிவழி, the street-way, may be the sushumna. The poet claims to pass beyond the gods who are themselves dissolved.

reading: Going through the sky, child, the wheel spun and danced; mounting the wheel without slipping I went beyond it; going a long way I surely saw the state of the pillar; it stands spread like fire, and no space or anything else could be seen.
nuance: சக்கரம் here is the spinning wheel of the cosmos or of the crown, which the seer rides past; கம்பம், the pillar of fire, is Siva as the lingodbhava column, the form in which neither Brahma nor Vishnu could find his ends.

reading: The pillar of fire is everywhere as one; in the pillar's middle a queen stands united; oho, when I looked at her face, seen from the front it was a male form and seen from behind a female form, son; and I stayed within the pillar as substance with substance.
nuance: The androgyne in the pillar is Ardhanarisvara, Siva and Shakti as one body; the poet's claim to have remained there வத்தோடே வத்தாக, substance with substance, is a claim of identity with it.

reading: So for endless time I lived within Parapara; when Brahman relented and gave grace to create the whole, the woman who was in the pillar appeared both as Vimala and as Uma, and from within the wheel she called Vishnu: see the resolve.
nuance: Creation begins as grace (அருள்) and a relenting (மனமிரங்கி) in Brahman; the agent is Shakti, who takes both Siva's and Uma's forms, and Vishnu is her instrument.

reading: Vishnu in the lotus called out all the lives of countless crores of eggs, showed them the three gunas, and set out the standing oceans and the earth, the sun and moon, the rising mountains, forests and living beings, the nine planets and the stars, and the four Vedas.
nuance: The Vedas are listed last among created things, after the planets, which is the cosmological form of the chapter's argument that scripture is not the way.

reading: Making gods and elements, sky and earth in the world, Meru and the mountains, temples, tirthas and tanks, with Brahman alone as witness he filled every life everywhere; without roaming, see silence, and listen to more so as to win.
nuance: கோவில், தீர்த்தம் and குளம் are placed among created things beside mountains and elements, which relativises them without denying them.

reading: So when the pralayas have numbered seven lakh crores, Hari and Ayan and living things are absorbed in the Brahman called the whole; I too go that way; and when it again becomes the whole, I took the form of the crow and perched in the nest of the northern mountain.
nuance: The grammar of lines six and seven is loose: whether the crow form is taken at each re-creation or once is not clear. The crow (காகம்) is finally explained as the teacher's own body between creations, Meru's nest being the head.

reading: So through the yugas I have been on earth, how many crores of times; is there anyone who knows as I do? I became the beginning of the primal siddhi; when I went to Vimala's place he lifted me with joy and kissed me and told me to stay on Kailasa; I remained in the crow form.
nuance: ஆதியென்ற சித்திக்கும் ஆதியானேன் claims that Kakapusundar is the origin of siddhi itself; the kiss from Siva makes him a child of the god rather than a pupil.

reading: In the crow form, watching all the causes as seed, watching steadily the race of the open space, I circled far and still saw no detail; then, making the spread mind an atom with longing, forcing the supreme space to become the mind's space, reaching the egg, I came to the middle of the centre of the crown.
nuance: The cosmic narrative ends by returning to method: the outer search over vast distance fails, and the mind made an atom at the crown succeeds. The last line's முச்சி is உச்சி in sandhi.

title: காகபுசுண்டர் ஞானம்
theme: The linga is one and inner; the perfected body (காயசித்தி) comes from the mind's absorption in Brahman and not from any herb; the disciple's questions on dream, the birth of life and the circling of sun and moon are answered with the place called suzhutthi, whose visions and sweetness are a lure to pass. The teacher gives his lineage and denies caste, blames the other siddhas for hiding the egg in cipher, reinterprets the three sandhis as sun, moon and fire, and then, with the purchase of rock salt, turns to alchemy: a red sindhuram that masters the nine metals, oils and a medicine for every disease.
structure_note: The one linga and the breath in Brahman (2376 to 2378); the disciple's question and kaya siddhi, the eight siddhis and the rejection of herbal kalpa (2379 to 2383); the disciple's questions and the suzhutthi (2384 to 2388); the teacher's birth, clan and the denial of caste (2389 to 2392); against the siddhas' cipher, and pooja reread as the three lights (2393 to 2397); the sindhuram and the oils (2397 to 2400).
source_issues: 2377: பாணம் பாணம் and தேனுக்குந் தேவனா are obscure and possibly corrupt.
2385 to 2387: சுழுத்தி is used for a body-place, where the rest of the work has சுழுனை (sushumna); either a different term or a scribal confusion.
2389: வடசாளி is unexplained.
2398: வப்பிலையும் is unclear, perhaps அப்பிலையும்; தமர்வாய் is uncertain.
2400: தலைப்பிண்டம், கொடி and மா are unidentified substances.

reading: A litany of the one linga: the linga grown in the central sky and on Mahameru's summit, the linga that is Shakti and the breath, the linga filled in sanchara samadhi, the linga praised by the mind made one through intellect, the linga sprouted in the flower, the linga come to be praised in every direction, the one supreme linga.
nuance: No stone is in the list; every linga named is a state or a place in the body-cosmos, and the eighth line makes them one. பூவரு is unclear, perhaps the lotus of the crown.

reading: Entering the small house called self, fix the breath that has turned its head so that it subsides in Brahman called the king; with mind subdued look closely; the arrow joins the sky; when you eat, son, hunger ends; the coats slip off, and one can be a god even to the gods.
nuance: தலைமாறிப் போன வாசி, the breath that has changed head, is the breath reversed upward, as tradition reads it. பாணம் பாணம் (arrow, arrow) and தேனுக்குந் தேவன் are obscure; the last may be 'a god to the honey' or a corrupt word for the gods.

reading: One can remain through all the yugas in the solitary Brahman; with the mind subdued and silence gained, and yet from great desire within Brahman, the great ones who know the state can take any avatara they wish, as gurus, as kings, as Indra, or as the three gods.
nuance: பேராசை, great desire, is given a positive sense: the one absorbed in Brahman can still choose to appear in the world. The verse grounds the teacher's own serial births (2389, 2390).

reading: The disciple says: my guru Pusundanatha, you said that living things, the whole, and the three murtis are absorbed in Brahman, and then told the sign by which the whole is created again; and you told me to drink the honey; tell me truly its details.
nuance: மது, the honey, is the kalpa of 2341 and 2353, the disciple having rightly heard it as something to be explained rather than taken literally.

reading: He will tell, son Vasinatha: truly when you go into the egg the praised fire enters, and joined with the five senses it becomes awareness; your body becomes very rare without changing, son, a wonder; and when shadow and reflection are lost, the kaya siddhi is firm.
nuance: நிழற்சாய்கை யற்று, losing shadow and reflection, is the traditional mark of the perfected body in Siddhar lore; the verse makes the test physical and observable.

reading: When it has become rare, the eight great siddhis all eight dance; the breath merges and subsides in Brahman; front rank and back rank become one; seeing the silence that bakes and bakes, the place where one stands with the kalai changed is the golden seat; when you see yourself there is no more swimming: the way called samadhi is fixed.
nuance: முன்னணி பின்னணி may be the two breaths or front and back of the body; நீச்சென்றுமில்லை, no swimming, is probably no more crossing the sea of birth; காச்சென்று காச்சிவிடும், the silence that bakes, uses the alchemist's firing for the inner heat. The sense of several words is guessed.

reading: Not knowing the state of tapas they wander disheartened in the world; the great ones who with longing saw silence within thirty years stay young, son; seeing the true guru's feet, worshipping them with compassion, and sending the mind firmly into Brahman, one can be life to life.
nuance: முப்பதுக்குள், within thirty, sets an age for attainment; those who find silence before thirty do not age after it. சீவனுக்குச் சீவன், life of life, is the state and not a metaphor.

reading: One can remain: there is no kalpa of plant or root; in the solitary Brahman, melting, with the mind subdued, as one looks the body itself became firm; not roaming in confusion, not talking sects, not consorting with wastrels, not keeping company with the ... , see the guru's feet and bow deeply.
nuance: செடிபூடு கற்பமில்லை is the plainest rejection of herbal kalpa in the work, and stands against 2353 and the formulas from 2397. கோளர் is unclear (slanderers? the planets?).

reading: The disciple asks the murti of true knowledge to divide and tell the foot and head of the Supreme, to tell firmly the place where dreams are seen in abundance, the place where smell is born, the way the sun and moon circle, and the place where life is born.
nuance: The five questions are answered in 2385 to 2396 with a single place, the suzhutthi; மணம் may be smell or marriage.

reading: He tells with his mouth: at the foot of great Brahman the nerve named before twines unceasingly, and sun and moon circle and dance; the breath stands in the middle without perishing; if the mind goes by that way to the place of suzhutthi, its name is body-suzhutthi; see, and knowing it is awareness.
nuance: சுழுத்தி is the name of the deep-sleep state in the avastha scheme, but here it is a place (சுழுத்தியிடம்) with the qualifier காயான, of the body; the verse seems to mean the sleep-centre where dreams arise, answering 2384. Possibly a confusion with சுழுனை.

reading: There many forms appear and it shows them again like your own deity; like a woman of flesh joining you, as if in intercourse, the suzhutthi that bewitches like honey shows a taste like sweetness; bowing to the guru's grace and knowing the sign, see the state of fullness beyond it.
nuance: Visions of one's deity and erotic dreams are treated alike as the suzhutthi's lure; the teacher does not deny them but ranks them below பூரணம், fullness, and makes the guru's grace the means of passing them.

reading: The unstable ocean became the suzhutthi; join the standing breath to the space; join the chief fire likewise; truly join sun and moon together; without wavering, saying 'one Parapara', with mind subdued look at the crown of the egg: the mind goes to the Supreme without wandering and dances along the sky-street.
nuance: The instruction is a series of joinings, breath, fire, sun and moon, that the tradition reads as the union of the two breaths with the central fire; the plain words are a sequence of 'join' with no measures given.

reading: It dances when, without desire or anger, forgetting mother and kin, one mounts the whole; lock the nine doors and the five senses join in purity; forest or town, what matter, once you see silence; the wish-cow and the wish-tree are yours as siddhi; a lamp set in the house shines, and taken outside it goes to waste.
nuance: நவத்துவாரம், the nine doors, are the body's openings. The lamp image argues against both pilgrimage and display: the practice kept within the body burns, carried out into the world it is lost.

reading: Becoming buddhi and chitta I took the name Pusundan in the world; they call me the son of Vadasali and the son of the rare virgin; among five I was the first born, son; see the vision within the span and the cubit, and they will call that substance Isvara.
nuance: வடசாளி is unexplained. சாண்முழம், a span and a cubit, is the body as the place of vision. The five brothers born of Brahma's seed (2390) are not named elsewhere in the work.

reading: Hear my clan: on earth we five were born from Brahma's seed; I went to the egg of the sky and lived very many crores of years, keeping the mind unfailing in fixity; those who talk are people of the world; see with desire the place reached by letting go and holding.
nuance: The lineage is from Brahma's விந்து, which prepares the claim of 2391 that his only clan is seed. விட்டடைந் தொட்டவிடம் is a riddle phrase: the place reached by releasing and touching.

reading: See, we have no caste or clan; my clan, son, is the clan of seed; one who without seeing talks of caste difference will curl up and perish; in Brahman at the first time all lives were born alike; I too arose that way before, and I sought well the place from which I arose.
nuance: சுக்குலம், the clan of semen, is the argument: all are born the same way from the same stuff, and all lives arose from Brahman together, so caste is a thing said by the unseeing.

reading: A list of faults: not seeking to know the place one arose, not seeing the place one came to in the middle, not seeing the place of birth, reviling the guru, not joining the substance, roaming with the idle, and staying without kinship; the sinner who does not know the Kumbhi and the stone oyster.
nuance: தோஷம் ends seven lines. கும்பி is the hell Kumbhipaka; கற்சிப்பி, the stone oyster, is obscure, perhaps the skull as the shell that holds the pearl.

reading: What jnana has the sinner who does not know? Look at the book Arumugan spoke: it is not said in cipher; look at my valorous book; the siddhas said their books at length but uselessly in concealment, hiding the egg that is the sign and telling it in different ways, which is their fault.
nuance: The charge is against பரிபாஷை, the Siddhars' cipher, by a poet who writes in it; ஆறுமுகன் சொன்ன நூல் is a Murugan-given text he sets beside his own as plain. 2404 then forbids giving his book away, which is concealment by another means.

reading: Without finding fault, going to the egg, seeing the sign of the unspoken mantra, with chitta one, doing pooja to the god at dawn, dusk and noon and gaining clarity; without finding fault, with a loving mind doing tapas facing the guru; when you look with longing and attachment, the supreme Goddess herself comes into your hand.
nuance: அந்திசந்தி யுச்சிக் காலம், the three sandhis, is the Vedic timetable of worship, surprising in a text that scorns pooja; 2395 explains that the three times are the three lights. பற்றாசை, attachment-desire, is for once commended.

reading: If you ask what the dawn, dusk and noon at which she comes are: father, they are the sun, moon and fire become three; go: where the three twine as one and stay is the state of the Brahma-egg; all the lust you have done goes by the grace of Bhuvanai of the trident; and if you join by that way Vani herself dances on your tongue.
nuance: The sandhis are made inner, so the pooja of 2394 is the joining of the three lights; the two gifts are the goddess's removal of past lust and eloquence (Vani on the tongue), which 2396 locates in the uvula.

reading: He tells the house where Vani dwells: along the creeper of the uvula, holding to the egg like a hanging root, the nerve stands fitted in the middle of the stable fire; by that way grace flows, and she speaks in heaven whatever Tamil she pleases.
nuance: Poetic speech is given a bodily seat, the nerve of the uvula; வேணதமிழ், whatever Tamil she wants, makes Tamil the goddess's own tongue.

reading: She speaks all the endless Vedas and Vedic texts, by the Brahman that rose where sruti ends; the great ones who have known themselves win, and do not boast but become silent; who in the world knows the Brahman that has no night or day? Seeing the place where speech ends, be clear; and cunningly buy rock salt, buy it.
nuance: The last line turns without warning from silence to the market: கல்லுப்பு, rock salt, opens the alchemical sequence. Whether this is cipher (salt is a common code for a body-substance) or a literal shopping instruction cannot be settled.

reading: Having bought it, join the brain in the egg and mix in the leaf richly, son; set it inside a twisted spurge, closing the mouth of the hollow and removing the curse; when three months have gone, take out the spurge and, doing no more rite, make a seal of cloth and clay and dry it.
nuance: The verse is an alchemical procedure read here for what it claims: a preparation of salt and some substance sealed in a கள்ளி (spurge) for three months, then sealed with cloth and clay for firing. அண்டத்தில் மூளை (brain in the egg, perhaps an eggshell, perhaps a skull) and வப்பிலை are unclear. சாபந் தீர்த்தே, removing the curse, is the alchemist's word for purifying a substance.

reading: After it has dried, take it, son, and set it devotedly in a kasaputa fire; let it cool, and when you take it out it is a sindhuram of the colour of the dawn sun; smear an atom of it on every drug and set them in the puta: the nine metals yield, and the whole art called vedai is in your hands.
nuance: செந்தூரம் is the red calcined product of Siddha chemistry; நவலோகம் the nine metals; the claim is a universal agent that transmutes. நீருமடா may mean the metals turn to liquid or lose their nature. Read as history of a claim, not as a method.

reading: It is done: all the diseases in the body fly away when an atom of it is eaten; body-siddhi has grown great and one can live joined to the substance; take the oil of the thalaippindam, of the creeper and of the mango; after taking the oil add camphor without hesitation and do pooja to the substance with joy.
nuance: தலைப்பிண்டம் is unexplained (a plant? a prepared ball?); கொடியும் மாவும் may be plant names or a powder. வத்து, the substance, is worshipped, the alchemical product treated as the god, which 2401 continues.

title: காகபுசுண்டர் ஞானம்
theme: The close of the Njanam: the oils and biles promised as collyrium in 2327, which claim to make the wearer unseen, to make courtesans swoon and to split open the netherworld, and a last verse that returns to the three lights made one in Brahman, from which crores of siddhis follow, with the command not to give the book to anyone.
structure_note: Three formula verses (2401 to 2403) continue the oil begun in 2400; the final verse (2404) returns to the method of the whole work and seals the book.
source_issues: 2404 says the work has eighty verses (எண்பதுமே); the corpus has seventy-nine (2326 to 2404), so one verse is lost or the count includes something not transmitted.
2401: ஆசைபுல்லா மணக்கதுவு may be one plant name or two; the metrical break does not settle it.

reading: Having done pooja, preserve it well; take the oil of the wild ridge-gourd, the oils of asaipul and manakkathuvu likewise, add the ghee of kesari, add the bile of the slender loris, add the oil of the thalaippindam, grind it without speaking, son, and add civet and musk.
nuance: A compounding of oils, biles and perfumes, read here for what it claims rather than as a method: the brow-collyrium of 2402. பேய்ப்பீர்க்கு is the wild ridge-gourd; ஆசைபுல், மணக்கதுவு and தலைப்பிண்டம் are not identified; கேசரி may be lion or saffron. பாசையடா பேசாமல், grinding without speaking, is a rite condition.

reading: Put an atom of it on the brow and go firmly: who then will see you, by the grace of the Brahman called the egg; and bring the bewildering herb, add the oil already named, grind it and put it on the brow: many courtesans will swoon.
nuance: Two claims: invisibility (the அஞ்சனம் promised in 2327), credited to Brahman's grace as much as to the paste, and the swooning of prostitutes, a love-charm. திகைப்பூண்டு, the plant of bewilderment, is a cipher-name or a folk name; the verse sits awkwardly beside 2349's condemnation of lusting after prostitutes.

reading: Add the milk of the thillai, black tulasi, the bile of the bat and the bile of the monkey, add the seed already named, grind firmly for one watch, take what is ground and put it on the brow and look: the netherworld splits open and runs, and you may see with desire the exploration of Vedanta.
nuance: பாதாளம் பிளந்தோடும், the netherworld splitting, is the claim of a siddhi of sight or of passage through the earth; வேதாந்த சாரணை, the exploration (or the charana siddhi) of Vedanta, is an odd phrase that joins the magical claim to the doctrinal word. Read as history of a claim.

reading: Going within Parabrahman, with sun, moon and fire made one, and looking surely at the Primal and at the enemy, he will turn to ash; crores upon crores of siddhis can be fixed by Brahman; do not give this book to anyone; with victory the eighty are complete.
nuance: எதிரி, the enemy, may be an outer foe burned by a glance or the inner adversary; the verse allows both. The seal of secrecy, இந்நூலைக் கொடுத்திடாதே, follows 2393's complaint that other siddhas hid their teaching. எண்பது, eighty, counts the work; the corpus has seventy-nine units.

title: அகஸ்தியர் ஞானம்
theme: Agasthiyar's first run of ஞானம்: the one God is the Self and Shakti within, known by a mind subdued through devotion and held at the inner whorl (சுழி), and such a knower is one in a crore. Around that centre the verses attack the four Vedas and their teachers as a livelihood path that leaves everyone wailing in the streets, ask where the breath goes at death and admit no one sees it, and close with a code of plain conduct: truth, no killing, no lying, no anger, no disputation.
structure_note: Nine எண்சீர் விருத்தம் stanzas addressed to 'my children' (என்மக்காள்) and 'அப்பா'. They chain by antadi, each opening with the last word of the one before (மோட்சம், பாரு, ஒருவன், மோட்சம், மூச்சு, பாரு, சத்தியம்). 2405 to 2409 set out the one God and the rarity of the knower; 2410 and 2411 turn to the breath's departure at death and what no one sees; 2412 widens to births in the cosmos and the body as cosmos; 2413 ends with rules of conduct.
source_issues: 2407 line 3: ஒன்றொன்றுக்கு கொன்றை மாறி is corrupt; the sense requires ஒன்றுக்கொன்று மாறி (each at variance with the other).
2412 line 6 (புழுக்கூடு வலைமோ தப்பா) and line 8 (குணவியவா னானக்காற்) are garbled and cannot be construed with confidence.
2411 and 2413 end with a semicolon rather than the stanza's usual close; the final line of 2413 (கதிர்தான் முற்றே) marks the end of the run, so the run is complete as printed.

reading: Shakti, the Supreme, alone is God and has become the life of every living being; those who know this by intellect are the meritorious, one in a crore on earth; the supreme jnani, mind subdued by devotion, stands in the state and does not let the mind drift into the void, and knowing the state in the whorl is itself moksha.
nuance: The sense turns on two coded words. பாழ் here is where the mind must not be let go, a negative emptiness, unlike the fertile void of Tirumular's usage. சுழி (whorl) is read by tradition as the suzhumunai, the central channel at the brow, so that 'knowing the state in the whorl' is a yogic instruction; a plain reading takes it as the still point in the turning mind. சுத்தியே யலைவதில்லை (does not wander in circling) is unclear in syntax.

reading: The secret for gaining moksha is this: do not lie, steal or kill with deceit, throw out fever and anger, set your mind on merit in this world, do not leap or go to waste, and look again and again at the many Vedas and shastras, the path made so the blameless may live; think it over, my children.
nuance: The verse is plainer than the rest of the run, and the line on the Vedas sits oddly beside 2407 and 2411, which say the Vedas are a livelihood and have come to nothing. பிழைக்கச் செய்த மார்க்கம் can mean 'the path made so they may be saved' or, as in 2407, 'the path made so they may make a living'; on the second reading the praise is ironic. காய்ச்சல் is literally fever, here perhaps heat of temper.

reading: Look at the four Vedas, all four: are they for planting attachment and desire, or a pledge worth crores? Each contradicts the other; it is a path made in vain for their livelihood; they wail street by street, and not one of them sees the divine state; who is going to stand firm? the wonder is one in a crore.
nuance: Line 3 ஒன்றொன்றுக்கு கொன்றை மாறி is corrupt; the sense wanted is ஒன்றுக்கொன்று மாறி, each at variance with the other. பிணையோ கோடி (a pledge of crores) may be a sneer at the price put on Vedic learning. அவர்பிழைக்க is here plainly 'for them to make a living', which colours the same phrase in 2406.

reading: Worship God as one, live on the earth as a noble man, sow the crop in its season, and like the supreme jnani do not let the mind go to waste; thieves roam by crores upon crores, cheats fill the land by crores, and many crores will come and beguile you with words: they are thieves.
nuance: The thieves are religious teachers, as 2410 (deceiving gurus) and the whole run make clear. பருவமதிற் சேறுபயிர் (sow the wet field in season) can be plain farming advice, as the verse's picture of an upright householder, or a figure for practice done at the right time.

reading: The Self that is called 'I' and 'he' is itself the one God; worship always the Lord who, when father and mother joined, came holding the embryo as 'I'; even the thief called king knows this one in crores upon crores; one must know the 'why' by the mind, and standing firm, my children, is moksha.
nuance: The God who 'came holding the embryo as I' is the self that enters at conception, so that the one God is the inner self rather than any external deity; this is the plainest statement of the run's theology. கோனென்ற திருடனுக்குந் தெரியும் is odd: either even the thief-king knows, or the thief who calls himself king (the false guru) knows of the rare one. ஏனென்றே அறிய வேணும், 'one must know why', is unusual and may mean knowing the cause.

reading: Hear the secret for gaining moksha: ask for the signs of those who went before, ask the lineages of the deceiving gurus, ask where they all perished together; in talk and in maya there is nothing, the babblers do not see the state; and when the noisy camp breaks up, the breath has gone with the whole of it.
nuance: பாளையம் is an army camp; the body as a camp that breaks up at death is the verse's own image, and கூட்டோடே போச்சுது (went with the whole) is the breath leaving with the body. Whether ஏய்ச்சலது குருக்கள் means gurus who deceive or gurus who are mocked turns on ஏய்ச்சல், which tradition takes as deceit.

reading: Where the breath subsided and went no one sees, nor the dwellings of moksha and hell, nor the ascent of the way by which it came, nor the jewelled way where the wind changes and stands; look well at the open space, for the Vedas and shastras have been emptied out; it is as if settled in the embryo, and only he knows it, so look with awareness.
nuance: The verse says four times that no one sees (காணார்), and leaves open whether 'he who alone knows' is God or the knower. வளிமாறி நிற்குமணி வழி (the jewel way where the wind changes) is read by tradition as the central channel where the two breaths exchange. வெளியாய்ப் போச்சே is either 'have gone to the open', that is, been exposed as empty, or 'have become space'. வெட்டவெளி, the open space, is the Siddhars' term for the void of awareness.

reading: Look: births in the world are crores, and creations of many kinds crores upon crores; births in the cosmos are crores; see how it dances in space; you are the one within the atom-space; the wonder is a worm's nest struck by a net; the cosmos becomes the body, and when one becomes of that nature it is truth.
nuance: Lines 6 and 8 are damaged (புழுக்கூடு வலைமோ தப்பா, குணவியவா னானக்காற்), and the reading of them is a guess. The clear claim is அண்டத்திற் பிண்டமாகும், the cosmos becomes the body: the macrocosm is in the microcosm, the Siddhars' அண்டபிண்டம். அணுவெளி (atom-space) places the self at once in the smallest point and in space.

reading: If you are human you must have truth; do no base act and do not err; do not drop the daily rites, and do not shift from your state, leaving observance, firm practice and samadhi; do not wander witless, do not lie, do not forget merit, do not pick quarrels and dispute with raised voice, and do not walk about as a ritualist: the ray is complete.
nuance: The verse keeps the daily rites (நித்தியகர்மம் விடாதே) yet forbids walking as a கர்மி, a ritualist; the distinction is between doing one's duties and making ritual one's identity. The syntax of lines 3 and 4 allows 'do not leave observance, firm practice and samadhi' or 'having left them, do not shift from the state'; the first fits the list of prohibitions. கதிர்தான் முற்றே (the ray is complete) closes the run.

title: அகஸ்தியர் ஞானம்
theme: A single four-line invocation (காப்பு) that is also the most quoted verse under Agasthiyar's name: if the mind is set right, there is no need to recite mantra, raise the breath or stop the vaasi, for a right mind is itself the right mantra. It places the whole of the following ஞானம் under the primacy of mind over technique.
structure_note: One அறுசீர் விருத்தம் of four lines, each beginning மனமது செம்மையானால் (if the mind is set right), the first three negating a practice (mantra recitation, raising the vital air, halting the vaasi) and the fourth affirming that the mind is the mantra. It is printed as the காப்பு of the work's second run, and 'ஞானம் - 2' is not otherwise headed.
source_issues: The work's second run consists of this one verse headed காப்பு (invocation); there is no run headed ஞானம் - 2, so the numbering of the headed runs skips from ஞானம் - 1 (2405 to 2413) to ஞானம் - 3 (2420 to 2425).

tamil: மனமது செம்மை யானால் மந்திரஞ் செபிக்க வேண்டா;
மனமது செம்மை யானால் வாயுவை வுயர்த்த வேண்டா;
மனமது செம்மை யானால் வாசியை நிறுத்த வேண்டா;
மனமது செம்மை யானால் மந்திரஞ் செம்மை யாமே
reading: If the mind is set right there is no need to recite mantra, no need to raise the vital air, no need to halt the vaasi; if the mind is set right, the mantra is itself set right.
nuance: செம்மை is straightness or rightness, not mere calm. The three practices named are the Siddhars' own: japa, raising the breath along the spine, and holding the vaasi (breath as the practice). The verse does not reject them as false, it makes them unnecessary once the mind is right; the fourth line can also be read as 'the mind is the mantra', the usual way it is quoted. Whether this is a dismissal of technique or a statement of its goal is left open.

title: அகஸ்தியர் ஞானம்
theme: Five units headed உயர் ஞானம் and தனி ஞானம் (higher and separate knowledge), addressed to Pulastya: a practice of drawing the life-letter upward in every act of the body, which makes one live to the end of the earth beyond Death's hand; the one Supreme beyond the crown and beyond Uma and Ganapati, which is one's own life as Siva; bindu, nada and the root from which the two came, whose knower becomes guru; and the siddha as the one who, having known the root, burns the shastras.
structure_note: 2415 and 2416 are the two halves of one eight-line எண்சீர் விருத்தம் split across two units; 2417 to 2419 are three full stanzas under தனி ஞானம், chaining by antadi (ஞானம் முற்றே / விந்து; மூலம் பாரே / மூலமதை). The disciple addressed is புலத்தியன், Pulastya, named in 2418 and 2419.
source_issues: 2415 and 2416 are the two halves of a single eight-line எண்சீர் விருத்தம் (the rhyme runs உண்ணும் / பெண்ணின் / திண்ணும் / மண்ணூழி) printed as two four-line units; 2415 ends in a semicolon mid-stanza.
2417 line 3 runs அம்பரம்ஓம் together without a space, and the heading changes from உயர் ஞானம் to தனி ஞானம் within the run without a new காப்பு.

reading: When you eat, draw the life-letter upward, and when you sleep let it all become that; whenever the organ lets go toward a woman, guard it, turn it to the right and upward, and stand in that state.
nuance: உயிரெழுத்து, the life-letter, is the vowel in grammar and, in the cipher, the breath or the seed-syllable; tradition takes 'drawing it upward' as raising the breath or the semen. The third and fourth lines prescribe retention and upward turning at the moment of emission, a practice the Tirumanthiram also teaches. பேணிவலம் (guarding, to the right) and அவத்தில் (in that state, or in the avastha) are compressed and the exact instruction is unclear.

reading: Food, fruit, leaf and medicine all become that very thing; those who can direct it so every day will live as long as the earth endures, and will not be caught in Death's hand.
nuance: The claim is the Siddhars' kaya-siddhi: a body kept beyond death by the daily practice begun in 2415, of which this is the second half. மதுவே யாகும் (becomes that) makes whatever is eaten feed the practice rather than the body; a plain reading is that food and medicine become nectar. The verse states the claim; it does not describe a preparation.

reading: Standing beyond the one space at the crown, with Uma and Ganapati left behind, the sky-light that is Om, 'a' and 'u', the ordained Supreme, is beyond anyone's reach; your own tuneful life has become Siva, and he who lay on the milk sea has become Vishnu; if you see Ganapati who is the eye with your eye, mingling and melting you will dance: knowledge is complete.
nuance: The sense turns on the letters: அவ்வும் உவ்வும், 'a' and 'u', are two of the three letters of Om, and tradition reads them as Siva and Shakti, or as the sun and moon breaths. The verse first sets the Supreme beyond Uma and Ganapati and then says one's own life is Siva and Vishnu, so the gods are inner states; உந்தி (navel) may also be read for முந்தி, placing Uma and Ganapati at the navel centre.

reading: If you know the standing of bindu and see its wonder, the many-voiced nada becomes the guru; if that nada with an end becomes the guru, you yourself become the guru who is beginning and end; there is no doubt, Pulastya, and all the arts and knowledges are not equal to this; if you do not know the root where the two joined on the day before, look to the root.
nuance: விந்து and நாதம் are the cosmological pair (bindu and nada, the first stirrings of manifestation) and, in the body, semen and sound; the verse's claim that the knower of them becomes his own guru is clear on either reading. முந்தாநாள் இருவருமே கூடிச் சேர்ந்த மூலம், the root where the two joined, is Siva and Shakti, or father and mother at conception (as in 2409); the two readings are the same in the Siddhars' logic.

reading: When the root is known, it is yoga; when it is seen in due order, it is alchemy; before the one who has seen it with skill they stand subdued; he who burns and throws away the shastras is the siddha; virtuous Pulastya, supreme yogi, if you find the salt without erring from the spoken word, and fix the knowing engine that is the light itself, it grants all siddhis: complete.
nuance: வாதம் is alchemy (இரசவாதம்), so the one root yields yoga and alchemy as two orders of the same knowledge. உப்பு, salt, is a cipher word: tradition takes it as the fixed mercury or the body's own substance, and the verse gives no key. எந்திரம் (engine, yantra) for the light is unusual. The burning of the shastras is the run's sharpest claim and conflicts with 2406's command to study them.

title: அகஸ்தியர் ஞானம்
theme: ஞானம் - 3, headed 'this knowledge is for living without hesitating': no one knows where the life goes at death, and the sayings about joining the sky-Siva or fire joining fire are the talk of people who do not know the embryo. The run then gives its own account of scripture: the ancients, Vyasa among them at Siva's order, made up stories, epics and Puranas, six shastras, dharma and adharma, heaven, hell and rebirth, gurus and disciples, to hold the bewildered and for livelihood, and the reader is told to see this clearly.
structure_note: Six stanzas chaining by antadi (மாடே / மாடு; தயங்கி / [missing]; பாடினாரே / பாடினதோர்; தானே / கழிந்திடுவார் loosely). 2420 and 2421 are on death and the unknowing crowd; 2422 to 2425 are one connected argument about the making of the Puranas and the shastras. 2422 has seven lines and no antadi opening, so its first line is probably lost.
source_issues: 2422 has seven lines where the stanza form has eight, and lacks the antadi opening (தயங்க-) that 2421's close calls for; its first line is probably lost. The heading தயங்காமற் பிழைப்பதற்கே இந்த ஞானம் placed before it may itself be a displaced line.
2422 line 4 இயலான ரசந்தனிலீப் புகுந்தாற் போலும் is obscure and may be corrupt.
2423 line 4 மேதஞ் சேர்த்து (மேதம்) is uncertain.

reading: Look: when the life leaves, some say a ruined corpse lies there, some say the life has gone; who has known it? No one; some say it joins the sky-Siva, some say fire joins fire, a crowd of human beings who do not know the embryo; the lustful band together and go seeking the evil way, like cattle.
nuance: The verse reports four sayings about death and rejects all of them with ஆரும் இல்லை, no one has known. கருவறியா, not knowing the embryo, makes the knowledge of conception (2409, 2411) the test of knowing death: the way out is the way in. மாடே, 'like cattle', carries into 2421 by antadi.

reading: Even cattle have one way of going, but man does not know even that much; they say much about hell and heaven, and do not reckon good deed or bad; listen: the dancing goddesses do not think even of joining the kin of the rare Father; they think pointedly of women to ravish, and hesitate at falling into the ground-fire.
nuance: The middle lines are hard: ஆடுகின்ற தேவதைகள் (the dancing deities) may be the gods of the Puranas, who in the next verses are shown as inventions, or the dancing-women; and தளமான தீயில் விழத் தயங்கினார் (hesitated to fall into the fire of the floor) may be the pyre or the fire of lust. The clear claim is that people talk of heaven and hell while reckoning neither deed nor consequence.

reading: The knowledge praised at large is something else; see the knowledge made to bewilder: the ancients gathered and tied on stories, kavyas and Puranas, as though fire had entered the natural essence, and set them to music as 'the six shastras'; and Vyasa too, so that the field might yield, tied them on at Siva's order.
nuance: The stanza has seven lines and lacks the antadi opening expected after தயங்கினாரே, so a line is probably lost, and இயலான ரசந்தனிலீப் புகுந்தாற் போலும் is obscure (perhaps 'like fire entering mercury', an alchemical figure for adulteration). The verse's own heading says this knowledge is 'for living without hesitating'. The charge that Vyasa made the Puranas at Siva's order is repeated in 2423, where the aim is a hidden play (கபடநாடகம்).

reading: Showing the Puranas as proof in this way, they made stories like the Bharata in the world, so as not to let one think that the Maker is oneself; adding deceit as a hidden play, singing much disputation as if it were substance, with treachery, for all who joined the way as true, and pouring on ornament for the Saivas as devotion, they sang the shastras, they sang.
nuance: The key charge is கர்த்தாவைத் தானென்று தோண வொட்டா, not letting one realise that the Maker is oneself: the Puranas are read as a device to keep God external. மேதஞ் சேர்த்து (adding மேதம், deceit or sacrifice) is uncertain. The verse does not spare the Saivas, whose devotion it calls ornament poured on. Whether 'they' are the ancients of 2422 or Vyasa alone is not fixed.

reading: Listen to the way they sang it, the light called the Bharata and the Puranas: that a long-lived Ravana was born, that steadfast Dasaratha's hand conquered, that there was a long-lived king, a sage, one who had received full grace, a god, a dancing demon, a man; they sang it every day as enmity.
nuance: The verse reduces the Ramayana and the Puranas to a cast list (demon, king, sage, god, man) and says their daily theme is enmity (பகையாய்). சோதி (light) for the Bharata-Purana is ironic or a received epithet. The claim is literary and moral, that the epics teach division, rather than that their events are false; 2425 extends it to the doctrines they carry.

reading: The four Vedas and six shastras that bind people say they will perish by sin, and said it only so that it might cease, nothing else; they made two, adharma and dharma, said one escapes, said there is birth and 'I shall be born noble'; and the worldly who are clear say 'gurus' and 'disciples'; all this is for livelihood, see it clearly.
nuance: The reading of அழிந்திடவே சொன்னதல்லால் வேறொன்றில்லை turns on what is to perish: 'said so that sin might cease' (scripture as a useful lie) or 'said only to destroy' (scripture as harm). On either, dharma and adharma, rebirth and the guru-disciple relation are placed among the things made up for a living (சீவனத்துக்கு). This is the run's conclusion and the Siddhars' most radical form of the attack on ritual religion; the reader is told to see (தெளிந்து காணே), not to believe.

title: அகஸ்தியர் ஞானம்
theme: ஞானம் - 4, a sixteen-stanza 'sutra' on பூரணம், the fullness that the elders called God: it is the sixteen kalas, kept by setting the mind at the suzhumunai and holding the vaasi, with the sun and moon breaths exchanged and gathered within the circle of the uvula, where body, life and fullness are one. Against this inner place the run sets the books, caste, idols of stone and copper, and the garbed beggars of 'mouth-knowledge', all invented so that the worldly might make a living; and it binds the disciple to secrecy and to living in accord with the world.
structure_note: Sixteen எண்சீர் விருத்தம் stanzas chaining by antadi throughout (ஆச்சே / ஆச்சப்பா; தானே / தானென்ற; பிழைக்கத்தானே / பிழைப்பதற்கு ... சொன்னேன் / பிரித்துரைத்தேன்). 2426 to 2430 define pooranam and attack the books, caste and idols; 2431 to 2434 give the practice at the suzhumunai in number-cipher (sixteen, eight, four, three, one); 2435 and 2436 are rules of conduct and a warning against garbed beggars; 2437 to 2439 locate pati in the body and list its names; 2440 and 2441 are the author's summary, which calls the run a sutra of twice eight stanzas, matching its sixteen units.
source_issues: 2429 has உழைப்பதற்கு at the start of both line 3 and line 7; one is probably a copyist's repetition (பிழைப்பதற்கு or தழைப்பதற்கு may be meant).
2432 line 3 வாதிகளே (disputants) as a vocative is odd and may be corrupt for a word in -ளே addressing the disciple.
2439 line 2 காசின்யா (for காசி) and line 3 மயிலாடு மேகம் are doubtful readings.
2441 calls the run a sutra of twice eight and of sixteen; the run has sixteen units, so the count is consistent and no unit is missing.

reading: They said that pooranam is God, but one must say what pooranam is; I will tell the cause, listen with attention: the sixteen kalas are pooranam; in this death-dealing world, bewildered and witless, they scorned pooranam; if you set your mind on the elephant and guard pooranam, it becomes the Siva-yoga life called vaasi.
nuance: The verse defines its own term: பூரணம் is the sixteen kalas, which tradition takes as the moon's digits matched to the breath, so that 'guarding pooranam' is keeping the breath whole. வாரணம் (elephant) is a cipher word, read by tradition as the breath or as Ganapati at the root centre; the verse gives no key. மாரணம் (killing) for the world is strong and may be a pun on மரணம்.

reading: In this way the eighteen, Brahma, Vishnu, Hara and all the gods told us to know it as God, and the sages and rishis said the same; without talking, look at the book and keep the renowned pooranam in mind; those who guard pooranam live within the centre of the vaasi.
nuance: பதினெண் பேரும் is the eighteen (gods, or the eighteen Siddhars, or the eighteen Puranas); the verse does not say. 'Look at the book' (நூலைப் பார்த்து) here means this book, in contrast to the many books attacked in 2428 to 2430. வாசி நடு மையம், the centre of the vaasi, is the central channel between the two breaths.

reading: The great ones in the world who said 'I am that', after knowing pooranam the mother, drank the honey-nectar and did the silent Siva-yoga that never cloys; it was for those who trusted the body of flesh that the worldly set up 'the four Vedas', 'the six books', 'I', 'you' and 'caste', so that they might make a living.
nuance: The verse makes caste, scripture and the I-you distinction one invention with one motive, livelihood (பிழைக்க), and the antadi carries பிழைக்க into 2429, where the argument is examined from the other side. பூரணம் is here தாய், the mother, which prepares the goddess-language of 2443 and 2448. தானென்ற பெரியோர்கள் are those who say 'I am that', the knowers of 2409.

reading: 'If the many books were not said for a living, they would stay without knowing pooranam; if books were not tied on for them to toil at, they would wander witless in the world; caste, bindu, father, mother, child and wife were said for them to flourish and to toil, and there is no other way': so, noble one, the knowers sang.
nuance: The verse gives the knowers' defence of the inventions of 2428: books, caste and family keep the unknowing from wandering witless. Whether Agasthiyar endorses the defence or reports it is left open; 2430 treats the result (fools who do not know the cipher) as a fact either way. உழைப்பதற்கு stands in both line 3 and line 7, and one may be a copyist's repetition.

reading: If they had not sung and said it so, the fools of the world would not know the cipher; some, having looked at many books and forgotten themselves, attack others, fall into the pit and die; they waste away on 'name' and 'form', and take stone and copper in the world for God; the fools who seek without knowing pooranam will cease only by barking like dogs.
nuance: பரிபாடை is the Siddhars' word for their cipher (பரிபாஷை), the coded language in which the books are written; the verse's point is that even the books are a cipher the fools cannot read. கற்செம்பைத் தெய்வமென்று, taking stone and copper for God, is the Siddhars' standard attack on idols, shared with Sivavakkiyar and Valmiki. நாய்போல குரைத்து, barking like dogs, is the disputation of 2413.

reading: Those who wandered without seeing are crores upon crores, and those who knew the cause are crores upon crores; will one know it by wailing in vain, and what use is talking science? When without bending you set the mind at the suzhumunai, join the four to the guru's feet in the two-fours, and guard it shamelessly as one thought, the four and the eight become one: fix it and blow.
nuance: The numbers are the run's cipher: tradition takes the four, the eight and the sixteen as the kalas of the breath (2432 maps them to life, pati's feet and pati), and ஊது (blow) as directing the breath. இருநான்கில் நாலைச் சேர்த்து (join the four to the two-fours) and குருபாதம் (the guru's feet, or the foot of the guru as a measure) are not explained. விஞ்ஞானம் here is discursive knowledge, not modern science.

reading: He who knows the blowing of the one who blew is the siddha; noble one, the sixteen is pati, disputants, the two-fours are pati's feet, and the four kinds are life; seeing this path, the light and the full pooranam and these three, when you guard it there sleeping without sleeping, the Primal Parai and Hara become one within the circle of the uvula: see.
nuance: This verse is the run's key to its own numbers: sixteen is pati, eight is pati's feet, four is life (உயிர்), and tradition matches these to the kalas of moon, sun and fire or to measures of the breath. அண்ணாக்கின் வட்டம், the circle of the uvula, is the place above the palate where Siddha yoga sets the union of Shakti and Siva (2433, 2438). தூங்காமற் றூங்கி, sleeping without sleeping, is the turiya state. வாதிகளே (disputants) as address is odd and may be corrupt.

reading: Look: rising at dawn, without hurry set the mind at the suzhumunai; when the sun and moon exchange and rise at the suzhumunai that is the womb, standing within the uvula without wavering, see it subside within the suzhumunai; of the sixteen, the eight and the four and the three, without scattering, join as one and go.
nuance: பரிதிமதி, the sun and moon, are the right and left breaths in the Siddhars' cipher, and their exchange at the central channel is the practice; a plain reading, that sunrise is the hour, is also present in உதயத்தில் எழுந்திருந்து. கருவான சுழுமுனை, the suzhumunai that is the womb or seed, repeats the run's link between the yogic centre and conception. The arithmetic of sixteen, eight, four and three is from 2432.

reading: This alone is the one pooranam; this alone is what is called the risen kala; for those who have become clear, knowledge is siddhi; would knowledge come from what is said without fixing? Do not let loose in the open the knowledge the many primal gurus spoke; it becomes sin; it cannot be seen by those whose mind staggers; this is the secret told to the clear.
nuance: The verse is the first of the run's three commands to secrecy (2434, 2438, 2441), and gives the reason: a staggering mind cannot see it, so saying it openly only makes sin. உகமை (secret, intimacy) is also the first word of 2435, where it turns into rules of life. பன்றான வாதிகுரு, the many primal gurus, claims a lineage for the teaching.

reading: I will tell more of the secret: in the world do not speak much pointed mockery, do not make enemies, do not speak idly, do not wander the open country, do not climb mountains, do not laugh, do not anger, do not sleep, do not slip and do not fall back from the suzhumunai; knowing the pooranam of the whole world and conquering, become clear and then live in accord with the world.
nuance: The list mixes social rules (no mockery, no enemies) with the yogi's regimen (no laughter, anger or sleep, and no retreat from the suzhumunai), and ends not in withdrawal but in உலகத்தோடு ஒத்து வாழ், living in accord with the world; 2436 then condemns those who leave the world in garb. 'Do not climb mountains' is against the wandering ascetic's life, which 2442 also dismisses.

reading: He who does not live, leaves the world, puts on the garb, talks and talks mouth-knowledge for his belly and begs from every low house is a husk, a chandala who does not know himself, a whole ox; do not listen to the words of such sinners and perish, do not panic, do not be bewildered for the belly; do not listen, do not keep hearing all the talk and be shaken, and do not say 'body and life' as two.
nuance: வாய்ஞானம், mouth-knowledge, is knowledge that is only talk, the opposite of the practice in 2431 to 2433. The verse turns the word சண்டாளர் (outcaste) on the garbed renouncer, as 2413 turned சண்டாளம் on base acts, so that caste language is used against those who claim rank by garb. The last line leads into 2437: body and life are not to be named as separate things.

reading: Body, life and pooranam, the three, are one, though in the world a few people say they are different; if you ask what body, life and pooranam are, noble one, they are the sixteen, the one-four and the eight; body, life and pooranam are Brahma, Vishnu and Isa, and the worldly, not knowing, went bewildered; body and life have become pooranam's foot and head; know the standing of the risen kala and stand in pati.
nuance: The claim is the run's monism: body, life and the fullness are one, mapped onto the three numbers (sixteen, four, eight, from 2432) and the three gods. பூரணடி முடியும், pooranam's foot and head, makes body and life the two ends of one thing. The numbers are cipher and the mapping is tradition's, not explained in the text.

reading: It tells of the guru who is the place where pati is; do not open it in public, your head will split in two; listen as I say what place fate is: it is the uvula within the sky of the sky; moon and sun, pooranam, eye, mouth, nose, the great ear and touch, eight; the place where pati dwells, its name is the suzhumunai; they call it heaven and Kailasa.
nuance: The verse names the place three ways: the uvula within the inner sky, the suzhumunai, and heaven and Kailasa, which 2439 expands into a list of all the holy places. The eight (moon, sun, pooranam and the five senses) is another of the run's counts. விதியின்ன விடம், 'the place where fate is', is strange; a variant sense is 'the place as ordained'. The threat that the head splits in two for telling it openly is a conventional curse on breaking secrecy.

reading: Kailasa, Vaikuntha, the gods' world, Kasi, Kumari and Setu, the cloud where the peacock dances and hell, maya, lightning and silence, the cold wind of sleep, the subtle, the wordless place and the contraction, the oil-smooth foot, foot and head, and the mother substance: these are the names of pati.
nuance: The list makes the pilgrimage sites (Kailasa, Vaikuntha, Kasi, Kanyakumari, Rameswaram), the cosmological places (heaven, hell) and the yogic terms (silence, subtle, wordless, contraction, foot and head) all names of the one inner place of 2438. That the holy places are within the body is a standard Siddhar claim; this verse states it as a bare list of names. காசின்யா for காசி and மயிலாடு மேகம் (the cloud where the peacock dances) are uncertain.

reading: I have told the name, told the town, told the place too; I have told the contraction of the back kala and the front kala; I have told the path of the many books of the wide world; I have told the trade that many people follow; I have told clearly what the glorious world is; I have told in brief all the siddhis that are siddhi; I have told the straight way, the way and the state; I have divided and told what your body is.
nuance: A summary stanza in which every line ends சொன்னேன், 'I have told'. பின்கலையும் முன்கலையும், the back and front kala, are the moon and sun breaths (idakalai and pingalai) in the cipher. 'The trade many follow' is the livelihood religion of 2428 to 2430. The verse claims the run has 'divided the body' (பிரித்துச் சொன்னேன்), that is, given its anatomy as a map of pati.

reading: I have set it out divided within a sutra of twice eight; madmen, if you look and understand it well, I have told the path of the book that was set out at length; do not blurt that this book exists; take it to heart with intent and do not change the kala; hold the matter in mind by thought; I have told in brief all the news the sruti told; I have strung the sixteen like a sutra: complete.
nuance: The run calls itself a sutra of ஈரெட்டு, twice eight, and of பதினாறு, sixteen, which matches its sixteen units and echoes the sixteen kalas it teaches. கலைமாறாதே (do not change the kala) is at once 'do not alter the text' and 'do not let the breath change'. The claim that the run condenses what the sruti said sits in tension with the attack on the Vedas in 2428, unless sruti is here the inner teaching.

title: அகஸ்தியர் ஞானம்
theme: ஞானம் - 5, thirteen stanzas the author says Siva gave him as guru: the kalpa that gives deathlessness is not in distant mountains but in the body, where the serpent's head, the undying breath and the black-gooseberry juice are found; the house of turiya is Valai, the goddess, whose feet alone are to be worshipped at the suzhumunai; and the letters of Om (a, u, m and the one letter) are mapped onto pati, pasu, the Supreme, the channels and the nada-bindu. Seeing the holy dance in the body is release and siddhi, and the knower of the one letter is the only guru.
structure_note: Thirteen stanzas chaining by antadi (கூடே / கூடப்பா; சித்தியாமே / ஆமென்ற; பாடினேனே / பாடுகின்ற; ஊணிப்பாரே / ஊணியதோர்; துறந்திட்டேனே / துறந்திட்டேனே; and so on to குருவாக). 2442 to 2444 give the inner kalpa, Valai and her worship; 2445 to 2447 the letters of Om and the central nadi; 2448 to 2450 the mind at the suzhumunai, the Devi and the Omkara pillar; 2451 to 2453 who the guru is; 2454 closes with the count of thirteen and a curse on mockers.
source_issues: 2446 line 1 மேல்முலங் is a misprint for மேல்மூலம் (upper root).
2451 line 3 ஊவெழுத்து (the letter 'oo') is unexplained and may be corrupt for ஓவெழுத்து or உவ்வெழுத்து.
2453 line 4 அறிந்தமென்பார் (for அறிந்தோமென்பார்) and line 7 ஒரெழுத்தை (for ஓரெழுத்தை) are misprints.
2454 says the run was told in thirteen (பத்தின் மூன்று); the run has thirteen units, so the count is consistent.

reading: For the kalpa you need not go far, nor wander the peaks of stone mountains; standing on the head of the serpent called the naga, find the undying breath, climb to the tip, stand in a mind made firm by resolve, and see the true juice of the black gooseberry; if you drop it as a small thing you will wander lost; go and join the Supreme called turiya.
nuance: கற்பம் is the rejuvenating herb or preparation of Siddha medicine; the verse says it is not gathered in the mountains but found within. The sense turns on cipher: tradition takes the serpent as kundalini at the base, சாகாத கால் (the undying foot or breath) as the breath that does not go out, and கருநெல்லிச் சாறு (black-gooseberry juice) as the nectar from the head; Kakapusundar uses the same herb-name for the deathless state. A plain medical reading, that gooseberry juice is the kalpa, is also possible and the verse plays on both.

reading: Join it: the house of turiya is Valai, and they call her Nathar-Maheswari, hard to describe; seek her alone and worship her; the beauty Nandi speaks of will appear and appear; everything up to the sikara boundary will appear; the flood of nectar called the mute will spring; seek this, this is the thing to seek; this alone is siddhi in the world.
nuance: வாலை, the girl-goddess of the Siddhars' cult, is here identified with the turiya state itself and with Maheswari, so that worship of her is entry into the fourth state. சிகாரவரை, the boundary of the sikara, may be the crown of the head or the letter சி of the five-letter mantra; ஊமையென்ற அமிர்தவெள்ளம், the mute nectar flood, is the nectar of the yogic tradition. The verse makes this inner worship the only siddhi.

reading: See the fullness called 'Aum' at the suzhumunai; the fair standing of bindu they see in the moon; the hum 'Om' is at the centre of the brows, noble one, and is seen in the house called the bow; worship her feet called 'Vam'; nothing else is worship, my son, I have said it; the Supreme called 'Pam' is the first letter; I have sung Vedanta, I have sung.
nuance: The verse places seed-syllables (ஆம், ஓம், வாம், பாம்) at body-places: the suzhumunai, the moon (the left channel or the head), the brow centre and the 'bow' (the arched brows). Only the worship of 'her feet' (Valai's, from 2443) is worship, a claim as exclusive as the Tirumanthiram's inclusive lists of lingam materials. பாமென்ற பரமனல்லோ முதலெழுத்தாம் is read by tradition as 'the Supreme is the first letter, a'; the syllable itself is unexplained.

reading: All that is sung is pati; the letter that stands in pati is 'a'; the Supreme that is sought is the Omkara; the pasu of great good is 'u'; the suzhumunai that endures is the stream; the idaikalai that stood is nada-bindu; this is the Omkara science that moves through; fix and see the rare letter of light.
nuance: The verse maps the letters of Om onto the Saiva categories: 'a' is pati, 'u' is pasu, Om as a whole is the Supreme, and the body's channels are the stream (தாரை) and nada-bindu. ஓங்கார வித்தை, the Omkara science, is the name it gives to this mapping. The third letter, 'm', is not assigned here, which may be deliberate (the one letter of 2453) or a gap.

reading: There is an Omkara higher than the one fixed; noble one, there is glory, fix and see; the central nadi that is the pin kindles in the middle; all the wondrous letters stand contained there; it stands as a ladder, the five houses; see that letter which has become solitary; that house appears like a boat; I will tell no one, I have renounced it.
nuance: அஞ்சு வீடு, the five houses on a ladder, is read by tradition as the five lower centres climbed by the central nadi; the boat-like house is unexplained, perhaps the crescent at the brow. சொல்லாதே ஒருவருக்குந் துறந்திட்டேனே is either 'do not tell anyone; I have renounced it' or 'I have renounced telling it to anyone', and the antadi carries துறந்திட்டேனே into 2447, where the author does go on telling.

reading: I have renounced it: see the upper root and the lower root; with care fix and see the middle state; I have declared it: see the middle root and the middle nadi; then the stream that strikes the boundary appears; the five who dwell there are seen dancing; light-space and the sound of anklets are seen as one; the full pooranam too is this; see the true great light steadily.
nuance: The upper, lower and middle roots (மூலம்) are the body's centres in cipher, and the five who dance may be the five elements or the five acts. சிலம்பொலி, the sound of anklets, is the dance of Siva heard within, which 2451 and 2453 name as the holy dance whose seeing is release. The verse identifies pooranam with this seen light and heard sound, giving the term of ஞானம் - 4 an experiential content.

reading: As you simply look, drive the mind to the suzhumunai and see the breath there; subside, saying 'Mother, you are the Devi', and see; then come kaya-siddhi and yoga-siddhi; 'Um-ma' and 'Am-ma' are seen there; with one mind plant the mind at the suzhumunai; we have told all that was made by us; among the Nathars no one sings this.
nuance: காயசித்தி, the perfected body, and யோகசித்தி are the two fruits claimed, and the means is the simplest the run offers: look, fix the mind, see the breath (கால்), address the Devi. உம்மாவும் அம்மாவும் may be two syllables (u-ma, a-ma) or the mother's two names; the text does not say. 'None of the Nathars sings this' claims the teaching goes beyond the Natha lineage.

reading: In the Omkara circle that is seen a little fire rises and a smarting appears in the eye; in the idaikalai that is worn it dances like the Supreme; the wicked body melts away; all the anavams perish; the non-dual turiya dance stands dancing; all the fixed letters become the Devi; the Omkara pillar is awareness itself.
nuance: The verse describes signs of practice (fire, smarting in the eye, the body melting) and makes the goal the destruction of ஆணவம், the ego-impurity, and the turiya dance that is non-dual (அத்துவிதம்). ஓங்காரக் கம்பம், the Omkara pillar, is the central channel as in the Thirumular Njanam's கம்பம்; here it is awareness (உணர்வு), which the antadi carries into 2450.

reading: As for awareness: climb into the moon and spread, run and stand there in the letter called the head; the atom is the house, Siva is the crown; 'a' and pati are the subtle; the knot is the bow-brow, the boundless street; what is called Kailasa is the house of the Supreme; see the fire of the sun called the particle, and sleep, sleep at the pillar called the nape.
nuance: A string of body-place glosses in cipher: the moon (head or left channel), the head-letter, the atom-house, the bow-brow, Kailasa, the sun's fire and the nape-pillar. Tradition reads them as the stations of the breath from the brow to the crown; the verse offers them as definitions (என்ன ... ஆகும்) without a key. 'Sleep at the pillar of the nape' is the turiya sleep of 2432.

reading: He who knows and tells the root that became the three letters and the two letters is the guru; it is within the letter 'oo'; he who has seen awareness itself and known it is the teacher; 'no one knows, we have known', say each of the fools who do not know; the gods with Vishnu and Brahma sought and did not see; seeing the holy dance is release and siddhi.
nuance: The three letters are a, u, m and the two letters are the pair of 2452 (root and seed, or Siva and Shakti); the root behind them is what the guru knows. ஊவெழுத்து (the letter 'oo') is unexplained and may be corrupt for ஓ or உ. The refrain திருநடனங் காண முத்தி சித்தியாமே closes 2451 and 2453, making the inner dance the one test.

reading: The two letters and the one letter, standing there as the ajapa that moves within the root; with the root letter and the seed letter both, it sprouts from the seed and stands shining; fix the fine letter, mount the good vaasi, cross the street and the road to the jewelled hall, and look to the Supreme that is the inner meaning of the letter: to those who reach it, it gives siddhi and release.
nuance: அசபை is the ajapa, the unrecited mantra of the breath (hamsa), which the verse places in the root centre. வாசி ஏறி, mounting the vaasi, uses the Siddhars' pun on breath and horse: the breath is ridden up the channel to the மணிமண்டபம், the jewelled hall at the crown. The 'inner meaning of the letter' is the Supreme, so the letter is a vehicle and not the goal.

reading: No one in this world has seen the fruit of the one letter called Ekam and expounded it; those who have learned the Agamas and many books and say 'we have known' and 'silence': ask such a one quickly about the unboiled, undying head and foot; he who tells what was left out is the teacher; he who sees the one letter in the body is the jnani; seeing the holy dance is release and siddhi.
nuance: The test of a teacher is a riddle: வேகாச் சாகாத் தலைகால், the head and foot that are not boiled and do not die, which tradition takes as the breath (கால்) and the head (the crown) kept deathless, as in 2442's சாகாத கால். Those who learned the Agamas and claim knowledge or silence cannot answer it. ஏகமெனு மோரெழுத்து, the one letter called Ekam, is the single letter beyond the three, the Omkara of 2446.

reading: The rare knowledge that Uma's consort gave me as guru I have told as meaning in thirteen; if you know the meaning, pooranam too will fit and be seen; those who mock this book without grace will reach dire hell and live as ghosts; those who examine it with grace may know the state in which the sky stands.
nuance: பத்தின் மூன்று, ten and three, matches the run's thirteen units. The closing curse on mockers and promise to examiners is conventional, but the promise is characteristic: not heaven but ஆகாயம் நின்ற நிலை, the state where space stands, the open void of 2411. Siva (Uma's consort) is named as the author's own guru, which grounds the run's repeated question of who the true guru is.

title: உரோம ரிஷி ஞானம்
theme: Romarishi Njanam, an invocation and thirteen verses attributed to Roma Rishi, is a breath manual in the voice of a guru to a son: the two channels are moon and sun, release is their becoming one in the sushumna; the breath is drawn in sixteen and held at twelve; the horse (breath) is stopped between the two petals; the counted pranayama kindles the six centres up to the brahmarandhra; the tongue sent to the palate yields nectar and the silence of nirvikalpa. Round this it sets a polemic: silence or Vedanta-talk without yoga gains nothing, forest penance kills by lust, the man who calls himself a renouncer dies ignorant, and the span of life is a count of breaths, so that fate is what one has thought.
structure_note: 2455 is the kaappu and 2456 the poet's name-verse; 2457 states the thesis (no siddhi without yoga, none while women are desired); 2458 to 2460 give the channels, the counts and the stopping of the horse; 2461 is an aside on unfit disciples; 2462 to 2465 give the counted pranayama, the six centres and the ascent to the palate; 2466 and 2467 attack talkers and ascetics without yoga and define the two kinds of release; 2468 closes with the breath-count of a life.
source_issues: 2457 lines 1-2 (கண்ணாடி சிலமூடித் தனுப்பினாலே) are obscure and possibly corrupt.
2462 and 2463 contain the unexplained word சரபீ / சரபீசம், and the pranayama ratio in 2462 (நாலு; ஒன்று மூன்று) appears to have lost a number.
2463 கையன் வட்டம் and 2464 பதினியிலே are unclear forms.
The invocation is numbered u1 in the unit id (siddhar:romarishi-njanam:u1) and the body 1 to 13; the chapter's own count is thirteen verses plus the kaappu.

reading: Protection is the guru's foot that is the root circle; protection is the first that is the seed of release; protection is the supreme Brahman that is the circle above; protection is the truth that stands beyond Vedanta.
nuance: A four-line kaappu that maps its refuges onto the body: the guru's foot at the root circle (mooladhara) and Brahman as the upper circle (the crown). வேதாந்தம் கடந்து, beyond Vedanta, sets the tone for the attack on Vedantic talk in 2466 and 2467.

reading: Staying in the circle of time, seeing the milk of the moon's nectar and feeding his hunger on it, removing deceit from the mind, trusting the feet of the great ones who play siddhi in the circle of the world: by that the one called Roman became Nayan.
nuance: A name-verse: the sage's name is explained by his living on the moon's nectar (மதி அமுதப் பால்), the fluid tradition holds to drip from the head in yoga, and by trusting the siddhas' feet. The three வட்டம் (circles of time, world, and the guru's foot in 2455) are a deliberate chain; how உரோமன் became நாயன் is not explained.

reading: Covering a few mirrors and sending by the bow ... not knowing the embryo he died; the fault of not seeking and looking at the sky is the fault, and all his learning turned to mere earth; if one leaves yoga saying that silence is the one thing, there is never any siddhi, nor alchemy either; if one comes having left desire for women, I will speak the path of great bliss and release.
nuance: The first two lines are obscure (கண்ணாடி சிலமூடித் தனுப்பினாலே); they seem to describe someone who hid behind tricks and died without knowing the source. The clear claim is polemical: mouna taken as the whole practice, without yoga, yields neither siddhi nor alchemy (வாதம்). Leaving desire for women is the entry condition for the teaching.

reading: I will speak: the left channel is the moonstone; the right channel is the sun from the first; when the light that stood lovingly in the middle departs and then becomes one without departing, that is release; for those who looked with love, this is moksha here; for those who do not see, what is there but a body of lust? As a test, draw the breath up in the left channel, hold it in the sushumna, and you will be entranced.
nuance: The cipher is stated and then decoded within the verse: இடைகலை is the moon, பின்கலை the sun, and the middle light the sushumna where they unite. சோதனையாய், as a test, invites the hearer to try the kumbhaka and see; சொக்குவீரே (you will be stunned, or absorbed) is the promised result.

reading: Having drawn in, exhale within that twelve; is not the standing fire let go the sun's life? One who knows these two places is a yogi; the supreme foot that is reached is sixteen; the foot of the wind that held is twelve; drawing gently in the sixteen, holding what strained in the twelve and blowing, the risen city of eight has subsided: see.
nuance: Twelve and sixteen are the Siddhars' breath numbers: the out-breath that runs twelve finger-breadths from the nose, and the moon's sixteen kalas, or an in-breath of sixteen measures held at twelve. Tradition reads பன்னிரண்டு as the sun's breath and பதினாறு as the moon's, matching 2458. புரியட்டகம், the city of eight, is the subtle body of eight parts; its subsiding is the goal of the exercise. The numbers are the whole content and their exact referents are not certain.

reading: See: the horse's leap at the level is gone; do not let the sound out into the expanse; set it straight between the two petals and meditate on Sadasiva who fills them; if it goes four finger-breadths within the roof, it has drawn itself in and held within the mark, sir; who is your equal, I will tell you; you may be called my dear son.
nuance: குதிரை, the horse, is the breath in the Siddhar cipher, and its leaping stopped is the breath stilled. இரண்டிதழ், the two petals, is the brow centre (ajna) in the usual scheme, and கூரை, the roof, the skull; four finger-breadths above is the crown. The last two lines are the guru adopting the pupil who achieves this as son, which 2461 at once qualifies.

reading: Calling one son is good if he is a good child; adding unfit disciples is a fault; if you tell him the way to live he will not look at it; he is an ox who talks to warm his wife's heart; he took birth only to toil, and of help to himself there is none at all; this fellow's talk grows slighter and slighter: why do we say any more to him?
nuance: An aside in the manual on whom not to teach: the householder bound to his wife and to toil, who hears and does not act. The guru's exasperation (ஏதுக்குச் சொல்லுகிறோம் இனிமேல்) is itself the lesson that the teaching is for the fit.

reading: Whether sitting or walking, raise the essences without letting them go through other talk; four or eight, all is one; in the good eight-limbed practice, the siddhi of practice; if you first do pranayama as the measure, by count the filling and the holding are four, the emptying one and three; without shortfall join the sarabhi and finish.
nuance: The verse gives a counted pranayama, but the ratio is garbled: பூரகம் கும்பகம் நாலு, ரேசகம் ஒன்று மூன்று may be the standard 1:4:2 with a number lost. சரபீ (also 2463, சரபீசம்) is unexplained; it may be a seed-syllable or a name for the combined breath. The claim that four and eight are all one is probably that the fourfold and eightfold yogas reduce to breath.

reading: After practising joining, if you achieve the sarabhi-seed without lack, it shows the brahmarandhra; otherwise, by the mark of the eye, see it in the middle of eye and nose; it kindles the six adharas too: in the root circle Ganapati, then the four-faced one, then Mayan, in the strong manipuraka the ... circle, and the fiery Rudra, and the fire.
nuance: The list of deities by centre is the usual Tamil scheme: Ganapati at mooladhara, Brahma at svadhishthana, Vishnu at manipuraka, Rudra at anahata, with 2464 adding Maheswara and Sadasiva above. கையன் வட்டம் is obscure. The brahmarandhra (பிரம ரந்த்ரம்) is the crown-opening the whole practice aims at; the alternative, gazing between eye and nose, is the easier method.

reading: The fire becomes the vishuddhi, the six-cornered circle; is not Sadasiva's circle the guru's seat? If you mark it and look in the house of the sixteen, from the middle it takes the coal and smoulders and smoulders; if the fire keeps rising, there is everything; if you let the breath out, the deed is evil; the path of the welling water is this way; for the wicked traitor is it not false?
nuance: The ascent continues: throat (vishuddhi, given six corners here though usually sixteen petals), then Sadasiva's circle, which is called the guru's seat. பதினி may be பதினாறு, sixteen; கரி (coal) and கனல் (fire) picture the breath as a smouldering fire that must be kept rising, and letting the breath out is called an evil deed. புனல், the welling water, is the nectar of 2465. துரோகி, the traitor, is the one who tells the secret or betrays the guru, for whom the path is false.

reading: What is sent goes to the uvula and the palate, sir; climbing there, meditation appears by the way of the nape; the four have grown strong and become nectar for you; it has become the life called silence, without distinctions; hold it in the twelve where it sounds, and blow; the sixteen-fold digit of the moon has waned away; the siddhi of yoga and the siddhi of knowledge have borne fruit; in due season set the channel and make it practice.
nuance: The tongue or breath sent to உண்ணாக்கு, அண்ணாக்கு (uvula, palate) is the khechari practice, from which nectar is said to flow. மவுனம் is here redefined as நிருவிகற்பம், the state without distinctions, reached through breath and not instead of it, answering 2457. சோடசமாம் சந்த்ரகலை தேய்ந்து போச்சு, the sixteen-fold moon has waned, is ambiguous: the moon's nectar consumed by the yogi, or the moon-breath exhausted. The four that grew strong are unexplained.

reading: Without cover, teaching their small minds a lesson, preaching as if the whole had come to them, saying 'where is release, where is the body, where is yoga' in empty talk, did they not die? Climbing forests and hills, bathing in rivers, eating fruit, tubers and dry leaves, heated by the fire of lust, crores upon crores died; those who gained release with form were few.
nuance: Two failures are paired: the Vedantin who denies body, release and yoga in words (வீடேது உடலேது யோகமேது) and the forest ascetic who starves the body but not lust. Both die; the verse's measure is that few reach சொருபமுத்தி, release in a form, which 2467 defines.

reading: If you ask what the sign of release with form is: the gross body is seen like a flame; the place of release without form is the knowledge of Brahman, the hearing that is called indirect; if yoga is left, it becomes like the old tale of the small ant that said it would shift the mountain; like a fly that has entered an empty pot, they are barbarians who do not know Vedanta.
nuance: The verse distinguishes two releases: with form, whose mark is the body shining, and without form, which is Brahman-knowledge reached by hearing. அபராட்சம் should mean direct (aparoksha), but சிரவணம் (hearing) is the indirect means, so the word may be a slip for பராட்சம். The polemic turns the Vedantin's own word against him: one who abandons yoga is the one who does not know Vedanta.

reading: Om: listen, pupil of ruined mind; in the world a man's years are a hundred; is it not twenty-one thousand six hundred breaths in a day? Because they went, going out with the breath, the days diminished and were gone; if they do not go out, there is no going; when a man thinks one thing, the god thinks it too; are not fates only what one has thought?
nuance: The breath-count of 21,600 a day is the standard figure of the hatha texts (fifteen a minute), and the verse's arithmetic is the Siddhar theory of life: a life is a fixed number of breaths, so the breath held is life saved. The last two lines go further and make விதி (fate) the product of one's own thought, with the god only concurring.

title: வால்மீகர் சூத்திர ஞானம்
