theme: Valmiki's sixteen verses call themselves the key to all the Siddhars' songs. The letter that is formless-with-form is the cosmos and the body; what comes and goes is the breath (vaasi), which is the sun and moon, the father and mother, and the four Saiva paths folded into one inhalation, retention and release. Against this the poet sets the many who read big books, melt before stone gods, wear matted hair, tiger skin and ash, build Vedas, puranas and castes in their own languages for a living, and howl in the forest without knowing the cause. The method is brief: the middle street from the perineum to the crown, silence, the mind kept where the breath arises, a guarded diet and daily duty; the secret is not to be shown to fools.
structure_note: 2469 to 2471 set the doctrine (letter, body as cosmos, breath as the paths); 2472 to 2478 attack the counterfeit forms of the four paths, of guruhood, of garb and of scripture and caste, closing on the one who sees Siva at the nose-tip; 2479 to 2484 give the key itself: the author's claim, the body's middle way, the two breaths, the sight without witness, diet, and the breath as the one need.
source_issues: 2473: தூடிப்பா ருலகத்தல் has a dropped vowel (உலகத்தில்); தூடிப்பார் itself is an uncertain word.
2477: மாமுனிர் is probably மாமுனிவர்; the line is one syllable short.

reading: Praising the feet of Siva, who stands as darkness turned to light, the poet promises to expound the letter: what stands formless-with-form is the letter, it is beginning and end, cosmos and body; the form that stands as sun and moon is the form of Siva-Shakti and of Vishnu; and he tells the hearer to set the mind on what came and what went.
nuance: எழுத்து (the letter) is not named; tradition hears the pranava or the first letter அ. வந்ததிலும் போனதிலும் (in what came and what went) is explained by the next verse as the in- and out-breath, so the whole opening resolves into breath. ரவிமதி (sun and moon) is a coded pair the Siddhars use for the two breaths or the two nostrils; the verse leaves it as a form of the gods.

reading: What comes and goes is the vaasi, and the sun and moon in the sky are the vaasi; the one of clear mind is the siddha, and the one who knows the whole world as Siva is the siddha; Nandi the mount is the gross body, four-faced Brahma is eye, nose, ear and tongue, the elephant-faced is the holy breath of Siva-Shakti; know the sun and moon as father and mother.
nuance: The verse is an allegory key: each god is a part of the body or of breathing. Which breath Ganapati (தந்திமுகன்) stands for, and whether father and mother are the right and left breaths, is tradition's reading, not the verse's statement. The definition of the siddha as one who sees all as Siva is plain and carries no cipher.

reading: Inhalation (pooraka) is the path of chariyai, retention (kumbaka) that subsides is kiriyai, exhalation (resaka) that parts is yoga, and what stands without slipping is jnana; the prana-air that turns and enters the body is the house in which great Siva-Shakti comes to rest; the one who joins it with a clear mind is the siddha and may be called Siva himself.
nuance: The four Saiva paths, elsewhere stages of a life or classes of practitioner, are here phases of one breath, and the fourth is the breath held still. வீடு in line 6 can be read as 'house' or as release; the breath's resting place is both.

reading: In the world those who have read the great books call all they have seen 'charitai'; they melt before stone and copper, call them god, worship them and call that kiriyai; calling it yoga they eat fruit and roots and wander like mutes; and saying 'jnana' they split hairs and go round like a crow-mad beast.
nuance: The verse is the counterfeit of 2471: each of the four paths as practised. சரிதை is probably சரியை (chariyai) bent to the rhyme, though it can also mean 'history', what they have seen written down. காக்கைபித்தன் (crow-madman) is obscure; the drift of the line is clear.

reading: Some few in the world, poring over the great books, hold forth; to make a living they put many costumes on the body and roam, call themselves gurus and others disciples, slyly give initiation and call others evil, and shout that they themselves are the holy Trimurti: dregs who do not know the cause.
nuance: தூடிப்பார் and தெற்றுவார் are uncertain words; the first is probably 'flaunt' and the second 'deceive'. The charge is economic as much as doctrinal: the guru-disciple relation and initiation are a trade (பிழைக்க, to make a living), a theme that returns in 2476.

reading: Some in the world put on matted hair, tiger skin, ochre robe and bead strings, smear the whole fleshy body with ash and call themselves yogis and jnanis; they call Siva worship and initiation honey, say they have seen Vishnu with their own eyes, and crores of them roam the forest howling, not knowing the cause.
nuance: The verse does not say ash or garb are wrong; it says they are worn without knowing the cause (காரணம்), the word on which the next verse turns. The forest-roaming yogi, elsewhere the ideal, is here the type of the lost.

reading: Those who howl are crores upon crores; those who have seen the cause are few; those who hold to the Supreme and have seen are a handful; the many in the world do not know within themselves the kala that rose; so do not scatter like the scattered, but when Siva-Shakti comes, stand in yourself.
nuance: The verbs பதறு, உதறு, சிதறு are chosen for the rhyme and their subjects are loose. உதித்த கலை (the kala that rose) is taken by tradition as the breath, or the inner moon's digit; and 'when Siva-Shakti comes' as the moment of the breath's rising (compare 2470, where Siva-Shakti is the holy breath).

reading: In the language of the great ones who said 'stand', within the wide world they built the four Vedas, the six shastras and the eighteen puranas that fill the belly, and Vedantas that dissolve stones, each in his own language; and in the old world they strung together the four castes and the many castes, each so as to make a living.
nuance: Scripture, sect and caste are treated alike as human constructions made for livelihood (வயிறு பிழை, பிழைக்க). The next verse softens this: embodied beings need a language, and the secret book came from Siva and Sivakami. 'Vedantas that dissolve stones' may praise their power or mock their pretension.

reading: Were there no 'I' in the world they would perish by their own greatness and fall into the world; but one who takes a body of flesh needs everything, and in the world each needs his own language; deer-eyed Sivakami and Siva together looked at the faces of the great sages and spoke the secret book, and by honey-like Sivakami's grace they gathered many crores of the languages of lands.
nuance: The first two lines are hard: தான் may be the ego or the self, and the sense may be that without self-assertion the world's builders would fall. What is clear is the concession: after 2476's attack, language and scripture are granted a divine source and a bodily necessity.

reading: Those who have studied languages hold forth confidently without knowing the language of the land; they praise all they see, meet a wonder and forget; the stubborn grandees who do not know the vaasi bewilder with words and have no method; but those who have seen Siva in the middle of the nose-tip are themselves Brahma, Vishnu and Siva.
nuance: நாசிநுனி (nose-tip) is where the breath is felt and where the yogic gaze is fixed; tradition takes seeing Siva there as the breath-practice itself. சண்டி மாண்பர் is an uncertain phrase, probably 'obstinate worthies'. The verse ends the attack on words with a place in the body.

reading: The key to the songs of all the eighteen is Valmiki's sixteen; the siddhas who had reached Siva all looked at my book and complained to Siva, and the Lord was angry; so that it not go to waste, by Siva's permission and grace I opened and told it for the world: within the nine planets, the tongue, mouth, ear and nose, beyond the middle.
nuance: பதினெண் பேர் are the eighteen siddhars, and பதினாறு this work's sixteen verses: the poem claims to be the cipher key to the corpus. நவக்கிரகம் (nine planets) within the body is taken by tradition as the nine openings; the verse only lists four organs and points beyond their middle, continued in the next verse.

reading: Beyond the middle of tongue, mouth, ear and nose runs the middle street from the perineum to the crown: strike there, saying 'there', and butt at it; worship the Mother and recite the Veda; with speech unmoving, taking silence, keep the mind at the place where the vaasi arises; then the mind, entering with the vaasi, is removed, and you will see the order in which it subsides into thought.
nuance: நடுவீதி (middle street) from குய்யம் to உச்சி is the central channel without its name. The instruction is in cipher ('strike', 'butt'), and the last two lines are syntactically loose; the plain point is that mind and breath are to be held together at the breath's source.

reading: Hard for anyone to see the two breaths; the one who sees them is the Siva-siddha; hard to attain, but if this book is got one may be called a siddha of the earth; hard to see, the holy breath of Siva-Shakti; do not show this book to fools; hard to appear, the dizziness of the eyes simply passes; I have told the subtlety that is hard to tell.
nuance: இருசுவாசம் (two breaths) is the in- and out-breath, or in tradition the sun and moon breaths of the two nostrils. விழிமயக்கம் சும்மாப்போம் may mean that the practice ends the eyes' bewilderment, or that the eyes' delusion is all that leaves.

reading: The poet tells the book's subtlety so that the vaasi may be seen; the subtle of subtles cannot be renounced; there is no witness, no companion, no hearsay and no doubt; the sight is like dwelling in the wishing-tree; having seen the cause with the eye, he saw Umai who gives rule just so, and the conduct of the dance of bliss is the guard.
nuance: சாட்சியில்லை துணையில்லை கேள்வியில்லை (no witness, no companion, no hearsay) is the poem's claim against book-learning: the seeing needs no authority. விழியைக் காண (to see the eye) is obscure; it may mean seeing with the inner eye. The last line's syntax is uncertain.

reading: Hear the diet for guarding it: eat fruits, the five juices and the finest foods in due measure and guard Siva; my son, read the siddhas' guru-book; the soul must suffer no decay; each must perform his daily duties; for those who stand firm comes vaasi-siddhi, and the sixteen bear fruit with distinction.
nuance: After mocking rite in 2472, the verse keeps நித்யகர்மம் (daily duty) as a condition of the practice, and adds diet and the study of a guru-text: the attack was on rite without the cause, not on rite. பதினாறு is again the sixteen verses, or the sixteen kalas of the moon in the yogic reading.

reading: To be He oneself, vaasi is needed, and a place to stand within oneself is needed; for all who stand as the sky-dweller there is siddhi, and when the mind is in the sky it is seen like the moon; for the siddhas who are honey, the herb that never cloys is the head, the seat of the body; I have told the sign so that you may be king, and on earth the sixteen draw to a close.
nuance: தெவிட்டா மூலி (the herb that never cloys) is the head: the siddhas' medicine is in the body, not in a plant, a reading tradition supports and the verse half-states. வானுக்குள் மனம் (mind in the sky) is the inner space of the head; மதிபோல் can be 'like the moon' or 'like intellect'. குறுகத் தானே may mean the sixteen verses end here, or that the sixteen kalas contract.

title: சுப்பிரமணியர் ஞானம்
theme: The invocation (காப்பு) of Subramaniar Njanam, which compresses the whole work into one stanza: subsiding in the unceasing suzhumunai, going by the vaasi into Siva-yoga, knowing the way, taking silence, climbing to the summit of the cosmic bound, taking the vel of Om, seeing oneself by the clarified mind, dwelling in the supreme void and becoming the Shakti-Siva of Vedanta. Murugan's vel is already the pranava, and his ascent is the breath's.
source_issues: 2485: the eight lines are printed with uneven breaks (line 3 and line 5 each carry part of the next line), so the metrical division is lost.

reading: Subsiding in the unceasing suzhumunai, going by the vaasi of the kala that has come into Siva-yoga, knowing the way and the ford, taking silence, going up to the great summit of the cosmic bound, taking the clear vel that is the shape of Om, seeing oneself by the clarified mind's knowledge, dwelling in the open supreme space and becoming the Shakti-Siva of Vedanta: this is the guard.
nuance: A kaappu normally invokes a god; this one invokes a practice, and Murugan appears only as his vel, which is named the shape of Om. The work's closing verse (2517) returns to the same summit and the same Om-vel, so the invocation is also its summary. The stanza's lines are unevenly divided in the source.

title: சுப்பிரமணியர் ஞானம்
theme: The first half of Subramaniar Njanam tells a myth and turns it into method. Sound born of the Supreme becomes Siva, Shakti, the sevenfold creation, and Ganapati and Shanmuga; the mango is offered to whichever son circles the hill, Murugan rides round the world while Ganapati circles his parents' feet and wins; Murugan is consoled, goes to Kailasa, and at the Himalayan sages' plea destroys the asuras with the vel. Agastya then comes as disciple and asks the inner cause of the outer act; Murugan performs a fire rite, consecrates him from the filled pot, and teaches: the breath fixed at the tongue-tip opens the door of true knowledge; inhale at the root with VANG, let out in samadhi with SING; the seed letters OM RING ANG UNG, the five letters reversed head to foot, strings of bija syllables for the adharas, sacred ash, and pranayama that drives off the diseases called Death. Rite and legend are kept, but as the gross of which the breath is the subtle.
structure_note: 2486 to 2495 are narrative: creation, the mango contest, Murugan's circuit and the asura war. 2496 to 2500 bring Agastya as disciple, his question, the fire rite and the consecration. 2501 to 2510 are teaching: the breath with its syllables (2501), the seed letters and Om Namasivaya (2502), permutations of the five letters (2503, 2504), bija strings for the adharas (2505 to 2508), and pranayama against Death (2509, 2510).
source_issues: 2500 has six lines where every other stanza of the work has eight; two lines are missing.
2503: சிவநம (four letters) in line 6 is probably a slip for சிவயநம; the permutation strings cannot be recovered exactly from the print.
2507: மங்கிலிங் in line 7 has lost a syllable (compare மங்கிலிசிங், மங்கிலிநங்).
2494: பந்திபந்தி யாங் is a broken sandhi for பந்திபந்தியாய்.
Several stanzas (2487, 2488, 2490, 2491, 2492, 2495, 2496, 2498, 2505, 2506, 2508) are printed with uneven line breaks, so the eight-line metre is not visible in the source.

reading: In the beginning the sound born of the Supreme became Parasiva, formless-with-form; as the place of Siva called light it became Shakti; in the old world it became the sevenfold creation; standing as itself by the knowledge called order it became the full partless one; and by the grace of Shakti and Siva, Shanmuga and Ganapati came to be.
nuance: Creation is traced from sound (சத்தம்), as in Tirumular's nada, and the two sons are the last and most concrete stage. எழுவகைத் தோற்றம் is the seven kinds of birth. சாதியென்ற is a rhyme-word whose sense here ('kind', 'gentle') is loose.

reading: When Shakti and Siva stood as one, ripe within and full, they took the mango in hand, looked kindly at Kumaran and Ganapati, and said they would give the good fruit to the one who came round the hill; Kumaran, knowing the fruit's worth, leapt on his peacock and went round the hill.
nuance: The mango legend is told without comment; its moral, that the inner circuit beats the outer, is left to the next verse. The fruit is the first of several objects in the work (pot, ash, nectar) that stand for what the practice yields.

reading: After he had gone, Ganapati reflected that the firm Meru hill is they themselves; the moment he saw this he went round the feet of Siva and Uma with intent, took the fruit, meditated on them, and knowing the sign and praising the holy within the path, he ate and knew its taste; as he stood there they called the firm Ganapati to come.
nuance: நீர் தாம் (you yourselves) resolves the contest: the mountain to be circled is the parents' feet. The verse adds meditation and 'knowing the sign' to the circuit, so that Ganapati's win is an act of knowledge, not of speed.

reading: Saying 'come', they lifted and embraced him, gave him the milk of grace, made him the seat for the great five, king of the root, the first that is life to the five letters, pure being-consciousness, the first guru and teacher risen gathered, and told him to dwell within the flower of a thousand and eight petals, abiding by the mind's knowledge.
nuance: மூலம் (root) is Ganapati's traditional seat, the muladhara; ஆயிரத்தெண் மலர் is the thousand-petalled lotus of the crown with eight added, an unexplained count. ஐவர் (the five) may be the five elements, the five gods or the five senses. The verse moves Ganapati from the legend into the body.

reading: At the moment they said 'dwell and live', the solitary peacock-hero came before them; seeing the state in which he stood as rare tapas, they said 'precious jewel of our eye, come', with sorrow gave him one mango too, and bade him circle the great cosmic bounds, be reformed, gain long life, and live firmly as king of the hill.
nuance: Murugan's loss becomes a commission: the circuit of the cosmos he already made is now his task, and மலைக்கரசு (king of the hill) is the Palani of the legend. The verse does not name Palani.

reading: Told to live, the peacock-hero took the great feet of Siva-Shakti upon him, mounted the peacock and eagerly circled Kailasa; as he circled, the pure-minded ascetics on the north side of the Himalaya saw him and bowed at his feet, and as they stood in reverence the ascetics and rishis came up.

Looking at those who came and stood at the hill and bowed to him as great satguru, they said: on this hill-slope we have long lived in joy doing tapas, sir, but rakshasas come through the sky, wreck everything and chase us; stay here in beauty and guard our tapas; and with pure minds they began their tapas.
nuance: The sages call Murugan சற்குரு before he has taught anything; the work's second half makes the title literal. Tradition reads the asuras who break tapas as the senses and thoughts; the verse itself tells only the story.

reading: As they began, subduing the mind and guarding their state, standing pure and at play, he saw the audacity of the asuras whose minds would not be subdued, who made trouble without fear; firmly he mounted the peacock, took the red vel, meditated on its point so that the reddened asura kin should die, and loosed it, and the asura kin flew away.
nuance: அடங்கி மனம் அடங்காத அசுரர் sets the sages' subdued mind against the asuras' unsubdued one in a single phrase, the nearest the narrative comes to saying what the asuras are. The vel is loosed by meditation on its point (தியானம் பண்ணி), not by the arm.

reading: Flying off, the asuras took many forms and came back in ranks; looking well at the armies, mounting the firm peacock and standing clear, so that dharma might flourish he took form as the cause called gross, subtle and formless, ground the wicked asuras who kept coming to dust, and stood firm in tapas.
nuance: தூல சூட்சம் அரூபமெனும் காரணம் names the three bodies, gross, subtle and causal, which the teaching later uses for the levels of the practice (2509, 2510). The war is fought with the same terms the instruction will use.

reading: Seeing the victory he stood in, the sages doing tapas with upright minds, their minds cleared and glad, cherished and praised the feet of the forest-peacock hero, bowed their heads to his feet and gained the eye of grace; the ascetics and rishis bowed, beheld the vel-bearer standing firm, and each went to his own abode.
nuance: சிலைகொண்டு நின்ற may mean standing like a hill, like an image, or with a bow; the sense is of a fixed, beheld form.

reading: As they went seeking their abodes, the devoted great sage Agastya came; knowing the ordinance, he meditated on the victorious vel that was to destroy the asura kin, and said: knowing the goal, becoming subtle with the gross, taking the form of the gracious cause, knowing their treachery you destroyed them, Shanmuga, my guru, refuge.
nuance: Agastya's praise already uses the work's technical pair, gross and subtle (தூலமுடன் சூட்சம்), so his question in 2498 is not naive: he asks for the inner meaning of an act he has described in those terms.

reading: At the word 'refuge' the vel-bearer standing as Shanmuga looked at the great sage Agastya, knew his humility, and asked who he was; 'the child who worships your holy feet'; 'what inner instrument has come here? come with compassion', and giving his gracious glance he said that to help at the right moment is dharma, and asked him to tell with care how he had come.
nuance: திரணமதாய் (as a straw) is read as humility, but the word is doubtful; கரணமந்தக் கரணம் plays on கரணம் (cause, instrument, the inner faculties) and its sense in the question is unclear. The exchange is the guru's testing of the disciple before teaching.

tamil: சொல்லென்று மயில்வீ ரன் கேட்க வந்த சோதிமய
reading: Asked to speak, Agastya full of light says to the peacock-hero: you destroyed the wicked asuras who came in a rush, with the vel, standing as Shanmuga; show the cause that stood as that holy form; tell as truth the cause of the inner form, gross and subtle.
nuance: The hinge of the work: the disciple asks for the cause (காரணம்) behind the outer deed, and the second half answers with breath and mantra. ஆகார may be the Sanskrit akara (form) or the letter அ; உள்ளென்ற ஆகார தூல சூட்சம் is then 'the inner form, gross and subtle' or 'the gross and subtle of the inner A'.

reading: Hearing the firm request, the peacock-hero affirmed it true and in order performed sacrifices; with observance he seated the great sage Agastya beside him, knowing the place, made the pit of Om, kindled fire with the mantra called the first, and knowing the fault, as the mantras were recited, the fullness came to be in the pot.
nuance: ஓம் குண்டம் is a fire-pit that is Om, and the fullness arises in the கும்பம் (pot); tradition hears in these the body's fire and the retained breath (kumbaka), but the verse describes a rite. புரையறிந்து (knowing the fault or the hollow) is unclear.

reading: Taking the pot that had become full, he anointed the great sage called truth, showed him the state of grace that is good for the nine planets, and the hill-like door of grace to be seen; with the mind gathered by knowledge, fix it with 'VINN'.
nuance: The consecration (அபிடேகம்) from the pot of the rite begins the teaching proper. நவக்கிரகம் (nine planets) in the body is taken by tradition as the nine openings. விண்ணென்று ஊணே, the refrain of the teaching verses, is 'fix it saying VINN' or 'drive it to the sky'; both readings stand, and VINN may itself be a seed syllable.

reading: With the force of 'VINN' within the tip of the tongue, the door of true knowledge opens; standing inside the way of that door, knowing the kala, looking at the lotus by the vaasi, fill at the root with 'VANG', and in firm samadhi let out with 'SING'; if you keep on this way always, hear the truth of the single tenfold initiation.
nuance: The breath's phases are given seed syllables and places: VANG for inhalation (பூரி) at the root, SING for exhalation (ரேசி) in samadhi, and the tongue-tip (முனைநா) as the door, which tradition connects with the tongue turned back. தசதீட்சை (tenfold initiation) is announced but not listed.

reading: Truly fixing 'VINN' in the suzhumunai, hear firmly the initiation that does not wear out: recite OM RING ANG UNG, and if you make sixteen repetitions with attention, Ganapati will shine gently; looking at yourself in the suzhumunai called the seat, if you subtly say OM NAMASIVAYA, the vision of Brahman comes before you look.
nuance: Ganapati, placed at the root in 2489, is here what the seed letters make shine, so the legend's god is a stage of the practice. ஆராத தீட்சை (the initiation that is not cooled or worn) is uncertain. The verse promises Brahman-vision from the five letters alone.

reading: Say NAMASIVAYANAMA, then VAYANAMASIVAYANAMASI; turn it head to foot and with care foot to head; say NAMASIVAYA SIVAYANAMA, and after that SIVAYANAMA SIVANAMA; say NAMASIVAYA and so change it: this is the siddhi of the true adhara.
nuance: The practice is reversal (தலைகால் மாறி, head to foot) of the five letters, where Tirumular's is rotation. சிவநம has four letters and is probably a slip for சிவயநம. The exact strings are not recoverable from the printed text.

reading: With mind on the five letters, son, properly changing them head to foot and foot to head, the deities of the adharas come purely and, as told, stand sweetly in the heart; meditating thus with devotion, firmly smearing ash as the ground, if you do this daily, the unstable gross body becomes stable.
nuance: The promise is kaya-siddhi: the body that does not stay is made to stay by mantra, meditation and ash. ஆதார தேவதைகள் are the presiding deities of the adharas, who are said to take their stand in the heart rather than in their own centres.

reading: Knowing the kala and standing in the state, hear with devotion the subtlety of the adharas: recite OM KILI ANG again and again; knowing the state recite ANG KILI NANG; recite VANG KILI SING, with compassion SING KILI VANG, VANG KILI YANG, and ANG KILI MANG.
nuance: A table of bija strings, each a seed letter, கிலி and another seed letter. கிலி is itself a seed syllable in the Siddhars' mantra lore; which adhara each string serves is not said. The verse is a formula and is read here as such, not as a practice to follow.

reading: After reciting, recite VANG KILI SING, truly ANG KILI SING, in order ANG KILI MANG, knowing the state MANG KILI RING, and from the first RING KILI OM; recite them changed head to foot; with light, fixing the mind's eye in the suzhumunai, purely wear the ash.
nuance: The strings continue 2505 and are to be reversed as the five letters were in 2503; the series ends on OM. Only the setting is clear: the mind's eye in the suzhumunai and ash on the body.

reading: Wearing the ash, sharply changing them foot to head, recite OM KILI RING, purely RING KILI MANG, MANG KILI SING; all the effects will appear in detail; recite MANG KILI (ING), and best one, SING KILI MANG.
nuance: The strings of 2506 are run in the other direction (கால்தலையாய்). தோற்றும் செய்கை யாவும் promises that the effects (or the acts to be done) will show themselves. மங்கிலிங் has lost a syllable.

reading: After reciting, recite VANG KILI SING, SING KILI MANG, in order MANG KILI NANG, knowing the state NANG KILI YANG, and with light MANG KILI OM; purely the twelvefold tapas is attained, the adhara called the street and the adhara above it; with the sky subsided and the eye subsided, stand established.
nuance: ஈராறு தவம் (the twelve tapas) is not explained; it may be twelve years or twelve stations. வீதியென்ற ஆதாரம் (the adhara called the street) echoes Valmiki's middle street (2480) for the central channel; மேலாதாரம் is the centre above the six. The closing phrase, sky and eye subsided, is the refrain of 2509.

reading: Stand with the eye subsided, fixing 'VINN', and if, knowing the state, you do pranayama, my son, the body is stone: where is Death? All the diseases called Death run away unseen; the vaasi becomes firm and the recited mantra is attained; I have told the gross with the subtle; hear now the compression of the gross that has shone.
nuance: காலன் என்னும் வியாதி (the diseases called Death) makes Death a name for disease, and pranayama its cure; the claim is of a body made durable (கல், stone), not immortal in so many words. The verse closes the teaching's gross level and announces its summary.

reading: Doing pranayama as told in the brief account of the adharas, gross and subtle, and with melting japa, tapas and puja truly seeing within yourself and becoming clear, abide in fullness, O living soul, and becoming the Supreme that stands as pranava, you too becoming it, go close into the cosmic void and with observance do pranayama with awareness.
nuance: The soul (சீவான்மா) is told to become the Supreme (பரம்), with pranava as the form it takes; and the destination is அண்டவெளி, the cosmic void, within. Japa, tapas and puja are retained alongside pranayama, as in Valmiki's keeping of daily duty.

title: சுப்பிரமணியர் ஞானம்
theme: The close of Subramaniar Njanam: the pranayama in full, with VINN fixed in the suzhumunai, VANG filling at the root, SING letting out and ANG retaining at the throat; the vaasi rises to the lotus whorl and comes to live in the body; Shakti's meditation with ANG SING and ash, during which Parashakti dances; Agastya is told to drink the moon-nectar at the whorl, shown the summit of the adharas, the six-faced state at the end of sound and the vel's point that is silence, and sent to Sathuragiri and Pothigai to practise the eightfold yoga at the guru's feet. Murugan climbs the summit of the cosmic bound and delights in the vel of Om, as in the invocation.
structure_note: 2511 and 2512 give the breath with its four syllables and the vaasi's rise; 2513 and 2514 Shakti's meditation and the nectar; 2515 the stations shown to Agastya; 2516 his dispatch to the southern hills; 2517 Murugan's ascent and the colophon முற்றே.
source_issues: 2511 and 2512: சுழுனை (lines 7 and 7) is a shortened spelling of சுழுமுனை, metrically short by a syllable.
2517: the work's own verse count is 32 (2.1 to 2.32) plus the kaappu, 33 in all; the tool splits them across chapters 132 to 134.
2511 to 2514 are printed with uneven line breaks.

reading: Doing pranayama with awareness, hear the working, Siva Siva; the prana-air will not go false, hear the novelty of its standing joined and at play: gently fix 'VINN' in the suzhumunai; as the seat, fill at the root with 'VANG'; truly let out in the suzhumunai with 'SING'; and swiftly retain at the throat with 'ANG'.
nuance: The fullest statement of the work's breath formula: four syllables for four acts and places, with கும்பே (retain) at the throat (கண்டம்) added to 2501's fill and let out. கருமானம் is read as 'working' or 'operation'; the word is uncertain. சுழுனை is a shortened spelling of சுழுமுனை.

reading: Retaining at the throat with 'ANG', the vaasi, the holy vaasi, unmoving, climbs to the body of the red-lotus whorl, turns, goes into that body and lives there; with care, itself as itself within itself, standing in its own nature the vaasi plays; auspiciously fixing 'VINN' in the suzhumunai, with method remain as this world and the beyond, and see.
nuance: பிண்டம் (the body) is where the breath comes to dwell after rising to the whorl (சுழி), which tradition places at the crown; the verse's picture is of the breath returning to live in the body rather than leaving it. இகபரம் (this world and the beyond) is what the practitioner becomes, not where he goes.

reading: To see, hear the meditation of Shakti, told as the seed; recite ANG SING, make sixteen repetitions with intelligence, smear the fine ash powder visibly, and purely Parashakti will dance; meditating in this way, see truly the firmness of pranayama.
nuance: The dance of Parashakti is what the meditation produces, and it is tested by the steadiness of the breath. ANG and SING are the retaining and releasing syllables of 2511, so Shakti's meditation is the breath's two halves; the sixteen repetitions match 2502.

reading: Firm great sage Agastya, listen: meditating on true Shakti, like the blaze of sun and moon, knowing the seat of the five agents, doing pranayama steadily, abiding at Pothigai which is the meaning of the sruti, mounting the vaasi of the kala of life's pleasant breath, with the mind made one standing at the whorl, take the untroubled drink of nectar.
nuance: அமிர்தபானம் is the yogic nectar held to flow at the crown when the breath is raised, as the next verse's மதியமிர்தம் (moon-nectar) confirms; it is tradition's reading and the verse's own image. பஞ்ச கர்த்தாள் are the five agents of the five acts. Pothigai, Agastya's hill, is called the meaning of the Veda.

reading: Taking the moon-nectar called the drink, he showed the way of the whorl that is Parabrahman, told the method of pranayama that knows the adhara called the seat and the adhara above it, showed the state called jnana and the root, showed the six-faced station at the end of sound, and showed the point of the vel that is silence; knowing that point, stopping the kala, stand on the crown.
nuance: The list is a map of the body's stations as Murugan shows them, and it ends by making Murugan himself a station: ஆறுமுக நிலையம் at நாதாந்தம், the end of sound, and the vel's point as மோனம், silence. The god of the legend becomes the state the breath reaches.

reading: Go to the summit of Sathuragiri and dwell at steady Pothigai; becoming yourself, fixing 'VINN', when you recite with meditation the one mantra you have thought in your mind, it will be attained purely; standing still, go by the eightfold yoga and stand clearly at the feet of the guru Sivaya.
nuance: Sathuragiri and Pothigai are the Siddhars' southern hills, and this is the work's version of Agastya's sending to the south. சும்மா நின்று (standing still, doing nothing) is a Siddhar phrase for the effortless state, set here beside the labour of the eight limbs.

reading: Seeing himself by the clarity of clarities, giving Agastya the imperishable boon of grace that he remain firm and do tapas forever, the peacock-hero with the vel eagerly went to the summit of the imperishable cosmic bound, became king of the eight-hill mountain, and, ceasing, being himself everywhere in the cosmic void, delighted in the vel shaped as Om: the end.
nuance: அட்டகிரி பாவதம் (the eight-hill mountain) is unexplained; it may be the mountains of the eight directions or Murugan's hill shrines. ஒழிவாகி can be 'ceasing' or 'becoming the remainder'. The verse repeats the invocation's அண்டவரை முடி and ஓங்கார வடிவேல், so the work ends where it began.

title: ஞானக்கும்மி
theme: The opening of Madurai Valaisami's Njanak Kummi: four invocatory stanzas (the guru, the maiden goddess, the Vel of Senthil and the Vinayaka of the root triangle), then the cosmology of the kummi told as a village estate. The one great void is a city; its lord is a mute Siddha, and the lady who speaks for him builds the town, lays down its law and farms earth and sky; five villages divided five by five grow from one seed; and a cast of tenants, headmen, an accountant, a Brahmin, a merchant, agents and servants hold shares in the land. Each is a coded element, faculty or tattva of the body, and the refrain asks the 'jnana girl' whether she can see the justice of their claims.
structure_note: 2518 to 2521 are the kaappu stanzas, one to each guardian; 2522 to 2523 announce the subject (tattva, the body as a vessel of filth, yoga as Tamil song); 2524 to 2528 set out the void-city, the mute lord and the lady who rules; 2529 to 2542 enumerate the estate's villages, hill and shareholders. From 2522 every stanza ends with the refrain ஞானப்பெண்ணே.
source_issues: 2525: line 3 begins with an ellipsis (...சுமகாரணமிரண்டினுக்கு); the opening syllables are lost in the source.
2532: the stanza ends with a stray comma after ஞானப்பெண்ணே.
2534: lines 2 and 3 are damaged (விசாரணை பும், நாமென்கிற ரீந்தப்).
2537: line 2 (ஊருக்குளூர்களூமய்படியாம்) is garbled; ஐம்பதி சேருவைக்காரர் in line 3 is also doubtful.
2518 to 2521 are kaappu stanzas without the refrain; the refrain ஞானப்பெண்ணே begins at 2522.

reading: By the grace of the true guru, the Paradesi whose form is excellent jnana, Ganapati the child of Siva is the guard for singing the Njanak Kummi upon the rock.
nuance: பரதேசிகன் (Paradesi, the wandering renunciant) is the guru's title; the singer credits the song to his grace before any god. பாறமீதின் (upon the rock) may be literal, a place of singing, or the firm ground of the practice.

reading: Praising the feet of Ambika the Maiden, to sing in Tamil the kummi of grace-bliss, Siva's Subramaniya, brother of the elephant-faced one, is the guard.
nuance: The goddess is invoked as வாலை, the maiden, which is also the singer's own name (Valaisami); the whole kummi is addressed to a 'jnana girl', so the maiden is at once deity, poet and listener.

reading: Praising on high him who stood as the fourth Veda, as the six, and as the many different distinctions, to sing the kummi, the feet of the Vel-bearer of Senthil are the guard.
nuance: ஓராறு (the six) is unglossed: the six Vedangas, the six shastras or the six adharas are all possible. நானாபேதம் (many distinctions) makes the god the ground of all differences, a theme the next stanzas take up.

reading: For the kummi that Valaisami of high Madurai sings, the feet of the Vinayaka of the root triangle at the base of Meru are the guard.
nuance: The poet names himself and his city. மேருவதன் அடி மூல முக்கோணம் (the root triangle at the foot of Meru) is the yogic body: tradition takes Meru as the spine and the triangle as the muladhara, where Ganapati presides; 2584 returns to the 'root Ganapati'.

reading: Beginning and end becoming one, growing as the two, the cosmos and the body, and standing as many different kinds: hear the tattva of this, jnana girl.
nuance: அண்ட பிரண்டம் is the Siddhars' pair அண்டம் and பிண்டம், the world and the body, here the first division of the undivided one. சாதி (kinds) is the many classes of beings, and may carry its social sense of caste as a product of the same differentiation.

reading: The body is a vessel of filth; the subtle thing that comes into it, and its origin, are the matter of this Tamil song called yoga: hear it with a glad mind, jnana girl.
nuance: சிற்பனம் and உற்பனம் are read as the subtle (சித்) that enters the body and its arising (உற்பத்தி); the forms are irregular. மலபாண்டம் (vessel of filth) is the stock Siddhar figure for the body, used here not to despise it but to introduce what enters it.

reading: The one great void is a city, and in it there is a certain Siddha; he has no mouth to speak the state of the vaasi; and that bridegroom is a woman, jnana girl.
nuance: ஏகப்பெருவெளி (the one great expanse) is the supreme space, told as a city. The mute Siddha within it is tradition's Siva as witness; that the bridegroom 'is a woman' makes the lord and his Shakti one, which 2525 and 2526 develop. வாசநிலை may be the state of breath (வாசி) or of dwelling (வாசம்).

reading: For Brahma called the witness, the child, a root ... became a woman; she stands as the ground of the two, the subtle and the causal, and says 'we are the gross', jnana girl.
nuance: The third line has lost its opening syllables, so the pair ending in ...சும காரணம் is restored as சூக்கும (subtle) and காரண (causal), the three bodies with தூலம் (gross). On that reading Shakti is the ground of the subtle and causal and declares herself the gross; the witness-Brahma is the still consciousness. பகைத்தி is unclear.

reading: She knew him to be mute, and says 'all that mute one's speech is us'; she organised herself to rule the country; that is the great lady, jnana girl.
nuance: The lord is silent and the lady speaks and governs: the Shakta picture in which all activity, speech included, is Shakti's and Siva is the unspeaking ground. சங்கட்டினாள் (organised, arranged) is read from சங்கற்பம் or from a dialect verb; it is uncertain.

reading: The ruby that is queen of women: is there even any hearing of her being called a woman? Hear the way by which she joined earth and sky and raised a crop, jnana girl.
nuance: The goddess is beyond the word 'woman' even as she is the queen of women. The crop raised by joining earth and sky is the stock cipher for creation, the body in the cosmos; the estate-and-farming figure of the rest of the chapter begins here.

reading: The great queen built a town and, with her lord, framed the law of its administration in good order; telling it would never end, so hear a little of the seed, jnana girl.
nuance: The 'law' (அதிகாரச் சட்டம்) is the ordering of the created world and the body, told in the idiom of a landed estate; விதை (seed) announces that what follows is a condensed account of its origin.

reading: It became a division of five villages; within it there came to be five-times-five parts; for the five villages there was one seed; and for that there is a tank, jnana girl.
nuance: The arithmetic is cipher: tradition reads the five villages as the five elements, the twenty-five as their fivefold products (the five-times-five tattvas of Siddhar reckoning), the one seed as bindu and the tank as the womb or the water of the body. ஆணகுளம் is unclear, 'the male tank' or 'the fitting tank'.

reading: Next to the village there is also a hill; those stationed within it are the holders of posts; hear now as their names are told, and what their greatness is, jnana girl.
nuance: The hill beside the village is, in the Siddhar body-map, the head above the trunk (Meru, 2521). The 'stationed men' who are named in the following stanzas are the faculties and powers lodged there; the names are place-puns and the readings below give them as tradition would, not as settled.

reading: That Sattaiyappillai who lives at Thalaimannar is tall; she asked what is sin and what is tax-free grant; do you know the truth of it, jnana girl?
nuance: தலைமன்னார் puns on தலை (head): the tall one who lives in the head may be the breath or the intellect. பாவம் and மானியம் (sin, and land held free of tax) set deeds and their exemption against each other; the question is whether anything in the body is exempt from karma.

reading: Appu Pillai at Kumbakonam came asking for a half share, saying that if his gathering fails there is great distress; how is the justice of this to be settled, jnana girl?
nuance: கும்பகோணம் carries கும்பம் (the pot, the head or the held breath of kumbhaka); அப்பு is also the element water. One reading is the breath or the water-element claiming its half of the body's produce; the stanza gives only the claim and the question.

reading: Have the five Vanni gods of the root household fierceness, resolve and a path? They say 'the share of the four banks is ours'; do you know the justice of this, jnana girl?
nuance: வன்னி is fire, and the five fire-gods of the root household are read as the five fires or the fiery powers at the muladhara (மூலக்குடி); the four banks they claim may be the four other elements or the four directions. The stanza queries their claim rather than granting it.

reading: For Katthavaraya the undivided one there is the guarding of the directions and all other inquiry; 'we are the ones who see to it', they say; will this state hold, jnana girl?
nuance: காத்தவராயன் is the village guardian deity, here a figure for whatever guards the body's eight directions, which tradition gives to the eight siddhis or the directional gods. The text of lines 2 and 3 (விசாரணை பும், நாமென்கிற ரீந்தப்) is damaged and the reading is approximate.

reading: The supreme light that is space says that the share of the five banks is gathered within himself; hear this news, jnana girl.
nuance: The one shareholder whose claim the song reports without challenge: the light that is space (the fifth element, and beyond it the inner space) holds the five, taken as the five elements, within itself. This is the pervasion doctrine in the estate idiom.

reading: The hall-men are three, and besides there is one head-accountant of the forest; if they make trouble, do you know the way the former's order runs, jnana girl?
nuance: அம்பலக்காரர் are the village headmen; three of them may be the three gunas or the three malas. மஸ்தக காட்டுக் கணக்கன் carries மஸ்தகம் (the head): an accountant in the head is tradition's reckoning faculty (buddhi or chitta). The stanza asks what rule governs them when they rebel.

reading: Nine dancers are also shareholders, and in which village their villages lie is the way of it; and for the fifty who are the clerks there is one elder brother, jnana girl.
nuance: The nine dancers are read as the nine gates or the nine planets; the fifty (ஐம்பதி, with the garbled சேருவைக்காரர்) suggest the fifty letters with their one 'elder brother', Om. Line 2 (ஊருக்குளூர்களூமய்படியாம்) is corrupt and the reading is tentative.

reading: The priest at Serai is a Brahmin, and his house is above the raft-tank; leaping about he slaps his thigh in challenge; will the land go to him, hear, jnana girl?
nuance: The Brahmin above the tank who struts and claims the land is one more shareholder whose claim is questioned; one reading is the ego or the ritual mind lodged above the water of the body. The stanza is satire of priestly claims as well as cipher.

reading: A merchant too is a shareholder; the one who joined there grew very great; if he brings the bound-up gold coin, will his title to the land stand, jnana girl?
nuance: The Chetti who tries to buy the body's land with hoarded coin (வராகன்) is read as desire or acquisitiveness; the song asks whether wealth gives any claim on the self. The stanza's claimants form a series of 'will it hold?' questions.

reading: The agents are five; to oversee their work there are twice five; the sorcerers of samadhi are three; hear the word, jnana girl.
nuance: Five, ten and three are the standard counts of the senses, the ten organs of sense and action (or the ten airs) and the three (gunas or states). மாரீசக்காரர் (men of Maricha, the shape-shifting demon) makes the three 'of samadhi' deceivers, perhaps the three states that counterfeit absorption.

reading: The servants are many, and they have plentiful stipend and wages; but if a ladder is set against the pot-fort, they will hide, jnana girl.
nuance: பானையங்கோட்டை, the fort that is a pot, is the body or the skull; the many well-paid servants who vanish when it is scaled are the faculties that fail at death or in the yogi's ascent. Both readings keep the point that the body's retainers cannot be relied on.

reading: For the void-form there is one superintendent, and if you look at him he seems a small boy; the man of Velur sells off his own half share, jnana girl.
nuance: The child-like overseer of the void (பாழுரு) recalls the Siddhars' child-god, Murugan or the ever-young Lord, who is tiny to look at and master of everything. The Velur man who sells his half share is unexplained; the ellipsis of the stanza is deliberate cipher.

title: ஞானக்கும்மி
theme: The estate allegory concludes and the body becomes a temple. Thirty-six households of which only two are real householders; one plough and one ox cutting three furrows; an accountant, a bailiff who seizes a third of 21,600 measures of paddy and the gods who squander the rest: the breath spent on living. Then the eight-span house is Siva's temple, with the head as tower, the uvula as flagstaff, the palate as fire-tank, a mandapam of forty-three triangles, seat at the centre and altar at the genitals; such a temple has a gate within its gate, whose lock opens by the silent letter and the mind's eye, and the path runs from the pit two fingers above the manure, past Vishnu's palace and the fire tree, to the six-cornered step. Cast off the gross guise.
structure_note: 2543 to 2552 finish the estate: the households (2543 to 2544), the plough (2545), the accountant and the seizing bailiff (2546 to 2550), the paddy of 21,600 (2551 to 2552); 2553 is a first exhortation to grace-bliss. 2554 to 2559 map the body as a Siva temple; 2560 to 2564 the gate, the lock and the key; 2565 to 2567 the inner path and its stations. All stanzas end with the refrain ஞானப்பெண்ணே.
source_issues: 2547: line 1 (புள்ளிக் சறைச்சலுமவாராமன்) is corrupt; the reading is conjectural.
2555 and 2556: the stanzas end with stray commas after the refrain; 2555 line 3 (காகமன விரண்டு கரக்கோடுங் கையாம்) is damaged.
2557: line 2 (நடுவீருக்குதஞ் சிங்காரம்) is garbled.
2559: line 4 (தெறியாமற் றெறிக் தலைகிறாரடி) is damaged.
2543: யஃதொட்டுகுடியடி runs the demonstrative into the noun; read அஃது ஒட்டுகுடி.

reading: There are six-sixes of households, and among them thirty-five are foreign households; among the six-tens of households, that one is the attached household, jnana girl.
nuance: ஆறாறு (thirty-six) is the Saiva count of tattvas and ஓராறு பத்து (sixty) their derivatives, together Tirumular's ninety-six. Of the thirty-six, thirty-five are 'alien' to the soul and one (அஃது, 'that') is its own; which one is not said, and tradition would name the soul's tattva or Siva-tattva.

reading: Though all these persons are there, among them only two are householders; if all the others are set aside, those two will raise the crop, jnana girl.
nuance: சமுசாரி is the settled householder with a family, the one who really farms. The two among the many tattvas may be the soul and the Lord, or the two breaths; the song's method is to count and leave the hearer to name.

reading: One plough, a single ox; in it the one beam cuts three furrows at once; having learned, have you seen the cause? Look with the eye of jnana, jnana girl.
nuance: One ox drawing one plough that ploughs three furrows: tradition reads the single breath moving through the three channels (idai, pingalai, suzhumunai). The stanza explicitly makes this a riddle to be solved by the 'eye of jnana'.

reading: The households of the two banks are tax-free grant, and in it the seed sown yields double; the old spotted man of long acquaintance looked it over and went away, jnana girl.
nuance: புள்ளிக்காரன், the man of dots, is the accountant who keeps tally; here read as the reckoner of deeds. The two banks held tax-free, where seed doubles, may be the two channels or the two eyes; the stanza keeps its estate idiom throughout.

reading: Before the spotted man's quarrel could be settled, with the fruit laid down earlier still unhandled, if a palm-leaf order comes saying 'plunder', tell how cruel that is, jnana girl.
nuance: The first line (புள்ளிக் சறைச்சலுமவாராமன்) is corrupt and the reading is a guess at its sense. The ஓலை (written order) to loot the estate before accounts are closed is read as the summons of death arriving while deeds are unresolved.

reading: Even if one stays saying 'it is the fate that came', he demands the bond and the arrears as well; is this his glory, and what pleasure is there in it, jnana girl?
nuance: The collector who takes both bond and arrears is read as karma, which exacts past debt on top of present lot; the stanza's irony (மகிமை, சுகம்) is at the expense of anyone who calls this glory or pleasure.

reading: He orders lake water to be channelled into the box lying at the tree-stump; when they said no tax is paid, he hangs up the worship, jnana girl.
nuance: The stanza is obscure throughout: தரு நிச்சி and பெட்டி (box) are unglossed, and பூசை மாட்டுகிறான் may mean he stops worship or he fastens it. One reading is that the bailiff makes even worship a matter of tax; no confident sense is offered.

reading: He does not let the household stay in the village, stopped them doing service and stopped their work; even when told there is no fortitude left, he keeps on levying the fine, jnana girl.
nuance: The oppressor here has the features of death or disease: he drives the body's tenants out, stops their functions and exacts penalty regardless of pleas. தெண்டகம் is read as தண்டம், penalty.

reading: Of that twenty-one thousand six hundred measures of paddy, did any capital come back once it was seen? Of it he seized one part in three as his share, jnana girl.
nuance: 21,600 is the yogic count of breaths in a day and night, so the paddy is the breath and the one-third seized is the share lost, which tradition explains as the breath that goes out beyond the nose and is wasted. The stanza asks whether any 'capital' (முதல்) is recovered from it.

reading: Of the paddy that remained, the share was destroyed by the madman with the sky-disease, together with Achyuta's son and the sleeping cowherd, jnana girl.
nuance: அச்சுதன் சேயன் (Vishnu's son) is Brahma and தூங்கு கோன் (the sleeping herdsman) Vishnu on his serpent; the madman of the sky-disease is unclear, perhaps Rudra or the wind. The three gods squandering the remaining breath makes creation, preservation and destruction consumers of the body's store.

reading: Did you not see what the land yielded, and will you not look at how it was spent? Without wandering in distress, reach grace-bliss, jnana girl.
nuance: The first turn from allegory to exhortation: having counted the body's produce and its loss, the hearer is told to stop fretting over the accounts and go to அருளானந்தம், the phrase the song uses for its goal in 2519 and 2575.

reading: A house eight spans long, and in it a filth-nest of eight and one; the panchayat men are twice five, and they said this is the city of god, jnana girl.
nuance: The eight-span body is standard. எட்டொரு பீற்றன் மலக்கூடு is obscure: 'the nine-fold nest of filth' (the nine openings) or 'a filth-nest of eight tatters'. The ten who declare it god's city are read as the ten airs or the ten senses, and the stanza turns on their being right despite the filth.

reading: The body is a Siva temple, and in it the head is the tower over the small gate; the crow-like mind ... and the two side-walls are the hands, hear, jnana girl.
nuance: The temple-body of the next five stanzas begins here. காகமன (the crow-mind, restless and thieving) is a stock figure; the rest of line 3 (விரண்டு கரக்கோடுங் கையாம்) is damaged and the reading of the hands as the side-walls is a guess.

reading: The uvula is the flagstaff, and at it is the tower's moon-tank; the palate on the right side is the Agni tirtha seen in the fire-pit, jnana girl.
nuance: The temple's two tanks are placed in the mouth: the moon-tank (சந்திர புட்கரணி) at the uvula is where the nectar of yoga is said to drip, and the fire-tank at the palate the heat that rises there; the pairing of moon and fire follows the yogic map rather than any actual temple's.

reading: The mandapam is of forty-three triangles, and in its centre is the ornament ...; what is seen is in the chakra fort, and so it stands, jnana girl.
nuance: நாற்பத்து முக்கோணம் gives forty-three triangles, the count of the Sri Chakra, so the temple hall is that yantra drawn in the body; it could also be read as 'forty, and the triangle'. Line 2 (நடுவீருக்குதஞ் சிங்காரம்) is garbled.

reading: The seat is at the centre, and the sacrificial altar is at the genitals; in the Siva temple with its storeyed hall the jewelled lamp is burning, jnana girl.
nuance: The பலிபீடம் (altar where offerings are left before entering) at the genitals makes the sexual act the outer sacrifice of the body's worship, and the inner seat (பீடம்) the centre, heart or crown. The lamp that burns in the temple is the inner light.

reading: For a temple made like this, how could there be no gate? Not knowing how it is, they wander about unable to find it, jnana girl.
nuance: The last line (தெறியாமற் றெறிக் தலைகிறாரடி) is damaged; the sense that people wander without knowing the gate is clear from the following stanzas. The gate is the opening of the body-temple, which the next stanzas locate and lock.

reading: A lock is opened by the hand; the mind's lock is opened by truth, or by the body; unable to open the house, they say this is the fate that left them, jnana girl.
nuance: மெய் is both truth and body, and the line works on both: the mind's lock yields to truth, and the yogic reading has it yield to work done in the body. வீடு is both house and release, so 'unable to open the house' is also 'unable to attain release', blamed on fate.

reading: In the gate there is an upper gate, and in that gate there is a small gate; with love look at the tightness of the lock on the holy gate, jnana girl.
nuance: Three nested gates: tradition takes the upper gate as the brow or crown and the small gate within it as the suzhumunai's opening, the 'holy gate' being the one that is locked. The word for examining the lock is நேசமுடன், with love, not with force.

reading: The letter is the letter of silence; if so, it is the good key; if one opens with it so as to free, the way to the crown is seen, jnana girl.
nuance: The key to the locked gate is a mantra that is not spoken: மௌனாக்ஷரம், the silent letter, which tradition identifies with the unuttered Om or the ajapa breath. முத்திதமாக is read as 'so as to release'. உச்சி வழி, the way to the crown, is the goal the key opens.

reading: With the eye, with the mind's eye, if you see that, a way will arise; without taking on desire for women, cherish the way and look, jnana girl.
nuance: The seeing is done by the inner eye, and the one obstacle the stanza names is sexual desire, which 2558 had placed at the body's altar; the two stanzas together make the ascent a redirection of that offering.

reading: Walking with care is the upper gate; how is that road to be known? Without parting from it even for the time of a measure, hear the method of the road, jnana girl.
nuance: மாத்திரை நேரம் is the time of a syllable or a breath-unit, so 'not parting for a measure' is continuous attention to the breath. The stanza promises the method, which the next three give in cipher.

reading: Crossing the pit where the manure lies, and crossing two finger-breadths above its edge, there is the sign where the embryo lies; see that and hear, jnana girl.
nuance: The road begins at the bottom of the body: the manure pit is the anus, two fingers above it the perineum, where the muladhara is placed in the yogic map, and the 'place of the embryo' the generative seat beside it. The stanza describes the body with the estate's farmyard words.

reading: Did you not see Mayan's palace? Did you not perceive the fire-tree standing? Beyond love, past them, is the six-cornered step, jnana girl.
nuance: The stations continue upward: Mayan (Vishnu) presides over the water and the navel region, the vanni tree is the fire centre, and the six-cornered step is the heart lotus with its six-pointed star in the adhara scheme. நேயம் (love) is the attachment to be crossed, or a textual slip for a place-name.

reading: Do not be bewildered standing in the corner; do not whimper while restraining the breath of the whirl; do not dither wandering in vain; cast off the gross guise, jnana girl.
nuance: சுழிக்காற்று, the wind of the whirl, is the breath drawn into the suzhumunai; the stanza warns against both faltering in the practice and parading it. தூல வேடம், the gross guise, is the outward body or the external form of religion; the next chapter opens by taking it as the gross body.

title: ஞானக்கும்மி
theme: From the gross to the subtle. The great path leads to a round city where nada sounds, the presence of the Lord; past the three voids are three lights whose circle is the chakra, the nose-tip is the suzhumunai, the guru Nandi sits in the fire-circle at the brow where sun and moon stand, and nada-bindu is the source of body and life. Then the practice: A at the kundalini breath, the second letter at the throat, M at the whirl; puraka thirty-two, kumbhaka double, rechaka sixteen; in by the left and out by pingala, kept from full moon to new; fire raised by the breath, nectar fed above the whirl, kechari and the root Ganapati; the five letters as five gods; the maiden's three unsayable letters that make life; initiation as the Siva-chakra with the goddess's letter at its centre; and in place of toddy and ganja the Soma-nectar, drunk with the Lord of the hall in a song of advaita.
structure_note: 2568 to 2572 give the path and its summit (gross to subtle, the city of nada, the three lights, nose-tip and brow); 2573 to 2577 nada-bindu, guru Nandi, the blissful place and the 1,008-petalled seat; 2578 to 2584 the breath practice (letters, counts, channels, fortnight, fire and nectar, kechari); 2585 to 2589 the five letters, the maiden's three letters and initiation; 2590 to 2592 nectar against intoxicants and the advaita song. Seven stanzas (2576, 2577, 2579, 2583, 2590, 2592, and 2591 in its first half) end in கும்மியடியுங்கடி, 'dance the kummi, girls', in place of the refrain ஞானப்பெண்ணே.
source_issues: 2569: the refrain is printed ஞானப்பெண்னே (ன for ண).
2570: றரத்துவம் in line 2 is corrupt, probably தத்துவம்.
2573: line 1 (நால்போனி தச) is damaged; line 3 (லுட முயிரும பர) has broken sandhi.
2578: அகாரம் is printed twice (lines 1 and 2); the second, at the throat, should be உகாரம்.
2580: the stanza ends with a stray comma after the refrain.
2585: கிவ்வெழுதே in line 3 is a misprint for சிவ்வெழுத்தே.
2592: line 1 (அக்லீதமாவத்துக்காதியடி) is garbled.
2576, 2577, 2579, 2583, 2590 and 2592 end in கும்மியடியுங்கடி rather than the refrain ஞானப்பெண்ணே; this is the song's own variation, not corruption.

reading: If you have not left the gross, you cannot see the subtle within it; if you climb onto the bridge and walk, is this not the great path, jnana girl?
nuance: Picks up the 'gross guise' of 2567 as தூலம், the gross body, which must be left for the subtle (சூட்சம்) hidden in it to appear. The bridge (பாலம்) is tradition's suzhumunai, the one crossing from the lower body to the head.

reading: Near the path, the great path, there is a city, and it is round; nada and song are heard there; it is the presence of the divine Lord, jnana girl.
nuance: The round city where sound is heard is the inner station where nada is perceived, which tradition places at the crown or the brow; சந்நிதி (presence, the space before the shrine) continues the temple figure of chapter 136.

reading: The presence: have you seen it? If you have, have you the skill to speak its tattva? Have you first crossed the three voids? Within it there are three lights, jnana girl.
nuance: றரத்துவம் is read as தத்துவம். முப்பாழ், the three voids, are Tirumular's term for the emptinesses passed before the final state; the three lights within them are sun, moon and fire in the yogic reading, which 2572 confirms.

reading: The circle of the three lights is the chakra; the tip of the nose is the suzhumunai; the one who sat in that circle of three lights is the guru, Anandanandi, jnana girl.
nuance: The suzhumunai is placed at the nose-tip (மூக்கு நுனி), the point of the nasikagra gaze, rather than between the brows as in most Siddhar texts; 2572 then puts the fixed gaze at the brow. Nandi, Tirumular's name for the guru-Lord, is the one seated in the light.

reading: Where Nandi sat is the fire-circle; the gaze fixed on the middle of the brows is the mark; the moon and the ray-sun stood in that place, jnana girl.
nuance: The three lights of 2570 are now placed: fire where Nandi sits, sun and moon at the brow-centre where the gaze is held. In the cipher sun and moon are the two breaths, pingalai and idai, which meet at the brow; both the plain and the coded sense stand.

reading: Is it not nada and bindu, the four wombs and the ten ...? Is it not nada and bindu, the seven kinds of birth? By nada and bindu come body and life; praise the supreme Nandi, jnana girl.
nuance: Line 1 (நால்போனி தச) is damaged; நால் யோனி (the four kinds of womb) and தச (ten) are the likely words. The stanza derives every form of birth, and the body and life themselves, from nada and bindu, sound and seed, which in the Siddhars are the cosmic pair and the sexual pair at once.

reading: In the place where bindu was, guru Nandi sat in state; if the mind grows clear and the letter M is placed there, that lord can be seen, jnana girl.
nuance: மகாரம், the M of Om, is set in the place of bindu, which 2578 locates at the whirl (சுழி); the lord seen there is சீமான், the landlord of the estate figure, now the Lord. The practice is a placing of a letter at a body-station, as in the Subramaniar Njanam.

reading: If one draws near the lord, the upper country becomes our dwelling; saying 'yes, yes', sing the kummi and reach grace-bliss, jnana girl.
nuance: மேலைச் சீமை, the upper country, closes the estate figure: the tenants of the body's village become settlers in the land above. ஆமாம் (yes) is the kummi's clap of assent.

reading: That is the place of bliss, that very place is the place of non-duality; praising Sadasiva who is the end of self, cross over and dance the kummi, girls.
nuance: அவ்வீதம் is read as அத்வைதம் (non-duality), as the spelling அத்வீதம் in 2591 supports. தானந்தம் can be 'the end of self' or 'that end'; on the first reading Sadasiva is where the 'I' ends.

reading: Jnana is the seat of a thousand and eight petals; the gaze is the house of the moon; silence sat there as the letter M; kindle that silence and dance the kummi, girls.
nuance: The crown lotus is given 1,008 petals (ஆயிரத்தெட்டு) rather than the usual thousand, a Siddhar count repeated in 2592. The moon's house is the gaze turned upward to the crown where the moon-nectar is; M, the letter of silence, is the end of Om.

reading: The kundalini-breath is the letter A; at the throat of the nape is the next letter; if you place the letter M at the whirl, is this not Siva-yoga, jnana girl?
nuance: The text has அகாரம் twice; the second, at the throat, must be உகாரம் (U), giving A, U and M of Om at the root, the throat and the whirl at the crown. குண்டலி வாசி joins the coiled power to the breath, as the Siddhars do: raising the breath is raising kundalini.

reading: She of the Omkara pranava sound, risen everywhere, of the colour of the Soma-digit; facing the Parashakti of the humming, dance the kummi, girls.
nuance: தாரல் and றீங்காரம் are the sound of Om as a hum, and Parashakti is that sound; சோமகலை, the moon's digit, gives her colour and ties her to the nectar of 2583 and 2590. ஓங்காரமான பிரணவத்தாரல் may also be 'the stream of the pranava'.

reading: Puraka is thirty-two; the mind's full kumbhaka is double that; and rechaka, to tell it, is eight-twos; know that mark, jnana girl.
nuance: The counts are 32 in, 64 held, 16 out, in units of maaththirai. Tirumular gives 16 in, 64 held, 32 out and calls any change of order deceit; Valaisami's intake and release are reversed. Whether this is a different school or a corruption of the kummi's text cannot be settled; the held count agrees.

reading: Pingala is where the rechaka is; placing the growing puraka in the left, so as to hold it as kumbhaka in Nandi: is this not the Siva-gaze, jnana girl?
nuance: Breath in by the left channel (இடம், idai), out by pingalai on the right, held 'in Nandi', the place of the guru at the brow of 2572. சிவநாட்டம், the Siva-gaze, makes the breath-hold and the fixed look one act.

reading: Know it together with the letter; from the full moon up to the new moon, doing it without forgetting according to the measure, the vaasi comes under control, jnana girl.
nuance: The fortnight from பௌர்ணை to அமாவாசை may be literal, a half-month of practice, or coded: the sixteen digits of the moon as the sixteen measures of the breath. மாத்திரை is the breath-unit of 2580.

reading: Raise the fire with the breath, girls; carry it above the whirl and feed it nectar, girls; proclaiming 'the muladhara's place is kechari', dance the kummi, girls.
nuance: கால் is wind as well as leg, so the fire at the root is kindled by the breath. The claim that the muladhara's own place is kechari, the mudra of the tongue turned up to the palate, folds the lowest centre into the highest act: raising the fire and tasting the nectar are the same movement.

reading: Lean on kechari, girl; first one can know oneself, as oneself; keenly worship the foot of the root Ganapati, jnana girl.
nuance: தன்னை அறியலாம் தானாக: self-knowledge comes from the practice, not from a text. The root Ganapati is the deity of the muladhara, as in the invocation (2521), so the kummi's end returns to its beginning.

reading: The letter NA is Brahma; in it Narayana became the letter MA; the letter SI is the god Rudra; I will say more, hear, jnana girl.
nuance: The five letters of நமசிவாய assigned to the five gods in order, NA, MA, SI here and VA, YA in 2586: a standard Saiva correspondence in which the mantra contains the hierarchy of the five functions. கிவ்வெழுத்து is a misprint for சிவ்வெழுத்து.

reading: To say it: VA is Mahesvara; completing the circle, YA, the honouring, is Sadasiva; by the faultless five letters the moving and the still have been sustained, jnana girl.
nuance: சராசரம், the moving and the unmoving, rests on the five letters: the mantra is the cosmos's support, not only an aid to worship. உபசாரம் (honouring, service) names YA's function, as the soul's offering of itself.

reading: The maiden's letters are three; who can say them with the mouth? Join the one above, the one below and the one between, and look quickly, jnana girl.
nuance: The Maiden's three-letter mantra is left unsaid, as the stanza says it must be; tradition identifies it with the Bala (Vaalai) bija or with A, U, M at the three places of 2578. The point is that it is formed by joining three body-stations, not uttered.

reading: Quickly I will say it: by the three letters, spreading always, life came to be; for those who have discerned and seen, is this not the initiation that is their protection, jnana girl?
nuance: சதம் is read as 'always' (சதா); it could be 'a hundred'. தீட்சை, initiation, is here the seeing of the three letters' work in life itself, and it is called a காவல், a guard, for those who have it.

reading: At the centre of the Siva-chakra called initiation, fixing the goddess's letter firmly, if Siva-puja is done with vision, siddhi comes into one's hand, jnana girl.
nuance: The yantra with the goddess's seed-letter at its centre is the Sri-chakra of 2557, now the object of worship; the condition is காட்சி, seeing, which the song has required at every step. Siddhi, the practice's attainment, is promised as a thing held.

reading: Do not drink toddy and reel about; do not take the sleep of ganja; feed from within on the drink of the Soma-digit and the rest, and dance the kummi, girls.
nuance: The intoxicants are refused not for morals but for a better drink: the moon-nectar of the crown. The stanza takes a position on the Siddhar use of ganja, which other works mention, by naming its sleep as the obstacle.

reading: Kummi-dancing girls, join the Lord of the hall and drink the nectar, girls; sing the non-duality that stands without saying 'am' or 'mum', jnana girl.
nuance: அம்பலத்தையர் is the Lord of the hall, Nataraja; அத்வீதம் is advaita. The non-duality is 'sung' and yet stands without a murmur (அம், மும், the sounds of hesitation), so the song's last word on its own singing is silence.

reading: ... is the beginning, girl; doing puja to the moon's thousand and eight petals, feed daily the Soma-milk that gives release, and dance the kummi, girls.
nuance: The first line (அக்லீதமாவத்துக்காதியடி) is garbled; அத்வீதம் from 2591 may be in it. The puja to the 1,008-petalled moon-lotus is the inner worship of the crown, and the Soma-milk the nectar of 2590; the chapter closes with daily practice.

title: ஞானக்கும்மி
theme: Vaalaisami's Njanak Kummi, fourth part: the breath-yoga stated as a sequence (kundalini's vaasi at the root triangle binding the four, the bindu held, the breath subdued at the whirl, Uma's initiation as the first of all yoga), then a Vedantic ladder above bindu (bindu, nada, Shakti, Siva, the Supreme and the sixth, the yoga-sadhaka's waking, the qualityless and partless) and a Vedantic cosmology (five elements, vikshepa, maya; Avyakrita, Hiranyagarbha and Virat with consciousness above them, the jiva a reflection of Brahman). The part closes with the Siddhars' horse: the breath as a horse of twelve legs, bound with eight ropes, mounted by kundalini's vaasi, which untamed will not enter the whirl's fort, and whose stable is the mind's fort where the enemy knocks.
structure_note: Every stanza ends in the refrain ஞானப்பெண்ணே or கும்மியடியுங்கடி; the reading is what the stanza adds. The part runs from practice (2593 to 2597) through the states above bindu (2598 to 2602), the breath and the whirl (2603 to 2604), the karmas and the triad of pasu, pasam and pati (2605 to 2608), the Vedantic cosmos and the reflection (2609 to 2611), and the horse of the vaasi (2612 to 2617), which the next part continues with the thirteen enemies.
source_issues: 2593: வாகியினால் is probably a misprint for வாசியினால் (so 2615); நியாபம் is unclear.
2599: the line ends with a stray comma after the refrain; so 2613 and 2614.
2606: விருவிசர்பமாம் and தேசமற்றார்பிர்ம் are garbled.
2607: சார்ர் is a doubled letter for சார்.
2610: இண்டமுண்ட and மிண்ணு are garbled; the sense is supplied from the Vedantic names.
2613: சருதாருயிருக்கின்றான் is garbled.
2614: the refrain is followed by a stray space and comma.

reading: What is to be kindled? At the root of the triangle in the circle, by kundalini's vaasi one establishes fullness and binds the four; is this not the knowing, girl of knowledge?
nuance: திரிகோணவட்ட மூலம், the triangle in the circle at the root, is the muladhara as tradition draws it. வாகியினால் is read as வாசியினால், matching 2615; the four that are bound are not named (2615 binds the eight and the four). நியாபம் is unclear, perhaps ஞாபகம் (knowing) or நியாயம் (the right way).

reading: Hold the bindu bound and do not push it out; subdue the breath at the whirl without struggling; do not struggle with the pointing mind; throw off the sloth of lust.
nuance: Three restraints and one dismissal: seed, breath and mind are held, and desire is called sloth (காமச் சோம்பல்), which 2595 then pairs with sleep. சுழிக்காற்று, the whirl-breath, is the breath at the suzhumunai.

reading: Sloth and sleep must not be; do not take on food-craving and grief; standing in the gaze on Samba Sadasiva, join and dance the kummi.
nuance: அன்ன சுதி is unclear: perhaps அன்ன ருசி (taste for food) or அன்ன சுத்தி (purity of food). The stanza turns the negatives of 2594 into the single positive, the fixed gaze (நாட்டம்) on Sadasiva.

reading: The sixty-four arts come to hand and the kalpa of knowledge comes and merges; the good siddhas and the freed said that such a one is a god.
nuance: சஷ்டிவித்தை is the சதுஷ்ஷஷ்டி கலை, the sixty-four arts. ஞானக் கற்பம் uses the medical word kalpa for knowledge itself, the rejuvenation that is knowing; 2607 calls this kalpa the true one. The deifying of the adept is credited to the siddhas and muktas, not claimed by the poet.

reading: Uma's initiation is the first for yoga, the first initiation for every yoga; do not abandon enjoyment; seek the worship of Shakti.
nuance: போகம் (enjoyment) is the word that carries the stanza. Taken plainly it tells the practitioner not to renounce the body's pleasure; in the Shakta reading of tradition it is the enjoyment of the goddess in the body that the yoga makes possible. Either way Shakti's initiation precedes every other yoga.

reading: Seek them: bindu, the ancient nada, Shakti, Siva who abides with her, and the Supreme; crossing these, the sixfold way is the yoga-practitioner's waking.
nuance: Five are named (விந்து, நாதம், சத்தி, சிவம், பரம்) and the stanza says six (வகையாறு); the sixth may be the waking (சாக்கிரம்) itself or an unnamed term. சாதக சாக்கிரம், the practitioner's waking, is the first of a set of yogic states that 2599 and 2601 continue; it is a 'waking' above the ordinary waking, as in the Tirumanthiram's avasthas within avasthas.

reading: That waking is the sphere above bindu; reaching it is the qualityless, the partless; if one looks, it is the stainless state without support; if one does not look at it, that is the end.
nuance: நிர்க்குண நிஷ்களம் are Vedantic and Agamic names for the Supreme without attributes or parts. நிராதாராமலம் is read as நிராதார அமலம், the supportless stainless, that is, above the six adharas. அந்தம் at the close may be 'the end' as goal or as death; 2600 takes it up as a name for the state.

reading: That is the end, girl; who, having seen these six above, knows the way of knowledge? See the great ones whose minds are discerning, serve them, and dance.
nuance: The ladder of 2598 and 2599 is declared unknowable from the text alone; the stanza sends the hearer to the living great (பெரியோர்), the kummi's usual name for the guru.

reading: Serving is the twilight rite of austerity; standing as yoga is bindu and nada; the Sadasiva-waking that agrees with the life-breath is that very place.
nuance: The stanza pairs three terms with three definitions: service with sandhya (தவ சந்தி), yoga with bindu-nada, and the Sadasiva-waking with the breath or soul (ஆவி). சதாசிவ சாக்கிரம் is a yogic state above the practitioner's waking of 2598; the names of the Siva-avasthas in 2685 to 2689 belong to the same scheme.

reading: Letting go 'a', letting go 'u', with the trace in the upper whirl, leaving fire by means of air, letting go 'ma', see the inner substance of nada and bindu, praise it and dance.
nuance: அ, உ, ம are the three letters of Om; the stanza releases them one by one and places what remains in the upper whirl (மேற்சுழி). அங்கியை விட்டுக் காலாலே is read as leaving the fire (the heat at the root) by the air (the breath); in cipher fire and air are also the right and left breaths. The 'inner substance' is what is left of Om when its letters are gone.

reading: What is the roaring? Prana and apana; kindling them in samadhi, the out-breath makes it shine, and the sun's radiance is the brightness; seek it and dance.
nuance: முழக்கம் (roar) is the sound of the breath or of nada. இரேசகம் is the rechaka, the out-breath, and இரவி காந்தி the sun's light, in cipher the right breath or the inner fire; the word order is loose and the sentence may divide otherwise.

reading: Those who look do not see the suzhumunai; they do not know that it is the tip of the nose; turning back the road, see the great ones, praise them and dance.
nuance: The kummi places the suzhumunai at the nose-tip (மூக்கு நுனி), the point of the yogic nasikagra gaze, where most Siddhar texts place the whirl at the brow or the crown; the difference may be of the opening rather than the channel. மார்க்கம் மறித்து, turning the road back, is read of the breath's outward road, as in 2616.

reading: Praise, girl, the gathered store; change deeds into fullness, girl; cast away the coming and the accumulated karma; destroy what is to be destroyed, and dance.
nuance: ஆகாமியம் and சஞ்சிதம் are two of the three karmas of Vedanta, the deeds yet to come and the stored deeds; the third, the deeds now ripening (பிராரத்தம்), may be the சேகரம் (store) of the first line. The stanza's cure for karma is to turn it into பூரணம், the fullness that 2639 says the ignorant merely name.

reading: The place without bond is the sky-going; standing in one half is yoga; for those without a country it is the Brahma-knowledge samadhi, and it is the twofold spreading.
nuance: கேசம் is read as கேசரம் (khechara, the sky-going state), as in 2642 and 2657. ஒரு பாதி, one half, may be the moon's half or one of the two breaths. விருவிசர்ப்பம் is obscure, perhaps இரு விசர்ப்பம், a twofold spreading. A short reading is that bondlessness, yoga and samadhi are three names for one state.

reading: This kalpa is the true one, girl; all other desires are very small; join the silence of Sadasiva, the bliss of the Supreme, and dance.
nuance: The kalpa (கற்பம்) here is the knowledge-kalpa of 2596, not a drug; it is set against காமம், all other wanting, which is அற்பம் (petty). The goal is named as silence and bliss together.
