reading: Call the bond the body and that bound soul the life; what stands in love is what they call fixity in Brahman.
nuance: Saiva Siddhanta's triad is recast: pasam is the body, pasu the soul, and in place of pati stands நேசம், love, as the state of Brahma-nishta. The attribution என்பார் (they say) keeps it as a received definition. 2662 will tell the hearer to drop pati and pasam altogether.

reading: The beginning of the body is the five elements; the beginning of the other, of action, is projection; the beginning of delusion is maya; hear all of it, girl.
nuance: விட்சேபம் (vikshepa) is the Vedantic projecting power of ignorance, paired with concealment (ஆவரணம்); the stanza assigns it to activity and maya to delusion (மோகம்). The three 'beginnings' (ஆதி) are a compressed Vedantic account of body, act and mind.

reading: Above the Avyakrita who holds the eggs, above Hiranyagarbha who is Vishnu, above the lightning-bright Virat Purusha, above these there is consciousness.
nuance: வியாகிருதன், இரணியகர்ப்பன் and விராட் புருடன் are the three cosmic selves of Vedanta, presiding over the universe's deep sleep, dream and waking; the kummi equates Hiranyagarbha with Vishnu. இண்டமுண்ட is garbled, perhaps அண்டமுண்ட (who swallowed the eggs). சைதன்னியம் (chaitanya), consciousness, is above all three and is named Brahman in 2611.

reading: The conscious substance itself is Brahman, girl; for that witness, what comes after is the reflection; by pure knowledge that stands true, the reflection can be cast off.
nuance: பிம்பம் and பிரதிபிம்பம் are the Vedantic image and reflection: Brahman as the witness (சாட்சி) and the jiva as its reflection in the mind. உபிந்தி is unclear, perhaps உபாதி (the adjunct, as in chapter 141). The stanza says the reflection is discarded, not the witness.

reading: Yes, girl, if this state is seen, you yourself are the beginning and the end; for us, by the horse of the vaasi, there is the greatly good way, girl.
nuance: The first half is the Vedantic conclusion of 2610 and 2611: the hearer is herself first and last. The second half introduces the கற்றிரை (horse) that fills the rest of the part, the breath as a mount rather than a thing held.

reading: The horse of good breed has great speed and stands above the life that is its load; if one gives it a course street by street, one can watch the horse's show.
nuance: சாதிக் குதிரை is a thoroughbred; in the cipher the horse is the breath, as 2612 has just said. சருதாருயிர் is garbled; the sense taken is that the breath rides above the life it carries. வீதிக்கு வீதி, street to street, is read as the breath's course through the channels, which 2627 names as streets.

reading: That axle-level cannot be bound, since its legs are twelve; but if one ties it with eight ropes, it comes under measure.
nuance: The numbers carry the stanza. கால் is both leg and wind: the twelve legs match the twelve finger-breadths that tradition gives as the breath's reach, and the Tirumanthiram's horse of twelve legs. The eight ropes are taken as the eight limbs of yoga, or the eight that 2615 binds with the four. அச்சு மட்டம், the axle's level, is obscure.

reading: Will it be bound? At the gate of impurity, in the middle of the centre, by kundalini's vaasi, if one binds the eight and the four and reveres them, one can mount and ride.
nuance: மலவாயில், the gate of impurity, is the body's lowest opening, so the centre is the muladhara of 2593. The eight and the four are not explained; tradition offers the eight petals and four petals of the lower lotuses, or the eight siddhis and four steps. The horse is bound where kundalini sleeps and ridden from there.

reading: Without taming the subtle horse one cannot go inside the fort of the whirl; the breath walks ahead for a thousand kadham.
nuance: சுழிக் கோடு, the whirl's fort or horn, is the suzhumunai as an enclosure to be entered. The last line is the plainest statement in the part of why the breath must be tamed: left alone it runs outward an immense distance (a kadham is some ten miles), that is, it is spent on the world.

reading: In the stable where the horse is tied, in the fort of the mind, in the market street, the enemy himself comes and knocks; ask what that is, girl.
nuance: The mind is at once stable, fort and bazaar; the enemy who knocks is not named here but in the next part, where Kama and twelve kin are counted. சந்தைப்பேட்டை, the market quarter, makes the mind a place of trade as well as defence.

title: ஞானக்கும்மி
theme: Njanak Kummi, fifth part: the enemy at the mind's fort is Kama, eldest of a family of thirteen (anger, greed, delusion, pride, envy, hypocrisy, egoism, rage and the rest), who all subside when one is mastered; the mind is a mad monkey, worldly bondage a snake in the heart, and the cure is the silent vaasi and the pincers of knowledge and dispassion. The part then turns on those who mistake the outside for the inside: mutterers of mantras who do not know the inner letter, mouth-shutters who call that silence, beard-and-matted-hair sannyasis, word-gurus against the sat-guru who is within, and alchemists who heat mercury and sulphur, melt cinnabar, calcine arsenic and talk of muppu without knowing the cause, the flower or the seed-syllable.
structure_note: Three movements: the thirteen enemies and the taming of the mind-horse (2618 to 2627); mantra, silence, garb and guru (2628 to 2635); and alchemy as practised by the ignorant (2636 to 2642), each formula named only to say it fails without the inner knowledge.
source_issues: 2619 and 2620: the names of the friends (சேகா வீரஷைடம்பனுஞ்சம்பனும், தீபவனா மோராங்காரி) are garbled; the count of thirteen in 2621 cannot be recovered exactly from them.
2625: பீத்தலை is unidentified.
2633: தங்க இறவ மோ is corrupt; the refrain is printed ஞானப்பெண்னே.
2634: நாடென் மங்காடென்றுஞ் and கல்ல (for நல்ல) are corrupt.
2636 and 2623: a stray comma follows the refrain.
2638: வெள்ளைப் பாலூட்டி குசைமூடி runs the words together; யீசானிய is unclear.
2642: சோசபீசம் is probably a corruption of சோகம் பீஜம் or a similar term.

reading: Kama is the eldest of all, and the arts he has learned are many; slow anger and greed are his younger brothers, hear it, girl.
nuance: The six enemies of Sanskrit ethics (kama, krodha, lobha, moha, mada, matsarya) are made a family with Kama as its head; 2619 and 2620 add children and friends to reach the thirteen of 2621. தாமதம் (slow, tamasic) qualifies anger, or both brothers.

reading: Delusion and pride are his two children; a fierce envious one, and Sega-Vira, Dambha and Sambha are his friends.
nuance: மசியக்காரன் is read as the மாச்சரியம் (matsarya, envy) of the standard six; the friends' names are partly garbled (சேகா வீர, ஷைடம்பன், சம்பன்), with டம்பம் (hypocritical show) the one certain member.

reading: The fit kinsman of that friend is the wicked Ahamkara; the rage who does many things without thought is his son, girl.
nuance: ஓராங்காரி is read as அகங்காரி, the ego, and ரோஷன் as rosha, rage; தீபவனா is unclear. The count reaches about eleven here; 2621's thirteen may include members the text has dropped.

reading: Hear it thus: there are thirteen enemies; if one alone comes under control, they will all subside, girl.
nuance: The one is not named; 2618 makes Kama the head of the family, and 2622 to 2626 treat the mind as what must be tamed, so either reading stands. The claim is that the vices are one system, not thirteen separate fights.

reading: There is no subduing by these; in the fort of the mind where there is no running toward gain, they catch the cow that grazes its way toward the battlefield.
nuance: பசு is the cow and, in Saiva usage, the soul; the enemies seize the soul that wanders into the field of battle, the mind-fort of 2617. பலனோட்டமில்லா is unclear, perhaps 'where no fruit runs' or 'without a fleeing from gain'.

reading: The snake lies inside the anthill, and worldly bondage lies inside the heart; if one subdues bluster and rises, one can watch the horse's show.
nuance: The snake in the anthill is a proverb for a hidden danger, and the stanza pairs it with சக பந்தம் (the world's bond) in the heart; the snake is also kundalini's usual image, so a coded reading has the coiled power waiting in the body as bondage waits in the heart. வீம்பு is boastful stubbornness.

reading: If the mad monkey of the mind, seized too by a frenzied ghost, starts its revels, when one makes the medicine to subdue it the horse can then be ridden.
nuance: மனக்குரங்கு is the standard image of the restless mind; the ghost that possesses it is the family of 2618 to 2620. The medicine is named in 2625 as the silent vaasi, and in 2626 as knowledge and dispassion.

reading: One can ride: the silent vaasi; without covering the four or five openings, by firmness, if the mind becomes accomplished, the siddhas can gain clarity.
nuance: மோனவாசி, the silent breath, is the kummi's name for the practice; பீத்தலை is obscure, read as the body's apertures that are not to be stopped, against the mouth-shutting of 2629. மனஞ் சித்தானால், if the mind becomes siddha, makes attainment a state of mind rather than a power.

reading: Having locked up the clarified mind, joining the understanding that ripens in it to the Lord, bending down, take the pincers of knowledge and dispassion and bind it.
nuance: குறடு is a smith's tongs; ஞான வைராக்கியம் (knowledge and dispassion) are the tool. சித்தகம் is read as சித்தம் (mind) and பதி as the Lord, though it could be 'the place'. குனிர்ந்து is unclear.

reading: One leap in the root street, a root-leap in the street of the three-way junction, one leap in the upper street: one can watch the horse's show.
nuance: The streets are the channels and the leaps the breath's movements, continuing 2613's course street by street. மூலத்தெரு is the muladhara, மேலைத்தெரு the crown; முச்சந்தி, the three-way junction, is where the three nadis meet, placed by tradition at the brow. The stanza gives no more than the three stations.

reading: Not knowing these ways, they wander saying 'gem' and 'mantra'; if one knows the inner letter, is that not itself the gem-mantra, girl?
nuance: மணி மந்திரம் is the pair of charm and spell in popular usage; the stanza keeps the name and moves its referent inward. அந்தரமான எழுத்து, the inner letter, is the single syllable that 2602 reached by letting go அ, உ and ம.

reading: By mantras of silence they wander with their mouths shut; for those who feed on the essence of youth, will the moon become their food, girl?
nuance: The first half mocks a vow of silence kept with the mouth. யுவனசாரம் is unclear, perhaps the sap of youth (sexual vigour, spent) or a corrupt word; மதி போசனம், the moon as food, is the nectar of the inner moon that yoga is said to drink, so the question is whether those who spend themselves below can feed from above.

reading: They say 'mother'; but when Kama's possession comes in a dream, will they remember? Even if one reads the Veda by mouth, will pure silence stay, girl?
nuance: The test of silence is the dream, where resolve is not in charge: the one who calls every woman mother by day is visited by desire at night. சுத்த மௌனம் is the silence of the mind, which recitation does not produce.

reading: Growing a beard, growing matted hair, putting on the costume of a good sannyasi, who here will accept the base antics of one who ran about in it, girl?
nuance: புலையாட்டம் is read as base or defiling behaviour; a variant sense is புலை ஆடு, a goat for the slaughter, which fits ஓடித்திரிந்த (ran about). The stanza is the kummi's one direct attack on the renunciant's garb.

reading: Finding the place where one stays without speaking, and having gained it, abiding there is the mantra; if a teacher gives that teaching, say 'the guru is the able one' and dance.
nuance: The answer to 2628 and 2629: mantra is the silent place itself. ஆசானென்று உபதேசம் விட்டால் may mean 'if one gives teaching as a master' or 'if one lets go the teaching that says master'; the first is taken, since the line ends by praising the guru.

reading: Can one be freed by a word-guru? Such men tell lies, and will their gold endure? Join those who are sat-gurus and hear their word, girl.
nuance: சொற்குரு, the guru of words, is set against சற்குரு, the true guru; the second line (தங்க இறவமோ) is corrupt and read as 'will their gold or standing last'. The sat-guru's word is still a word, so the contrast is in the speaker, not the medium.

reading: Those who do not speak the ego that says 'I', who speak of a good land and a dim land alike, who have seen all things as themselves: that is the boon of the sat-guru, girl.
nuance: ஆணவம், the first impurity of Siddhanta, is glossed here as the saying of 'I' (நான்). நாடென் மங்காடென்றும் is garbled; the reading takes it as indifference to places, matching 2660's 'going to lands is desire'. கல்ல is read as நல்ல.

reading: The guru dwells in the heart; the cutting of the mind's crookedness is within oneself; without knowing how the substance dies, how can one do the calcination, girl?
nuance: The hinge of the part: the inner guru of the first half and the furnace (புடம்) of the second are set in one stanza. பொருள் இறப்பது, the dying of the substance, is the alchemist's killing of mercury; read inward it is the death of the mind's crookedness, which the stanza says must be known before any firing.

reading: Not knowing the alchemy, saying 'we practise rasavaadham', they put mercury and sulphur in the crucible; will gold grow from it, girl?
nuance: சூதம் (mercury) and கெந்தி (sulphur) are the base pair of Siddha alchemy; the stanza does not deny transmutation, it denies that heating the two without the knowledge (வாதம்) yields it. The claim is historical, that practitioners of the time did exactly this.

reading: They bend their effort to melting the lingam, not knowing the lingam of the right kind; the tale of joining lead with gold, is it not a disgrace, girl?
nuance: லிங்கம் here is the alchemists' word for cinnabar (ரசலிங்கம், சாதிலிங்கம், red sulphide of mercury), and சாதிலிங்கம் is that mineral's name; the stanza plays on the word's other sense, Siva's emblem, so a second reading has them melting idols while not knowing the true linga. வங்கம் is lead or tin, and the gold-and-lead story is the coiner's fraud.

reading: Even if one sets arsenic in a crucible, feeds it with white milk, covers it with grass and gives it the north-east firing, what is there in it, girl?
nuance: பாஷாணம் is the class of arsenical and other poison-stones; குகை is the covered crucible; புடம் the calcining fire, here of a named kind (ஈசானியப் புடம், perhaps by direction or by name). The stanza lists a real procedure only to ask what is gained; it is not a recipe and the text gives no quantities.

reading: The cause is what becomes the effect; those who do not know to point it out are utter fools; even if they wander saying 'fullness', will any merit come of it, girl?
nuance: காரணம் and காரியம் are the Vedantic cause and effect, the one Brahman and its appearances. பூரணம் is the Siddhars' name for that whole, which 2605 told the hearer to turn karma into; here it is a word in the mouths of those who cannot trace effect to cause.

reading: They wander saying 'muppu', but they do not see the way that muppu came to be; if one turns back and says 'that is the flower', it becomes attainment, and dance.
nuance: முப்பு is the Siddhars' three-salt preparation, the catalyst of their alchemy, whose identity is itself a secret of the tradition. The stanza puns on பூ: முப்பூ as three flowers and அப்பூ, 'that flower', as something turned back toward (மறித்தால்), which in the kummi's cipher is the breath turned inward; the plain and the coded readings both stand.

reading: They do not know how to bind the alkali; without turning the fierce essence into calx, by joining veesam with camphor, is it not all in vain, girl?
nuance: காரம், சாரம், நீறு and பூரம் are terms of Siddha chemistry: alkali, a salt or essence (sal ammoniac in some lists), calcined powder, and camphor or borax. வீசம் is unidentified, perhaps a measure or a substance. The verse argues the order of operations matters and the ignorant skip the binding step.

reading: Not knowing the fierce science, they wander in the garb of the world; if one knows the seed of the soham, the alchemy becomes the sky-going, girl.
nuance: சோச பீசம் is read as the seed-syllable (பீஜம்) of சோகம் (so'ham, 'I am He'), the breath-mantra of Vedantic yoga; a corrupt word may lie behind it. கேசரம் (khechara) is the siddhi of moving in space and the state of 2657; the alchemy that works is the inner one made by a syllable, which closes the part's argument.

title: ஞானக்கும்மி
theme: The sixth part of Madurai Valaisami's Njanak Kummi finishes the attack on the alchemists who live by trickery (fumes blown through a tube, calx sold to the credulous, flying mercury and magnet cups) and on ganja-smoking cave ascetics, then turns the alchemist's words inward: the salt, the root, the black gooseberry and the white root in the tank are in the house, and the true alchemist is the one who knows the salt. After naming the Siddha books it trusts (Konkanar, Sattamuni, Tirumular, Agastya, Machamuni), it lists as mere desire every outward observance, the breath-counting of rechaka, puraka and kumbhaka included, along with giving up salt, eating once a day, pilgrimage, the family god, sect difference and Ganga bathing, and ends by turning from the six adharas to the Vedantic count of tattvas.
structure_note: False alchemists and false gurus (2643 to 2647); alchemy read as an inner work, its salt, root and herbs coded as in the body (2648 to 2652); ganja ascetics, and the books of the true Siddhas (2653 to 2656); the litany of what is only desire (ஆசையடி), with the gate within the gate set among it (2657 to 2661); casting off Pati and pasa, the tattvas, the Veda and the six adharas (2662 to 2664); the turn to Vedanta and the count of tattvas, which the next part sets out (2665 to 2667). The refrains ஞானப்பெண்ணே and கும்மியடியுங்கடி alternate; the readings give what each stanza adds.
source_issues: 2644: lines 1 and 2 (திருசுசுன்னமுடிந்தாச்சு அசைச் சோதிக்க வெட்டாரை மாற்றாச்சு) are compressed or corrupt.
2649: மிதல்வவோ is a misprint for மிதல்லவோ.
2650: கருஞ்சூரசூரை is corrupt; வைத்தெடுப்பச் has a stray final letter.
2651: பெணணே is a misprint for பெண்ணே.
2652 and 2662: the stanzas end with a stray comma after the refrain.
2653: வரியலாகுமோ is probably அறியலாகுமோ.
2656: மொறு is probably ஒரு.
2660: சே.தி has a stray full stop, for சோதி; கும்மி படியுங்கடி for கும்மியடியுங்கடி.
2661: யடிடியுங்கடி doubles a syllable.
2665: சேளடி is a misprint for கேளடி.
2667: line 3 (மறைக் குட்சொலலிய சித்துருதாலாகு) is garbled.

reading: They do not see the key of alchemy, nor perceive the drug of the five elements; why do they blow smoke through the tube? Ask what this is, girl of knowledge.
nuance: The திறவுகோல் (key) of vaadham is what the kummi will say is inward; பஞ்சபூதச் சரக்கு, the drug of the five elements, can be read as an actual mineral set or as the five elements of the body. குழல் புகை ஊதுதல், blowing fumes through the blowpipe, is the outward craft being mocked.

reading: They say the sacred calx is finished and the test-piece has been changed, tell of the substance and carry off money: are these not false gurus, girl of knowledge?
nuance: Lines 1 and 2 are compressed and partly corrupt (சுன்னம் is calx; வெட்டாரை is unclear, perhaps a test or a vessel). Line 3 is plain: the alchemist-guru describes the marvel and takes fees. The charge is fraud, not the falsity of alchemy as such.

reading: They say the flying mercury is done, they say they have made even the needle-magnet into a cup; it is by the trickery of their world-alchemy that they make a living, girl of knowledge.
nuance: கவன சூதம், mercury fixed so that it gives the power to fly (கமனம்), and the magnet worked into a vessel are boasts of the alchemical literature. புவனவாதை may be புவன வாதம், alchemy for the world's eyes, against the inner alchemy the kummi prefers.

reading: Living on without knowing release or the knowledge brought from former births, they feed on rain, wither to dry leaves and falter, girl of knowledge.
nuance: மழையைத் தின்று, 'eating the rain', is read as the ascetic who lives on water or air and wastes to a dry leaf (சருகு); the line may be corrupt. The point is that bodily austerity without knowledge is only a slower way of failing.

reading: What fruit is there in faltering? Is it skill to master the mind and then sell it? Do not be deluded: how does the greatness of the vazhalai come?
nuance: வழலை is the Siddhars' alchemical salt (in some lists the base of muppu), and in their cipher a thing of the body. The question 'how does its greatness come?' prepares the next stanza's answer that the salt is known, not bought. மனம் சாதித்து விற்க may mean making a trade of mental powers.

reading: He who knows the salt is the alchemist, he who has destroyed the world's dross is the yogi; there is no fault in this; lean on the glory of earth and nada and see, girl of knowledge.
nuance: The stanza redefines both titles: வாதி is not the one with the crucible but the one who knows உப்பு, the salt that in Siddha cipher stands for a bodily essence, and யோகி is the one rid of the world's குப்பை, its rubbish. பூமி நாத மகிமை, 'the glory of earth and nada', is obscure; it may pair the base centre with the sound at the crown.

reading: There is a root in the house, and in the forest outside is Tirumular; for the great ones who are caught in it, is this not rasavada, girl of knowledge?
nuance: The stanza puns on மூலம்: the herb-root sought in the forest, the மூலாதாரம் at the base of the body that is 'in the house', and திருமூலர், the Siddha whose name is the 'holy root'. The plain sense is that the root for alchemy is at home; the coded sense is that the true rasavada is the root centre, as Tirumular taught.

reading: Taking the drug they say does not appear, setting it in the black ... and drawing it out: like the thing seen by one who cannot see, siddhi is that itself; dance the kummi.
nuance: கருஞ்சூரசூரை is corrupt or a coded vessel name and is not rendered. காணான் கண்ட பொருள், 'the thing the blind man saw', is a Siddha paradox for what is seen without the eye; the attainment is the seeing, not the product.

reading: The gooseberry is in the forest and the black gooseberry is in the house; even if you go off to the Kolli hills, will the guru bring it to you, girl of knowledge?
nuance: கருநெல்லி, the black gooseberry, is a famous kalpa herb of the Siddha tradition, said to grow on the Kolli hills; the stanza moves it 'into the house', the body. The question about the guru can be read as scorn (no guru will fetch it for you) or as a pointer (only the guru shows where it is).

reading: In the tank of Kayampatti the white kasa root has sprouted; if one rises upright from the mouth-river, the body will not perish, girl of knowledge.
nuance: காயாம்பட்டி reads as the 'village of the body' (காயம்), its tank a bodily place; காசாம் வேர், the root of the kasa (white-flowered) plant, is a herb or its cipher. வாயாற்றினின்று நிமிர்ந்தால், rising from the river of the mouth, may point to the turning of breath or nectar upward. The claim is the kalpa claim of an undying body, here located within.

reading: Without thinking to know the kalpa state they smoke maddening ganja and stay so; even if these petty men go to caves and mountains, can they know the thing, girl of knowledge?
nuance: The target is the ascetic who uses ganja as a shortcut and the remote cave as a credential. கற்பநிலை, the kalpa state, is again inward.

reading: In the Kadaikkandam that Konkanar told, knowing what is in doubt is the Brahmanda; see the two hundred of our guru, the great muni Sattaimuni, girl of knowledge.
nuance: The stanza names Siddha books: Konkanar's கடைக்காண்டம் and Sattaimuni's இருநூறு (two hundred verses), and claims Sattaimuni as 'our guru'. The middle phrase, that knowing the doubt in it is பிரமாண்டம், may mean the book's secret is the cosmic egg, or simply that it is vast.

reading: What the true jnani told in the hundred, what Tirumular realised, is jnana; see the locked secret of the sutra that Purna Kumbhamuni told, girl of knowledge.
nuance: கும்பமுனி is Agastya; 'the hundred' is not identified. பூட்டகம், a locked thing, names the Siddha habit of writing so that only the initiated can open the text.

reading: In initiation, Machamuni's initiation and the hundred of knowledge he declared: no lowering will come; see the great ones and hear the vision, girl of knowledge.
nuance: மச்சமுனி (Matsyendra in the north) is cited for தீட்சை, initiation, and a work of a hundred verses. The stanza closes the list of authorities by sending the hearer to living great ones.

reading: Doing the vaasi exactly by rechaka, puraka and kumbhaka is also desire; reach the non-dual Brahman that is the sky-going state and dance the kummi.
nuance: This opens the litany of ஆசையடி, 'that too is desire'. Breath-counting is placed among the observances to be outgrown, although the same kummi taught the vaasi at the root triangle (2593, 2615). One reading is that the measured pranayama of the manuals is the desire, and the vaasi proper is the khechara Brahman itself; another is that at this point the song leaves practice for Vedanta. கேசரம் is the 'moving in space' that 2642 promised the inner alchemy.

reading: Giving up salt is desire, eating food only once a day is desire; join the Manonmani god who cannot be spoken and dance the kummi.
nuance: The vows of abstaining from salt and of a single daily meal are reckoned with desire, as wanting a result. The salt here is literal, unlike the coded salt of 2648, so the kummi both praises knowing the salt and dismisses giving it up. மனோன்மணி is the Shakti of the crown, 'jewel of the mind'.

reading: In the gate there is an upper gate, and in that gate a small gate; lovingly close the small gate and look closely, girl of knowledge.
nuance: The first two lines repeat 2561 almost word for word. The gate within the gate is the Siddhars' cipher for the opening of the central channel at the crown; பூட்டி நெருக்கி, locking and pressing, is read as the inward seal of breath and mind. Set between two 'desire' stanzas, it marks what is not desire.

reading: Going to far lands is desire, saying there is a family god is desire; join the light of the Brahman-knowledge we love and dance the kummi.
nuance: தேசங்கள் போவது is pilgrimage or wandering; குலதெய்வம் is the lineage deity of the household. Both are put on the side of wanting.

reading: Sect difference is desire, bathing in the Ganga and puja are desire; praise the 'mine' that remains without 'mine', and dance the kummi.
nuance: மமதை அற்றிருக்கின்ற மமதை, 'the mineness that stays without mineness', is a paradox: perhaps the Self that alone can say 'I' without ego, perhaps a scribal doubling. The first half is the common Siddha rejection of sect and sacred water.

reading: Push away the cow that gives no milk, leave even Pati and pasa and be done with them; seek the Supreme light that shines above and dance the kummi.
nuance: பதி and பாசம் are two of Saiva Siddhanta's three categories (with பசு); telling the hearer to leave the Lord-category itself is a Vedantic move beyond the Siddhanta scheme. பால் கறவாப் பசு, the cow that yields no milk, may be the barren practice or, by pun on பசு, the bound soul's identity.

reading: Push away the rubbish heap of the tattvas, close up the holes of Veda and sastra; call the knowledge-thing that gives release to come, kindle it and dance the kummi.
nuance: பொத்தல் is a hole or gap (or a scribal form of பொத்தகம், book); either way the Veda and the sastras are to be shut. Two stanzas later the kummi takes up Vedanta 'by the word of the Siddhars', so the dismissal is of book-learning, not of the Vedantic conclusion.

reading: The six adharas are trouble, and beyond them there is nothing; women standing in good order, join and dance the kummi.
nuance: அதற்கு அப்பாலே ஒன்றுமில்லை, 'beyond it there is nothing', can mean that the climb through the six centres leads nowhere, or that beyond them is the void, the nothing the kummi elsewhere calls the goal (2698). Both readings stand.

reading: By the Siddhars' word see Siddhanta and be clear about Vedanta; hear the relation of the subtle origin that is tattva, girl of knowledge.
nuance: The kummi claims Siddhanta and Vedanta both, with the Siddhars as the authority for each, and announces the Vedantic account of how the tattvas arise, which the stanzas following set out.

reading: What is the relation? The tattva that Vedanta tells is of this kind; I will lay out the account of the states, the causal and the rest, girl of knowledge.
nuance: காரணாதி அவஸ்தை, the states beginning with the causal, announces the scheme of bodies and states (gross, subtle, causal; waking, dream, sleep) that the next part develops.

reading: The tattvas spoken of are seen as four sevens, the chit-form told is four sixes; see the greatness of the chit-form spoken within the Veda, girl of knowledge.
nuance: நாலேழு and நாலாறு are read as 28 and 24; the text could also mean eleven and ten. A count of twenty-eight tattvas is known from Tirumanthiram 2176; what the 'chit-form' of twenty-four is, the stanza does not say, and line 3 is corrupt (சித்துருதாலாகு).

title: ஞானக்கும்மி
theme: The seventh part of Madurai Valaisami's Njanak Kummi lays out the Vedantic analysis of the great saying in three tiers of bodies, states and their owners. For the 'thou' (tvam-pada), the gross body in waking is owned by Visva, the subtle in dream by Taijasa and the causal in deep sleep by Prajna. For the 'that' (tat-pada), the Lord named omniscient, all-doer, inner controller and the rest takes the same three as Virat, Hiranyagarbha and Avyakrita, and his adjuncts are said to stain release. A third, Saiva tier follows: Siva's waking, dream and deep sleep (named world-devouring and upasanta) and Siva's turiya. Beyond all of them is the turiya that has not been seen, the form of Brahman-bliss, and the song ends on bowing to the feet of the guru whose form is that.
structure_note: The tvam-pada and its seven causes (2668 to 2670); Visva, Taijasa and Prajna with waking, dream and deep sleep (2671 to 2674); the tat-pada, its names and adjuncts (2675 to 2679); Virat, Hiranyagarbha and Avyakrita (2680 to 2682); the Siva-pada and its states, waking, the world-devouring dream, upasanta sleep and Siva-turiya (2683 to 2689); the turiya beyond, bliss and the guru's feet (2690 to 2692). The text of this part is badly corrupt in places; the readings follow the Vedantic scheme where the words allow, and the scheme is the tradition's, not something the stanza always spells out.
source_issues: 2668: முன் சொன்னவசித்திரு is unclear, perhaps சித்துரு.
2669: காசலையா is unclear.
2670: அரியத்திற் is probably துரியத்தில்; தொம்பத்ததைத் doubles a letter.
2671: போல்லோ is garbled; the stanza ends with a stray comma.
2672: சைதனாம் is probably தைசதன்; lines 1 and 3 are damaged.
2673: வாயுவடன் for வாயுவுடன்; the stanza ends தேகமடி without the refrain and may be incomplete.
2674: கண்டராமத்தை is doubtful.
2676: அறிவகென்னடி and சருவதற்பா are garbled.
2678, 2683: ஞானப்பெண்னே for ஞானப்பெண்ணே; 2678 line 2 (வாதம் தரியமடி) is corrupt.
2679: பானுக்கு and சாயாகிரகம் are doubtful; the stanza ends with a stray comma.
2680: காமர் is doubtful.
2682: வியாகிருதன் for அவ்யாகிருதன்; பார்சுழித்தி for பர சுழுத்தி.
2683: பதைக் and சிவகாதத்தி are garbled.
2684: தன்னுடலாச்சுக has a stray final letter.
2686: line 3 (சேகரமாயிடிறசிறசொலிதையென்று) is garbled.
2687: the line contains a stray dash (பத்தனென் - சொல்).
2688: இருர்தாக்கால் for இருந்தாக்கால்.
2689: the stanza ends with a stray comma.
2690: முற்றிரியம் is probably முற்றுத் துரியம்.

reading: I will make known the tvam-pada, which is glory, and the adjuncts that came into it; hear what its nature is: the working of the conscious form told before, girl of knowledge.
nuance: தொம்பதம் is the 'thou' of tat tvam asi, here the individual self considered with its உபாதி, limiting adjuncts. வசித்திரு is read as சித்துரு, the chit-form of 2667; the line is uncertain.

reading: The body full of vasanas, the prana breath, the senses joined as one, and the mind with the rest that grew together: these are the causes, girl of knowledge.
nuance: வாசனை (latent impressions), body, prana and the senses are listed with மதி and its fellows; காசலையா is unclear. The next stanza counts the list as seven, which suggests body, prana, senses and the four inner faculties, but the stanza does not name them all.

reading: These seven called causes came and mingled with the tvam-pada; in the turiya of the causal tvam-pada they became its own body, girl of knowledge.
nuance: The claim is that what the self takes as its body is the seven adjuncts mingled with it. அரியத்தில் is read as துரியத்தில், turiya, the fourth state; the syntax is loose.

reading: The self that holds the gross waking as its own is afterwards named Visva, by its identification, girl of knowledge.
nuance: In the Vedantic scheme விஸ்வன் (Visva) is the self identified with the gross body in waking. அபிமானம், owning or identifying, is the operative word: the names belong to the identification, not to the self.

reading: Joined with the adjuncts that bear names, the subtle comes in dream, and the name of the one who stands in it is Taijasa, girl of knowledge.
nuance: சைதனாம் is read as தைசதன் (Taijasa), the owner of the subtle body in dream; the stanza is corrupt in lines 1 and 3.

reading: When prana with its breaths subsides and is joined to the root, and the gathered nada-turiya is joined, that is the causal body.
nuance: The causal body is described in yogic terms, breath withdrawn into the root and the nada reached, rather than in the textbook terms of ignorance; the stanza lacks the refrain and may be damaged.

reading: The state joined is deep sleep, and the one who joins it is Prajna; bow to the one who has seen all three keenly, and dance the kummi.
nuance: பிராக்ஞன் (Prajna) owns the causal body in deep sleep, completing the triad Visva, Taijasa, Prajna. கண்டராமத்தை is read as 'the one who saw' the three, the witness; it may be a corrupt or punning word.

reading: Having bowed and seen the settled meaning of the tvam-pada, by the same rule I will now tell the discrimination of the tat-pada, girl of knowledge.
nuance: சித்தார்த்தம், settled meaning, and விவேகம், discrimination, are the method: each pada is analysed by stripping its adjuncts, and the same procedure is turned on 'that'.

reading: What is to be known? As the tvam-pada thing had its adjuncts, so for the all-pervading thing of the tat-pada there are its own body, its jiva and its turiya.
nuance: The parallel is the point: the Lord too has adjuncts, a body and states, so 'that' as ordinarily named is no less conditioned than 'thou'. சருவதற்பா is read as சர்வ தற்பதம்.

reading: The omniscient, the all-doer, the inner ruler of all, the lord of all, the creator of all, the preserver of all and the destroyer of all are its names, girl of knowledge.
nuance: Seven Sanskrit epithets of Isvara (sarvajna, sarvakarta, sarvantaryami, sarvesvara, and creator, preserver and destroyer of all). Calling them 'names' prepares the next stanza's charge that they are adjuncts.

reading: What are these names? Spoken at length these seven are turiya; but because it took on adjuncts that do not yield, a fault has come upon release, girl of knowledge.
nuance: தூஷணம், fault or blemish, is the striking word: the Lord's own attributes, as adjuncts, count against liberation, so the 'that' must be stripped as the 'thou' was. Line 2 (வாதம் தரியமடி) is corrupt.

reading: The faulted jiva, having seen these seven, became the body of the one they name; because it is called the eternal place, its name is the shadow-grasp, girl of knowledge.
nuance: சாயாகிரகம் may be the reflection (chaya) of 2611, the jiva as Brahman's reflection, or a corrupt word; பானுக்கு is unclear (the sun, or பரனுக்கு, 'for the Supreme'). The reading is tentative.

reading: Calling the waking oneself, and beyond it the one who owns it: the wise will name him Virat; know it, girl of knowledge.
nuance: விராட்டன் (Virat) is the cosmic counterpart of Visva: the Lord identified with the gross universe in its 'waking'. காமர் is probably a misprint for the wise or the learned.

reading: The three adjuncts known, and joined in them, it is the supreme dream; the inseparable owner of it they call Hiranyagarbha, girl of knowledge.
nuance: இரணியகர்ப்பன் (Hiranyagarbha) is the cosmic counterpart of Taijasa, owner of the subtle universe as 'dream'. பர சொப்பனம், supreme dream, marks it as the Lord's state, not the jiva's.

reading: With one part of this, for the Supreme there is a deep sleep; the one who joins it, see in your mind, is called Avyakrita, girl of knowledge.
nuance: வியாகிருதன் is read as அவ்யாகிருதன் (Avyakrita, the unmanifest), the cosmic counterpart of Prajna; 2610 named the same three, Avyakrita, Hiranyagarbha and Virat, from the top down. பார்சுழித்தி is read as பர சுழுத்தி.

reading: See: as the meaning of the tat-pada was seen and known, hear the truth of the Siva-pada of knowledge, girl of knowledge.
nuance: Having done 'thou' and 'that', the kummi adds a third pada, Siva's, which is the Saiva extension of the Vedantic scheme found in Tirumular (the third, Siva's turiya). சிவகாதத்தி is read as சிவபதத்தின்.

reading: Having seen the true supreme turiya, but by the fault of not seeing it to the end, the Supreme became the body of the pure one of the cool Siva-pada, girl of knowledge.
nuance: The pattern repeats: each tier's 'body' is the tier below seen incompletely. Here even the Supreme (பரன்) serves as the body of Siva, the pure one, so that Siva stands above the Isvara of the tat-pada.

reading: The supreme world-devouring and the upasanta, which are spoken of: for the Siva who has practised one of these three kinds, there is the supreme waking, girl of knowledge.
nuance: விஸ்வகிராசம், 'devouring the universe', and உபசாந்தம், quiescence, are names for Siva's states, the world absorbed and the stillness beyond it. பர சாக்கிரம், supreme waking, is the first of Siva's states. The grouping 'one of three' is unclear.

reading: The one who owned the Siva-waking, which is the thing that comes to be, is Siva-turiya, gathered; so the saying declares, girl of knowledge.
nuance: Line 3 (சேகரமாயிடிறசிறசொலிதையென்று) is garbled and the stanza is read only in outline: the வாக்கியம், the great saying, is said to declare the owner of Siva's waking.

reading: The saying is the world-devouring; the Siva-dream that is the path of bondage, and its fortunate owner, they call Prajapati; say it, girl of knowledge.
nuance: பிரசாபத்தன் may be Prajapati or a corrupt name; the source has a dash in the line. Calling Siva's dream பந்த மார்க்கம், the path of bondage, is odd and may be corrupt.

reading: And what is told as upasanta is the Siva deep sleep; if one stays in it, he is the good and graceful one called Santa; is that not desire, girl of knowledge?
nuance: The final question, அது காமம் அல்லவோ, turns on the scheme itself: resting in Siva's deep sleep as a 'peaceful one' is still a wish. It echoes the litany of ஆசை in 2657 to 2661.

reading: In the named Siva-turiya, losing identification and standing alone, is that not the true welfare? They have not seen the state of the first turiya, girl of knowledge.
nuance: அபிமானம் இழந்து தனித்து, losing the sense of owning and standing alone, is the sign of the last tier: no one owns this state. ஆதி துரியம், the first or primal turiya, which 'they have not seen', leads into the next stanza's turiya beyond.

reading: What has not been seen is the complete turiya; seeing it and whirling, it is the highest; bow to the ancient form of Brahman-bliss and dance the kummi.
nuance: முற்றிரியம் is read as முற்றுத் துரியம், the complete turiya, or turiyatita, beyond all three tiers. சுழன்று, whirling, may be the dance of the kummi or the whirl of the central channel.

reading: This is the knowledge bowed to; this is the supreme bliss; look boldly, worship the one whose form is bliss, and dance the kummi.
nuance: After the analysis the stanza turns to praise; துணிந்து பாரு, 'look boldly', asks for a direct seeing rather than more counting.

reading: The happy jiva to be worshipped and the pure supreme thing are this; is this not the foot of the flawless guru whose form is the Self, girl of knowledge?
nuance: The identity the whole analysis sought, jiva and supreme thing as one, is finally located at the guru's foot, a pun the kummi also makes in 2693 (பாதம், foot, and பதம், word). சொரூபக் குரு is the guru who is the Self.

title: ஞானக்கும்மி
theme: The last ten stanzas of Madurai Valaisami's Njanak Kummi, sung to the 'woman of knowledge' as a dance song, compress a Vedantic conclusion: the 'thou' and the 'that' of the great saying are one, the whole world is of one's own nature, moksha is knowledge itself and all other rules are the mind's delusion, egg and body alike become void and beyond them the great void. The thing cannot be told or heard, has no far, and will not stand in word or stone; the song ends by counting its own 185 stanzas and blessing the sadguru's feet and the Tamil of the kummi.
structure_note: The great saying and its names (2693 and 2694); the world as one's own nature and moksha as knowledge (2695 and 2696); what cannot be told, and the void (2697 and 2698); what word and stone cannot hold, and the subtle the guru alone tells (2699 and 2700); the colophon, counting the stanzas and blessing guru, poet and learners (2701 and 2702). The refrains ஞானப்பெண்ணே and கும்மி அடியுங்கடி alternate; the readings give what each stanza adds.
source_issues: This text writes அறிந்து as அரிந்து (2699 கையரிந்துகொள், 2701 அரிந்துகொண்ட).
2699: சோதிபையாகியை is corrupt or compressed and is not rendered beyond 'Brahma-light'.
2697: தாரார் is doubtful.
2694: அகக்தெளிந்து has a stray letter for அகந்தெளிந்து.

reading: It became the pada that is 'thou', and in it the foot that is the pada 'that'; the differences, the limiting adjuncts, the states and the many names all became it.
nuance: தொம்பதம் and தற்பதம் are the Tamil forms of the tvam-pada and tat-pada of 'tat tvam asi'; the stanza says the one became the other, with பாதம் (foot) punning on பதம் (word). What 'it' is that became them is carried over from the previous chapter and is the one thing of 2696. The syntax is a chain of nominals, so the reading supplies the subject.

reading: For the sake of a name it is called the peaceful turiya; what is spoken of is self-luminosity; having seen the thing no one can see and become clear within, dance the kummi.
nuance: பேருக்கு, 'for the name's sake', concedes that சாந்த துரியம், the fourth state at peace, is only a label; தற்பிரகாசம், shining of itself, is the Vedantic svaprakasa. The stanza names the state and in the same breath says the naming is a convenience.

reading: Like the Devadatta who gains release, the whole world became of its own nature; Nandi, do not let go; is this not the rule of the grammar?
nuance: தேவதத்தன் is the stock 'Devadatta' of Sanskrit logic and grammar examples, the anyone who serves as the subject of a sentence; the stanza seems to say that, as in the textbook example, whoever is released finds the world to be himself. நந்தியே may address the Lord as Nandi or the guru; விட்டு விடாதே, 'do not let go', then asks him not to release the hold of grace. இலக்கண ஞாயம், the justice or rule of grammar, keeps the textbook figure. The whole stanza turns on this learned joke and the reading is tentative.

reading: This knowledge is moksha itself; every other rule is the mind's delusion; one's own resolving and doubting, and the sects, all became one's own nature.
nuance: ஞானமாம் மோட்சம்: release is not a result of knowledge but is the knowledge. சங்கற்ப விகற்பம், resolve and doubt, is the mind's whole activity in Vedantic terms; adding சமயம் to it puts the religions among the mind's constructs, yet the stanza absorbs them into the one nature rather than condemning them.

reading: There is no far and no farther; there is no telling it and no hearing it; women, look at the Brahman state that none can grant, and leaping, dance the kummi.
nuance: தூரதூரமும் இல்லை, no distance at all, denies that the goal is reached by going anywhere. தாரார் is unclear: 'they will not give', so a state no one can hand over, or a corrupt word; the reading takes the first. The stanza's denial of telling (சொல்வது) stands in a song that goes on telling for 185 stanzas.

reading: The egg and the body both became void, and beyond the cutting-away is the great void; delighting in the Parapara Brahman as what is and is not, dance the kummi.
nuance: அண்டமும் பிண்டமும், cosmos and body, go together as the Siddhars' one system and are voided together. அறுக்கப்பாலும் may be 'beyond what is cut off' or 'even on the side of cutting', that is, beyond the act of negation itself. உண்டு இல்லை, 'is, is not', is the paradox the Vedantic Siddhars use for Brahman; the stanza asks for delight (உவந்து) in it, not for argument.

reading: It will not stand in word or in stone; know and take in hand the Brahma-light, the pure space, the strong silence that shines of itself, O woman of knowledge.
nuance: சொல்லினும் கல்லினும் நில்லாது: neither speech nor inscription holds it, a nod to the song's own limits. சோதிபையாகியை is corrupt or compressed; the reading keeps only 'Brahma-light'. கையரிந்துகொள் is கை அறிந்து கொள், 'know and take in hand', since this text writes அறிந்து as அரிந்து (so also 2701). தூவெளி, the pure space, is Tirumular's word.

reading: In the earth-element purity came under sway, and in return differences arose many and many; the guru will tell the end of the sruti; can the wide subtle be known, O woman of knowledge?
nuance: The first line is obscure: பிருதிவியில் தூய்மை வயமாச்சே may say that the pure one came under the sway of earth, the grossest element, and that from this the many differences (பேதம்) arose, a Vedantic account of the one becoming many in matter. The second half makes the guru, not the sruti, the one who tells its end, and leaves the subtle (சூட்சம்) as a question.

reading: Worshipping the feet of the great ones who have come to know, and not departing from the Tamil of the kummi, the poet says he has spoken a hundred and eighty-five stanzas; long live the sadguru's feet.
nuance: நூற்றெண்பத்தைந்து கண்ணி, 185 stanzas, matches the count of the work as parsed (this unit is the 184th and the next the 185th), so the colophon's count is intact. அரிந்துகொண்ட is அறிந்துகொண்ட, 'who have known'. கும்மித் தமிழ் claims the dance song as a vehicle of knowledge, as Tirumular claims Tamil for the agama.

reading: Long live the sadguru's feet greatly; long live Valaisami's Tamil daily; long live greatly the path of knowledge of those who learn the virtuous Tamil of the Njanak Kummi.
nuance: The poet names himself, Valaisami, and blesses his own Tamil alongside the guru's feet; the வாழி formula is the conventional close of a Tamil work. ஞானநெறி, the path of knowledge, is what the learners gain, not the stanzas themselves.
